Besides, we were leaving from Calais, heading for Lyon. It wasn’t like we were crossing into Switzerland. Aye, well, I'm glad you didn’t. Imagine the bother. "Mr. Davies, we believe you are attempting to violate Article 47 of the EU's agricultural import regulations with a suspicious quantity of cured meat products." But everything was so stressful beforehand, planning the route, the accommodation, trying to navigate the French autoroutes… I just needed something familiar. A taste of home. But – and it's a big but – I’d booked a supposedly "charming" Airbnb. Turns out “charming” meant "dated," "smells faintly of damp," and "shared bathroom with a family of six who seem to think midnight showers are perfectly acceptable." Ouch. That sounds… less than ideal. Did you complain? Complain? I wrote a strongly worded review. And switched rooms. After practically yanking the duvet over my head and pretending I wasn’t there. The worst part was, I’d brought all these fancy research notes – you know, the ones I’ve been working on for months – and the little table they gave me was wobbly. I spent the entire trip terrified I was going to spill coffee all over my findings. You and your precious notes.

Right, this Monopoly game has officially broken me. I’ve landed on Mayfair for the third time, and honestly, I think I’m going to have to sell my kidneys to pay rent to Leo. I'm going to be richest! A castle on Park Place. It's a bit ambitious given you started with £1500. Perhaps we can focus on a slightly smaller… bungalow? Bungalows are boring! Castles have dragons, Mummy! And knights! Leo, would you be a dear and help me find the sprinkles? The pink ones are in the top cupboard. I will supervise! Make sure Mummy doesn’t accidentally make a boring cake! Can I have the candle first? Please? It's for my castle! One thing at a time, darling! Sprinkle retrieval is priority number one! And Leo, be careful up there, you’ll knock everything over. And no eating the sprinkles!

Honestly, Liam, I'm fair knackered. That tagging project nearly did me in. Four days straight sorting through verb conjugations… it's enough to make a girl lose the plot, it is. You always say that, Maisie. You’re a marvel, honestly. A corpus administrator dealing with verb conjugations? Sounds about as exciting as watching paint dry, but you seem to thrive on it. Thrive? Don’t be daft. I tolerate it. There’s a difference. And it weren’t just conjugations, Liam! It were archaic verb forms, dialectal variations… a right mishmash. I swear, I learned more about 18th-century Northumbrian farming practices than I ever wanted to know. Well, that  is  a little niche. You were talking about that professor yesterday, the one from Durham. Did he share any particularly illuminating insights? Aye, he did. He were on about how the Northern dialect retained older forms of grammar longer than the Southern ones, because of, like, less interaction with the rest of the country. Keeps things pure, he reckons. Pure and utterly baffling when you're trying to categorise it. I’m starting to think he romanticises being geographically isolated. There’s definitely something to that. The preservation of linguistic heritage, it’s quite fascinating, isn't it? It's the same in engineering, actually. Old bridge designs, for example – you can often see the ingenuity of the original builder shining through, even if modern techniques would do it quicker. They understood the fundamentals, didn't they? Fundamentals, yeah. I think the people writing these texts just understood how to… well, how to  speak  properly, proper and honest. Not like all that manufactured poshness you get down South. No offence. None taken. Although, I’d argue Hertfordshire isn’t exactly dripping with manufactured poshness. It's… comfortable. And there’s a difference, you know? It's… it’s just…  different . Aye, different. And usually involves a lot more money. Look, I'm not trying to start a thing, alright? Just saying, there’s a certain… sincerity about the way folks talk up North. Less conscious of how they’re sounding. True. There's a certain…directness. Which can be refreshing. So, you’re completely done with the tagging project now? Back to analysing sentiment in 21st-century Twitter posts? Don’t remind me. At least the Twitter stuff is relevant. People complaining about the price of petrol, arguing about politics… it’s messy, but it’s  real .

Right then. Kettle’s on, Marjorie. Fancy a cuppa? Rain's comin' down a treat out there, innit? Proper Norfolk drizzle. Aye, Arthur, put the kettle on, you old fool. Been waitin’ for a cuppa since breakfast. And stop whinging about the rain. It’s good for the roses. Roses can fend for themselves, Cyril. They’ve been doin’ it for years without me frettin’ over ‘em. Besides, it’s dampenin’ the telly signal. Can't get a decent picture of  Antiques Roadshow  with this weather. Honestly, you two. Always complainin’! A bit of rain never hurt anyone. Arthur, dear, you look like you’ve lost your best friend. What’s botherin’ you today? Just… things, Marjorie. Just things. They’re buildin’ a new roundabout down by the Moulton Road. Another one. Don't they ever stop? They’re diggin' up half the village. Roundabouts! Waste of money, that’s what they are. More traffic congestion than they solve, mark my words. Remember that one they put in by the park? Absolute chaos. Oh, Cyril, you’re exaggerating as always. Roundabouts are perfectly efficient. They keep the traffic flowin'. Although, I do agree, sometimes it feels like they put them in just to annoy us. It’s a conspiracy, I tell you! A conspiracy, Marjorie? You’re off your rocker. Though, there  is  somethin’ odd about it. They're always puttin' 'em where old allotments used to be. Know what I mean? Used to be people growin' vegetables, now it’s just… concrete. That's right. Mrs. Higgins used to win prizes for her marrows down there. Absolute monsters, they were. Now, it's all swirling cars and frustrated drivers. Progress, they call it. Bah! You're both being terribly nostalgic. People have to move on, Cyril. And besides, you can’t grow decent marrows in this weather anyway. It’s too blustery. Though, I do miss Mr. Finch's prize-winning pumpkins. Remember those, Arthur? He used to carve them into the most extraordinary shapes. Aye, remember. Used to be a proper spectacle, that. He even had one shaped like Nelson's Column once. Took him weeks, he did. Now everything’s just… mass-produced. And this roundabout... it’s disrupting the badger sett. I read about it in the  Norfolk Gazette . Badgers! Honestly, Arthur, you'll be startin' a petition next! Worryin' about badgers when they’re diggin’ up our heritage.

Honestly, Anon, your place is lovely. So much brighter than I remember! Birmingham’s really changed, hasn’t it? Feels… more cosmopolitan. Glad you think so! Took ages to decorate, but it’s finally starting to feel like home. Right, about Honest Skincare… I massively appreciate you coming round, Chloe. I’m proper stuck. Don’t be daft, it’s no trouble at all. I’m fascinated to hear how it's going. You really hit the ground running with those initial batches, didn’t you? The lavender and chamomile balm is divine, by the way. My skin has been thanking me. Thanks! That means a lot, actually. The balm’s been our best seller, for sure. It's the thing people keep coming back for. But getting the word out… that’s the killer. I’ve been trying Instagram, obviously, but it just feels like shouting into a void sometimes. Instagram is tough. Algorithm's a nightmare. Have you considered targeted Facebook ads? They can be surprisingly effective, especially if you focus on interests – natural skincare, cruelty-free beauty, things like that. We did some targeted advertising for the language school and it made a difference. I’ve looked, but it all seems so complicated! Honestly, I'm terrified of wasting money. And I’m not even sure what measurements to use – impressions, reach… it’s all a blur. Do you understand all that stuff? A bit, yeah. Let's break it down. Impressions are how many times your ad is  seen , reach is how many  unique  people see it. You want a good reach, obviously. And click-through rate – how many people who see it actually click on it – is crucial. We monitored that closely. I used to have a spreadsheet, it was a proper mess, but it did show which ads were performing best. A spreadsheet! Oh my. I can barely manage the stocktake. Speaking of which, I've got a huge problem with the sizing of my shipping boxes. I ordered a load of them, thinking they’d be perfect for the new face masks, but no. The masks are thicker than I initially anticipated, and they're squashing the little dried flowers I put in as a finishing touch! It's awful. Oh, that's frustrating. Did you measure the masks properly before you ordered? I'm terrible at that myself, always underestimate. It’s like trying to picture furniture in a room – it always looks smaller in your head.

Dreadful news about the flooding up north, isn’t it, Arthur? Honestly, heartbreaking to see those poor people displaced. Makes you appreciate a dry roof, doesn't it? Even this slightly damp one. Absolutely, Elsie. Terrible. They’re saying it's the worst they’ve seen in decades. The coverage is relentless, of course. Though, I must say, the government’s response seems… sluggish. As usual. Sluggish is putting it mildly. It’s always the same, isn’t it? Promises and hand-wringing, but very little practical help until well after the damage is done. I read a piece earlier about the communities struggling to get insurance. It's just infuriating. Reminds me of the miners' strike, in a way. Feeling utterly abandoned. I can see the parallels. Although the specifics differ, that sense of being let down by those in power... it’s a horrifying echo. Did you hear they’re linking it to climate change again? More and more extreme weather… Hard to ignore it now, isn’t it? Even  you , dear brother, used to scoff at all that climate change talk. Remember? Said it was all exaggerated for political gain. I may have been a bit... sceptical. Let's say I was keeping an open mind. But you're right, Elsie. It’s hard to rationalise away what we’re seeing. The evidence is piling up. Still, I think politicians like to have their fingers crossed on these things, hoping it all blows over before they have to actually  do  something. Exactly. Speaking of doing something... how's the marking coming along? Still drowning in those essays, are you? Drowning is an accurate descriptor. Year 11 Geography. Bless their little hearts, they think a blank map and a vaguely relevant anecdote constitutes a compelling argument. I’ve marked three essays already and I'm considering a strong cup of coffee and a lie down. One student actually wrote an entire paragraph about… wait for it… Minecraft’s impact on understanding landscapes. Oh, Arthur! You're having a laugh, surely? I wish I were. I actually had to Google it. Apparently, it’s a “popular educational tool.” I’m not entirely convinced. Though, I suppose it does show they’re engaging  somehow . Goodness me. Well, at least it's not dull. Do you ever think about… well, what you’ll do when you finally retire? I mean, properly retire.

Right then, everyone dig in! I've made enough for a small army, I think. Hopefully, there's something for everyone. I was trying to incorporate some seasonal things – roast goose, obviously, cranberry sauce… and I even managed to get some decent mulberries from that little farm shop near Swindon. Anyone else fancy them? Goose! Brilliant. Thanks, Elara. You know I'm a sucker for a good roast. Mulberries, you say? Sounds interesting. I’ve never been a massive fan of berries in general, but I'll give them a go. This is amazing, by the way. So much better than lukewarm turkey and soggy sprouts. Oh, you're preaching to the choir, Liam! My family is  notorious  for their festive culinary disasters. Last year, my Aunt Carol tried to deep-fry a whole Christmas pudding. It didn’t go well. Anyway, this all looks lovely! Mulberries, you say? Yes, please. They’re lovely with a bit of cream. Deep-fried Christmas pudding… right. That’s… ambitious. I’ve seen some questionable attempts to salvage Christmas dinner in my time, though nothing quite that dramatic. Though, my Nan used to put pickled onions in everything. Everything! Christmas dinner, Sunday lunch… you name it. Mulberries sound good though. Are they like… raspberry-but-different? More delicate, I think, Rhys. Slightly sweeter, a bit of a subtle tang. They're surprisingly hard to find good ones. Right. So, aside from the food, has everyone been surviving this ridiculous weather? It's freezing! I'm burning through a fortune on heating. Tell me about it! The workshop's been absolutely Baltic. I’ve got the industrial heater on full blast just to keep the bits and bobs from seizing up. I'm seriously considering investing in one of those fancy smart thermostats. Optimise the heating, save a few quid… maybe even afford a proper holiday next year. Retirement feels impossibly far away still, though. Retirement! That’s a concept I can barely grasp, honestly. I'm still in the thick of my PhD. The thought of not being buried in research papers is actually quite terrifying. Though, I do dream of a little cottage in Cornwall, gardening, and just… being. Away from all the academic pressure. Cornwall sounds alright. I’m thinking more of Skye, myself. Somewhere wild and dramatic. Somewhere I can build a studio and really focus on the woodwork. I’m trying to expand my range, experimenting with some new tools actually.

Honestly, Mum, this cutlery situation is ridiculous. You’ve got three forks for every spoon, and a mountain of knives. It's like you’re preparing for a siege. It’s classic Mum, isn’t it? She's a collector, bless her. Remember that time she bought twelve identical tea cosies from a car boot sale? Don’t you start, you two! It's not collecting, it’s being prepared! You never know when you might need an extra setting. And besides, your father insists on having a specific knife for spreading butter. A specific one! Aye, she's right. Can’t have just any old knife doing the job, can we? Butter deserves respect. Proper respect. Butter... used to be a decent bit of butter, it did. Not like this spread stuff. Tasted like nothin'. Not a proper taste. See? He’s already joined the cutlery debate. It’s a family tradition. Dad, you're worried about butter, and Grandma's lamenting the demise of real butter. Speaking of traditions, did you see Sarah's photos from her holiday? She’s in Santorini. Looks amazing. We really should try and book something next year. Somewhere hot, eh, Mum? Santorini, you say? Costs a fortune, that does. But… yes, a holiday would be nice. We haven’t been away properly in ages. How about somewhere a bit closer to home though? Bournemouth? We could get a nice little B&B near the beach. Bournemouth's alright. Bit… predictable though, isn't it? I always thought the Lake District was lovely. Walking boots, fresh air… you know. The Lake District? Dad, you'd complain about the midges the entire time. And Mum hates walking. Remember that brief attempt you had at getting her to climb Snowdon? Don't remind me! I haven’t felt so tired in my life. I nearly had to be carried down. Your father kept saying, "Just a little further, love! The view will be worth it!" The view was grey rain! You were a trooper, Mum. You really were. Look, maybe Santorini is a bit ambitious. We could look at Cornwall. Nice beaches, some decent walks if Dad insists, and Mum can have afternoons of cream teas. Cornwall sounds good. I'd like that actually. It's been ages since I've been near the sea. I miss the smell of salt air. It’s funny, growing up in Germany, you take the sea for granted.

This shepherd's pie is lovely, love. You've really outdone yourself tonight. Though, honestly, I could eat a whole other one. This day… just completely drained me. It  is  yummy, Mummy! Can I have more peas? Pleeease? Of course, darling. So, tell me, did you have a good day at school? Did you learn anything exciting? We did painting! I painted a sparkly unicorn! It has rainbow hooves. Miss Davies said it was very… vibrant. Vibrant, eh? Sounds delightful! She’s got a good eye, Miss Davies. Right, where were we? Oh yes, my day. It was… well, it was a saga. Honestly, Mr. Harrison seems determined to make my life difficult. Who’s Mr. Harrison? He’s... a colleague. A particularly frustrating colleague. We're working on the Peterson account, you know, the big one? And he's constantly undermining everything I suggest. Today he presented  my  marketing strategy as his own in the meeting! Can you believe it? That’s not fair! Why would he do that? I don’t know, love. Probably just wants to climb the ladder a bit quicker. It’s infuriating, though. I spent weeks researching and developing that strategy. Weeks! It’s like all my hard work is being ignored. I might have to speak to Sarah in HR. Will that make him stop being icky? Hopefully, love. Hopefully. It’s not pleasant having to deal with that sort of behavior. It takes away from actually  doing  the work, doesn't it? And right now, I'd rather be planning our skiing trip. Have you been looking at the pictures of the resort I sent you? Mmm-hmm! The snowy mountains are really big! And there are fluffy bunnies! Are there  really  fluffy bunnies in the snow? Well, I haven't seen any bunnies yet, but the pictures definitely show lovely snow-covered scenery. And the ski school has a brilliant reputation, you know. They have special lessons for beginners. I was thinking you could have a few lessons, just to get the hang of it. No pressure, obviously. Can I wear a sparkly hat? One with pom-poms? Absolutely! You can wear the sparkliest, pom-pommiest hat they’ve ever seen! We’ll have to get you a proper pair of salopettes, though. Pink ones, I think. With glitter, maybe? Pink  and  glitter! Yes, please! Will Daddy ski with me? He will, of course.

Ugh, this homework is brutal. Seriously, Mrs. Davies is trying to kill us with quadratic equations. I swear, I’m having flashbacks to Year 7 Maths. Tell me about it! Mr. Peterson gave us, like, fifty vocabulary words for English. Fifty! And they’re all proper obscure ones. Did you get 'ephemeral'? I had to Google it. Ephemeral? Yeah, I looked that one up too. Something about being fleeting? Honestly, why are we learning words no one actually  uses ? I'd rather be learning Spanish. Exactly! Remember how Mrs. Ramirez said we could actually, like,  use  Spanish when we go on holiday? Imagine ordering tapas in Barcelona without sounding like a complete muppet. Right? I’m picturing myself pointing at random things on the menu and hoping for the best. Although, I did kinda like that little programme we used in class, Duolingo. It’s less terrifying than actually speaking to someone. It's alright, but it doesn’t really prepare you for actual conversations. My mum’s trying to get me to watch Spanish dramas on Netflix. I said I'd give it a go, but I’m worried I’ll just end up crying because I don't understand a word. Oh, proper relatable. My little brother tries to watch those Brazilian football matches and just gets frustrated. He just yells at the screen. It's hilarious, actually. Speaking of hilarious... Food Tech today! Don’t even  start  me. What even WAS that supposed to be? The teacher said it was a "deconstructed shepherd's pie," but it looked like a building collapsed on a plate. Honestly! My mashed potato was rock solid, and my peas were swimming in watery gravy. At least Liam dropped his mince all over Mr. Henderson. That got a laugh out of everyone. Oh yeah, I saw that! Poor Mr. Henderson. He looked like he wanted to cry. Remember last year when Chloe set off the fire alarm trying to deep fry something? That was a proper chaos. Don't remind me! The whole school had to stand outside in the rain. It was freezing. Still, better than eating that Shepherd's Pie… though I'm not sure how much. Thinking about it, I’m proper peckish now. Are your parents home yet? Not yet. Mum's still at that meeting with the parents association. She's been on about it for days. Said something about fundraising for new sports equipment.

Cor, this Cambridge air is a bit nippy even indoors, innit? Mind you, it's a blessin' after Essex, always feelin' like you’re steppin' into a sauna back there. So, you were sayin' about this film, love? The one with the… superheroes? Yeah, ‘Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3’. It's brilliant, Nan. Really brilliant. I know you’re not always keen on those superhero films, find ‘em a bit… noisy, you say? Noisy is the word, alright. All bangin' and flashin' and shoutin'. Give me a good drama any day. Something with a bit of heart, you know? Like ‘Brief Encounter’. Now  that  was a film. Proper weepie. Right, but this one... it's got heart, too. Honestly. It’s still got the humour, obviously, you know, Rocket's a riot. But it also deals with… some pretty heavy stuff. Animal cruelty, loss, finding your family even when you don’t expect it. It’s more than just explosions. Animal cruelty, you say? Oh, I don't like that, do I? Not one bit. Animals are precious. Remember old Jasper, our dog? Used to follow me everywhere when I was a girl. A proper scamp, he was. It’s done sensitively, Nan, really. It’s showing the background of the characters, you know? Why Rocket is the way he is. It's actually quite moving. And the soundtrack is incredible. Classic 70s stuff, all the songs I grew up listening to. Seventies, eh? That was a right mess, the seventies. Three-day week, punk rock… Not much good came out of the seventies, apart from… …well, I can’t think of anything! Come on, Nan! David Bowie! Fleetwood Mac! Fleetwood Mac… now you’re talkin’. Rhiannon, wasn’t it? Proper haunting. Makes you feel a bit sad, doesn't it? I always thought Stevie Nicks looked like she was carryin’ the weight of the world on her shoulders. Exactly! It’s got that vibe. Anyway, James really loved it, and he's pretty hard to impress with anything that isn't a gritty Scandinavian noir film. He even said he cried a little bit. Oh, the man blubbered, did he? Didn’t think I’d ever see the day! So, it's got you both proper taken with it then? Yeah, completely. It’s… well, it’s emotionally draining, but in a good way. Restorative, almost. Makes you appreciate the good things you've got.

Right, so, Dad’s definitely up for the cricket match next Saturday, isn’t he? He was saying how he hadn't seen Warwickshire play in ages. Oh, yes, dear. He was practically bouncing when I mentioned it. Kept going on about how they needed a proper shout-out from the stands. You know your father and cricket. It’s like a religion to him. Though, goodness, the parking around Edgbaston these days... dreadful. We'll have to leave early. I was thinking we could carpool. I'm happy to drive. Less hassle than both of you trying to navigate the one-way systems. Though, honestly, Birmingham drivers… sometimes I think they’ve never seen a roundabout in their lives. It’s a bit terrifying. Oh, you're not wrong about that, love. It's gotten worse. All these new people, you know? Not everyone knows their Highway Code. Though, you're a good driver, you are. Much better than your dad, bless him. He still insists on using his indicator  after  he’s turned. Says it’s “more of a courtesy.” A courtesy to the oncoming traffic, maybe! He’s hopeless. Remember that time he nearly drove into that bollard outside the library? Don't remind me! I thought my heart would stop. Luckily, it was only a little scrape. Though, having to deal with the paperwork afterwards... You know, sometimes I think being a court usher isn't all standing around looking important. It's a lot of forms and filing. And the legal jargon! Absolute gobbledegook half the time. You do a fantastic job, Mum. It must be fascinating though, seeing all those cases come through. Anything particularly interesting recently? There was a rather odd one last week, involving a parrot. Apparently, the bird was inheriting a considerable sum. A will dispute, of course. Very complicated. The solicitor was arguing the parrot was “a beneficiary,” and the other family members were claiming it was ridiculous. Honestly, you wouldn't believe the arguments people come up with to contest a will. Reminded me of Auntie Maureen and that fight over Grandma’s collection of ceramic cats. Oh, don't even start me on Auntie Maureen. Always causing drama. Speaking of money though, have you looked at your energy bill yet? Mine's astronomical this month. I’m thinking of switching providers, but it’s such a faff. I haven't, actually.

Honestly, this air is just  divine  after being cooped up in that stuffy lecture hall all day. I think I've officially inhaled enough dust to last me a lifetime. You and history. It’s a dangerous combination, apparently. Did you manage to wrangle those essays back from the students? I swear, marking those Byzantine Empire papers felt like deciphering ancient hieroglyphs. Nearly. I’ve got about seven left. Sarah’s done a really thoughtful one actually, surprisingly. She usually just parrots back everything I say. This time, she’s brought up some interesting points about the role of women in the court, particularly the Empress Theodora. It's made me reconsider some of my own arguments, actually. Perhaps I’ll integrate a little of it into the next lecture. See? Always something to learn, even from the students. Speaking of integrating things, did you see the WeChat message from Mrs. Chen about the silk market? She said they’re having a huge clearance sale this weekend. No! Seriously? A clearance sale? You know I’ve been meaning to get a proper silk scarf for ages. The ones you can get here are just...well, they’re often a bit flimsy, aren’t they? I want something that feels luxurious, you know? Like it will last. Exactly! She said there's a stand with some seriously high-quality stuff, direct from Hangzhou supposedly. Worth a look, I think. We could make a whole afternoon of it. Maybe grab some dumplings afterwards? Dumplings sound  wonderful . My stomach's been rumbling something fierce all afternoon. Though, thinking about shopping, are you absolutely sure you don't need anything? Don’t want you lugging bags and complaining all the way home. Always a worry, isn’t it? No, honestly, I'm good. My wardrobe is currently operating on a ‘minimalist’ approach – meaning I haven't bought anything new in six months. Besides, I suspect you'll end up buying me something regardless. You always do. That’s not true! . Though I might pick you up something... maybe a new tie? You’re running dangerously low on decent ones. That navy blue one you wore last week looked a bit crumpled. Crumpled? It was vintage! Perfectly distressed. And besides, I prefer my ties simple. No need for flashy colours. Unlike some people . It’s vibrant! One has to add a little cheerfulness to the gloom, wouldn’t you say?

Right, okay, so let’s just solidify this. Saturday then? I’m clear to babysit both of you, Florence and Leo - all day. From, say, eightish? That gives me time to actually finish this Victoria Sponge before it gets too… gooey. Eightish? Can I have sprinkles on it, Mummy? Please? Of course, darling. Mountains of sprinkles. As long as you help me lick the bowl clean afterwards. That's the really important part, isn't it? Leo, darling, don't knock the blocks over! Those are new, remember? Almost… almost… got it! So, Saturday is sorted. That means I can properly catch up with Sarah and Emily. It's been ages! Literally months since we all managed a decent coffee and a proper natter. I'm so overdue for a girl's day out. Are Sarah and Emily bringing ponies? Can I ride a pony? No, love, I don't think Sarah and Emily are bringing ponies. They’re bringing… grown-up conversation. Honestly, you'd be bored stiff. Although... maybe we could look up some pony videos on my phone later? No! It fell! It's alright, sweetheart. We can build it again. Higher this time! Speaking of things needing building, your hair, Leo. It’s getting a bit… wild. Think we need to bite the bullet and get you a haircut? Mine too, Mummy! It’s tickling my face when I eat. I know, my sweethearts. I was thinking maybe next week? I've booked a slot at Little Snips, they're really good with kids. Less tears, more bravery rewards, that’s their motto. And Florence, you've been wanting to get your fringe trimmed for ages. We could do that at the same time. Can we get glitter spray? Like Princess Aurora? Let’s not get  carried  away with glitter, darling. We'll stick to something a little more… practical. Maybe some hair gel? Can I have a superhero cut? Like Spider-Man? We’ll see, don’t push your luck. Now, about the photoshoot. Remember Gran mentioned wanting some pictures for her birthday? I was thinking we could do it next Sunday, in the garden, if the weather holds up. We'll need to get the fairy lights out, and maybe that cute little straw hat you love, Florence. Yes! Can I wear my sparkly shoes? Of course, you can wear your sparkly shoes. It's a photoshoot, darling, sparkle is practically mandatory.

Honestly, this canteen food is getting worse, innit? Last week it was that grey, congealed gravy on everything. Today, the chips are practically soggy. Tell me about it! My nan always says university food is a special kind of torture, designed to make you appreciate a proper home-cooked meal. She's from the Philippines, you know, makes the  best  adobo. Way better than this… this beige buffet. Proper. My mum tries, bless her, but she’s always got, like, five different things on the go. Last night it was shepherd's pie, roast veg, and a fruit crumble. I felt guilty eating all of it, but I  did . You’re a champion! Me, I’m just trying to survive on instant noodles and the occasional stolen biscuit from the library. Studying for that History essay is killing me. It's just so much detail! All those dates... ugh. Oh, don't even get me started on the essays. My Sociology one is even worse. It’s all theoretical frameworks and whatnot. I feel like I'm just regurgitating what the textbook says without actually  understanding  anything. Professor Davies is proper intense too. Davies? He’s the one that makes you feel like you're failing just for breathing wrong, yeah? I had him for a guest lecture last year, and I swear I didn't look him in the eye the entire time. Did you hear about Chloe and Mark? Apparently, he pulled them aside after class to tell them their arguments "lacked intellectual rigor." Brutal. No way! Poor things. See, that’s why I’m terrified to ask any questions. I'll probably just sound daft. You won't. He's just a showman, loves a bit of dramatic pause. Anyway, forget about essays for a minute. Friday night – are we still on for going to that new cocktail bar in Richmond? ‘The Velvet Fox’ or something? Yeah, definitely! I checked it out online, apparently their raspberry mojitos are to die for. I need a serious wind-down after this week. I was thinking maybe we could convince Liam and Sarah to come too? Good shout! Liam’s been looking a bit stressed lately. He's got that massive presentation next week for his Marketing module. He's been talking about target demographics and brand loyalty non-stop. It's a bit much, to be honest. Tell me about it.

Aye, this brew’s a bit weak, innit? Not like me Nan used to make. Strong enough to stand a spoon in! You're always comparing everything to your Nan, aren't you, Maisie? It's a lovely thing, though, all that family pride. And this  is  a decent Earl Grey, honestly. Your Nan probably used some obscure blend only available in Sunderland. It's a really nice flat, Anon. Very Cambridge, very… curated. Plants everywhere. You’ve done well. Thanks, Tom! Anon's a natural interior designer, apparently. It takes hours, though – you should see the effort that goes into arranging those succulents. Maisie, you look like you’re about to launch a complaint. What's wrong now? Nah, not a complaint, just…different. Everything's so tidy! Back home, if you tripped over somethin', you'd just apologize to it. Here, I'm scared I’ll knock somethin’ over and Anon’ll have a heart attack. She’d be mildly annoyed, at most. And then she'd get out the dustpan and brush. Seriously, though, how was the train journey up? Everything go alright? I know you said you were a bit nervous about it. It were grand, actually. Got a window seat, which were a bonus. Saw loads of countryside – proper green, not the grey I'm used to. And I managed to avoid any awkward small talk with the bloke opposite. He kept lookin’ at me, though. Like I were a rare species or summat. Men do that sometimes, Maisie. It’s usually harmless. Probably just admiring your… vibrancy. Vibrancy? You think I’m vibrant? I were wearin’ me best trainers, so maybe he thought I were an athlete. You're certainly full of energy. Anyway, we were talking about holidays. Did you manage to book anything for the summer? I’m still stuck on deciding between Greece and Italy. I were lookin’ at the Lake District. Me Auntie Carol reckons it’s beautiful up there. Lots of walkin', fresh air… a good chance to burn off all the chips I’ve been eatin' this week. Reckon it’d be a bit quiet for you two, though, eh? Quiet isn’t always a bad thing, Maisie. A bit of peace and quiet is exactly what I need after these past few months with the Thames project. Constant meetings, endless revisions… my brain feels like scrambled eggs. Speaking of eggs… Anon made this incredible shakshuka for brunch this morning.

Cor blimey, London. Right posh place it is, innit? Reminds me of… well, reminds me of when I went with me auntie Elsie back in '68. Never thought I'd be goin' again, though. All that hustle and bustle. Gives a fella the jitters, it does. It will be nice, Harold. A change of scenery. And we can finally see that play you wanted to, the one with the chap from… what's his name? Poldark? Aidan Turner, that’s the lad! Lovely fella he is. Not got much hair, mind you. Like me, in that respect. Though I always liked a full head o’ hair. Used to spend hours greasing it back, I did. Proper Elvis style. Right, so are we all agreed then? London it is for next month? I’ve just been looking at train tickets, and they're not cheap, are they? Especially on a weekend. No, they aren’t. But we've been saving, haven't we? And it's been ages since we've done anything properly. Remember that Youth Hostel trip to Cornwall years ago? That was a laugh, wasn't it? The dorm full of youngsters, all playing their music… Aye, that was a right knees-up. Though I recall complainin' about the smell of damp blankets something fierce. Me sinuses weren't takin' to it, see. You always complain about something, Harold. Honestly. I’m thinking of putting my car up for sale, actually. The Fiesta’s got a bit too big for me now, with the school runs easing off. Wonder if it's worth much these days? Well, let me see… what year is it? Probably not a fortune, dear. But it’s always good to have a bit extra, isn't it? This market’s bonkers with houses too, isn't it? Seems like everyone's sellin' up. Tell me about it. Old Mr. Perkins down the road's put his place on. Been there fifty years, he 'as. Says he's tired o' lookin’ after the roses. Shame, really. A lovely garden it was. Though he did shout at me once for me dog diggin' in 'em. Little rascal, Toby was. Speaking of houses, did you hear about the election? It's all anyone's talking about at school. The kids are fascinated by it all, even if they don’t quite understand. So much to sort out.

Honestly, this is such a blessed relief. Just to be somewhere quiet and not surrounded by grant proposals and linguistic analyses. How's little Leo doing? He seems… bigger than the last time I saw him. He is, isn't he? Growing like a weed. He’s hitting a bit of a clingy phase at the moment. Doesn’t want to be put down for five minutes. Keeps giving me this look, you know? Like, “Mum, where are you?!” It's adorable and exhausting in equal measure. He’s mostly been feeding well though, which is a win. Still exclusively breast, which I'm determined to keep up for as long as I can. Good for you! It’s such a commitment. I remember reading a lot about the benefits for the research – the cognitive development, the gut microbiome… But actually  doing  it is another thing entirely. Mum keeps going on about how she bottle-fed us both, and how ‘perfectly well’ we turned out. Oh, Mum. Always. She genuinely believes formula is as good as the real thing. It’s a generational thing, I think. She just doesn’t get the science behind it. And she's worried I'm not going to be able to go back to… well, anything, if I'm constantly on demand for feeding. I can see that. The idea of going back to work full-time feels so distant right now. Trying to balance everything even  without  a baby must be tough. Are you thinking about getting any help? Not just from Mum, although she’s clearly been amazing. Mum's been a lifeline, truly. I don't know how I’d cope without her popping in. But I’m trying to think about something more… formal, I guess? A childminder, a nanny, even just a few hours a week. But the cost… it's scary. And finding someone I trust… that’s another hurdle. You know how I am about people watching  my  baby. I do. You've always been fiercely protective. And rightly so. I can look into it, actually. My work has a network of vetted childcare providers, some of whom are quite affordable. I could pass on some leads. No pressure, obviously. Honestly, that would be a huge help. Thank you. I'm just feeling a bit overwhelmed. Little things, you know? Like trying to choose a reusable nappy brand.

Honestly, David, did you  see  the price of petrol yesterday? It’s just ridiculous, isn’t it? Absolutely daylight robbery. I swear, every time I fill up the Clio, I feel like I'm donating to a charity I didn't choose. Morning, love. I did see it. Shocking, innit? They keep bleating on about inflation, but it feels like it’s specifically targeting anyone who needs to drive. Got to say, these government policies… they're a right mess. Shall I pop down to the garden centre later? The roses need a good feed. Morning, everyone. Petrol’s awful, yeah. Makes the commute so much more expensive. I’m thinking about trying to cycle in a couple of days a week, weather permitting, of course. Though dodging those lorries on the A20 is a bit terrifying. Anything exciting planned for today? Morning, all. Oh, petrol, don’t even get me started. I nearly had a heart attack at the pumps yesterday. And did anyone see that report about the sewage discharges into the Thames? Absolutely appalling. I'm volunteering at the beach clean-up on Saturday. Anyone fancy joining me? Need all the hands we can get, really. A beach clean-up? That’s lovely, Brenda. I wouldn't be able to manage it, though. My knees are playing up again, you know. Fiona needs to be dragged off the sofa to do anything strenuous these days. She’s still snoring, bless her. The teenager. Fiona’s a late riser, always has been. Always loved sleeping in. Reminds me of myself at that age, sneaking out to Southport pier at dawn with my mates… those were the days. Anyway, about the garden… I was thinking of trying those climbing roses up the back wall. You reckon that’s a bit ambitious for this time of year, love? Climbing roses sound gorgeous, Dad! A bit ambitious, maybe? It  is  getting a bit chilly, isn't it? But definitely worth a try. I have some tips gleaned from Pinterest if you need them. It’s probably best to prep the wall first, get it cleaned and all that. Easier to train them properly then. Actually, speaking of Pinterest, I’m trying to revamp the living room. I was thinking a deep teal accent wall behind the sofa? What do you all reckon? Teal? Hmm. A bit dark, isn’t it? For a Kent living room?

Ugh, Maths test tomorrow. I’m properly dreading it. Mrs. Davies is being extra brutal this year, innit? Like, quadratic equations? Seriously? Tell me about it! I spent ages trying to understand those. I think I got, like, half of the homework right. Though, honestly, I’m more stressed about the Science one after that. Mr. Patel expects us to actually  know  stuff, not just parrot back from the textbook. Science is alright, I guess. Plants are kinda interesting. You know, how they like, photosynthesise and all that? My nan’s got a right jungle in her garden, it's incredible. She's got this massive fern, bigger than me! What about you? Any good plant knowledge? My dad tries to grow tomatoes, but they always end up a bit…sad. He blames the slugs. He’s really into gardening though, you know. He showed me how to propagate succulents last week. It's actually pretty cool, making new plants from cuttings. Bit science-y, actually! Yeah, I guess! My art teacher, Mr. Finch, keeps going on about the Fibonacci sequence and how it’s in nature and everything. Claims it explains why the sunflowers grow the way they do. Blimey. It’s all a bit much when I'm trying to draw a decent still life. He does that, doesn’t he? Mr. Finch and his maths-in-everything thing. I saw him trying to explain perspective using stamps the other day. It was… something else. Look at this one! Do you collect stamps? Not really. My grandad used to, used to have a whole album full of ‘em. All proper old and dusty. He was always going on about their value. I didn’t really pay much attention. He and Gran used to travel loads, bought them from all over the place. They’re in Norfolk for Christmas, you know. Norfolk! That’s miles. Are you going? Yeah, we’re off on Boxing Day. It's a bit of a trek. Still, it’ll be good to see everyone. Are you seeing much family at Christmas? Just my immediate family. We’re having Ed Sheeran on repeat, obviously. My little brother is obsessed. He's trying to learn 'Castle on the Hill' on his recorder. It's… an experience. Oh, blimey. Poor you. Remember last Christmas when Tilly kept calling Dad 'Santa'? Oh god, don't remind me! She was convinced he was the real deal.

Cor blimey, Brenda, look at this. Found it clearin' out me attic. Remember these things? A rat puppet. Proper little thing, innit? All felt and whiskers. Used to scare the living daylights outta young Timmy when 'e were a lad, 'e did. Oh, Arthur! Goodness me, yes! I remember. You made that, didn't you? For the village fete, years ago. You were ever so clever with your hands. Did a smashing job. Timmy was terrified, bless him. He’d hide behind me, screaming like little. What's all the commotion? Sounds like a squadron of Spitfires taking off in here. And what’s this I see? A rat? Arthur, you haven't taken up taxidermy in your retirement, have you? Don't be daft, Peter. It’s a puppet. A little bit of fun back in the day. Before all this…you know… . Remember the fete, Peter? You won the coconut shy that year. Vaguely. Coconut shy wasn’t exactly my forte, was it? Honestly, I'd have been better off managing a chain of coconut shy businesses, thinking back. More profitable, likely. Though, I suppose that wouldn't suit my skillset. Tea, anyone? Earl Grey, as usual, Brenda? Lovely, thank you, Peter. You always were a good host. Arthur, do you remember those handbell ringing practices at St. Mary’s? That was a right lark, wasn't it? Though I always struggled with ‘Greensleeves’ – kept messing up the high notes. You did, love. Sounded like a cat fightin' a badger sometimes. But it were good fun. Miss them days, I do. Proper community spirit, that was. Not like it is now. Everyone glued to their screens. That’s progress, Arthur. Inevitable, I suppose. Though, I admit, I do occasionally miss the days when a conversation required nothing more than a cup of tea and a bit of chit-chat. Speaking of which, Brenda, have you booked your eye test yet? You were saying last week… Oh, goodness, no. I've been putting it off. Dreadfully bad at remembering things these days. It's like my brain's got cobwebs, it 'as. And the buses…oh don’t even get me started on the buses! They’re never running on time anymore. Used to be able to set your watch by them. Now, you're lucky if one turns up within twenty minutes. Makes visiting the shops a real ordeal.

Right, so, that canal boat tour sounds dead good, doesn't it, Mum? I reckon we should book it for this afternoon. It's supposed to be lovely weather. Could do with a bit o' sunshine after that drizzle we had yesterday. Aye, it does. A canal boat, that’d be nice. Though, remember when this place was just… well, just a building site? Café Venice? Ha! It used to be O’Malley’s chip shop, you know. Proper greasy chippy it was. Best chips in Bolton, mind you. Seriously? I can’t imagine it. All fancy coffees and cakes, and it was a chip shop? I only know it as Café Venice. It's always been Café Venice to me. You never told me that! O'Malley's... that sounds like something from a black and white film. Oh, aye. Early eighties it was. Kevin O’Malley ran it. Big fella, Kevin was. Always had a smile on his face. Used to know me from when I was a kid, back when we all used to play down at Smithills School playground. This whole area used to be full of fields then, you know. Not all this paving and building. Crazy. It’s hard to picture. They built that new housing estate practically on top of those fields. Remember trampling through them as kids, trying to find wildflowers? I do. Used to pick armfuls of daisies for your grandma. She adored daisies. Anyway, O’Malley’s was a lifeline for us, honestly. After a long shift at the hospital, a portion of chips and gravy was just what I needed. Good, honest food. Not like all these avocado toasts and things they have now. Don't sound so grumpy about the avocado toast, Mum! It’s tasty. Still, I do miss a good chip shop dinner. We should get some tea tonight. Proper fish and chips. That's the plan, love. After the canal boat. I’ve been readin' up a bit about Venice itself, you know. Apparently, they’ve got some amazing seafood. Risotto al nero di seppia… that’s risotto with squid ink! Sounds a bit weird, doesn't it? Squid ink? Definitely weird. But then, I did have escargots in Paris once… That was an experience. I'm not sure I’m brave enough for squid ink risotto though. Maybe I'll stick to pasta. There’s always pasta. They do a lovely seafood pasta there, apparently, with mussels and clams.

Honestly, this is  exactly  what I needed after that meeting. Mr. Henderson was going on and on about stakeholder engagement - like, do I need to write a sonnet about it? Tell me about it! My boss, Sarah, is obsessed with wellness initiatives at the moment. Apparently, Bupa needs to  really  demonstrate it cares about its employees' mental wellbeing. So, we’ve got yoga on Thursdays and mindfulness workshops... It’s almost comical. Yoga? Seriously? Do you actually  do  yoga? I tried that once, felt like a pretzel. Ended up pulling a muscle reaching for my water bottle. I’m only pretending, mostly. I’m absolutely terrible. But it looks good on paper, you know? Management seems pleased. How’s the project going then? Still firefighting? You have  no  idea. The supplier keeps messing up the delivery dates. It's like pulling teeth to get them to stick to the schedule. I spent most of this morning writing passive-aggressive emails. Need to get back to beating my head against a brick wall tomorrow, I suppose. So, how was that holiday you were planning? Bali, wasn't it? Bali was incredible! Seriously, you absolutely have to go. The beaches were gorgeous, the food was amazing… I'm still dreaming about the mango smoothies. I went with Chloe and Liam. Liam mostly just complained about the humidity, bless him. Typical Liam. Were you both, you know…? Oh god, no. Absolutely not. It was purely a friendship trip. Besides, I’m still recovering from  that  disaster. Remember Tom? How could I forget? The one who ghosted you on your birthday? Seriously, what a tool. Still hearing anything about him? Nope. Vanished. Like he was abducted by aliens. I’ve actively avoided the group chat where he used to be. It's far too tempting to unleash my inner Karen. I'm trying to be better about moving on, you know? Focusing on myself. Hence, Bali. Good for you! You deserve that. Honestly, I've been so consumed by work, I haven’t really had time for anything else. The gym is pretty much the only thing keeping me sane. Have you been back since your holiday? Actually, how's your knee feeling? Last time we spoke you were worried about it. It's better, thanks! The physio gave me some exercises, so I’ve been religiously doing them. Although, I might have overdone it a little yesterday… a  slight  twinge this morning.

Honestly, Arthur, having little Leo in our lives has just been… transformative. It’s a whole new level of joy, isn’t it? Even you, with your rather stoic demeanour, you seemed quite moved when you met him. Moved? Possibly. Alarmed, more likely. All that gurgling and grasping. It reminds me a little too much of being a newborn, truth be told. One forgets the sheer intensity of it. Though, of course, he's a delightful little chap. But tell me, has Eleanor decided where she’s planning to settle? I understand she’s considering France. She is! She and Mark are seriously looking at a small village in the Dordogne. Apparently, property is surprisingly affordable – or at least, it  was  when they last looked. Mark's hoping to start a small, online business – artisan cheeses, he thinks. Something niche. Artisan cheeses! Of course. France. It suits them. Although, don't romanticise it too much, my dear. Bureaucracy there can be… astonishing. Layers upon layers of it. And then you have the anarchists! A bewildering combination, really. Though, I did once meet a delightful gentleman in Toulouse who ran a vineyard and declared himself an anarchist with a socialist heart. Rather confusing, wasn't he? Sounds like it. We had some lovely French visitors last summer, actually. The Dubois family. They were fascinated by everything – even the humble London bus. Asked a million questions about the workings of the transport system. It's always amusing to see it through foreign eyes. They perceive something entirely new. Speaking of things crumbling, have you heard about Chichester Cathedral’s spire? Apparently, part of it collapsed. Dreadful business. I saw it on the news! Terrible. And utterly shocking. I remember reading about the architect, George Gilbert Scott, and his work on it. Something about the original structure and the challenges of reinforcing it. Did you know there was an architect called Porden who had some influence back then? A bit obscure now… Porden… Yes, vaguely familiar. He was rather touched by the Pre-Raphaelites, wasn't he? There's an open day coming up at the Architectural Heritage Society, actually. A photo exhibition and an art competition themed around threatened architectural landmarks. Might be of interest to you. That sounds wonderful! I'll look into it. It’s just such a shame about Chichester. It's a glorious cathedral. On a completely different note, have you seen what they've done with the bollards on Streatham High Road?

Ugh, these are… okay. Not amazing. My nan makes way better. You know she puts a secret ingredient in hers? Nobody knows what it is, she just smiles mysteriously. Your nan's cooking is legendary, yeah. This is alright, though. Better than the chips we had last week at Ben’s. Remember that? They were practically fossilized. Fossilized is spot on, Liam. They had that weird grey tinge to them. Ben’s clearly lost his touch. Still, beats the school canteen, right? Agreed. At least here they have something that vaguely resembles food. I’m starting to think they just chuck whatever’s left over in the bin into the school pasta. Seriously! Remember last Tuesday's 'chicken' pasta? It tasted distinctly of… something else. I’m sticking to the spring rolls, even if they  are  a bit bland. So, anyone actually managed to finish the history essay? I’m completely stalled. I stared at the blank page for an hour last night and all I got was a headache. Cromwell felt very judging. I did, surprisingly. Got it done on Sunday. Found a really interesting documentary on YouTube, actually. Explains the whole religious stuff much better than the textbook does. You should check it out, Leo. YouTube and history essays. Bold move, Rhys. Mrs. Davies would have a heart attack if she found out. Worth the risk. Got a decent grade on my last one after doing that. Plus, it was genuinely interesting. What about you, Mark? Did you at least  start  yours? Started? I wrote the title. That’s about it. I’ve been busy battling Doctor Doom all week. New comic dropped on Wednesday. Absolutely incredible. He's finally revealed his master plan. Doctor Doom again, Mark? You’re obsessed. You spend more time saving the fictional world than you do studying for real one. Hey! Saving the world is important! Besides, it's stress relief. School’s stressful enough. You guys should get into comics. It’s a much more engaging way to spend your time than… I don’t know… writing about dusty old kings. Point taken. But someone's gotta write about the dusty old kings, otherwise who'd learn about them? Then how would you know which ones were actually alright, and which ones were total villains? Like, Cromwell. So, speaking of villains… Heard anything about Sarah and Ben splitting up? Apparently, she saw him messaging another girl.

Oh, this clearing out is something fierce, isn't it? Feels like a lifetime of things just… accumulating. Poor Jonathan, having to deal with all this birthday paraphernalia on top of it. Aye, it is. Though, I must say, seeing these pictures is lovely. Remember that trip to Whitby, Elsie? Jonathan was about Finn’s age then, absolutely glued to that fossil shop window. Whitby? Is that near the seaside? Dad says it’s really windy there. Windy doesn't even cover it, Finn. It’s practically horizontal. Right, needs some more fairy lights for the banner, I think. It’s just… lacking something. Branding, really. Jonathan's birthday needs  branding . Branding? For a birthday? Goodness me, Michael, you’ve got your writer's hat on tight, haven’t you? It's a lovely boy's birthday, not a product launch. Just a bit of fun, Elsie. A touch of pizzazz. Besides, you said it felt like a lifetime of accumulating things. A celebratory banner helps solidify the moment, doesn't it? Captures it. Back in my day, a bit of string and a handwritten card was all you needed. Fancy banners and ‘branding’... the world's gone mad. Though, I will say, that picture of Jonathan with the donkey at Scarborough is rather charming. He was terrified, absolutely petrified! But stubborn as a mule - just like his dad. Speaking of which, where  is  David? He said he’d be back from the supermarket ages ago. I asked him to get those ginger biscuits Jonathan likes. He was muttering something about the price of everything doubling. That new supermarket on the edge of town... charging a fortune. Absolutely scandalous, it is. Mum, can we have chips with the biscuits? Please? It's a birthday! David texted. Said there was chaos at the tills. Apparently, they're having problems with their new self-checkout system. Nobody knows how to use it properly. It's ridiculous, really. These companies think technology is the answer to everything. Technology! Don't get me started. Trying to use that new television remote is enough to drive a person to distraction. Give me a button and a knob any day. It’s simpler. Well, that’s settled then. No chips with the biscuits, and we'll skip the supermarket entirely. Elsie, do you think you could rustle up a nice cheese and onion pie? Jonathan always loved your cheese and onion pie.

Honestly, choosing GCSE options is like, the worst. How are we supposed to know what we’re going to  need  in like, ten years? It's mental. Tell me about it! My mum's being all, "Think about your future careers, darling!" Like, I'm fourteen! My future career might be professional cloud watcher. That’s actually quite a dreamy job. I’m really torn between History and Geography. History’s got all the drama, right? Wars and monarchs and… well, drama. But Geography's, like, actually useful, innit? Like, understanding climate change and stuff. Geography's definitely more practical. My cousin did it and now she works at some environmental thing. She's always posting on Instagram about recycling, which is great, but… a lot. Like, loads of stories about compost bins. Oh god, no. I'm not getting into that depths of compost bin enthusiasm. Do you ever look at those bogs and bloggers? The ones doing “sustainable living” stuff? It’s all curated perfection. Ugh, totally! It's all like, hand-woven baskets and organic kale smoothies. No one's got time for that! Remember that one who pretended to be living off-grid in a yurt, and then it turned out she was renting a posh cottage in the Cotswolds? Oh my gosh, yes! That was ridiculous. It's like, be real! I'd rather watch Alfie Deyes. At least he’s honest about the fact he films in his bedroom. True. I'm obsessed with that new beauty YouTuber, Chloe Ting. Her workout videos are brutal, but I need something to distract me from the impending doom of choosing subjects. Do you think people actually make a living from YouTube? I reckon some do. Like, MrBeast, right? He’s crazy rich. I saw an interview with him and he was talking about how he started by just reacting to videos. Mad. Makes you wonder if I could, you know, start posting clarinet covers. You? Playing the clarinet on YouTube? That would be brilliant! You're actually pretty good, remember that school concert? Mrs. Davies kept going on about your intonation. Yeah, well, she has to, doesn’t she? It's her job. But I do like playing it, it’s just… clarinet videos aren’t exactly trending, are they? Maybe you could do something different. Like, clarinet covers of popular songs? Or...a series explaining the history of the clarinet?

This Earl Grey’s a bit weak, innit? Not like Mrs. Higgins used to make. Proper brew, that woman. Mind you, she’d put anything in it – rose petals, lavender… said it was 'good for the soul'. Rose petals! Right, that she did. Remember when she tried to convince us all that nettle tea was the secret to a long life? Nearly choked poor Elsie on it, she did. Elsie swore off tea entirely for a week after that. Costessey was full of characters, back in the day, wasn’t it? Full of 'em. It certainly was. Though I suspect Mrs. Higgins invented half the stories about Costessey. She had a knack for embellishment, that one. Though I miss her terribly. It's quiet, isn't it, without voices buzzing around. It is, yes. Though, honestly, I’m finding this new software utterly baffling. I’m trying to grade these essays, and the system keeps insisting I haven’t attached a rubric. I  know  I attached a rubric! It's infuriating. It’s supposed to be making my life easier, not adding another layer of technological misery. Technology. Don’t get me started. Remember when a slide rule and a bit of paper was all you needed? I designed entire bridges with a slide rule! Now it’s all CAD and simulations and… and things I can barely comprehend. Tried to help your mum with her email yesterday, ended up nearly deleting her entire contact list. Nearly gave her a heart attack, I did. Progress, they call it. More like a right bother, if you ask me. Used to be, you could fix things. A bit of elbow grease, a few choice words to the offending component, and it was right as rain. Now? Now you need a degree in computer science just to change the channel. Oh, Arthur, you're such a technophobe! It's not  all  bad, you know. I could video call my granddaughter in Canada. Wouldn’t have dreamed of that in my younger days. Though I still prefer a good handwritten letter. Feels more… personal, somehow. I agree, Mum. There’s something to be said for the tangibility of a letter. But trying to explain to a university student that they shouldn't rely solely on online research for their history essays… well, that's a losing battle. They just stare blankly and then start quoting Wikipedia.

Cor blimey, that rain's comin' down a treat, innit? Like a waterfall, it is. Never seen it so persistent, even for Norfolk. It is dreadful, Arthur. Absolutely dreadful. Makes you want to just curl up and do nothin’ but knit. Though I did promise Elsie I'd have that cardigan finished for her birthday. She’ll be ever so pleased, you know. Elsie always was a good soul. Well, at least it’s kept the delivery men away. Had a package expected this morning, important documents for the school. Still nothin'. Been tryin' to track it all mornin'. It's frustrating, to say the least. You wouldn't believe the hassle with the printers this term. Delivery men, eh? Had a young fella round earlier wi’ a parcel for Mrs. Higgins next door. Looked about as pleased to be deliverin' it as I am to be wearin' these trousers. Faded floral, they are. Brenda bought 'em for me back in '98. Bit past their best, they are. She reckoned they were “cheerful.” Cheerful for the moths, more like. Oh, Arthur, you and your wardrobe! Remember that bright orange shirt you had? Honestly, it could have blinded a man at twenty paces. Brenda has good taste, though. Always did. Aye, well, Brenda liked bold. It weren’t to everyone's taste, I'll grant you. Reminds me of that joke I heard the other day. What do you call a lazy kangaroo? Pouch potato! Oh, Arthur. You’re terrible. A pouch potato. Good one, though. I was telling the kids at school some jokes yesterday, trying to lighten the mood. They're all stressed about these new exams. Trying to cram it all in. Exams! They've got so much pressure on them these days. When I was a girl, it was a case of learnin' the basics and hopin' for the best. Now, it's all data and analysis and… well, frankly, it’s confusing. Do those youngsters even  read  proper books anymore? Read? They’re all twitterin’ and that. Saw young Kevin, Mrs. Miggins’ grandson, glued to that mobile phone of his the other day. Said he was "following a cat." A cat! Spendin' his life starin' at a cat on a screen. Mental, it is. Social media, eh? It's a double-edged sword. Can connect people, but it can also be a huge distraction. I’ve tried to get involved a bit, but it just seems to be a lot of… well, negativity.

Aye, look at this! Proper blanketed, isn't it? Never seen this much snow in Cambridge before, 'as I've been. Reminds me of back 'ome in Sunderland, right enough. Used to build proper snowmen, we did. Massive ones. It’s a bit ridiculous, isn’t it? The whole city’s ground to a halt. Should be used to this sort of thing, being in England, but everyone’s acting like it’s the end of the world. Good for a snowball fight, though. Fancy a quick one in the garden? Not a bad idea! Though the garden's probably all buried. Speaking of which, how’s your prize-winning roses doing under all this white stuff? Did you manage to get them properly mulched before it hit? They’re... resilient. I covered them as best I could, but I'm not sure how they'll fare long-term. Honestly, I'm more worried about the rhubarb. It's supposed to be coming along nicely this year. So, snowball fight, or hot chocolate and discussing the absolute chaos of ‘Come Dine With Me’ last night? I nearly choked on me tea. Oh, don’t even get me started on the ‘Come Dine With Me’! That woman with the taxidermied squirrel collection… absolutely bonkers! And the music! I couldn’t breathe. Rhubarb's more important than snowballs, so let’s stick with hot chocolate and dissecting the madness. Good call. I’ve got that dark chocolate with the orange peel you like. So, squirrel lady aside, did you pick up anything useful from that research conference? Any breakthroughs in the field of obscure Victorian postage stamps? Don’t remind me. It was mostly regurgitated stuff, to be honest. A few interesting points on provenance, but nothing ground-breaking. Spent most of the time dodging awkward small talk and trying to look like I knew what I was talking about. It's all a bit exhausting sometimes, this research lark. I can imagine. My PhD is no picnic either, you know. Constant pressure. Still, at least I get to spend my days immersed in the fascinating world of early Medieval monastic manuscripts. Slightly less glamorous than obscure postage stamps, perhaps, but equally rewarding. Oh, I'm sure. Monks and their fancy writing. Right, stop showing off. Speaking of pressure... Ben’s stag do is looming. Have you had any more contact with his mates about it?

Cor, this is a right tasty pud'n, it is. Proper peas, these. Not them frozen ones, mind you - them’s like little green bullets. Your mum always did know how to cook a decent pea, Annie. Always did. Well, thank you, Arthur. Takes time, doesn't it? Proper peas need simmering, not just chucking in boiling water. Are you having enough, love? You haven't touched your roast. It's alright, Annie. Just not really feelin’ my appetite tonight. Bit of a rumblin’ in me stomach, that’s all. Probably somethin’ I ate. Though I can't rightly remember what it was. Been a quiet day, you see. Quiet as a mouse in a biscuit tin. Dad, you always say that! Quiet as a mouse in a biscuit tin. It's a very specific image. Everything tastes lovely, Mum. This gravy is especially good. Salt and pepper just right. Thank you, darling. I’ve been experimenting with a little smoked paprika this time. Just a pinch, you don’t really taste it, but it gives a lovely depth. Now, Daniel, how’s the vegan shepherd’s pie? Is it holding up alright? Honestly, it's fantastic, Sarah. Really good. The lentils are perfectly seasoned, and the sweet potato topping is… well, it’s smashing. Much better than anything I could have conjured up in my tiny student kitchen, that's for sure. Remember those days, Sarah? Living on beans and instant noodles? Vaguely. Mostly I remember you complaining about the lack of decent coffee. You were insufferable. Desperate times, darling, desperate times! But seriously, this is brilliant. You've really outdone yourself. Although, I wouldn’t mind a little clotted cream with my crumble later, if that’s alright. Always thinking about your stomach, aren't you? Of course, there's clotted cream. Plenty of it. It's practically a Norfolk requirement. Arthur, you want some cream with your crumble as well? Nah, I’m alright, Annie. Don’t want to overdo it. Gets a bit rich, doesn't it? Though… A small dollop wouldn’t go amiss, I suppose. Just a tiny one. So, how was your day, Dad? Did you manage to finish that puzzle you were working on? The one with the… boats? Aye, got that finished, I did. Took a bit o’ rootin’ about, it did. Lost the little mast for the fishing boat, didn't I?

This is lovely, Mum. Honestly, it’s so nice to just  sit  and eat a proper dinner. Work has been absolutely manic lately. Spreadsheet errors, endless emails… you wouldn’t believe. Tell me about it. The new software implementation has been a nightmare. Half the team still thinks Comic Sans is an acceptable font choice for client reports. It’s staggering. At least this roast smells amazing, though. Dad, did you buy that from Mr. Henderson at the market again? Aye, that I did, lad. Best beef in the county, that fella’s got. Always gives me a good deal, too. Reminds me of the butcher we used to have in Sale, back when I were a kid… Old Man Fitzwilliam. Now there was a character. Used to tell the worst jokes, but he knew his meat. Oh, don't even start with the Fitzwilliam jokes, Arthur! They were appalling. I remember one specifically, something about a sheep and a… well, never mind, it was too rude even for me. You look tired, love. That job of yours is really taking it out of you. Are you sleeping properly? It’s okay, Mum. Just a bit stressed. I’m trying to move into the sustainability department, though. It’s a bit of a long shot, but if I could get a role focused on green initiatives, that would be amazing. It feels so much more… meaningful than shuffling paperwork, you know? Sustainability, eh? Back in my day, we just called it ‘not wasting things’. My mum, bless her soul, she never threw anything away. Every scrap of fabric, every peel, every bone… went into something new. Made the best darn soup from leftovers you ever tasted. That’s amazing, Grandad. You should write a book! "Grandad's Guide to Not Wasting a Thing." It’d be a bestseller. He’d hate that, lad. He's a simple man. Still, he’s got a point. We do waste so much these days. Remember when we were kids, and you had to finish everything on your plate? Mum would make you wear your pyjamas to school if you didn’t! Don't exaggerate, Arthur! It wasn't that bad. A stern word, maybe. But your Dad  did  once make you eat Brussels sprouts with custard when you refused to eat them. Oh god, don't remind me! That was the worst culinary experience of my entire life.

Right then. So, this whole “flipped classroom” concept… it still feels a bit… brittle, doesn’t it? Like it needs a serious dose of kiwi pragmatism. All that pre-recorded material, relying on students to self-regulate… I've seen it crash and burn spectacularly in a few start-ups I've been advising. A lack of structure, you know? Creates chaos. I agree. The theory's lovely – freeing up class time for deeper discussion, application, critical thinking. But in practice, especially with the students I have… there’s a significant portion who won't even  look  at the pre-reading. And then you're trying to catch them up in a session that’s meant to be for higher-level engagement. It’s exhausting. I was thinking maybe a hybrid approach is needed? Something that's…layered. Layered, I like that. Like a good pavlova. Got the base, the fruit, the cream… each element building on the last. We could utilise micro-learning, surely? Short, sharp videos – three, four minutes max – focusing on one very specific concept. Then, interactive quizzes to check comprehension  before  the class. Not just multiple-choice, but something that requires them to apply the knowledge. Little simulations, perhaps? Yes! Exactly! And maybe embed them within a broader narrative. Storytelling, you know? It’s amazing how much more engagement you get when you frame things within a story. I read this article the other day about a history lecturer who completely revamped his course by presenting it as a detective investigation. The students were hooked. They felt like they were actively solving a mystery, rather than passively absorbing dates and names. Brilliant. A bit like that viral video of the tour guide in Iceland – the one who acts like a Viking shaman? The way he combines factual information with myth and performance… it just went ballistic. Viral for a reason. You could apply that principle. Instead of lecturing on macroeconomic theory, you present it as a crisis meeting for a fictional country facing inflation. Oh, I love that! It could work. But how do we ensure it’s accessible? Not everyone thrives with that much theatricality. Remember that entrepreneur I was telling you about, the one developing the app for autistic children? He was adamant that simplicity and predictability were paramount. Any deviation, any unexpected element, and it would trigger anxiety. Absolutely. Accessibility is key. Perhaps we offer different levels of engagement?

Honestly, this lentil soup is a lifesaver. I'm knackered. The Henderson project is threatening to swallow me whole. Three different stakeholders, all with wildly different ideas about what "user-friendly" means. It's mental. Tell me about it. My shift last night was… intense. Had a patient experiencing a particularly bad episode, requiring constant monitoring. It makes you grateful for a quiet cup of tea and a potential lentil soup dinner. Are you actually going to let me have some of that, or are you guarding it like a dragon? Don’t be daft. Of course! It’s a massive batch. Comfort food is vital after a day like mine. So, what part of intensive care did you say you're working in now? Still the acute wing? Yeah, still the acute wing. Though they're talking about re-organising. Might move some of us to the early intervention unit. Which, honestly, sounds much more rewarding. Helping people  before  things get too bad… less crisis management, more preventative care. That does sound better. Less rollercoaster, more… steady incline? Speaking of changes, remember that conversation we had about potentially moving? Yeah, I remember. Trying not to dwell on it too much, to be honest. Five years, though… feels a long way off. Where are you thinking? Still Sussex? Sussex is lovely, but a bit… limited, isn’t it? I was thinking maybe further north. Yorkshire, perhaps? I've always wanted to see the Yorkshire Dales. The landscapes look incredible. And it’s supposed to be more affordable, which is a definite plus. Yorkshire? That’s a big change. Don’t get me wrong, I love Sussex, but I'm not adverse to the idea of moving either. Yorkshire… I've been to Harrogate, it’s lovely. Proper quaint. But my family's all down here. That would be tough. I know, right? That’s the biggest hurdle. But five years… it’s a decent chunk of time. We could make trips back. And think of the opportunities! You could specialize in rural mental health provision—it's a growing field. You’ve clearly done your research. Smart. Okay, Yorkshire's back on the list. What about Halloween? Did you hear about Sarah's party? Apparently, she’s going all out this year – theme is ‘Haunted English Manor’. Oh, bloody hell! Sarah and her theatricality. I’m dreading it, to be honest.

Cor, this Cambridge air is a bit nippy, innit? Not like back home in Essex, mind you. Never been so cold in September. Though, I suppose it is a bit further north. Are you alright, love? You’ve gone a bit quiet. Yeah, yeah, I'm fine, Nan. Just… work’s been a bit stressful lately. Big shipment delayed, and Brenda in logistics is being utterly useless. Honestly, she’s got the organisational skills of a hedgehog. A hedgehog, you say? Bless her. Brenda, eh? Sounds like a right handful. Production Controller, you said? That sounds important. More important than me ever did, anyway. Worked in a sweet shop for years, you know. Now  that  was a life. Sticky fingers and happy children. Could never complain. It is important, Nan, but it’s just… pressure, you know? Meeting deadlines, chasing people, making sure everything runs smoothly. It feels like constantly putting out fires. And Brenda keeps misfiling the paperwork! It's ridiculous. They really need to invest in some proper training. Training’s all well and good, but sometimes you can’t teach old dogs new tricks, can you? Remember old Mr. Higgins down the butcher's? Tried to get him to use a computer once. Nearly had a heart attack, he did. He ended up just sticking to his scales and his carving knife. Much happier that way, the poor man. That’s a good story, Nan. But Brenda’s not like Mr. Higgins. She  knows  what she’s doing is wrong, she just doesn't seem to care. It's frustrating. I was thinking about talking to my manager, but I don't want to seem like I’m moaning. Now, don't you go thinking you're moaning, love. You're speaking up for yourself, that’s what you’re doing. And if Brenda's making your life difficult, you’ve got every right to say something. Managers are there to sort things out, aren't they? Don't let her walk all over you. You're a clever girl, you went to university and everything. Don’t let some dithering Brenda get you down. Easier said than done, Nan. I'm trying to be professional, you know? I don't want to create drama. Professional doesn't mean letting yourself get taken advantage of. Your mum always said you were a bit too good at keeping things bottled up.

Right, so, like, I’m still fumin’ about that match last night. Honestly, the ref was blind! Proper blind, I tell ya. Could’ve given a penalty clear as day. Oh, here we go. Don't tell me you’re still going on about it? It was a close call, Liv. A really close call. And anyway, it’s not like it massively affected the final score. Close call? Elsie, you weren’t watchin’ were ya? It could’ve changed the whole game! And it’s not just about the score, it's the principle! They’re gettin’ away with murder, they are. Proper scandalous. You wouldn’t understand, you're all posh and used to fair play in your Cambridge bubble. Oh, please. 'Posh'? And Cambridge isn't a bubble. It just means we appreciate a slightly more nuanced approach to… everything. Including football. Anyway, speaking of nuanced approaches, how's your translation project going? Professor Davies seemed pretty pleased with your initial draft. Aye, he did. Said I was gettin’ the gist of it. But it’s hard, isn’t it? Translatin’ poetry practically breaks me brain. Like, the words aren’t just words, are they? They're got feeling and rhythm and all sorts. It’s not just about findin’ the right English words, it’s about recapturin’ everything. I spent hours yesterday wrestling with the bit about the willow tree. Just couldn't lock onto it. I can imagine. It’s like trying to recreate a feeling, isn't it? That’s what makes translation so fascinating, though. It's not just a linguistic exercise – it’s a scientific method almost. You’re forming a hypothesis about the meaning, testing it against the original, refining… it’s brilliant. What are you comparing it to again? Baudelaire? That's right. Baudelaire’s 'Les Fleurs du Mal'. Proper depressing stuff, some of it. But then, the way he uses imagery… powerful, it is. Makes you think. What about you? Still buried in your neuroscience textbooks? Any breakthroughs with the memory experiment? Breakthroughs? More like brick walls. We’re getting conflicting results. Some participants show enhanced recall with the stimulation, others... nothing. It’s driving Mr. Hawthorne mad. He's swearin’ we need to re-evaluate our entire control group. Apparently, the biscuit color influenced something. I kid you not. He’s convinced the blue ones skewed the results. Blue biscuits?

Honestly, Brenda, I nearly jumped out of my skin this morning. Massive spider. Right in the bathroom, dangling from the ceiling. Honestly! It was easily the size of my hand. Oh, you and your spiders, Sarah! You always exaggerate. Probably just a garden spider. They do get big this time of year, mind. Though, I've seen some whoppers myself, working in houses, you know? Had one in Mrs. Henderson’s conservatory the other week. Proper hairy beast it was. Nearly spat my tea out. This wasn't a garden spider, Brenda. This was... different. Dark, almost black, and the legs… they were all… spidery. I googled it, you know, and now I'm even more terrified. Apparently, there's this thing called a False Widow. They're spreading. False Widow, you say? Blimey. Never heard of 'em. Sound nasty. Thankfully, I just tend to shoo the ones I see. Don't like killing things, you know? Even spiders. I considered letting it be, honestly. But then I thought about the children! They were due to come round later. And you know little Emily... she’s terrified of everything creepy crawly. Aye, she is. Remember when she thought the dust bunnies under the sofa were tiny monsters? Still gives me a giggle that does. Luckily, I managed to get a glass and a bit of paper and trap it. Released it in the garden at the back. Hope it finds somewhere nice. That's kind of you. I just… I don’t understand how they get in. I sealed the windows, checked the gaps in the door… They're clever little blighters, aren't they? Probably came in on something. Maybe a box from the shop. Or even a plant. You never really know.
