Speaking of clever… I had a right battle with a mouse in the bakery last month. Oh dear! A mouse? Really? Proper cheeky one it was. Kept darting out from behind the flour sacks. I swear it was laughing at me. The manager was fuming, of course. Said I wasn't catching them fast enough. It's hard work, you know, getting rid of them completely. They're like Houdini, those mice. Pop up in the most unexpected places. They even got into the pastry display case once. Made a right mess of the custard tarts. Goodness me. That's awful. Do you ever feel… invaded? Like your home isn't really yours when you're constantly battling pests?

Do please, Nesta, help yourself. It’s Earl Grey, your favourite, I hope? ANON mentioned you preferred it. Oh, that’s awfully kind of you, Eleanor. Earl Grey is lovely, yes. It’s been a while since I've had a proper pot. ANON’s always been a good egg, remembering little things like that. It’s lovely to finally put a face to the name, isn’t it? It’s a bit…unexpected, finding family like this so late on. I know exactly what you mean. It was a huge surprise for me too when we started looking into the family tree. ANON's been absolutely fascinated by it for years. You know, he’s been trying to trace our lineage back even further than we've managed so far. He's got charts and photos piled everywhere. Bless him. A proper little genealogist, then. My own family history is…complicated. Lots of movements, lots of branching off. My mother’s side was all Bristol dockworkers, rough and tumble lot, they were. My father’s were Welsh miners, from the valleys. Quite different lives, wouldn't you say? Very different indeed. My family’s more…settled, I suppose. Primarily Dorset. Farmers and tradesmen for generations. My grandfather ran the local hardware store, you know. It was a fixture in Dorchester for decades. We have some old photographs of him, all serious and proper in his tweed suit. I rather miss it, actually. Small towns feel different now, don’t they? They do. Progress marches on, doesn't it? Though sometimes I think we’ve lost a bit of something along the way. A sense of community, perhaps? I used to teach in a small village school in Carmarthenshire. Everyone knew everyone, looked out for each other. Bristol’s changed drastically since I left. I can imagine. I became a teacher too, you know. Didn’t end up back in Dorchester, though. Ended up in Stevenage. Bit of a culture shock at first, moving from a rural market town to a new town, but you adapt. I teach Year 5 now, a lovely bunch of children, chaotic as all get out, of course, but full of spirit. Year 5! That’s a good age. Lots of energy to channel, I imagine. I taught primary for most of my career. The young ones are always a delight, even when they're testing your patience.

Honestly, it’s quite a day for it, isn't it? Perfect clear blue, a gentle breeze… you could practically see five hot air balloons floating across the sky. Remember that trip to Cappadocia? Absolutely breathtaking. I do, vividly. Still think it was a bit terrifying, though. Being suspended like that, no real control… makes me appreciate solid ground a lot more. And Bess here wouldn't have been thrilled, I reckon. Too much open space to fall from. She'd have probably tried to chase it! She does have a penchant for anything airborne, doesn’t she? Saw a pheasant earlier, and she nearly pulled my arm out. It's a wonder she hasn't developed wings of her own trying to catch them. She’s a determined one, that's for sure. Found her trying to steal a badger’s lunch the other day. A badger! Can you imagine? Oh, goodness. Badgers are feisty. Served her right if she got a nip! Speaking of wildlife, have you noticed how much the skylark population seems to have dwindled in recent years? It’s quite sad. Used to hear them singing all day long when I was a kid, and now… barely a peep. It is noticeable, isn't it? Probably a combination of factors, I suspect. Loss of habitat, pesticide use… it's all a bit depressing, really. See those power lines over there? They're an eyesore, I know, but I wonder how much impact they have on bird migration patterns. Do you think they confuse them? I've often wondered that, too. There's been research, I believe. Something about how they disrupt the magnetic fields and disorient birds. It's another one of those things, isn't it? Progress vs. nature. It’s a constant battle. Makes you think about how much we sacrifice for… well, what, exactly? Convenience, I suppose. Comfort. And frankly, a lot of it is just habit. We've gotten used to having everything readily available. Did you ever think about suggesting a proposal to the university about a wildlife corridor along some of the fields bordering the campus? It might help mitigate some of the impact. It’s crossed my mind. It would be a mammoth undertaking though, wouldn't it? Getting the funding, the permissions... It would swallow up a significant chunk of my research budget, even just for a pilot project.

Honestly, that was a tougher set than last week. The heat's really baking down today, isn't it? Feels more like July than October. Aye, lass, it does. Proper daft weather, this. Remember when we used to get proper autumn? Crisp leaves, a bit of drizzle... Now it’s just… this. Scorching one day, shivering the next. Makes a fella miss a proper winter, it does. Absolutely. I’m starting to think ‘seasonal’ is a myth now. Though, I suppose it’s good for the tennis – keeps us playing longer. What are the gyms like at the moment? Are people still trying to squeeze in a workout before the weather properly turns? They are, aye. Though the summer rush has died down a bit. We’re seeing a bit of a downturn in the evening classes, people going back to routines, I suppose. The mornings are still busy, though – proper determined lot getting their fitness in before work. Managing all those locations and instructors… it's a constant juggle, you know? Trying to motivate people, especially now, when the motivation wanes. I can imagine! It's similar with my students. Getting them excited about verb conjugations in August is... a challenge, let’s say. What are your go-to motivational techniques these days? We're focusing a lot on positive reinforcement in our teaching workshops. Positive reinforcement, eh? It’s a sound principle, but sometimes, you need a bit of a nudge, eh? I find a bit of playful competition works wonders. Leaderboards, challenges… tapping into that bit of Yorkshire grit. My instructors are decent, but sometimes they need reminding that a bit of firmness can be a good thing. It’s not about being nasty, mind, but setting expectations. What about you? Do you find strictness helps for language learning? It’s tricky. You have to balance it. Too much strictness can cause anxiety and shut people down. We're trying to incorporate more communicative exercises - real-life scenarios. Like, they have to order coffee in French or negotiate a price at a market in Spanish. Much more engaging than drilling vocabulary lists. I've been reading this fascinating book about linguistics, actually. "Lost in Translation" – it's not just about subtitles, it's about how culture influences language and communication. "Lost in Translation"... sounds interesting. I’m not much of a reader, myself. Give me a good sports biography any day.

Right then, love. Grandparents due any minute, aren’t they? Did you get the biscuits out, Ben? Chocolate digestives, like Gran likes? Aye, Nan. Got 'em. And the fruit cake. Grandpa's been badgering me about the fruit cake for days. Says it’s not Christmas without it. Bit rich, coming from a man who claims to be on a diet! Bless you, Ben, lad. You’re a good grandson. Fruit cake, you say? Splendid! My bones are colder than a butcher’s slab, though. Is there a fire on properly, Elsie? Now, now, Doris. Don’t you worry your head. The fire’s roaring away nicely. Got it just the way you like it – not too fierce, just a good warm glow. Arthur, sit yourself down, love. You’re looking paler than a ghost. Pale? I’m always pale, Elsie. It’s the Hull air, I tell you. Never got any sunshine in that place. Always grey. You said that last time, Grandpa. And the time before that, and… well, every time you visit. Don’t you start, Ben. Your Grandad’s got his stories. And he likes tellin’ ‘em. Remember that time he tried to build a bird table, Elsie? Ended up with a pile of splintered wood and a very angry robin. Oh, I remember! He swore he’d follow the instructions, didn’t he? Ended up using more duct tape than wood, that one. It was a structural hazard! Duct tape? Seriously? Was it even safe to put a bird on it? It was perfectly safe! Just… aesthetically challenged. And I was learning! You don’t learn much sitting in an armchair, do you, Ben? Now, now, let's not start bickering. Ben's been busy. He's got his A-Levels to worry about, hasn’t he? Ben, did you manage to get that extra tutoring session booked? For the statistics? Aye, Nan. Tuesday after school. Mr. Harrison says I’m getting there. It's just... distributions are a nightmare. They keep shifting and… I just can’t visualise it properly. Distributions, eh? Like snowflakes. No two the same. But they all fall. Simple as that. Life's a distribution, Ben, lad. Sometimes you’re up, sometimes you’re down. Just gotta weather the storm. That’s a very wise thing to say, Doris. Perhaps you should write a textbook. Though I doubt it’d be approved for GCSE Maths.

Aye, this thing’s got us round in circles again, hasn't it? Honestly, these satnavs… they think they’re smarter than me, they do. I swear, last week it tried to send me down a farmer’s field. A  field , David! It's just trying to be helpful, love. Though I do admit, its routing choices can be… creative. At least we’re moving. This area's lovely though, isn't it? That ridge over there – that’s part of the Yorkshire Dales. Used to hike there a fair bit when I was a lad. Remember that time I slipped and landed in the beck? Covered head to toe in mud. Oh, I remember! You looked like you’d wrestled a badger and lost. Serves you right for trying to climb that dodgy bit of bank, didn't it? You always were a bit reckless. Speaking o'reckless, are you sure your back's alright for lugging your amp and all that equipment out of the car tonight? You were complaining something awful about it last week. It’s manageable, pet. Just a twinge. The physio gave me those exercises, you know, the ones I’ll probably forget to do the minute we get there. Anyway, the audience deserves a good show, even if it means enduring a little back pain. Did you see that kestrel hovering earlier? Beautiful sight, wasn't it? Proper hunter. Reminds me of that poem by Ted Hughes, ‘Crow.’ Bit bleak, that one, though. Aye, I did. Gave me a shiver down me spine, it did. Ted Hughes… always a bit dark, weren’t he? We need something a bit more cheerful for this gig, don't we? Maybe we should squeeze in a wee bit of The Proclaimers? “500 Miles” always gets a good reaction. Just needs a bit more practice before we get there. The Proclaimers it is then. Though I’m still convinced you're going to try and get everyone to do a ceilidh. Remember the last village hall we played? You nearly turned it into a full-blown Highland storm. Well, where's the fun if you don't?! It’s good to get folks moving. Keeps the blood flowing. Are you sure you haven't got any ideas for a poem about this journey? You know, about the rain we’ve got – it’s started lashing down now – and the grey skies and the…charm… of rural North Yorkshire?

Honestly, I’m still reeling from that site visit. The client’s vision is… ambitious, to put it kindly. They want brutalist concrete with a Scandinavian minimalist interior. It's a clash of titans, really. Brutalist and Scandinavian, eh? Sounds like someone’s been reading too much architectural theory and not enough building manuals. So, the usual 'we want something different, but also timeless and affordable' brief then? Precisely. And they keep mentioning “biophilic design” but can’t articulate what that actually  means  to them. It’s just a buzzword at this point. I spent twenty minutes explaining the principles of light diffusion and natural ventilation, and they just nodded politely. The nodding game. Classic. Remember that project we did for Henderson down in Bristol? Everyone had an opinion, and none of them aligned. We spent six months just placating egos. Don't remind me. Right, breakfast orders? I'm starving. I think I need something substantial after that mental gymnastics. I'm feeling a full English. Eggs, bacon, the works. Sounds good. I’ll have the granola with berries and honey, please. Trying to be healthy, you know. Although, your full English does look awfully tempting… Did you see Chloe last night? She looked absolutely drained. Chloe? No, what’s up? I messaged her yesterday, but she didn’t reply. She's really struggling at Finchley & Partners. Apparently, David’s being a nightmare to work with – constantly changing his mind, taking all the credit, and generally making everyone miserable. She was saying she's seriously considering jumping ship. Oh, that’s awful. Poor Chloe. David's always been a bit... much. He thinks shouting equates to leadership. I wouldn't put it past him to try and sabotage her. Exactly. It's heartbreaking to see. She's such a talented designer. Have you got any ideas? Maybe she could freelance for a bit, build up a portfolio? Possibly. It’s tough though, getting started on your own. Especially in this market. Though, remember that conversation we had last year about communal living? I was reading an article about co-living spaces designed with architects in mind - integrated studios, shared workspaces, communal kitchens… It's actually becoming pretty popular. Maybe she could find a place like that, network with other creatives, take on smaller projects to get back on her feet? That's a really smart idea, actually. It’s not just about the space, it's about the community.

Right, love, how was work today? Anything exciting happen at the DWP? You looked a bit knackered when you came in. Ugh, don't even ask. Absolute chaos. Apparently, there's been a system glitch with the Universal Credit payments again. People are properly stressed, ringing up non-stop. And Brenda from Payroll called in sick, so I ended up having to cover her stuff too. I’m running on fumes, honestly. Oh, sweetheart, that sounds dreadful. Dealing with people when they’re worried about money… that's a weight, isn’t it? You're doing a really important job, you know. Just remember to breathe. Milk and two sugars in your tea? Please. And yeah, I know, Mum. Everyone keeps saying that. It’s just… sometimes I feel like I'm not actually  helping  anyone. Just shuffling papers around and sticking plasters on things. Well, even a plaster can make a difference, can't it? Small comforts. Listen, let's not dwell on work. Tell me about Chloe and Liam - are they still going on about that camping trip next weekend? Yeah, they are. Liam’s been meticulously planning everything. He’s got colour-coded maps and a spreadsheet for the food. It’s ridiculous, but also kind of sweet, I guess. Chloe's just excited to get away from everything. I told them they should definitely go. They need a break. They do. Honestly, they work themselves ragged sometimes. You should go with them! Just a weekend? Fresh air, bonfire, proper laughing. I don't know, Mum. I’ve got so much on. And besides, I’m not exactly Bear Grylls, am I? Camping and I don’t get on. Tents, sleeping bags... damp everything. Nonsense! It's just a camping trip, not an expedition to the Arctic. You’d love it. And it would be really good for you to get out of the house. When was the last time you did something just for  you ? I don't know, honestly. Probably… that pottery class I signed up for and then abandoned after two sessions. Right, well, that’s a start. Look, how about this? Chloe and Liam are going, I’ll go with you for one night. Just a little breather. We could pop down the pub on the Sunday afternoon before you head back. You'd really do that? You hate camping. Well, I’d hate you burning out, even more.

Right, so let's have another look at this covering letter. I’ve made a few tweaks, but I still feel like it's… a little safe, isn't it? You’re applying for a Senior Producer role at BBC Radio Leeds, for goodness sake! They want someone with fire. Fire is good. But BBC Radio Leeds is also...official. They need to know you’re responsible, you can meet deadlines, you’re a team player. It’s a tricky balance, innit? My brain’s just a tangle of ‘show them you’re brilliant’ and ‘don’t frighten them off’ at the moment. The last interview I had, the interviewer kept looking past me like I was invisible! Dreadful. Oh, that’s awful! Were you any closer to finding out why? Did you mess something up? No idea. I just felt…disconnected. They asked me about my experience with managing large teams, and I talked about the community radio project I did, about how we built it from scratch and fostered this incredible sense of ownership amongst the volunteers. They barely reacted. Then they asked about audience engagement, and I tried to bring up the podcast series I spearheaded, and they cut me off to ask a technical question about file sizes. Honestly, I was flummoxed. Gosh. That sounds like they weren't even listening properly. It's almost insulting. Regarding the letter, I'm thinking, instead of saying "I possess excellent communication skills," – which, let's be honest, everyone says – maybe something like, “My experience crafting engaging narratives for diverse audiences, honed through years of teaching, has equipped me to connect with listeners on a personal level…" It’s a bit longer, yes, but it’s also showing, not telling. I like that. “Crafting engaging narratives…” That’s much stronger than just ‘communicating.’ See, this is why I needed you here. My brain's been looping on ‘responsible’ and ‘reliable’ – slightly boring qualities to highlight, aren’t they? What about the bit where you mentioned the action verbs? Yes! I've tried to weave a few in. 'Spearheaded', 'developed', 'implemented' – a bit of dynamism. I also changed "I am proficient in" to “I have a strong understanding of”. Much more confident. And I've focused on the specific skills they listed in the job description: commissioning, editing, scheduling... Good. So, you’ve definitely tied it back to what they're looking for.

Right then, so, let’s actually drill down a bit on this pottery thing, shall we? It's lovely dreaming, having a cuppa and watching the kookaburras, but we need a plan. A semi-sensible one. More than just, "I fancy making mugs." I know, I know. The "fancy" part is the dangerous bit, isn’t it? I’m not trying to dismiss it; it feels really…right, somehow. More right than assemblies and marking essays, anyway. But ‘right’ doesn't pay the bills. I've been doing some research – online, mostly – about setting up a small studio. It's overwhelming, the permits and regulations. Welcome to the world of entrepreneurship. Overwhelming is its middle name. Though, Australia might be easier than New Zealand in some respects. Less red tape, perhaps? Still, we need to figure out our niche. ‘Mugs’ is… lacking ambition. What are you thinking beyond mugs? Sculpture? Vases? Something unique? I was thinking more… functional art, really. Bowls, plates, serving dishes. Things people would actually  use . I’ve been experimenting with a lot of natural glazes – using clays and oxides that give a really earthy, textured finish. Quite a lot of influence from Japanese pottery, actually. Wabi-sabi, you know? Celebrating the imperfections. I’m quite excited about it. Wabi-sabi, good call. It has appeal. Upscale appeal, potentially. People are increasingly valuing handmade, one-off items. That’s a good starting point for marketing, too. Think Instagram, Etsy… we’ll need a decent photographer to showcase the stuff properly. We could get someone local here, for the initial shoots. Exactly! And I've been considering workshops. Running small pottery classes. A nice little income stream, and also a way to build a community around the brand. Teach people the basics, maybe a slightly more advanced glazing class? It feels like… it feels like the full package. Workshops are brilliant. People love learning something new, and they're connected to the product in a more meaningful way. But... time. That's the thing. Both of our time is limited. You with teaching, me with… well, everything else I currently juggle. Are you ready to scale back your teaching hours significantly? Because committing to pottery properly  and  teaching full-time? That's a recipe for burnout. That's the terrifying part, isn't it? I've been thinking about going part-time. Just a few afternoons a week, maybe.

Honestly, Nana, I'm feeling utterly useless. Little Finn just won't eat anything that isn't beige. Beige! It's a culinary crisis. He’ll glare at a carrot like it’s personally offended him. Goo! Och, bairns. They're a handful. Remember young Angus, when he was Finn's age? Refused to eat anything green. His poor mother nearly went mad trying to disguise spinach in everything. Ended up puréeing it into his custard. He never knew the wiser. Ingenious, Margaret! Absolutely ingenious. Though I suspect Finn, being a modern child, is more likely to detect the subterfuge. Children, you see, become incredibly astute at detecting manipulation. It's a survival mechanism, really. Like noticing which parent is more likely to yield to a tantrum. You’ve hit the nail on the head, Arthur. He’s a little negotiator. Speaking of things that are hard to manage, have you heard about the state of the schools around here? Apparently, there’s a massive shortage. They’re saying some kids might have to be bussed miles out of the catchment area. Miles! Aye, I've heard whispers. Terrible, isn't it? When I was teaching, everything was so much easier. We even had a thriving Polish community children joining our school. Lovely families, very keen to learn. It was wonderful to see their culture and perspective enriching the classroom. What’s happening now, though…it’s dreadful. The government seems to be building shopping centres instead of classrooms. It’s a symptom of a much larger problem, Margaret. Planning, or rather the lack thereof. Housing shortages, school shortages…it all stems from a fundamental failure to anticipate growth. And the consequences are borne by the next generation. I read a piece just last week…about developers bribing council officials… Oh, don’t even go there, please! My head is already spinning. It’s overwhelming. I feel like I'm failing him on so many fronts. He needs a good school, decent food…and I’m here, mostly just playing Peppa Pig and trying not to have a nervous breakdown. Then there is the treasurer who is trying to claim healthcare costs for when he had a fall last year. It really is something. Now, now, don’t be so hard on yourself, love. You're doing a grand job. Finn is a happy, healthy little boy, isn't he? And Peppa Pig never hurt anyone.

Honestly, Janet, I still can't quite believe the fallout from that referendum. It feels like it all happened a lifetime ago, doesn’t it? But the ripples are still going on, you know? Such a divisive thing. Aye, it does. It felt like the whole country was split clean in two. I remember arguing with my brother for weeks afterwards. He was staunchly Remain, and I...well, I wasn’t. Though I don’t think anyone really knew  what  we were voting for, did they? It all got so muddled. Anyway, enough of politics! How’s the proofreading going? Still got those marketing clients keeping you busy? It's alright, busy enough. Keeps me ticking over. Though the marketing side feels a bit… frantic at the moment. Everyone's trying to adapt to the changes, you know? Different rules, different markets. It's exhausting. But the proofreading is a lovely little balance. Peaceful, really. Speaking of peaceful, I was thinking about getting the piano tuned. Remember when your dad used to play? He was brilliant, wasn’t he? Oh, he was. He’d play anything, really. Show tunes, classical… He used to try and teach me, but I was hopeless. Absolutely hopeless. Always forgot the fingering. Gave it up at sixth form, I did. Too much to juggle with everything else. Sixth form! Oh goodness, that feels like another lifetime entirely. Remember Mrs. Davies? The English teacher? She used to mark my essays in red ink, relentlessly! But she was brilliant, actually. Made me work hard. Oh, Mrs. Davies! Yes! She was a force of nature. She’d glare at you if you used the word “very” more than once. And the school dances! Honestly, a bunch of awkward teenagers trying to look grown up. I was dreading them, to be fair. Remember Mark from the rugby team asking you to the Christmas one? Oh, don't remind me! He smelled of liniment and old socks. Awful! But you were with Paul, weren't you? Seemed a good match, you two. We were! For a while, anyway. Life moves on, doesn’t it? Speaking of moving, have you heard about that new car park they're building down by the canal? Apparently, it’s going to be extortionate. Really? No, I hadn't. I've been avoiding driving as much as possible lately. Knees aren’t what they used to be, you know?

Och, this is grand, isn’t it? Proper peace and quiet for a change. Away from the constant digital din. Though, I’m confessin’, I’m already feelin' a wee bit restless without a quick scroll through Twitter. Restless, are ye? You’re practically surgically attached to that thing, Hamish! I'm enjoying the pause. It’s good for the soul, disconnecting. Though I confess, I did have a sneaky look at the university’s feed before we left Edinburgh. Just to see if young Fiona McMillan was still posting inspirational quotes about critical thinking. Fiona McMillan. The woman's a social media marvel. Seriously, the way she’s built the department’s online persona... it's somethin' else. Makes you wonder if we in comms are even tryin’. I mean, our stuff's functional, aye, gets the message across, but it lacks... spark . Spark, aye. You're talkin' about engagement. She’s brilliant at creating a community, isn't she? Uses those student spotlights really well, too. Shows the real people behind the lectures. We tried a 'Staff Stories' thing last year – fell flatter than a pancake. Nobody seemed interested in Professor Davies’ passion for collecting miniature spoons. Miniature spoons! Right enough. You needed a better hook. See, that’s what I’m wrestlin’ with at the office. We're pushing this new sustainability initiative, and the marketing team wants to do a series of infographics. Infographics! Seriously? Who actually  reads  infographics unless they’re being forced to for a PowerPoint presentation? Aye, they can be a bit…clinical. You need to humanize it, Hamish. Think about visuals that tell a story. We've been using short video interviews with students involved in the university’s environmental societies on Instagram. They’re much more impactful than charts and graphs. Have you considered something like that? Even just quick testimonials. Video... that’s actually a canny idea. Easier to digest than a lengthy report on carbon emissions. But then comes the whole 'algorithm' nightmare. Twitter’s a constant battle, you know? You post a perfectly good piece of content, something genuinely useful about, say, the impact of climate change on local wildlife, and it gets lost in the ether. Meanwhile, some blithering idiot's got six thousand likes for a picture of their cat wearing a tiny hat. The internet giveth, and the internet taketh away. I had a similar issue with LinkedIn a wee while ago.

Right, I am  officially  done. Weekend? More like a relentless assault on my sanity. Honestly, organising that charity bake sale… you wouldn't believe the drama. Oh, tell me about it. You look like you’ve wrestled a badger. How bad was it? And smells amazing, by the way, want some? Bad doesn't even  begin  to cover it. Mrs. Higgins brought a Victoria sponge that was drier than the Sahara, insisted it was a family recipe, and then proceeded to complain when nobody ate it. And Kevin from accounts tried to sell me his homemade fudge… fudge that tasted suspiciously of sawdust. Kevin and his… adventurous baking. Right, I remember. Sounds like the usual chaos, then. So, worth it? Did you raise a decent amount? We did, actually! Surprisingly. Despite the culinary disasters. We made, like, five hundred quid. But I swear, organising people is my nemesis. Remind me again why I agreed to this? Because you have a massive soft spot for rescued kittens and you wanted to help them get to the vet? Don't pretend you didn't. Look, I’m just glad you did. How was Liam at the bake sale? Did he help out? Oh, Liam. He was… Liam. He spent most of the time trying to convince everyone that his lemon drizzle cake was secretly a holographic projection. Seriously. Apparently, he’s been watching too much sci-fi. Classic Liam! He's got a weird imagination, doesn’t he? Speaking of weird… how's things going with you and him? You seemed a little vague on Saturday. Vague is a polite word. It's… complicated. We had a bit of a row. Oh dear. About what? Don’t leave me hanging! Is it about him wanting to name our future dog 'Nebula'? Because I'm drawing a line at that. No, not Nebula. Though I suspect that's coming up. It was… he keeps questioning if I actually  want  to be a Project Coordinator. Keeps hinting I should go back to university and do something ‘more fulfilling’. Wow. That’s… not very supportive, is it? You enjoy your job, don't you? It's something you worked really hard for. I do! I like it! It’s stressful, don't get me wrong, but it’s challenging, and I’m good at it. I don’t need him telling me I ought to be doing something 'better'.

Right then. So, about this visit from Derek… are we sure he’s up to it? Last time he came, well, you remember. He was barely coherent for half the afternoon. Dad, we’ve been over this. He  wants  to come. He’s been talking about it for weeks. And honestly, he seems… clearer than he has in a while. Dr. Evans seems to think it’s a good idea, keeps him engaged, you know? Don’t you fret, love. We’ll keep an eye on him. He knows we’re here. It's good for him to be around family, even if it's only for a few days. Reminds him of things, you know? Things he's forgotten. Reminds him of the stairs, more like. Last time he insisted on going up to the spare room himself. Nearly took a tumble. We’ll need to block those off, won't we? Just for safety. Definitely. I’ll sort that tomorrow. Mum, could you check the spare room is generally tidy? He gets agitated if things aren’t... orderly, shall we say. Orderly? Derek's definition of orderly and mine are two entirely different things, darling! But yes, I’ll tidy up. I’ve got some of those floral sheets you bought, remember? Might cheer him up. It's a bit much, but… Floral? Derek hates floral. He always said it reminded him of Auntie Mildred's ghastly wallpaper. Navy blue, preferably. Something solid and dependable, like… like a battleship. Right, battleship sheets. Noted. We'll scrap the floral then. Speaking of which, what are we planning on doing with him while he’s here? Last time was just… a lot of sitting and staring. Well, there's the village fete on Saturday. He used to love the fete. Remember the year he won that ridiculous oversized marrow? Oh, I do. Showed it off for weeks. Thought he was some sort of agricultural champion. We could take him, but he might get overwhelmed with the crowds. And the noise… his hearing isn't what it was. Maybe just a quiet afternoon in the garden? I could bake him that apple crumble he likes. Good idea, love. The garden’s looking lovely, with the roses just coming out. We could sit on the patio, in the shade. Have the crumble and a cup of tea. Simple. Speaking of the garden… have you seen the state of that hedge?

Right then, Arthur. Another go at Duolingo today, and I swear, it's like banging me 'ead against a brick wall. "El gato come pescado," it keeps saying. The cat eats fish! I know that, love, but it’s not sticking! Me memory's not what it used to be, that's for sure. Fifty years teaching English, and I can still recall the rules of subjunctive mood backwards, but this…this Spanish…it’s a different beast altogether. Aye, I 'ear ya. It’s brutal, isn’t it? I was havin' a go at Babbel earlier. They reckon their immersion method is top-notch. Loads of listening and speaking practice, they say. But I ended up just repeatin' phrases about ordering coffee in a café. Lovely coffee, mind you, but not exactly conversational Spanish. They give you these little quizzes, yeah? And you think, 'Right, I've got this,' then  bam!  A question about the colour of someone's shoes comes up, and you're completely lost. Shoes! That's exactly it! It’s all these tiny details. I tried that Memrise thing too, you know, with the little flashcards. Seemed a bit… childish, to be honest. I felt like I was back in primary school. But I did notice somethin’… it’s the genders, isn’t it? Masculine, feminine... why can't everything just  be ? “La mesa,” “el libro.” It feels totally arbitrary. It's like there’s no logic to it. Exactly! Completely random. And don’t get me started on the verb conjugations. French, at least, is relatively predictable. Spanish? It's a minefield. I read somethin' about how they have, what, seven different ways to say 'to be'? 'Ser' and 'estar', innit? I can barely tell the difference. They both mean ‘to be’ but they're used in different situations? It's… head-scratching. Aye, 'ser' and 'estar'. A right bugger, that is. I read somewhere that some languages are just naturally harder for English speakers to learn than others. Latin-based languages are tough, apparently – all that romance stuff. German, on the other hand… I heard it’s more logical, structurally. I reckon you’re on to somethin’. You know, I was lookin’ into how they do it in places like Catalonia. Apparently, a lot of kids there grow up speakin’ both Catalan and Castillian Spanish. They just pick it up. Like it’s part of the air they breathe.

Right, Dad, seriously, this is a mountain. You’ve got years of… everything. Utility bills from 2008, bank statements older than I am. Are you sure we need to keep all this? Well, you never know, do you? You can't just bin it. HMRC could come knocking any time. Plus, there’s Ms. Brook. Remember that time I had that signed photo? Kelly Brook? What’s she got to do with paperwork? Don't be daft. It’s proof of purchase! I got it at a charity auction, a few years back. The paperwork proving I owned it, for insurance purposes, is somewhere in this mess. You know, in case of… well, you know. Right. Insurance for a signed Kelly Brook photo. Of course. Okay, let’s try to categorize this. Banking stuff definitely needs to be scanned and backed up digitally, at the very least. I can do that. Where’s the scanner again? Over there, behind the telly. That thing’s older than you are too, you know. Found it at a car boot sale. Did a grand job, though. Though it jams up a bit sometimes. Need to be gentle with it. This  is  ancient. I’ll connect it to my laptop. You wouldn’t believe the projects I could do with this data though. All this banking history… It's a goldmine for corpus linguistics! Imagine, analyzing spending habits over decades. Trends in consumer behaviour… Cor-what-now? Sounds like a load of bother to me. Just scan the stuff, son. Got a flight to Malaga next month, need to keep those boarding passes safe. Although, I wouldn’t put too much faith in that airline, easyJet, they’re always cancelling flights. I know, they're notoriously unreliable. Actually, scanning those boarding passes is a good idea. We should scan everything important. I can even set up a folder system, tag things by year… It’ll be a proper archive. Much safer than leaving it all crammed in boxes. Sounds like a lot of effort. You’re good with computers, though. Unlike me. Tried to set up online banking recently. Nearly gave myself a stroke. The security questions! “What was your childhood pet’s name?” Seriously? My childhood pet was a greyhound, and I had six of them! How am I supposed to remember which one? I get that. They design these systems to be secure, but they’re often a nightmare for users.

Honestly, this petrol price is  criminal . I swear, every week it's creeping up another few pence. I'm practically donating to the oil companies at this point! Dramatic much, Liv? It's not  that  bad. You’re used to using minimal fuel in your little hatchback anyway. I’m the one feeling the pinch with this beast. Aye, well, at least I’m not lugging around a Tonka truck! And it's not just  that  bad, it's the principle of it! They're taking the mick, pure and simple. Did you see the one we just passed? Shell? It was like, ten pence more than the BP just five miles back. It's daylight robbery, I tell ya. They use dynamic pricing, you know. It’s all algorithms and supply and demand. They analyse traffic flow, time of day, competitor pricing... it's all very clever, but yeah, slightly irritating when you're trying to fill up without breaking the bank. Algorithms, my foot! It's a con! And don’t start with the 'clever' bit. Clever people figure out how to make petrol cheaper, not how to charge us through the nose. I miss the days when you could fill up and not feel like you needed a second mortgage. You're a ray of sunshine, you are. Look, we're almost to the A1. There's a Morrison's there; their prices are usually a bit more competitive. And it’s got that weird little forecourt layout – always feels like you’re maneuvering a cruise ship in there. Morrison’s is alright, I suppose. Anyplace is better than that Shell we just bypassed. Speaking of maneuvers... did you see that lot of bikers just whizzing past? Sounded like a swarm of angry wasps. Yeah, pretty impressive. Proper roaring engines. I always admire them, to be honest. Bit mad, though. Mad  and  noisy! Honestly, I don't know how you stand it. That rumble, constantly. Feels like your insides are vibrating. My Nan used to say bikers were all show ponies, just trying to show off. Nan was a character, wasn’t she? There's definitely some showboating involved, but there's also a real skill to it. Controlling those machines, the coordination... plus, I think there's something primal about the freedom of the open road, a sense of rebellion, you know? Rebellion? They're on the road amongst us!

Right then, Liam, your tennis coach called today. Apparently, you've been grumbling about the drills again. They're boring, Mum. Just running, running, running. Hitting the same shots over and over. Are they  really  that bad? Seems like a good foundation to me. You can’t just waltz onto Centre Court at Wimbledon and expect to win without drills, love. Exactly! Your coach, Mr. Davies, is a very good one. He's seen loads of players come through. He says you've got the potential, but you need to put in the work. You can’t expect to be the next Federer just by… well, by wishing. I'm not trying to be the next Federer! I just… I want to play matches, not practice hitting forehands against a wall for an hour. Remember when I used to get like that playing football? Dad was relentless with the passing practice. I used to moan just like you. Then he’d tell me a story about Gordon Banks and how he practiced catching tennis balls for hours. Said it improved his reflexes. Made me feel a bit silly. Your dad had a point. It's all about building those fundamentals. And Mr. Davies isn't just making you run, he's focusing on your footwork. That's crucial, Liam. You can have the best swing in the world, but if you can’t get into the right position, it’s useless. But everyone else seems to be playing loads more matches. Ben’s playing in a tournament next weekend. Ben’s a year older than you, darling, and he’s been playing competitively for longer. Don’t compare yourself to him. Focus on your own game. Mr. Davies mentioned he’s going to integrate some more tactical drills next week, work on your strategies and placement. Should make it a bit more engaging, shouldn't it? Tactical drills, eh? Now that sounds more interesting. Back in my day, tactics were just shouting “go on then!” at the top of your voice. Didn’t seem to work very well. Yeah, but… what's the point of tactics if I'm just hitting the ball to the same spot every time? It's predictable. That's what the drills are for, love! To make you  less  predictable. To give you options. Think about it – you need to learn how to vary your shots, hit deep, hit short, angle it wide… Surprise your opponent.

Right, who thought these napkins were a good idea? They look like…well, they look like Dad’s old underpants, honestly. Black and… ruffled. Oh, stop it, Liam. Your mum thought they were a laugh! She saw them in that little shop in Buxton. Said they were "festive." Festive and vaguely indecent, more like. They  are  a bit much, aren’t they? Reminds me of that awful Christmas jumper Uncle Barry got last year. The one with the reindeer that looked like they were mid-breakdown. Barry always has a knack for the questionable. Though, come to think of it, this year's Christmas has been mostly questionable choices so far, hasn’t it? Like putting Mariah Carey on at lunchtime. Now, now, Michael. Don’t be like that. Mariah’s a Christmas classic. Gets you in the mood. Remember when we used to play it on repeat every December when you were little, Michael? You'd be dancing around like a…a startled heron! Nan, please! Don’t dig up ancient history. And I was  not  a startled heron. I was expressing joy. Festive joy. You were flailing and nearly knocking over the tree, love. Speaking of Christmas, are we doing the same thing this year as last? Auntie Carol and Uncle George coming over after the Queen's speech and then the charades? That's the plan. Carol’s been practicing her impressions already, apparently. Keeps saying she’s going to be Dame Judi Dench this year. She’ll be a right nightmare to beat. I used to love those charades nights. Brings back memories of your grandad trying to act out "Swan Lake." Honestly, he looked more like a confused penguin. Nan's stories are the best. Okay, moving on from embarrassing family memories… I'm still stressed about this essay I’ve got for uni. It’s due after Christmas. It's about the significance of music in film. Feels massive! Oh, have you started it? It does sound daunting. What films are you thinking of using? I was thinking about  The Social Network  - Trent Reznor's score is incredible. And maybe something classic like  Singin' in the Rain ? My mates at uni call me "Rez" now, because of that film - it's ridiculous. “Rez”? Liam, honestly! What will people think? Don’t worry about it, son. They’re just having a laugh. University life, eh? Dizzying.

Right, so, update time! Work’s been… well, work. We’re launching the new sustainability initiative next month and it's proving to be more complicated than initially anticipated. Loads of stakeholders to wrangle, as always. But it  is  good to feel like we're actually doing something positive, you know? Less spreadsheet wrangling, more green projects. How about you, Mum? School still a whirlwind of teenage angst and exam stress? Oh, you’ve no idea. Absolutely relentless. This year’s Year 11 cohort are particularly… dramatic. One boy, bless him, tried to argue that because he dreamt he aced the history exam, he didn’t  need  to revise. Told him politely, but firmly, that his subconscious wasn't worth marks. Still, the staff are all pulling together. Sarah’s been a godsend, covering the extra marking. Speaking of, have you met her properly yet? Sarah Davies? Lovely girl, just back from Uni. Sarah, eh? Another one back from Uni. Seems everyone's got a degree these days. When I was your age, love, a good apprenticeship was all you needed. Though, I suppose things have changed. This article here... They’re saying the price of fertiliser is going through the roof again. Honestly, it’s a nightmare trying to keep the farm running profitably. Don’t remind me about prices. My rent went up again last month! I’m thinking of having a serious conversation with the landlord. It feels absolutely extortionate. I’m working hard, and still feel like I’m constantly just about managing. It’s a bit disheartening, to be honest. Still, at least I'm not battling fluctuating fertiliser costs! I know, darling. Everything’s so expensive. Remember when we used to be able to get a decent Sunday roast for a fiver? Now you’re lucky to find one for ten. I tell you, it’s not like it was in my day. We didn't have all these fancy avocado toasts and oat milk lattes. A cup of tea and a biscuit was a treat! Avocado toast? Oat milk? Sounds like a lot of fuss to me. Give me a proper bacon sandwich any day. Speaking of food, Amelia, is that your famous apple crumble I smell? It is! I was trying out a new recipe actually. It’s got a little bit of ginger in the crumble topping. Thought it might give it a bit of a kick.

Honestly, this Bolognese needs a serious amount of seasoning. It's tasting a bit…bland. Did you manage to find those sun-dried tomatoes at Marks & Spencer? They were on offer last week, weren't they? Yeah, I did! Managed to snag a couple of jars. Their food hall's just…it’s something else, isn’t it? Honestly, I could spend a fortune in there. Did you see they’ve got those mini Yorkshire puddings now? Filled with roast beef? Tempting, very tempting. Don’t even start! I’m trying to stick to a budget. Although, those look rather delightful. Maybe as a treat next week. Anyway, sun-dried tomatoes are going in now. Right. You’re on vegetable duty, love. Are the carrots adequately diced? Don't want any huge chunks. Perfectly adequate, I'd say. Much better than your attempts last time, I recall. So, about that appraisal… It wasn't all sunshine and roses, was it? You seemed a bit quiet when you got home. It was…a mixed bag. They said my transcription speed is excellent, practically unmatched, which is good. But apparently, I need to be ‘more proactive’ with suggesting improvements to the workflow. Honestly! As if I have the time to be redesigning their entire system on top of typing out endless documents! Proactive, eh? Sounds like corporate speak for “make yourself look busy even when you’re not.” Classic. Don’t let it get to you. You’re indispensable. They need your fingers, not your strategic planning skills. Easier said than done. I’m just worried about it affecting any potential salary increases. We could really use a bit more wiggle room, couldn’t we? Maybe a new blender? This one’s on its last legs. It sounds like a dying badger when I try to make smoothies. A new blender it is then! We'll get a decent one. Speaking of food… fancy ordering a pizza next weekend? Just a change from all this home cooking. Maybe a Hawaiian? You know I hate pineapple on pizza. Absolutely loathe it. But a pizza sounds lovely. Perhaps we could grab some decent wine to go with it too? Found a bottle of fourteen-year-old Merlot recently. Needs airing, though. Fourteen-year-old! You’re spoiling us. Good shout. Right, how about we get the garlic bread dough rising while this simmers? And after supper, we  must  tackle that crossword.

Honestly, this shopping trip’s been a write-off. Absolute write-off. Found nowt I like. Everything’s either miles too pricey or looks like somethin' my grandma would wear. Oh, comin’ from Chester, I’m used to pricey! You'd think they'd invent a sale, eh? What were you lookin’ for, love? Just... somethin' decent for Saturday. We're goin' to Revolver, aren't we? Need somethin' that’s smart but not, like,  tryin’  too hard. You know? Not like a debutante goin' to a ball. Revolver's always a good shout. Loud, colourful, decent music. I’m wearin' a black jumpsuit. Simple, but you can dress it up with some good jewellery. What about you, Liv? I've got this velvet dress, right? Proper dark green. Thought it'd be good. But it feels a bit… heavy for a Saturday night. Like I’m goin’ to a funeral. Tell me about it! I was tryin' on this glittery top, but it just looked… tacky. All over the place. Like tinsel on a Christmas tree that’s been raided by a squirrel. A squirrel, Bethany? That's a brilliant description! You lot and your imagery. I’ve got a little black dress. Nothing fancy, but it’s figure-hugging and has a bit of a sparkly belt. Should do the trick. Are you girls wearin’ heels? I was thinkin' about it. But I swear, wearin' heels all night makes me feel like a wobbly penguin. My ankles just give way. I might stick with some Dr. Martens. They’re comfy, but still look alright. I might do the same. Tried on these impossibly high stilettos, looked like I was about to faceplant. Not worth the risk, is it? Heels are definitely an investment in pain. I'm crappin' myself about Saturday. I bought these new boots, chunky ones with a platform. Not heels, exactly, but they still give you a bit of lift. Hopefully, I won't twist an ankle. I got these wedge sandals, right? Lookin' like something from the 90s, I know, but they’re comfy. And they  kind of  go with everything. See, practical! That’s the key. Bein' comfy enough to actually enjoy yourself. And drinkin' enough, obviously. Aye, the drinkin' part is essential. Reckon they’ll be doin' those raspberry daiquiris at Revolver? Those are proper good. Ooh, yes! Definitely need to get a few of those.

You know, I was thinking this morning… about personality types. I read this article about Enneagrams, and apparently, I'm a 9 – the peacemaker. Which… rings strangely true, doesn't it? Always trying to smooth things over, avoid conflict… sometimes, a bit too much, I suspect. A peacemaker, eh? Suits you. Though I’d have pegged you more as a quietly tenacious one. You don’t let things go, you just… absorb. Like a very efficient sponge. A sponge! That's wonderfully unflattering. But I suppose there's some truth to it. Do you know what yours would be? Honestly? Probably an 8. The Challenger. I like to be in control, I'm decisive… sometimes a bit  too  decisive, according to my team at work. Though, I prefer to think of it as ‘efficient leadership.’ Of course you do. It’s a good fit. It’s funny though, isn't it? How these things can categorize us. Do you ever think about… deeper things? Like, soul mates and all that? I know it sounds a bit woo-woo. I used to dismiss it entirely. Pure romantic fiction. But… after all this time, after everything we’ve been through… I'm not so sure. There's a comfort, a familiarity, a lightness with you that I haven't found with anyone else. It's more than just companionship, isn't it? It feels… integrated. Like two halves of something bigger. That's beautifully put. It’s a strange feeling to describe, isn’t it? Like knowing something without ever having been told. Speaking of strange feelings… I had this absolutely vivid dream last night. Oh? Do tell. You've been having some fascinating dreams lately. It was… a party. But not just  any  party. It was a gathering of historical figures. Queen Elizabeth I was arguing eloquently about the merits of ruffs with Marie Antoinette, and Leonardo da Vinci was sketching on a napkin while trying to explain perspective to Jane Austen. And there was this incredible band – they sounded like Django Reinhardt but with synthesizers – playing this frenetic, joyful music. Everyone was dancing, laughing… even Julius Caesar looked like he was having a genuinely good time. Right then. You need more sleep. Though, that's quite a guest list. Elizabeth and Marie Antoinette in the same room? That would  have  to be explosive. Did you talk to anyone? I tried to, but I was a silent observer.

Honestly, Sarah, this whole Etsy venture is proving to be… more challenging than I anticipated. I thought, "knitting little hats, easy money," you know? But the competition is fierce, and the marketing is a nightmare. I’m spending more time wrestling with SEO than actually knitting! Right? Everything’s a hustle these days. It's not like people just stumble across your shop, is it? Mum always said you were a whiz with spreadsheets, though. You'd be brilliant at the figures side of things, anyway. Figures are important, love. Absolutely crucial. But you’re right, the online world changed everything. Remember when you'd just pop a stall up at the village fete, and that was enough? Now, you're competing with manufacturers in China! Exactly! And the customer service… don't even get me started. One woman complained her hat was "slightly off-kilter."  Slightly off-kilter!  It's handmade, for goodness sake. Slight imperfections are part of the charm! But you can’t argue with a negative review, can you? Nah, it's brutal, innit? Proper hard to fight. Though, people do appreciate genuine effort. Remember when I got that bollocking at work for using a bit of local dialect in an email? Apparently, it wasn't "professional." Oh, give it a rest, love! The hoops you civil servants have to jump through! It's ridiculous. They want you all homogenised. "Standard English" this, "inclusive language" that. It's just stripping away what makes us who we are. My niece, bless her, was being tested on her grammar the other day. Trying to correct her use of “we was”. Honestly, makes my blood boil. It is, isn't it? I think people from the South East get unfairly stereotyped. Like they're all posh and aloof. It’s a terrible generalisation. Although… I do sometimes overhear conversations and think, 'Good heavens, how are they  saying  that?' It's not that it's wrong, just… different. It's just the way we talk! Nothing wrong with it. It’s comfy, innit? Don't let those Southern toffs make you feel bad. Though, speaking of things that make your blood boil… I was listening to the news the other day about that surge in gun violence in America. Honestly, makes you shudder. It's terrifying. And the ease with which they get hold of the things. It's just barbaric.

Right, so, housing. Honestly, I'm proper fed up. The damp in my room's gettin' worse. I swear I can see moss growin' on the wallpaper now. Moss! In Barrow, we had rain, aye, but not  this  kind o' rain, if you catch my drift. It soaks in, ya know? It’s proper grim. Moss, eh? That's rough. My flat’s okay, touch wood. Though, the heating’s still dodgy. Took three calls to maintenance to get it fixed last week, and it’s still clickin’ like a dodgy washing machine. Filipino standard, innit? Reliable as a… well, you get the picture. Bless you both. I feel like I live in a sauna. They promised me a "modernised" room. All it is is slightly less horrifying than the rooms they had ten years ago. My Norfolk grandma would have a fit. She’d be out there with a rolling pin, threatening the uni maintenance guys. Your grandma sounds brilliant! Speaking of things that’d give you a heart attack, did you see Liam's Insta story last night? He was tryin' to cook lamb chops. Looked like a crime scene. Proper exploded all over the kitchen. Oh, that's classic Liam. He'll blame the oven, of course. Did anyone manage to get tickets for the Arsenal game next week? I've been refreshing the website for days. It’s madness. No luck, sadly. Sold out instantly, obviously. It's always the same. You think, ‘right, I’ll be there, supporting the Gunners!’ And then...nothing. I’m gonna have to resort to watching it in the student bar, surrounded by stressed-out people trying to cram for midterms. That sounds like a special kind of hell. I'm thinkin' of just stayin' in, orderin' a pizza and hidin' under a duvet. My brain's fried anyway. This essay on Romantic poetry is killin' me. Wordsworth? Honestly, who gets excited about daffodils? You're harsh, Sarah! Daffodils are iconic. It's all about the imagery. Speaking of imagery… I was trying to explain the concept of  baon  to my tutor the other day. She just looked completely lost.  Baon ? What’s  baon ? It's a Filipino tradition. You pack a lunchbox with food from home every day. My mum always made me these elaborate bento boxes as a kid. Rice, chicken, fruit, everything. It's a symbol of love, practically.

This is dead lush, isn't it? Proper good. I didn’t think I’d like Croatian food, but this grilled octopus… unreal. Aye, it is that. Istrian food is always a winner. Better than chips and gravy, eh, Liam? Yeah, alright. Could do with a bit more ketchup, though. Ketchup with grilled octopus? Liam, you are a marvel. You'll put off the locals completely. You know, I had a client last week complaining about seemingly minor cultural differences in a deal – all over whether to offer coffee  after  or  before  the presentation. Ketchup on octopus… that's a whole new level. Don't start, Dad. He's just being Liam. He’s got a face like thunder if he doesn't get his ketchup. So, Mum, how’s the knee feeling after that physio appointment? Did they ramp up the exercises again? It’s a bit sore, reet enough. They got me doing lunges, can you believe it? Lunges! At my age! I felt like a right fool wobbling about. Though, the young lad doing the session was dead nice, he kept telling me I were doing grand. I just kept thinking about them buses home, trying to stand steady on those things. Nightmare, they are, especially when it’s rush hour. The 79's always packed, Mum. It's like a sardine can. I had to stand all the way home yesterday after football practice. See? Even Liam’s getting the bus home! Shouldn’t he be getting a lift with his mates? They all got lifts. I wanted to save some money. Plus, I needed to think about what Mr. Henderson said in history. It was proper boring, about rationing and… Rationing? Liam, they're rationing chocolate bars at the supermarket these days, it’s just as bad. Supply chain issues, apparently. You wouldn’t believe the price of avocados. You're always moaning about the supermarkets, Dad. You practically live in Waitrose! It’s just… you’re so particular about your free-range eggs. Quality, Elodie, quality. It matters. Just like choosing the right consultant matters for a company. Speaking of, I’m heading back to London on Sunday, got a crunch meeting on Monday. Trying to restructure a logistics firm. They’ve got more vans than they know what to do with. Always working, aren't you, David? Never a break. You need to relax a bit.

Cor, that was a right proper trip, weren't it? Cornwall, eh? Never thought I'd see the likes of it. Bit blowy, mind you, but lovely. It was, wasn't it, Arthur? A bit more wind than I’d anticipated, actually. My hair never stood still the entire time! But the scenery...absolutely breathtaking. Showing you those photos later, you simply  must  see. Especially the one of the lighthouse. Aye, that lighthouse was something else. Right perched there on the cliff edge, seemingly defying the wind. Properly atmospheric, innit? Reminded me of a Turner painting. How was the YHA, Brenda? You were looking after the volunteers, weren’t you? Oh, the YHA was lovely, David. Really welcoming bunch. Mostly young folk, doing that volunteering scheme. Such enthusiastic kids! They were there helping with coastal path maintenance. Some of them hadn't been away from home before. It was lovely to see them enjoying themselves and appreciating the beauty of the place. One young lad, Liam, he was a gem. Always helping out, always cheerful. Reminded me a bit of…well, never mind. Always helping out, eh? Reminds me of young Barry, down at the shops. Always willing to lend a hand. Though he did nick a few sweets when he was little, the little rascal! Remember that, Brenda? Of course I do, Arthur! And you chased him around the greengrocer’s with a rolled-up newspaper! Goodness, time flies. David, what about you? Did you manage to get any decent cycling in? Tried, Brenda, truly tried. The Cornish hills aren't for the faint of heart, you know. I attempted that cycling challenge – cycling across Yorkshire in a day. Pretty foolhardy, in hindsight, considering the terrain out there. Got about halfway before my knees started protesting rather loudly. Ended up hobbling the rest of the way! Still managed a good few miles though. Spectacular views though, stunning. Across Yorkshire in a day? Bless yer heart, David. You're a stronger man than I am. Just getting up the stairs sometimes is a trial these days! Speaking of trials, did you manage to get any crabs on the beach? I were hopin' we'd find a few. Little somethin' for supper. We did try, Arthur. We really did. But the beach was remarkably crab-free. Apparently, the tides weren’t right. We did see lots of seagulls though, hoping for a tasty morsel!

Cor, this bread’s reet good, innit? Proper crusty. Better than that stuff we get up north, honestly. Mind you, I’m biased, aren’t I? It is good, yeah. Mum’s been experimenting, apparently. Said she found a new local bakery, down by the river. It's nice to have something different for once, not just the usual shop-bought stuff. It's all lovely, really. Though I’m still trying to figure out how she got the sweet potatoes so caramelised. It's an art form. So, Chloe, you were saying something about a… disaster date? The last one? Don't remind me! Honestly, I thought it couldn’t get any worse than the fella who quoted poetry at me during the main course. But this… this was a new level. He brought his mum. His  mum ? Seriously? Dead serious. Apparently, he was worried I'd “not be proper” and wanted her there to “keep an eye on things.” She spent the entire evening examining my cutlery and asking about my intentions for Tuesday. Tuesday! We’d just met. Oh my god! That’s… that’s incredibly bizarre. Did you just… leave? Eventually. It was excruciating. I made some excuse about having to feed my cat. It's a lie, I don't have a cat. But needs must, eh? I just got up and walked out. Didn’t even bother saying goodbye to the mum. You did right. Mum interference is a massive red flag. People need to learn to function independently, let alone set you up for a failsafe. Exactly! And he didn't even seem embarrassed! He just nodded and said, “She just wants what’s best for me.” Like… like I'm some prize he's trying to win. I'm not a trophy, Liam! Wow. That’s… intensely awkward. Honestly, Chloe, you deserve better. You've got a great job, loads of friends, you're funny… Thanks, Liv. I know, I know. But it’s hard sometimes, isn't it? Everyone else seems to be coupled up, or at least having better dating experiences than me. Don't listen to that. It's all curated on Instagram, Chloe. Nobody puts the bad stuff online. Take my mate, Ben. He went on three dates last month and ended up with a nosebleed on each one. He's not posting  that  on his story. That’s true, isn’t it?

Oh my god, it’s so good to be back! Barcelona was… overwhelming, honestly. In the best possible way, of course. But my feet are absolutely killing me. Welcome back! You look exhausted, but happy. Did you have an amazing time? I missed you – this place felt weirdly empty without you. Empty and suspiciously clean, probably. Don’t get any ideas about keeping it like that. Yeah, it was incredible. The architecture is just… bonkers. In a beautiful way. Gaudi was a genius, obviously, but seeing it in person? Wow. We spent, like, a full day just wandering around Park Güell. Oh, I've seen pictures. Looks surreal. Did you get to see the Sagrada Familia? Of course! That was the main event. I'm still processing it, to be honest. It's so massive, and intricate... Pictures don't do it justice  at all . We managed to get one of those guided tours, which was definitely worth it – learned loads about the history and the symbolism. Did you miss me terribly? Or were you out saving the world as usual? A little bit of both, actually. Had a fairly hectic weekend with a couple of particularly tricky patients, but nothing I couldn’t handle. So, tell me everything! Food? Did you eat all the paella? All the paella. And tapas, churros, crema catalana… I think I gained about five pounds. It was totally worth it. We stumbled across this tiny tapas place in the Gothic Quarter - just amazing. Seriously, the best food I’ve had in ages. You  have  to try and go sometime. We also did a cooking class, which was hilarious. I’m pretty sure I’ll never be able to make paella properly, but it was a fun disaster. A cooking class? That sounds brilliant. You and your culinary adventures. Anything you hated? Because I know you're not one to shy away from an honest opinion. Hated? Hmm… Honestly, not much. The crowds were intense, especially around La Rambla. Felt like I was being herded like cattle sometimes. And there was this one street performer who was  determined  to get me to take a photo with his pigeon. Seriously, a pigeon. Offered me five euros. I politely declined. Oh, you are  not  falling for that one. Those guys are relentless. So, did you go out dancing at all? Barcelona nightlife is supposed to be insane. We did!

It’s just breathtaking, isn’t it? Reminds me a little of Cornwall, but… less grey. Much less grey. Absolutely. It's a bit of a revelation, actually. I was expecting… well, I wasn't expecting  this . My business trips usually involve concrete jungles, you see. So, this is a welcome change. The light here is just… different. You’re a businessman, then? I gathered as much. Not the sort of holiday someone in your line of work usually takes, is it? Not typically, no. I run a tech startup – mostly remote, so I can work from anywhere with a decent Wi-Fi signal. Which, thankfully, is proving reliable here. It’s a scouting trip, really. Looking at potential partnerships, maybe even setting up a small support hub. How fascinating. What sort of tech? I'm terribly un-techy, I’m afraid. My world revolves around ten-year-olds and Shakespeare mostly. Don’t worry about it. It’s quite dry stuff. We’re developing AI-powered marketing tools for small businesses. Basically, helping them reach more customers without needing a huge advertising budget. That  is  helpful. Small businesses always need a leg up. I used to work part-time in a little bookstore, you know, before I properly qualified as a teacher. It was run by this lovely old woman, Mrs. Higgins, and she was  drowning  in paperwork. Anything that could have streamlined things for her, she would have jumped at. See? That’s precisely the kind of need we’re trying to address. You realize, it’s funny – my background is completely different. Went to Cambridge, studied Economics. Expected to spend my life in a pin-striped suit, crunching numbers in the city. It all feels like a lifetime ago. Cambridge! That's impressive. I did my postgrad at Exeter. A far cry from Dorchester, my hometown. Dorchester’s… well, it’s Dorchester. Lots of history, very little excitement. Before the bookstore, I spent a summer working at a farm. Picking strawberries! Honestly, I thought I'd have died of boredom. My hands were raw for weeks. A strawberry farm? That’s quite the contrast to AI marketing. I once worked in a pub in Shepherd’s Bush while I was at university. Just serving pints, cleaning glasses. The things you do to pay the bills, eh? You learn a lot about people working behind a bar. More than you would anywhere else, I reckon.

Honestly, Liam, I'm proper stressed about this house situation. It's gettin' to me, it really is. Aye, I heard you say that earlier. What is it now, then? Is it Gareth leaving his socks on the bleedin’ radiator again? It's not just the socks, is it? It's everything! Gareth’s socks are just the tip of the iceberg. He’s been leaving his dirty dishes in the sink for three days now. Three days, Liam! It's like livin' with a badger. A messy, sock-hoarding badger. Gareth’s always been a bit… chaotic. Remember that time he tried to cook a full roast dinner and set off the smoke alarm? Aye, that was a disaster! But this is different. This feels… deliberate, almost. Like he’s testin' us. And then there’s Emily. She’s fine, don’t get me wrong, but she’s got this habit of rearrangin' the kitchen cupboards whenever she feels like it. Rearranging? What’s wrong with that? Wrong with it? Honestly! I'd put my teacups back and she’d move ‘em to a completely different shelf, just because it "looked better”. I’m tryin’ to find me favourite mug in the mornin', eh? It's a nightmare! I spent a good ten minutes lookin' for me lucky mug yesterday. The blue one with the little sheep. The one your Nana bought you? You’re still using that? Of course, I am! It brings me luck, doesn’t it? Anyway, the point is, it's all just…a lot. And then there's Ben. He doesn't contribute much at all. He just plays video games and orders takeaway. I’m doin' most of the shoppin’ and cleanin', it feels like. So, what exactly are you suggestin’? We move out? That's a big step, lass. I don't know! That’s the thing, innit? Movin’ is a nightmare, especially with uni on top of everything. But I can't keep on like this. I feel like I'm the only adult in the house. I was thinkin' maybe a house meeting? A proper sit-down and talk about expectations. Like, maybe a rota for chores, or somethin'. A rota, yeah. That might help. At least it’ll set out who's responsible for what. Though, gettin' Gareth to stick to a rota...that might be wishful thinkin'. He'll probably forget it exists by Tuesday.

Cor blimey, that were a mission, weren't it, Doris? Felt like I were luggin' bricks, I did. My back's givin' me a right ol' ache already. Oh, Arthur, you always say that. You’re tougher than you think! Let me take some of those. Honestly, you’d think you were trying to move the furniture yourself. What did you get? Anything good? Right load, as usual. Got the bread, the milk, the sausages… Mrs. Higgins was cluckin’ about the price of ‘em, she were. Said they’ve gone up again. Said the world were goin’ to pot. Well, she’s not wrong, is she? Everything’s dearer than it used to be. Though, I suppose, we're managing. Did you remember the digestive biscuits? I was fancying a proper cup of tea after all that baking I did yesterday. Aye, got ‘em. Right at the bottom, they were. Nearly lost me grip on the lot trying to wrestle ‘em out. They didn’t ‘ave the proper ones neither, you know. The cream ones. Just the plain ones. I told the young fella behind the counter, I did, but he just shrugged. No manners these youngsters. No respect. Oh, that's a shame. Still, biscuits are biscuits, I suppose. Speaking of youngsters, did you see young Emily the other day? She's grown so much! Emily, that little whirlwind? Can’t keep track of 'er these days! Last I saw, she were off to some dance class or another. Always dancin', that one. Reminds me of me sister, Ethel, used to go to ballroom dancing, she did. Dressed up proper, she did. Sparkling shoes and everything. Ethel always was a bit of a glamour. Ballroom dancing! Imagine that today. These children are all hip-hop and TikTok, aren't they? It's all a bit…fast. Fast indeed. Too fast for this old boy, it is. Remember when things were a bit slower? When you knew your neighbours, and you'd sit out on the doorstep and have a natter? I do. Much more friendly, wasn't it? Though, I suppose, even back then, not everyone was perfect. There was old Mrs. Featherstone down the road… always complaining about something. Aye, everyone’s got their quirks, haven’t they? Still, it were a simpler time. Fewer worries. At least, that’s how I remember it. Makes you think, don't it?

Right then, love. Grandparents due any minute, aren’t they? Did you get the biscuits out, Ben? Chocolate digestives, like Gran likes? Aye, Nana. Got 'em. And the shortbread for Grandad, too. Did you remember to put the heating up a bit? He’s always moaning it’s nippy. Course I did, lad. Wouldn’t want him catching a chill. Malton’s a bit colder than Hull, you know. Used to grumble about the cold myself when I were a lass visiting my auntie up 'ere. Not like our nice, sheltered East Riding. Speaking of sheltered, did you tell your auntie Sheila not to bring that blasted wind chime again? Last time it nearly drove Grandad mad! Told her. She said she’d leave it in the car. But you know her, she’ll sneak it out later. It’s like a compulsion with her, that chime. What’s all this commotion about wind chimes? Sounds like a right kerfuffle. Aye, Doris is on about that infernal thing again. Says it's ‘soothing and zen’. Zen! I nearly jumped out of my skin last time she hung it on that little rose bush. Scared the robins away! Gran! Grandad! Lovely to see you both. Come in, come in. Sit down, get yourselves comfortable. Ben’s put the heating on for you. Oh, that's lovely, love. My bones are aching something fierce today. This old house is colder than a butcher's slab, wouldn't you agree, Arthur? Aye, that’s right, Doris. Cold enough to freeze the marrow in yer bones. But not as cold as that wind chime’s going to make me if Sheila gets 'er way. I’ll get you both some tea, Nana. And maybe a little sherry for Grandad? That’d be grand, Ben. Thank you, love. Now, Doris, Arthur, how was the drive up? Did you manage to avoid that awful roundabout near York? Always gives me the jitters. Dreadful, dear. Arthur had to tense every muscle in his body to navigate it. It’s like a wasps’ nest, that roundabout. Cars buzzing all over the place. He wasn’t best pleased, I can tell you. Women drivers, that’s what it is. Can’t trust ‘em near a steering wheel. Oh, Arthur! Always with the jokes. You haven’t changed a bit. Remember when you tried to build a bird table out of old teacups?

Right, so, fifteen minutes 'til Dr. Patel, yeah? Reckon we'll be alright, then? This waiting room's proper depressing, innit? All beige and sad-looking plants. Aye, depressing's the word. Feels like a dentist's waiting room, not a GP's. Think they deliberately make it this way to discourage people from getting sick. Seriously! It’s like they're designed to induce anxiety. Speaking of which, has anyone checked out that new vitamin thing everyone’s raving about? The 'Bloom & Thrive' one? Loads of influencers are going mad for it. Bloom & Thrive? Sounds a bit poncey, doesn't it? Like something you'd get at a farmers market. I reckon good old-fashioned fruit and veg is a better bet. My mum's been on about spirulina and chlorella for ages. Says it's like, superfood gold. She's right, you know. Those algae things are packed with stuff. Though, I did read an article saying some are farmed in dodgy conditions. Need to do some research before you start guzzling it down. Plus, thinking about supplements, I'm trying this new sleep tracker on my smartwatch. It's fascinating! Apparently, my REM sleep is all over the place. A sleep tracker, eh? Fancy. I'm more of a “just go to sleep and hope for the best” kind of guy. Technology's gone mad, hasn’t it? Remember when a phone just... made calls? Now they monitor your heart rate and tell you you need to go to bed earlier. Tell me about it. My Nan still thinks the internet is a fad. Last time I visited, she asked me how to "fax something to Google." Took me a good half hour to explain that wasn’t even remotely possible. Bless her! My grandma’s still convinced Facebook is full of spies. She refuses to use it, says they’re stealing all her thoughts. She spends her days playing solitaire on a tablet, though. So, you know, priorities. Solitaire, right? My grandad is obsessed with those Candy Crush things. He'll glare at you if you even  suggest  he stop playing. Says it keeps his brain sharp. Keeps him from talking about his knees, anyway. It’s the same with my aunt. It’s always “I’m just doing one level…” then three hours later, she’s still glued to the screen. Has she told you about her pottery class?

Right, so we’re doing the big shop tomorrow, yeah? Need to make sure we don't forget anything. Mum, what’s running low? Oh, love, we’re proper short on milk. And that oat milk you like, definitely need some of that. And tomatoes. We’ve only got two left and Leo’s been having ‘em on everything. They’re well good on toast, Mum. Proper good. Yeah, Leo’s a tomato fiend. Okay, milk, oat milk, tomatoes. Anything else? Dad, are you needing any of your fancy cheeses? Perhaps a bit of Gruyère, yes. And some proper sourdough. The stuff from that bakery in town is the only stuff that'll do. Gruyère again, David? You’ll bankrupt us at that rate. Don’t be getting carried away. Don’t be dramatic, Margaret. It's a treat. A little bit of civilisation in this... this northern landscape. Oh, shut it, Dad. Right, Gruyère, sourdough. Write those down. Need any fruit and veg, Mum? Apples, definitely. And a few bananas. Oh, and some washing-up liquid. We’re scraping the bottom of the bottle, like. And fabric softener. I’m having a right go at washing with just water at the moment. Feels like me clothes are scratchy. Mum, there’s a massive spider in my room. Like, a really proper big one. Oh, is there now? Where? Don’t go near it, pet. Let me have a look. You know they can bite and give you a nasty reaction. A spider, eh? What kind? Probably just a house spider, they’re harmless. Though last summer, we had one that was practically the size of your hand, Leo. Gave me a proper fright. It's got long, skinny legs, and it’s webbed up in the corner behind my wardrobe. Don’t want to go near it to look properly. A spider. Honestly. I deal with hostile mergers and acquisitions all day, and I'm supposed to be worried about a spider? Get a fly swatter. Problem solved. Don't be like that, David. Leo's frightened. And it's better to be careful. Maybe I should get some of that insect repellent spray. The one with the lemongrass. Does wonders for spiders and mosquitoes, that one. Yeah, that stuff works a treat. Although, you have to be careful not to spray it everywhere, it stinks to high heaven for a while.

Ugh, P.E. was  such  a disaster today. Miss Davies made us do those bloody circuit training things again. I swear, my legs are going to fall off. Circuit training? Seriously? At least you're moving. I had double Science. Mr. Harding was going on about the Krebs cycle for like, an hour. I think I actually hallucinated a giant lemon at one point. A lemon? That’s brilliant! I just zoned out and stared at Chloe’s hair. It was braided like, with ribbons and little flowers. Ridiculous, obviously, but distracting from the lactic acid building up in my thighs. Chloe’s always doing something extra. Remember when she tried to convince everyone that Mr. Henderson was secretly a wizard because he knew so much about constellations? Oh my god, yes! And she was totally serious! She even drew him a little star chart. Poor Mr. Henderson just looked bewildered. Did you see her Instagram story later? She’s got filters for  everything . Makes her look like a cartoon character. I know, right? It’s getting a bit much. Everyone’s trying to be an influencer these days. Even Jamie from Year 9 is doing those little dance videos. Jamie?! Blimey. I saw a snippet of one. It was… something. Speaking of influencers, have you checked out 'Study Vibes' yet? That girl, Anya, is amazing. She breaks down all the biology stuff so clearly. I'm actually using her revision videos for the exam next week. ‘Study Vibes’? No, I haven’t! I’ve been stuck on ‘The Quirky Bookworm’ – she does these book reviews, and they’re hilarious. You should check her out. She just did one on ‘The Hunger Games’, and it was spot on. Although, I still think Katniss is a bit… intense. Intense is an understatement. Right, focus. Science. The Krebs cycle… lemony hallucinations… I'm going to need a serious amount of chocolate. Did you hear about what happened with Liam and Maya? Liam and Maya? No! What?
