Used to say Costessey always had a bit more of it than Norwich, but I reckon it’s all the same across the county now. Everything’s shifting, innit? Even the weather. Remember summers we had as lads? Scorching, they were. You could fry eggs on the pavement. Oh, don't remind me of those summers! The heat used to be dreadful in Harrow. At least the rain’s a bit refreshing, though it's not exactly what we needed for the roses. Hello, dears! How are you both? Biscuits? Ginger or chocolate? Chocolate, please, Maureen. Thank you. Harrow, eh? Always seemed a bit… distant to me. A London suburb, proper. Never been much for London myself. Too much hustle and bustle. Give me a quiet road and a bit of green any day. Always said you were a Norfolk lad through and through, Harold. Costessey to the core. Never understood why you went and got yourself involved in all that engineering nonsense, anyway. Seemed a grand waste of a good head for… well, for nothing much really. It wasn’t a waste, Arthur! I designed a few bridges, you know. Down in Ipswich. Solid work, it was. Kept me busy. Though truth be told, the politics of it all… the paperwork… it weren’t worth the bother in the end. That’s why I… well, you know. Politics. Don’t get me started. The way they go on about building more houses, more houses! Where are they going to put them all? They’re swallowing up the countryside, Harold. Destroying it. My sister in Harrow… she’s got a new estate being built right next to her. All these little boxes, crammed together. No gardens, no space to breathe. Looks like a prison, it does. Remember when you could get a decent bungalow for a song, Maureen? Before all this… this “investment” nonsense? The council houses they built back then, solid they were. Thatched roofs, even! Now you’re lucky to find a place that doesn’t leak. Speak of investment, did you see young David on the news yesterday? Driving about in a gleaming new Tesla. A Tesla, can you believe it? Says he's a software engineer, making a fortune.

Right, so, the south-east corner… this is currently housing the pottery group, isn't it? They’ve been lovely, really lovely, but their numbers have dwindled drastically. We’re barely covering the rent from them now. Aye, that's right. Barbara from the pottery group was saying just last week she only had three regulars left. It's a shame, really. They were good folks and used to bring a lot of life to the place. But you’re right, it's becoming a drain really. So, what are you thinking we do with that space then? I've been mulling it over. We desperately need to increase our income streams, and that corner gets fantastic light. I was thinking… perhaps a co-working space? Something flexible, aimed at small creative businesses, freelancers… that sort of thing. Co-working, eh? Could be good. Brixton’s got loads of that going on, though. We’d need to make ours stand out. What incentives would we offer? The light's a big selling point, you’ve got that right. But we’d need to compete on price and facilities. Speaking of facilities, that awful leaky radiator in that corner already needs attention. Maintenance is going to be a nightmare. Absolutely. And before we even consider that, we need to sort out the fire escape route. It’s completely blocked by those cardboard boxes from the last fundraising sale! Honestly, people just leave things wherever they fancy. Nigel, bless him, keeps promising to sort it, but...well, Nigel. Aye, Nigel’s got a lot on his plate. He's still battling with that damp patch in the basement, isn’t he? And the pigeon problem is escalating. Saw one perched right on the fire escape this morning, eyeing up Mrs. Peterson's lunch – she was having a cheeky sandwich outside. Don’t even remind me about the birds. I'm considering getting those netting things. It's unsightly, but it might be the only way. We’ve had complaints from the tenants downstairs. They’re saying the noise is driving them mad. Netting could work, yeah. But we need to be careful about the aesthetics. Brix needs to have a certain…vibe. We don't want to look like a giant birdcage. Maybe some strategically placed deterrents? Those shiny things that spin in the wind? Possibly. We could also target that income with a new marketing push.

This is lovely, honestly. Such a change from school lunches. I’m actually managing to relax for the first time in ages. Did you manage to find any decent cider, Rhys? Aye, love. Found a proper Somerset one down at the farm shop just outside of Hereford. Not too sweet, proper tangy. You’ll like it. It’s on the table. Though, to be fair, anything’s better than that fizzy rubbish they serve the kids at school. What did you think of the apple crumble, Seren? Gareth? Crumble was bang on, Rhys. Absolutely spot on. You wouldn’t believe how hard it is to find a proper crumble these days. Too many chefs slinging some soggy concoction with frozen fruit. Yours was…holds his own hand up to express quality…that was the stuff. Properly buttery crust, warm apples...  chef's kiss.  It was good, Gareth. Really good. Now, Gareth, don't go flaunting! A bit of humble bragging wouldn't go amiss. Remember your mother always said... Oh, here we go. Arthur's going to launch into another one of his mother stories, aren't you? It's important to remember your roots, Seren. My mother used to make the  best  crumble. Trust me, Gareth, you've still got a ways to go to reach her standard. It was all about the spice. A secret blend of nutmeg, cinnamon… just a tiny pinch of allspice. That’s what gave it that  zing.  Arthur, leave him be. Gareth’s crumble was delicious. Don’t be comparing him to my mother now! You know she was a legend. Nobody could touch her. Though, I did try to replicate it once... disaster! The kitchen looked like a hurricane had blown through. Speaking of disasters, Seren, did you find that recipe you were looking for? The one with the saffron risotto? You were saying something about it being your grandmother's? Oh, yes! I did. It was tucked away in a box of old letters. It's handwritten, so it's a bit tricky to decipher, but I think I’ve got it. It involves a surprising amount of butter. And bone broth, apparently. I’m a bit nervous about it, actually. Risotto is always a gamble. Saffron makes it even more high-stakes. Risotto’s easy! Just keep stirring, keep stirring, keep stirring. That’s the key. And good stock. Seriously, don't skimp on the stock.

Right, so, we're actually  doing  this then, are we? Driving all the way down to London? My poor mam’s going to miss me like I’ve popped off to Mars. Don't be so dramatic, Chloe. It’s only a few hours. And she’ll be having a right laugh with your Auntie Brenda, I reckon. At least you're escaping the constant rain. Sunderland’s been grey as a badger's backside for weeks. Aye, tell me about it! I’m practically growing moss. Though, I do love the grey skies, mind. Reminds me of home. London’s just... bright. Too bright. And everyone’s rushing about. Makes me feel like I’m in a perpetual advert. Remember that Boots advert with the sparkly London streets? Gave me the shivers, that did. You and your adverts! You analyse them for work, you know. It's a bit ironic you find them unsettling. Honestly, you'd think you’d be used to seeing manufactured happiness. It’s different when you’re  living  it, isn’t it? It feels… fake. I’d rather see a proper, honest grey day. Like this. Anyway, are we actually going to talk about anything that isn’t the weather or the merits of dreary skies? Remember Liam and Sarah? I haven't heard from them in ages. Liam and Sarah? What about them? Last I heard, Sarah was halfway through her postgraduate training. Stressful, I imagine. Aye, that’s what they said. But it feels like more than that. They’ve proper gone silent on social media too. And I’ve noticed they’ve unfollowed a bunch of people, even folk from uni. It's a bit… weird. People change. Maybe they're just focusing on their studies. Or on each other. They might just need a bit of space. You know how Sarah can get when she's stressed. Remember that time she tried to organise a full-blown Renaissance Faire for her history project? Oh, god, don't remind me! That was a disaster! We were all stuck making cardboard swords and pretending to be royalty for a week. Still, it was brilliant. Proper laugh. Reckon they’d appreciate a visit? Should we give ‘em a bell once we’re settled in London? Let's give them a day. They're probably exhausted from unpacking. I’m actually looking forward to getting into the flat.

Honestly, Sarah, this hospital business is just relentless, isn’t it? Another appointment next week for the scans. It’s all just…a blur. They’re quite insistent on these follow-ups after the, you know… the procedure. Tell me about it. I’ve been juggling Mrs. Peterson’s knee replacement recovery and trying to find a decent cleaner for Ms. Davies. She's convinced her parrot is judging her dusting. Parrots! Honestly. But the hospital stuff… it’s awful. My brother’s been having trouble with his back. They’re talking about cortisone injections. Sounds like something out of a science fiction film, doesn’t it? It does, a bit. Though I suppose the procedure I had wasn't exactly natural either. It's just… unsettling to even think about. And the waiting! The waiting is the worst bit. I keep thinking, ‘Am I doing the right thing just sitting here, worrying?’ You know? My daughter, Emily, she’s trying to keep me distracted with baking. Lemon drizzle cake, mostly. Lots of butter and sugar, doesn’t really help the anxiety, but it’s something. Bless her heart. My niece, Chloe, she's always going on about healthy eating. Gluten-free, dairy-free, sugar-free... Honestly, sometimes I think she finds more things to  not  eat than things to eat! She keeps offering me these kale smoothies. Green sludge. I'd rather have a biscuit, thank you very much. Though, my sister, your cousin, Margaret, she's lost a stone on that new juice cleanse. Said it’s working wonders. Margaret? Good for her, I suppose. Though I think the restrictions probably drive her mad. She’s always been a comfort eater, hasn’t she? Remember that wedding we went to, years ago, when she practically ate the entire dessert table? It’s a coping mechanism for some people, isn’t it? And I can’t judge, can I? Though I do try to eat more vegetables. My doctor keeps going on about fibre. It’s a hard thing, isn’t it? Dealing with all this… stuff. My Uncle Arthur passed away last month. Sudden, it was. Heart attack. Just like that. The whole family's been… well, you know. Oh, Sarah, I'm so sorry to hear that. Arthur was always such a character. I remember him telling that ridiculous story about getting chased by a goose on the village green.

Right then, that was a lovely meal, wasn't it? Mark, your roast potatoes were spot on again. Thanks, love. Just followed my mum's recipe, more or less. Bit of extra rosemary this time, you noticed? Yeah, they were good. Best thing on the plate, honestly. They were alright. I reckon you could do with a bit more gravy next time, Dad. Definitely. Always a critic, are we, Finn? Right, so, holiday talk. We're still set for Austria, then? Absolutely. Flights are booked, chalet’s confirmed. I’ve even started looking at ski schools for you two. Liam, you’re probably ready for a proper lesson now, aren't you? Maybe. I mostly just fall over. It’s good fun though. Falling over is the  best  part. Very mature. Anyway, work’s been mad this week, as ever. That new client for the online proofreading, ‘Crimson Quill,’ they’re absolutely relentless with their deadlines. And the edits… honestly, some of the stuff I've had to correct... it’s like they’ve never seen a comma in their lives! Sounds stressful. Still, good to have the work, eh? I’ve been drowning in spreadsheets and logistics since the new warehouse opened. Trying to get everyone settled in, dealing with the transport glitches… it's a constant firefighting exercise. A warehouse? Like a really big storage place? Exactly. For all sorts of things. Mostly electronics, these days. You wouldn’t believe the value of some of the stuff going through there. Do you get to drive a forklift truck? Not anymore, Finn. Sadly. Used to when I was a student, working at a distribution centre. Those were the days - blasting round on a forklift, playing forklift tag with my mates. Never a dull moment. I got quite good at it, actually. Could parallel park one blindfolded. I highly doubt that. Though I remember you always were rather...confident. Speaking of student jobs, Liam, you ever thought about what you’d like to do when you’re older? Besides falling over on a ski slope, that is. I don’t know yet. Maybe something with computers. Or gaming. Gaming? You’re going to be a professional gamer? That’s awesome! Maybe. It’s just…a thought. Well, it's good to have thoughts, isn't it? Anything you're enjoying at school right now? History’s alright. We’re learning about World War Two.

Right, let’s see… This one’s from Hokkaido. Remember Hokkaido? That little ramen shop we found down a side street? The one with the grumpy-looking chef who made the  best  shoyu ramen I’ve ever had. Oh my god, yes! The one where you tried to compliment his cooking in Japanese and completely butchered it? He just stared at you with this… blank expression. I did, didn’t I? “Oishii desu…but a little…fuzzy?” I still shudder thinking about it. Fuzzy! What does that even  mean  in that context? He probably thought I was saying his ramen tasted like a badger’s burrow. It was brilliant! Absolutely brilliant. And look at this photo – you’re covered in snow and he’s got this tiny, amused smirk on his face. You looked like a very lost, very fluffy penguin. Harsh, but fair. See, this is what I love about these old prints. They capture the  moment . Digital photos… they’re just… sanitized. This has grit. This has memory attached. It even smells faintly of… damp. True, digital is so easily lost. I’m trying to get my class to understand the beauty of analog. They’re all obsessed with their phones, of course. Explaining that developing a roll of film is more than just hitting a button… it’s a slow, deliberate process that connects you to the image somehow. It’s a craft. It's like learning to brew your own beer. There’s something deeply satisfying about controlling every step. Speaking of crafts, did you ever finish that badger portrait you were sketching? No! The badger mocked me, basically. I couldn’t get the stripes right. They just wouldn’t cooperate. It ended up looking like a very grumpy, slightly deformed squirrel. I may have to abandon it. Badgers are far more complicated than they appear. Their faces… they're so expressive. They are. They've got that… intelligent glint in their eyes. Like they're constantly plotting something. I read something the other day about how they’re expanding their territories. Apparently, they’re becoming bolder. Bolder? As in… raiding gardens bolder? Because Mrs. Higgins down the road keeps complaining about them digging up her prize-winning tulips. Exactly. Apparently, they’re adapting remarkably well to the changing environment. They're even venturing into more urban areas. Imagine – badgers in Norwich! A little unsettling, isn’t it?

Blimey, this is proper good, Anya. Honestly, this is miles better than anything you get in a supermarket. What's the secret, yeah? It’s mostly time, Liam. And good quality flour, obviously. My nan's recipe, mostly. She always said the dough needed to feel  right  in your hands. You can't rush it. Bit like life, innit? Deep, Anya. Deep. Though, I'd argue rushing a latte is essential to survival in my line of work. People want their caffeine fix  now . Tell me about it! I’m battling a queue of sleep-deprived office workers as we speak, just trying to fling decent coffees at ‘em. So, Liam, you were saying about Ireland... you had a bit of an adventure, didn’t you? Beyond just the Guinness, I presume. Oh, yeah. Right adventure. We were down in County Clare, hiking along the coast. Beautiful, man, genuinely stunning. And then… well, then we decided to go for a swim. Skinny dipping, wasn't it? You told me about it earlier. Reckless, Liam. Absolutely reckless. Reckless and glorious, yeah? It was freezing, obviously, but the water was so clear and the stars… honestly, it was magical. Miles of sand, nobody around. Just us, a few sheep, and the Irish Sea. Wow. Sounds incredible. I’ve been meaning to get to Ireland for ages. Keep promising myself I'll take a week off but... you know how it is. The café runs itself, apparently. I reckon you need a good mate to drag you, Chlo. Like Liam evidently had. Speaking of dragging... Anya, you and I need to sort out that photo app you showed me. I’ve still got shots of my dog looking perpetually grumpy on my phone. It’s a crisis! It's fantastic, Damo! You just need to learn the filters. I can show you. Although, speaking of crises, my aunt Ruth is coming for Shabbat dinner next week, and she’s  expecting  the whole shebang. Gefilte fish, brisket, the works. Honestly, it’s terrifying. Ruth! Oh lord. She's a force of nature, isn’t she? Tell you what, Anya, I’ve been experimenting with a really good slow-cooked lamb tagine – the spices are incredible. Could be a sneaky alternative to the brisket, if you’re feeling brave. That’s a brilliant idea, Chloe! Claudia Roden's got a recipe for a Moroccan chicken that might also work.

Right, so you’re seriously saying you spent three hours yesterday trying to beat that one level in  Stellar Horizon ? Three hours, Liam? I thought you said you were behind on your reading for Professor Davies? Look, it was a particularly tricky boss fight, alright? And honestly, sometimes a Strategic Pause is exactly what a PhD student needs. It’s… a mental reset. Plus, I finally figured out the rotational shield bypass – you wouldn't believe the sequence! A rotational shield bypass? Sounds a bit… intense for a Sunday afternoon, doesn't it? I was wondering why you were giving me the 'don't bother me' look. You looked like you were decoding the Enigma machine, not relaxing. It felt that important at the time! Anyway, speaking of intense, did you see that new Thorpe Park advert? The one with the drop tower going practically vertical? I'm terrified, but also… intrigued. Oh, heavens, no. I actively avoid theme park adverts. They induce palpitations. Remember Alton Towers when we were kids? The Nemesis? I swear I aged ten years on that ride. You screamed the whole way around. And then demanded a double helping of chips. Happy days. But seriously, I'm thinking about going. Sarah's been nagging me to be more… adventurous. Adventurous? Trying to balance your budget after the council tax bill is adventurous. Hanging upside down 100 feet in the air, that’s just questionable life choices. You’ll break something, Liam! And then who's going to help me re-categorize these survey responses? Dramatic as ever, aren't you? I'd be fine. And you’re brilliant at re-categorizing survey responses. Seriously, your presentation on the Northern property market trends was top-notch. The detail you go into... Aye, well, I do like a good spreadsheet. But back to the absurd – did you manage to see anything at the cinema recently? That new Sci-Fi with Anya Taylor-Joy... 'Echo Bloom', was it? Yeah! I saw it last week. The visuals were stunning. A bit slow in places, but the ending… wow. Really got you thinking. They did a remarkable job with the simulated alien landscape. It felt genuinely  other . I've been meaning to see it. Sarah says it's a bit bleak. I’m not averse to bleak, mind, just… not depressing. I need something to cheer me up after dealing with the Home Office’s latest proposals on border security.

Oh, this is just lovely, isn't it? Proper chips, not those skinny fries you get everywhere these days. Cambridge does know how to do a fish and chip shop. It really does. Though, I could do with a bit more vinegar, I think. So, you’re still battling with the rowing, then? You mentioned it last time we spoke. Battling is the right word! It's proving... challenging. I thought I’d be naturally graceful on the water, given my love of kayaking, but rowing is a whole different beast. It’s all power and technique, isn’t it? Not the gentle gliding I was hoping for. My back’s aching something awful. Oh dear! Kayaking is much more forgiving. Remember that trip we did in Cornwall? The sun was glorious, the water was so blue… How could I forget? You nearly capsized trying to photograph a seal! Thankfully, I managed to pull you back. Anyway, rowing… the instructor keeps saying ‘engage your core’ and I’m just thinking, ‘I’m trying, love! Stop telling me to engage my core!’ Typical instructor speak. They mean well, I’m sure. It’s like learning French – so many phrases that sound utterly ridiculous when you say them aloud. Remember "Il pleut des cordes"? “It's raining ropes” indeed! Exactly! It’s utterly absurd. Right, changing tack slightly... I was thinking about getting a proper waterproof jacket. The one I’ve got is letting in so much water. Have you got any recommendations? Something that actually keeps you dry, not just vaguely damp? Absolutely. I’ve been through a  lot  of jackets over the years, tutoring in all weathers. You need something breathable, definitely. Mountain Warehouse do some decent ones, though they can be a bit…loud. Jack Wolfskin are good, but pricier. I’ve got one from Columbia that's been brilliant for kayaking, and I think it would suit rowing too. It's got a hood that actually  covers  your head. A hood that covers your head! A revolutionary concept. I'll definitely check those out. It’s just…everything seems so expensive these days. It’s just such a nuisance with needing kit for everything. Tell me about it! Speaking of expenses, I finally managed to meet my cousin, Eleanor, last week. You know, the one on my father’s side? We’ve never met before, not even as children.

Honestly, Dad, it’s like nobody communicates properly anymore. It's all emojis and abbreviations. "LOL" and "OMG" and… I saw someone use "IYKYK" the other day. What even  is  that? “If you know, you know,” lass. It’s just… lazy, innit? Back in my day, you had to actually  write  somethin'. And if you wanted to send a message quick, you learned Morse code. Morse code? Seriously? Did you, like, actually use it? Aye, did! Used to sit with my grandad, used to tap it out on a table. Dot-dash, dot-dash-dot… easy as pie once you get the hang of it. Could send messages to me mates across the street. Much better than pinging a load of smiley faces, eh? I guess. But it would take forever. I need to reply instantly. Like, if I don't answer a text within five minutes, people think I've died or something. You kids and your phones! Remember results day? All that waitin', no instant gratification. Used to be scribblin' down numbers, lookin’ around for your mates… Proper tense atmosphere, it was. Honestly, I'm terrified of results day. What if I didn't get into Manchester? What if I have to defer a year? It's stressful. At least Vodafone let me use their Wi-Fi while I was checking the UCAS track app. That was a lifesaver. Manchester’s a grand city, you'll be fine. But don’t get me started on Vodafone! Tried to get a new contract last month, it was a nightmare. Everything’s about upselling and confusing jargon. You'd think for the money they charge, they could at least explain things properly. You know, like telling you where to get a decent pint. Speaking of money… student finance. Ugh. It's just… a scary amount of debt. Aye, I know. It is. But you'll earn it back. Just make sure you eat proper food, yeah? Not just noodles and pot noodles. You need some vegetables in you. Mum’s making a roast tonight, so at least I’m covered for one meal. I’ve been meaning to do a proper food shop though. They're doing those nice glass water bottles on eBay, you know, the ones you can add fruit to. Think I’ll get one. Much better than plastic. Good lass. Less plastic, good. I saw a delivery driver from Amazon struggling with a huge parcel earlier.

Blimey, it’s good to be back in a proper flat, innit? This place is…cosy. Liam’s mum does love her cushions. Cosy's one word for it. Grandma vibes, for real. Glad you made it over, man. It's been ages! University life swallowing you whole, yeah? Tell me about it. Feels like a lifetime since we last properly chilled. Exams were brutal, absolutely brutal. Data Structures…don’t even get me started. I spent a solid week living on coffee and Red Bull. My brain feels like scrambled eggs. Data Structures, eh? Yeah, that’s a proper beast. Remember when we tried to code that game together back in school? Failed spectacularly, didn't we? Oh god, yeah! 'Space Invaders 2.0'. More like ‘Space Invaders .0001’. I’m sticking to design and UI for now, thanks. At least that lets me get creative, you know? Less… logic-heavy. What about you? How’s robotics coming along? Still building little metal spiders? Still tinkering, yeah. Got a project going, actually, using machine learning to help navigate autonomous drones. It’s pretty sweet, once you wrap your head around the maths. The uni's got some top-notch labs, you know. They’re letting me use some of the advanced simulation software. Sounds intense. Listen, I was reading online last night, about Tokyo… They've got proper robot cafes there now. Like, fully automated baristas. Insane, right? No way! Seriously? Wicked! I’ve been wanting to go to Japan for years, man. The tech scene there is just on another level. I saw this documentary about a company building humanoid robots specifically for customer service roles. I know! It got me thinking… I’m trying to figure out what to do after uni. Like, realistically. Everyone's talking about Silicon Valley, but… it’s just…  so  far away. Japan feels a bit more manageable. Maybe a year abroad? You should definitely look into it. Uni have connections, right? Maybe they’ve got exchange programs. Imagine, wandering around Shibuya crossing, eating ramen… Proper culture shock, but in a good way. Exactly! Though, the language barrier…that's a bit scary. I can barely string a sentence together in French. There's apps for that, man. Duolingo, Rosetta Stone... don’t be daft. Plus, loads of people in Tokyo speak English, especially in the tourist areas. I reckon you’ll pick it up quick.

Right, look at this! Little Thomas did a finger painting at school today. It’s… abstract, let's say. Bright red and yellow, mostly. Apparently, it’s meant to be a dinosaur. Honestly, you can barely tell. I put it on Facebook, you should see it, Mum. Facebook, eh? Still using that thing? I keep forgetting my password. And honestly, all those pictures of people's dinners… what's the point? Give me a good photograph any day. Something to look at properly. Not a tiny square on that little screen. Dinosaurs, you say? Reminds me of the Birmingham Natural History Museum. Took your grandmother there, you know, back when it was properly grand. Not like it is now. All computer screens and interactive… nonsense. Give me a good old fossil any day. Granddad, you’re ancient! Everything’s interactive now. It’s how kids learn. Though I do agree, sometimes I miss the days of dusty museum displays. Anyway, Mum, you wouldn’t believe the comments on Thomas’s dinosaur painting. Some people are just… so clever. One woman said it represents the existential angst of the modern child. Really! I just replied with laughing emojis. Existential angst! Good heavens. People do make things complicated. Speaking of complicated, have you had a chance to look at that insurance quote for the cruise? It’s a minefield, isn't it? Pre-existing conditions, cancellation policies... it's enough to give you a headache. I have, yes. It’s daunting. We should probably get something sorted soon though, shouldn't we? The Mediterranean cruise sounds lovely, especially after this awful weather. Buckfast Abbey was quite bracing, wasn’t it? Beautiful, but a bit chilly wandering around the grounds. Buckfast. Yes. Smelled a bit like cider, didn’t it? Though I don't mind a good cider. Reminds me of Somerset. Your mother and I used to go to cider farms when we were courting. Proper revelation, that was. Never thought I'd be drinking cider, being a Wolverhampton lad. Oh, don’t start, David. You’ll be reminiscing all afternoon! We were young and foolish. And the cider was very good. Though, speaking of foolish, did you hear about David Cameron and his tax affairs? Honestly! Some people think they're above the law. Dreadful, isn't it? It's just… baffling. And then you read about these big corporations avoiding tax… it’s frustrating.

Right, so tell me everything! Belgium, eh? Sounds lovely. You both look…relaxed. Dad, you’re practically glowing! Well, you know, a bit of sun does a man good. More than I've seen in… well, ages, to be honest. Brighton’s grey, isn't it darling? It is a bit gloomy today. Though, Belgium was brilliant. Honestly, I’m still dreaming about those waffles. Proper Belgian waffles, not the ones you get here. Thick, fluffy, with real Belgian chocolate…  sighs dramatically . Oh, please, don't torture me! Were they  really  that good? I've been craving waffles lately. What else did you eat? Did you try any of that weird stuff like moules frites? We did! Brussels sprouts with fries. Sounds odd, doesn’t it? But it was actually rather nice. Salty, crispy, a bit… different. Though, I’m not sure I could eat it every week. And the beer, of course. They take their beer seriously over there. Of course they do! Did you go to any of those markets you were talking about before you left? Mum always goes on about wanting to find authentic European markets. Oh, yes! We went to a fantastic one in Bruges. Huge! All sorts of stalls – antiques, clothes, cheeses… Honestly, I could have spent a whole day just wandering around. We bought some gorgeous little linen napkins, perfect for the summer. And some chocolate, naturally. Couldn't resist. Naturally! And what about cycling? You were planning to do loads of cycling, weren’t you, Dad? That was… an experience. The sat nav, for starters. Utterly useless. Kept trying to send me down cobbled side streets and one-way systems. At one point, it insisted I drive through a park. A  park , mind you, with a rather large fountain right in the middle! It was a bit of a nightmare, wasn’t it, love? I warned you about relying completely on those things. I used to get lost all the time when I first started driving abroad. Always better to have a map as a backup. You should have downloaded offline maps, Dad. It's so easy these days. Did you end up having any accidents? I was worried about you driving on the other side of the road. No accidents, thank heavens! Just a lot of near misses. Roundabouts are  terrifying  in Belgium. So many of them! And they spin so fast!

Honestly, David, this smells absolutely divine. You’ve really outdone yourself. Though, I still think a  touch  more ginger wouldn't hurt. Just a whisper. A whisper of ginger? Right, because apparently, my curry’s already perfect. You're always hovering, aren't you, making suggestions. Are you secretly planning a cookery takeover? Don't be ridiculous. I just appreciate good food. And yours is generally very good. Much better than my attempts at risotto last week, anyway. That was… an experience. An understatement. The dog refused to eat it. That’s a new low, even for culinary disasters. Tell you what, to redeem yourself, you can tackle the rice. Alright, fine. But you owe me. Did you see Fiona’s post on Facebook earlier? She's finally bought those lilies she’s been wanting. Absolutely gorgeous, they are too. Bright pink ones. Do you think she's playing at being a florist now? Fiona? Lilies? No, I missed that. Facebook... It’s a vortex, isn’t it? I try to limit my exposure. All those carefully curated lives. Though, I do like seeing pictures of little Leo growing up. He’s a miniature version of her, really. He is. And she's put a ridiculous amount of effort into his Halloween costume this year. A tiny pirate. I’m almost jealous. Remember when we used to dress up for Halloween? Simple things, back then. A sheet with eyeholes. Triumphantly wielding a plastic sword. Simpler times. Speaking of simple, have you used that new perfume I bought you? The one with the sandalwood? I have! It's lovely, really. Very sophisticated. Not at all like that citrus one you got me a few years ago. I smelled like an orange for weeks! Actually, it reminded me… it’s funny, isn’t it, how accents change even with perfumes. That citrus one felt very… Californian. This sandalwood one feels distinctly… European. You're thinking too deeply about perfume, darling. Still, you have a point. Accents influence everything. Sometimes, I feel like my Edinburgh accent gets buried under all these years in London. It surfaces occasionally, especially when I'm tired or stressed. I love your Edinburgh accent. It's a part of you. It would be a shame to lose it completely. It's much more interesting than this rather bland, generic London sound everyone seems to adopt. Easy for you to say.

It’s a lovely home, Anon. Very… calming. Quite a change from the hustle and bustle of Bristol, isn't it? Though, I must say, Bristol’s got a certain charm. Full of interesting people. Aye, Bristol’s got its grit, that’s for certain. But this... this is peaceful. Reminds me a bit of the quiet suburbs back home in Manchester. You said you were teaching in Bristol? EFL, wasn’t it? Yes, English as a Foreign Language. For quite a while. A rewarding job, really, even if the salary wasn't exactly… generous. Though I managed, of course. It's funny, isn't it? Spending your life helping others learn a language, and sometimes struggling to articulate what you truly mean yourself. You know exactly what you mean, love. It's just a matter of finding the right words. I found lecturing at Sheffield University was the same. Lots of explaining grammar, when really, you just need to get the student to  feel  the language. It’s all about rhythm and intonation. Rhythm and intonation. Precisely! I’ve always said, a good suit has rhythm and intonation. Look at those old Savile Row tailors. They understood the body’s movement, the way a fabric should drape. That's business, isn't it? Understanding the needs of the customer, having everything fall perfectly in place. I was a director for a logistics company for years, before I retired. It was all about anticipating the flow, ensuring everything arrived on time, in one piece. Like a well-formed sentence, really. You're quite the philosopher, aren't you? I always found business men’s clothing incredibly intimidating, actually. Too ostentatious. Though I did appreciate a well-made wool coat. Keeps you warm on those damp Bristol days. Speaking of far away places… I’m planning a trip, you know. To Australia. Australia! Wonderful! I've only ever dreamt of going. Queensland, isn't it? Heard lovely things about the Sunshine Coast. My niece went out there a few years back – she’s a nurse. Said the weather was divine. Yes, Queensland! My cousin’s living in Brisbane. He emigrated decades ago, during a bit of his own upheaval, really. He's offered to put me up. It’s quite a jump, isn’t it? A world away from Gloucestershire. I'm a bit nervous about the long flight, truthfully. And a bit worried about the finances.

Honestly, Lizzie, this is lovely. Proper lovely. I didn’t think I’d find decent vegan food in Poland, you know? Though, I suppose having you around has broadened my horizons a bit. Everything’s broadened my horizons since I decided to... well, you know. That’s what I’m here for, Aunt Penelope! To drag you into the 21st century, one delicious plant-based meal at a time. Though, you’ve surprised me too. I thought you'd be a total technophobe, glued to daytime telly. Not entirely undeserved, darling. But I’ve been… experimenting. Mostly out of boredom, if I'm honest. That TEFL work only gives me a few hours a week, and the rest… well, the rest is a lot of thinking about how the world has moved on without me. I get that, I really do. It’s just… you're on TikTok now! Aunt Penelope, posting videos of yourself sorting through antique buttons? Who would have thought? Don't you start. It’s a niche market, Lizzie. People are fascinated by vintage haberdashery, apparently. And the algorithm is quite insistent. Besides, it’s… strangely therapeutic, categorising them all. Gives me a purpose. And those little dances? They keep me young, or at least pretending to be. You’re brilliant! You’ve got, what, twenty-three thousand followers? It’s mad. I’m struggling to get a hundred on my language-learning account. All I post are videos of me explaining grammar rules, and nobody wants that! Sad, but not entirely surprising, dear. People want entertainment, not lessons. Have you tried incorporating humour? A bit of… what do they call it… relatable awkwardness? I've tried. It just comes across as me being genuinely awkward. It’s a fine line, isn't it? I was thinking of doing a collaboration with a Polish content creator, someone who does travel vlogs. Maybe I can weave in some language tips subtly? That's a clever idea. Collaboration is key, isn't it? Like that podcast you’re so keen on now. “Crime Junkies,” was it? You’ve got that on repeat. Honestly, darling, all that true crime! It's a bit morbid, don't you think? It’s fascinating! It’s psychology, it’s social commentary, it’s… well, it’s addictive. And it’s certainly more engaging than the news, which is just relentlessly depressing. I’m actually listening to one now, about this unsolved mystery in Cumbria... near where I grew up, actually.

Right then, plans for this afternoon? Pippy, are you and Finn ready for a swim? It’s supposed to be gorgeous out, proper summery. YES! Can we do handstands, Mummy? Please, please, please! And can we pretend we’re mermaids? What's that, Mummy? Is it sausages? I  really  want sausages. Nearly, sweetheart. It’s pasta. Sausages are for tomorrow’s barbecue. And Pippy, yes, we can absolutely do handstands. Though you have to promise to listen to me about staying close to the edge. Right? Promise! Can ANON come swimming with us? Well, that's a good question. ANON’s got that circus to pack up tonight, hasn’t she? I spoke to Mrs. Davies - she’s been saving her for us specifically. She said she’ll be exhausted after the show. Circus! Will we see the circus? Will there be lions? Not  lions , Finn. Remember, it’s a travelling circus, a smaller one. But there’ll be clowns, and acrobats, and probably some very clever dogs. Remember we saw posters for it at the village shop? And juggling! I love juggling! Do you think ANON will juggle for us? I’m sure she will! I told her we were really excited to see her. Actually, speaking of exciting... I was thinking, wouldn't it be brilliant if we got a proper photograph of you two, dressed up all smart, to send off for that Blue Peter Badge? A badge? What for? For being brilliant, Finn! You’ve both been doing so well with your crafts. Remember that amazing cardboard castle you built, Finn? And Pippy’s watercolour of the garden was lovely. I want a shiny badge! You deserve one. We just need a good photo. It needs to be action-y, though, not just standing still. Maybe with you both holding your favourite toys? Can I hold Mr. Snuggles? Even though he’s a bit… smelly? Mr. Snuggles has clearly seen better days. Perhaps something a little less pungent? We could try something else. Right, on the subject of things seen better days… did you hear what Mrs. Peterson was saying yesterday? About how some people in China eat  old  eggs? Old eggs? Ew! Yucky! What does 'old' mean? Like, really, really old? Like, dinosaur eggs? No, not dinosaur eggs, darling. It means they’ve been preserved in something so they keep for a long time. Apparently, they taste quite… unusual.

Right, so… you said you wanted to talk about summat a bit…awkward? I’m braced, then. Though I’m having a right mental blank about what you were hinting at last week. Was it about your nan’s cat again? 'Cause honestly, if it relates to Mr. Snuggles’ dodgy bladder, I’m gonna need a strong brew. No, not Mr. Snuggles. Though, bless him, he  is  a character. This… this is a bit… different. It’s about… well, it’s about Liam. Liam? Everything alright with him? He seemed fine when I saw him at your mum’s last month. A bit quiet, maybe, but you know how he is. Always the quiet one. That's… kind of the thing. He hasn’t been quiet, exactly. He’s been… anxious. And then… well, things haven’t been… going well, you know? In  that  way. Oh. Right. Going well? What d’you mean, not going well? Don’t shut me out, love. You know you can tell me. We've known each other since we were practically knee-high to grasshoppers. He… he can’t always… get it up. Like, consistently. It's started happening more and more, and he's clearly really stressed about it. He hasn’t said exactly what he thinks is wrong, just that he feels… inadequate. Cor blimey. That’s… rotten luck, that is. Proper rubbish. Poor lad. It must be knocking his confidence something fierce. Has he… been to the doctor? That’s what I was trying to broach. He  doesn't  want to. He's saying it’s embarrassing, that he'll be labelled as… well, you know. Broken. He called it a "man thing" and said it’s just a phase, but I can see he's struggling. He spends ages staring at the ceiling, looking miserable. Aye, I can imagine. Men can be daft like that. All that laddish bravado, and then they get a bit poorly and suddenly they’re shrinking violets. It’s daft, isn’t it? Tell him, give him a good telling off, you should. I have! I told him it’s a medical thing, not a character flaw. I told him loads of men go through it, that it's nothing to be ashamed of. He just gets all defensive. Says he’s fine, just stressed. "Fine, just stressed." That’s a classic. My grandad used to say the exact same thing when he had his dodgy knee.

Honestly, I’m starting to feel like a walking Slimming World advert. Every conversation revolves around ‘syns’ and Healthy Extras. Did you know a packet of Quorn mince is a Green? I was genuinely shocked. Yeah, it’s good though, isn't it? At least we’re eating better. Remember that week we lived on ready meals? My skin was dreadful. And yours smelled faintly of microwave. Don't remind me. Anyway, I’m trying to figure out whether to have a banana or an apple with my dinner. It's a monumental decision, apparently. You’d think I was choosing between a Ferrari and a bicycle. It’s the small choices, isn't it? You know, I was reading this article about artificial sweeteners and flavourings…it was a bit grim. Apparently, some of them mess with your gut biome. Oh brilliant. That’s just what I needed to hear while I'm drowning my sorrows in 0 calorie syrup on my coffee. Well, you could try a little bit of mint in your coffee instead? Freshens it up. Better than questionable chemicals. Tea, by the way? I'm making a pot. Builder’s brew, strong. Please! Yes, please. Strong and milky, if you’re feeling generous. This cooking is making me dehydrated. What are we even making? Cauliflower cheese and roast? Ambitious for a Tuesday. It's treat day prep! Saturday's the big one. I’m thinking a proper roast with all the trimmings. I want to splurge, you know? We deserve it after all this healthy eating. I’ve been thinking about getting a massive block of proper cheddar. Cheddar? And how many syns do you think  that  will be? Right, I need to mentally prepare. Are you using Frylight for the roast potatoes? Because if you aren't, I’m intervening. Obviously! Frylight is a godsend. Saves a fortune on olive oil too. Speaking of saving money…did you see that posh supermarket had veg box deliveries with loads of obscure vegetables I'd never heard of? £40! Absolutely ridiculous. We're sticking with the basics. Agreed. Plus, the double peas in the freezer are doing their job. They're practically a meal in themselves. It’s just…the scales are playing up again. They’ve been stubbornly refusing to budge for a week. I’m convinced they're plotting against me. Scales are notoriously unreliable.

Right, so, Greece or Italy? It's really between those two, isn't it? We haven't had a proper holiday in ages. Director’s been particularly demanding lately, honestly, it's been relentless. Italy, definitely. Greece is lovely, don't get me wrong, but Italy just... more to do. More to  eat . And the history... you know I'm a sucker for a bit of Roman architecture. Plus, I could probably tie it in with a little consultancy work near Milan, make the trip pay for itself a bit. You always find a way to justify work, don't you? Honestly! This is supposed to be  us  time. No spreadsheets, no client calls. Just sun, pasta, and maybe a gelato or two. Though, realistically, I'll probably spend the first two days catching up on emails anyway. Old habits, I suppose. You’re incorrigible. Look, I promise, minimum work. Tops. Unless there's a catastrophic server failure in Northern Italy. Then you'll be hearing from me. Seriously though, picture this: we're in Florence, right? Wandering along the Arno, you’ve got a ridiculously large ice cream... And you're lecturing me about the Duomo, probably. You'd find a way to turn gelato consumption into a history lesson. Naturally. It wouldn't be a holiday with me otherwise! Okay, shifting gears slightly... I was thinking, actually, about that writing thing you mentioned. Oh? What about it? You seemed really enthusiastic about starting that short story collection. Have you made any progress? Just curious. Don't feel you have to, you're obviously busy. A little. Just bits and bobs, mostly character sketches, bits of dialogue. Trying to work out a through-line, you know? It's harder than I thought. I keep getting bogged down in the details. I even considered getting a tattoo – a little typewriter… it’s ridiculous, I know! A typewriter tattoo? That  is  a bit… committed. Though, not a bad idea, actually. A conversation starter. Might scare off the more pretentious literary types, though. Don’t want to be attracting the wrong kind of attention for your burgeoning literary career. You're such a tease. Honestly! It was just a fleeting thought. I'm probably better off with a good notebook and a cup of tea. Speaking of fleeting thoughts… did you see what they’re saying about that new environmental policy? It's utterly ludicrous, isn’t it?

That pheasant was quite superb, wasn’t it, David? Agnes really outdid herself this time. The jus was particularly well-reduced - a touch of juniper, I believe? Aye, brilliant. Absolutely brilliant. Agnes does know how to put on a spread, doesn’t she? Better than any Michelin-starred place I’ve been to, honestly. Though, I reckon a spot more gravy wouldn’t have gone amiss. Just a bit more, mind you. Not complaining, not at all. You and your gravy, David. It’s a constant quest, isn’t it? Right, so, the weekend. Agnes mentioned she’d booked us a table at The Old Bell Inn on Saturday? She did. Chimney cake flavoured cream tea, apparently. I was a bit dubious at first, but Agnes insisted it’s "the bee’s knees.” I reckon I'll just go for a proper scone with clotted cream and jam. Chimney cake, eh? Sounds… adventurous. Adventurous is certainly one word for it. I’m more than willing to try it, of course. Wouldn't want to disappoint Agnes. Speaking of which, have you had a chance to look at the list she gave us for Thomas’s birthday? It's rather… ambitious, isn't it? A bouncy castle, face painting, a magician… for a six-year-old! Ambitious is putting it mildly, Alistair! It's like planning a stag do, not a children’s party. Thomas will be buzzing for a week, no doubt. But I’m a bit concerned about the logistics, you know? Space in the garden, getting the bouncy castle delivered... Precisely. I offered to take charge of the music. Something less… boisterous than what Agnes initially suggested. No techno, for goodness sake. Some gentle jazz, perhaps. Something the adults can appreciate too. Good man. Leave the music to you. I’ll tackle the bouncy castle situation. I'll ring Martin tomorrow, he runs a local hire business. He's a decent lad, Martin. Gets things done. Did you see that postcard Agnes sent from Cornwall? The one with the ridiculously blue water? Ah, yes, quite lovely. Polperro, wasn't it? She seemed to have thoroughly enjoyed herself. Though, I must confess, wishing I were on that beach right now. No rain, no deadlines… Just the sound of the waves. Aye, looked proper peaceful. I was thinking, though… all this talk of Scottish independence again, it’s a bit unsettling, isn’t it?

Right then, you two. Let’s try and focus, shall we? We’re drawing chairs, remember? Pictures of chairs. Not… dinosaurs wrestling rainbows. But dinosaurs  do  like rainbows, Mummy! My dinosaur, Sparkle, loves rainbows! Mine’s got wings! And he breathes glitter! Okay, okay, Sparkle sounds amazing. But tonight, we’re trying to think about people who… who don't have all the things we do. Remember we talked about those people from Syria? The ones who had to leave their homes? The sad people? Yes, love. Sad people, but also brave people. And sometimes, when people have to leave everything, they lose things too. Like… like a comfy chair to sit on. Do they not have chairs? Well, some might. But lots might not. Think about it, if you had to pack up and go somewhere new, what would you miss most? Apart from me and your dad, of course! My teddy! Bartholomew! Good girl! And what about you, sweetheart? My racing car! The red one! Exactly. So, we’re going to draw chairs. Not just any chairs, mind you. We’re going to draw lots of chairs! And we'll take them to the community centre. They’re doing a collection for the Syrian families who’ve come to live here. It’s a way to show them we’re thinking of them. Can I draw a sparkly chair? For Sparkle the dinosaur? Absolutely. A sparkly chair is perfect. Maybe it's a magic chair that travels anywhere! What kind of chair should we draw, Leo? Do you want to do a wobbly one, or a really tall one? Big! A  really  big chair! Like a giant! A giant chair! Wonderful! Now, tell me, what kinds of chairs do you know? What chairs have you sat on? My chair at school! It’s… hard. And blue. Hard and blue. Good description. And what about at Grandma’s? She has lots of chairs. Her big comfy one! With the cushions! It’s like a hug! Grandpa’s got a rocking chair! It goes… That's right! A rocking chair. Very clever, Leo. So, we can draw a comfy chair, a rocking chair, a hard blue chair… even a sparkly dinosaur chair! The more different chairs we have, the better. It shows them we understand there are lots of kinds of chairs, just like there are lots of kinds of people.

Honestly, Mark, I'm feeling a bit stressed about Sarah and Tom. Did you hear back from her about the baby shower? Not yet. I messaged her last week, offering to help with the decorations. She seemed… distracted. Probably overwhelmed, to be fair. It's a huge thing, isn’t it? Becoming a mum. It is. And she’s always been so fiercely independent. I worry about her relinquishing some of that control. Tom, bless him, seems utterly clueless about the actual work involved. He's focused entirely on the cute outfits and the baby gadgets. Not the sleepless nights, the feeding schedules, the constant worry… Men, eh? They see a tiny, adorable human, and they think it's all sunshine and photo opportunities. They don’t realise it's a marathon, not a sprint. Poor Sarah, she’s going to need a lot of support. Have you talked to her about getting a night nurse, even just for a couple of weeks after the birth? I mentioned it gently. She brushed it off, said it was a waste of money. Typical Sarah. Always the martyr. She'll be running around, exhausted, trying to be Supermum, and then crashing spectacularly. Sometimes I think she needs to listen to me more. I’ve been through it, you know. With Leo. I know, love. You’ve survived the trenches. And you are an excellent resource. But pushing too hard… well, it'll just make her defensive. Let’s just be there for her, offer practical help without being preachy. Maybe a meal train? Everyone loves a good home-cooked meal. Good idea. I’ll float that by Emily. She’s brilliant at organising things. Speaking of Emily, how’s her dissertation going? She sounded so bogged down last time we spoke. Apparently, she’s hit a wall with the methodology section. Keeps changing her mind about which framework to use. Classic Emily. Overthinking everything as usual. I offered to have a look at her draft, no pressure, just a fresh pair of eyes. Oh, she’ll appreciate that. She gets so caught up in her own head. Sometimes she just needs to hear someone say, "Actually, this is fine." I was the same with my thesis, remember? Drowning in academic jargon and self-doubt. Vaguely. You were a force of nature back then, though. Didn't let anything stand in your way. We  all  wanted to be you.

Honestly, I still can’t quite believe the response to that little sketch. Did you see the article in the Norwich Evening News? They actually called me a ‘Norfolk Comedy Icon.’ A bit much, isn't it? A Norfolk Comedy Icon! That's brilliant. You deserve it, love. It was genuinely funny. The bit with the parking warden and the suspiciously large pasty? Gold. I mean, the university’s PR department must be thrilled. More publicity than they’ve seen in years. That's precisely what’s stressing me out a bit. They've already asked me to do another one, something specifically targeted at attracting prospective students. Apparently, “quirky Norfolk lecturer charm” is key to boosting enrollment. Can you imagine? Charm? Me? You  are  charming. Endearingly awkward, perhaps, but undeniably charming. And you’re good at physical comedy, you shouldn’t be discounting that. Remember the disastrous attempt at the inflatable dinosaur at the Christmas ball? Pure genius. Let’s never speak of the inflatable dinosaur again. It nearly took out Professor Davies. And it prompted a rather heated discussion about health and safety policies at the faculty drinks afterwards. Honestly, the whole thing felt…cursed, somehow. Cursed? Don’t tell me you’re starting to believe in that nonsense your grandmother used to go on about. Salt over your shoulder and all that? Well, she swore it kept the bad luck away. And I did trip over a badger two days later. Coincidence? Maybe. But I also saw a black cat crossing our path this morning, right before the filming started. You’re impossible! It's Norfolk, love. You’re practically guaranteed to see a black cat. It's part of the rural charm. And badgers are everywhere. Don't start attributing everything to superstition. It was just a slightly clumsy incident with a rather large inflatable reptile. I'm just saying! I felt like I was walking under a cloud all morning. It probably explains why the policeman kept giving me funny looks. Funny looks? What did he do? He was parked just down the lane, giving me stares. I swear he was writing something in his notebook when I walked past. I kept expecting him to pull me over and ask if I was filming without a permit or something. Probably just admiring the scenery, love. Or wondering what a Norfolk Comedy Icon was doing wandering around the fields.

Honestly, Dad, this phone is driving me mental. It keeps freezing. I tried clearing the cache, but it’s still doing it. It's brand new, too. Only got it last month. Proper rubbish, isn't it? Newfangled technology, eh? Always the same story. My brother used to have one of those smartphones. Said it was brilliant, then complained it was 'eating his data'. Spent more time trying to get it to work than actually using it. Give me a good old landline any day. Reliable. A landline? Dad, who uses a landline anymore? It’s all about being connected, you know? Though if it means constantly battling glitches… Ugh. Anyway, speaking of battling… have you booked the van yet for when we move? Mum's got a few quotes, but she wants your input. She says you’ve got ‘an eye for a decent deal.’ Well, I do know a bargain when I see one. Haven't driven a van in years, mind you. All this moving… reminds me of when your Mum and I first got together. Packed up everything from her little flat in Bromley and brought it all down here. Small world, innit? Funny the things you remember. Yeah, Mum keeps reminiscing too. She’s talking about boxing up all her antiques. Honestly, she’s got enough porcelain figurines to stock a museum. I think half of them have been gathering dust for twenty years. Are we having a clear-out? Because I'm not taking a ceramic badger with me. The badger… yeah, that’s a stubborn one. Your Mum's got a soft spot for it. Always loved collecting those things. Remember finding that old clock at the car boot sale? Remember that one, love? Vaguely. Was I even born then? I was more interested in video games, you know. Still am, actually. Been playing this new one – it’s a farming sim, but it's  addictive.  Utterly addictive. I’ve spent hours tending to virtual turnips. Farming, eh? Now look at me. Used to spend my days trying to catch actual fish! Proper fishing, with a rod and line down by the Medway. Good times. Shame I don't do it anymore. Getting a bit stiff in the joints, you see. Still, wishing I had, seeing them youngsters fishing today. You should get back into it, Dad. It’d be good exercise. Maybe we could go together sometime?

Honestly, this teal is just… too much. It’s shouting at me, isn’t it? Like a particularly aggressive parrot. We want the chairs to be calming, a bit of a haven, you know? Not a tropical disturbance. I thought you liked teal. You had a teal scarf last year. That scarf was a  delicate  teal. This… this is teal that wants to conquer the living room. Besides, we’re covering the whole sofa and the armchairs. It’s a commitment! I’m leaning towards that charcoal grey now. It’s understated, elegant. Charcoal grey will absorb all the light. Remember how gloomy the dining room was when we painted it that colour? We had to install those extra lamps. That's a fair point. Maybe a slightly warmer grey? Or a taupe? Oh, goodness, the choices! I've been looking at upholstery samples for three hours, and I'm no closer to a decision. It's exhausting. Speaking of exhausting, did you hear about the library? The Council’s proposal to demolish it and build flats? Yes, I saw something online. Absolutely dreadful. Another example of them prioritising profit over… well, over everything. Exactly! It's a bloody disgrace. It's been there since 1928! My grandmother practically lived in that library. It's a cornerstone of the community. I signed the petition, of course. Did you? Yes, early this morning. I also sent a strongly worded email to Councillor Davies. Though, let's be honest, they rarely listen, do they? It’s all about the bottom line and developers throwing money at them. It’s utterly depressing. They're tearing down buildings with character left, right, and centre. Do you remember that wonderful old bank on High Street? The one with the ornate carvings? The one that’s now a vape shop? Yes. A tragedy. They just obliterate the history. It's all shiny glass and steel now, isn't it? No respect for the architecture of the past. I wish they’d at least try to incorporate the facades into new developments. Preserve a little bit of the old. Precisely! Keep the front, build behind it. It would be a compromise, wouldn't it? Something to retain some semblance of the town's identity. But no, they’d rather build another bland block of flats. I was just reading about preservation laws in Edinburgh. Apparently, they're far stricter than here.

Right then, music first. Anyone got a particular vibe they're craving? The radio’s been a bit… predictable, hasn't it? All endless repeats of stuff from the 80s. Good tunes, mind you, but a bit much. Ooh, can we have some Little Simz? I’ve been obsessed with ‘No Thank You’ all week. It’s proper fire. Simz is good. Though, if we're being honest, anything blasting that loud when Dad's driving makes me feel a bit… anxious. Bit much for a Sunday afternoon, innit? Anxious, are we? Right, noted. Perhaps we can steer clear of anything  too  intense then. Anything calmer, perhaps? I was thinking a bit of Elbow, maybe? Elbow’s alright. Reminds me too much of those terribly depressing adverts for… something or other. Can't place it. Anyway, I'm pushing for some classic soul. Marvin Gaye, Otis Redding… something with a bit of groove. Oh, Dad, always with the soul! You're going to make me sing along. And you know I’m terrible. Terrible and enthusiastic, my dear. A winning combination! Besides, it’s good for the soul. Literally and figuratively. Okay, okay, compromise. One Marvin Gaye track, then something a bit lighter? I've been listening to a lot of Florence + the Machine lately. Very atmospheric. Florence it is, then. A bit of both worlds. Splendid. Right, moving on - presents. Have you all started your Christmas shopping? Because I certainly haven't. I’m dreading the high street. It’ll be a complete battlefield, won’t it? I’ve got a few bits for Mum. Candles and some fancy bath salts. Trying to be all luxurious for her. What about you, Uncle David? I’ve been thinking about getting Mum something for the garden. She’s been going on about wanting some new lavender bushes. Practical, I know, but she does love her gardening. It's her real hobby, you know. Honestly, you guys are so predictable with the presents. It's always garden stuff or scented things. I'm trying to find something genuinely original for my brother. He's obsessed with… obscure Japanese animation. It's a nightmare. Now  that  sounds interesting. Anything I can help with? I might be surprisingly useful. You never know. I’ve got a nephew with similar tastes. You do? Really, Dad? That’s… unexpected. Hey, don't judge. Restricting your interests is a terrible thing.

Right then, Liam, love. Come and sit y’self down. Been starin’ at these quotes all afternoon, it’s enough to give a body a headache. Motor insurance, eh? It’s gettin’ ridiculous, ain’t it? Absolutely robbery, some of ‘em. Yeah, it is mad expensive, Nan. I was lookin' earlier, and even with you on the policy, it’s still… a lot. I mean, I get it, I’m young and inexperienced, but still! Experiened? You’re barely out of short trousers! Don't get me started on young drivers. It's a minefield, it is. Remember when I was learnin’ to drive? My dad, God rest his soul, he was proper nervous. Nearly had a heart attack every time I took the Clio round the block. But at least then, insurance wasn't bleedin' you dry. Clio? Seriously? That's ancient history, Nan. I was thinkin’ somethin’ a bit… newer. Maybe a Fiesta ST? Or even a little Polo? Something sporty, y’know. Sporty! Liam, you’re goin’ to be payin’ for that sporty ‘til you’re thirty! A Fiesta ST, eh? Fancy. Alright, alright, I'm not sayin' you can't have ambition. But let’s be sensible, shall we? We need to think about budget, not just what you  want . Have you even considered what the excess would be? Excess? I knew there’d be somethin’ else. What's that then? Right, let me explain. It’s the amount you’d have to pay towards any claim. So, if you had an accident, and it cost £500 to repair, and your excess was £250… you’d pay £250, and the insurance would cover the other £250. See? Oh, right. That makes sense. So, a lower excess means I pay less if somethin' goes wrong? Generally, yes. But bear in mind, if you go for a lower excess, your premium – that’s your monthly payment – will be higher. It’s a trade-off, love. They’re always tryin' to get one over on you, these insurance companies. Spendin’ all their money on fancy adverts and posh spokespeople, while we’re scrubbin’ round tryin’ to find a decent deal. It’s a disgrace, it is. So, like, what’s a sensible excess then? For somethin’ like a Polo, maybe? Well, for a young driver, I'd say a minimum of £300, maybe even £500. It shows you're willing to take some responsibility.

Jaysus, this curry’s grand, alright. But the chicken’s a bit… rubbery, isn't it? Not like that place in Killarney. They knew how to do a proper chicken tikka. Nah, it’s fine, Dad. I like it. You're always moaning about the chicken. Don't you start, Liam. Your dad just has high standards. It  is  a bit chewy, I’ll admit. Still, it's good to have a takeaway tonight. I've been feeling completely frazzled. Frazzled is an understatement, love. Work's a right pressure cooker at the moment. This new project, the Alpha upgrade... it's relentless. I swear, I'm starting to see algorithms in my sleep. I was thinking about those stress tests they do, you know, the ones with the heart rate monitors and the cortisol levels. Should I be getting myself checked? You could. But then you'd probably just stress yourself out more worrying about the results. You’re probably right, lad. Just venting, you know? It’s hard to switch off these days. Remember when it was just dial-up and a screeching modem? Now it’s 24/7 connectivity. It’s tough. I keep meaning to start some yoga, but honestly, trying to find ten minutes to myself feels like a monumental task. Especially with little Leo. Everything revolves around him at the moment. Speaking of monumental tasks… did you hear about the vote, love? The equality vote? The one for same-sex marriage? Of course! It was incredible, wasn’t it? How Ireland voted ‘yes’. It makes me so proud to be Irish, even if I grew up in London. It’s about time, really. Yeah, it was brilliant. Like, a really big deal. I read about it online. Did you see that documentary, Dad? The one about the whole campaign? I did, Liam. Powerful stuff. It just goes to show, doesn't it? People can change. Attitudes can change. Though, you sometimes wonder if they just say what people want to hear. Right, well… is anyone else feeling like we’re being filmed? It’s a strange feeling. What do you mean, love? It's just... I feel a bit self-conscious. Like a reality show. We  are  being recorded, aren’t we? Liam, you set something up, didn't you? Uh… maybe. Just for a bit. It's for a podcast thing I’m doing at school.

Right, so, are we nearly there then, Nan? My back’s killin’ me. This road’s all twists and turns, innit? Not long now, love. Just past Cliviger, then a bit further up the hill. You're alright, are ya? I’ve got blankets in the back if you want one. It's a bit nippy, even for August. Remember that summer of '86? Proper scorcher that was. Barely a cloud in the sky for weeks. Nan, did you know a peregrine falcon was spotted over Manchester last week? Proper fast, those things. Like a fighter jet. A fighter jet, eh? More like a very determined pigeon. Though I suppose the speed is comparable. Manchester, though… far too chaotic for a falcon. Give me the Cotswolds any day. All those charming little hilltop villages, slate roofs, honey-coloured stone… picturesque, simply picturesque. Picturesque doesn’t pay the bills, Granddad. Give me a bit of concrete and a decent park any day. All that old-fashioned stuff’s a bit… stuffy, isn’t it? Reminds me of Shakespeare, all those flowery words. Now, now, lass. Don't you be disrespectin’ Shakespeare. He’s a legend. And a bit of history never did anyone any harm. Your Granddad’s got a point, mind. Used to go to Bibury with your Uncle David when he was a lad. Lovely spot. What’s Bibury, Nan? Is there Wi-Fi? Wi-Fi? Good heavens, no! It's a village. A very quaint village. Though, I suppose even quaint villages now have a signal. It’s all relative, isn't it? Like miles versus kilometers. People get so confused. Why can't we stick to miles? It’s much more… intuitive. Oh, here we go again. You and your obsession with old ways, Granddad. Everything’s metric these days. You need to get with the times. I’m lookin’ at law conversion courses, y’know. Need to know all the metric stuff, weights and measures and all that. Scales, kilograms, grams… it’s all important for contracts. Law, eh? That's a brave choice. It weren't exactly a popular thing to openly discuss back during the EU referendum, was it? A lot of strong opinions. Still think it was madness, all that business. An unfortunate decision, undoubtedly. Severely hampered trade. Though, one can’t deny it sparked a… spirited debate. Do you remember Terry Wogan used to read out the listener’s letters?

Honestly, I’m just feeling… conflicted tonight. This is lovely, by the way, Maya, seriously. But seeing all this food, knowing where most of it  used  to come from… it’s a lot. Conflicted how, Liv? It's just dinner. And this is all plant-based, remember? No woolly lambs or squealing pigs involved. I know, I know! That’s the whole point. But I was reading this article about cultured meat, you know? Shmeat, lab-grown meat. It feels… strange. Like we’re side-stepping the animal cruelty issue entirely, rather than solving it. Are we really making a difference if we just create a new, synthetic way to satisfy the craving? It's horrifying, isn’t it, the idea of 'meat' from a bioreactor. But look at it this way, Liv. The environmental impact of traditional farming is catastrophic. Deforestation, methane emissions, water usage… cultivated meat, theoretically, could drastically reduce all that. Less land needed, less waste. It’s not about avoiding the ethical line, it’s about drawing a different one. But doesn't it still feel… unnatural? Like playing God, almost? And what about the ethical implications of the cells they use to start the process? Are they sustainably sourced? It just feels like swapping one complex problem for another, potentially equally complex one. I feel like I need to take a vitamin tablet just thinking about it all. You always do, Liv! Seriously, you’d think you’d spend half your life dispensing pills if you had to deal with  your  anxieties. As for the ‘playing God’ thing, I get it, but humans have been manipulating nature for millennia, haven’t they? Selective breeding, genetic modification… it’s just the scale and the method that’s different. And the potential is huge. Imagine, no more factory farming. No more cramped conditions, disease outbreaks, antibiotic resistance fuelled by overuse in livestock. Hunting becomes… obsolete. Hunting is hideous anyway! I can't even look at a deer. Remember Uncle Barry's "trophy room" when we were kids? That was pretty traumatising. At least, with abattoirs, there's some regulation, theoretically. There's a system, however flawed. This cultured meat, it feels… unregulated. No real standards. You’re right. Regulation is  essential , absolutely. But we can’t let the potential pitfalls stop us from exploring the possibilities. Think of the mass starvation we could potentially avert with efficient, lab-grown protein.

“Right, that’s enough o' that. My brain's turnin' to mush. Let's put somethin' on that's actually…entertainin’.” “Anything’s better than watchin' a bunch o' blokes talkin’ about slate. My thumbs are properly achey from this gammin' though. Fancy a movie instead? Seen anythin’ good lately?” "Oh! There's that new rom-com, 'Snowfall in Solway.' I saw the trailer, it looked right cozy, didn’t it? All snowy and sparkly, and there’s a wee café that looks like somethin' straight outta a postcard." “Rom-coms? Seriously, Bethany? You know I can’t stand those. All that predictable nonsense. Give me an action film any day, somethin’ wi’ explosions, or maybe a decent thriller. Remember 'The Vanishing'? That gave me nightmares for weeks.” "Aye, that was a proper scary one. Remember old Mr. Henderson swore he saw the same bloke in the park every evening after that?” “You two are ridiculous! It’s Christmas next month, Daniel. Don’t be such a grump. A bit o’ sweetness is good for the soul. Besides, I've been doin' a bit of Christmas shopping online. Got Mum a lovely hand-knitted scarf from Etsy – a proper clever lass, that one. What are you lot gettin' sorted?” “I’ve ordered Dad a new toolkit. He’s always moanin’ about his old one being useless. Got it from Amazon, naturally. Takes a bit o’ the faffin’ out o’ findin' it, doesn't it? And yourself, Liam? Still spendin’ all your time on that thing?” "Yeah, well. Got a new game comin' out next week. 'Kingdoms of Albion.' Heard it's proper immersive. It’s got, like, a hundred different quests and all sorts. It's gonna take a while to work through it. Wish I could get some holiday hours down the pub. Might actually have some proper money to blow on it." “Liam, you need to be lookin' for somethin' more than holiday hours. They aren't goin' to train you for anything. Have you looked at anything at the community centre? They were talkin' about some digital skills courses." “Aye, I know, I know. It’s just… hard, isn’t it? Sent out loads of applications, but it’s like, no one’s even read 'em. Everyone wants experience, and how am I supposed to get experience if no one’s givin' me a chance?” “Don't start feelin' sorry for yourself, lad.

Honestly, this place is just  stunning , isn't it? I mean, Cambridge Law Faculty? Who'd have thought I’d be back wandering these halls, albeit for Alumni Day Four! It's a bit surreal, really. Proper posh, even for me. You’re right, it is. My mum would absolutely adore this. She's always wanted to come to Cambridge. The architecture... she’d be taking pictures of every gargoyle. Though I think she'd mostly be interested in the history of the legal statutes, to be fair. She's a bit of a law geek, my mum. Sounds like her! My nan’s more into stately homes and antique tea sets. Speaking of which, we're going to Blenheim Palace next weekend. Apparently, Aunt Penelope’s convinced it's vital for my ‘cultural enrichment’. Blenheim! Wow, that's fancy. Did you ever go on a family holiday that just stuck with you? One that you think about all the time? Ooh, definitely. When I was about ten, we went camping in the Lake District. Proper muddy, rained practically the whole time, but it was brilliant. My dad tried to build a fire and kept setting his eyebrows alight. We were all laughing so much. And the stargazing... Honestly, I'd never seen so many stars. Living in Aylesbury, you just don’t get that kind of sky. It was just... amazing. Changed my perspective a bit, you know? Got me thinking about, like, the vastness of everything. What about you? That's lovely! My most vivid childhood holiday memory is probably a trip to Cornwall when I was eight. My grandparents rented a cottage near St Ives. The smell of the sea, the pasties… pure bliss. But the best bit was definitely climbing up to Minack Theatre. Such an incredible location, perched on the cliffs overlooking the ocean. It was pouring with rain while we were there, but it somehow added to the atmosphere. We saw a play, soaked to the bone, and it was totally magical. Wow, Minack Theatre! That’s on my list. It  looks  incredible. You know, I’ve been trying to book a trip to Iceland for ages. Just craved something completely different. Wide open spaces, glaciers… properly wild, you know? Iceland! That is on my list too, actually. Have you looked into the Northern Lights tours? Apparently, they are phenomenal. I was thinking of going next year, maybe in February.

Honestly, Liam, I’m ready to chuck it all in. University, I mean. Not you, you're alright. Chuck what all in? The entire concept of higher education? Bit drastic, innit, love? What's gone wrong now? Did Professor Davies start speaking in Latin again? Nah, worse. It’s just… everything. The lectures are rubbish, the readings are longer than  War and Peace , and I swear half the people on my course are just nodding along pretending they understand stuff. I went to that seminar on Post-Structuralism this morning, and I left feeling like I'd lost ten IQ points. Ten! Right, alright. Deep breaths. Post-Structuralism  is  a headache. Even I struggled with that one, and I’ve got the fancy postgraduate degree to prove it. What specifically was horrifying? Try and break it down a bit. I don't know! It was all just... words. So many confusing words, all swirling around trying to explain things that don't  need  explaining. And this bloke, Malcolm, kept going on about deconstructing narratives and challenging assumptions, and I was just thinking about bacon sandwiches. Urgent bacon sandwich thoughts. I can relate to the bacon sandwich thoughts, definitely. But seriously, you’re panicking. It's normal to feel overwhelmed, especially with that stuff. It’s deliberately designed to make you question everything you thought you knew. That’s… the point. Easy for you to say, Mr. Master of Critical Theory. You probably dream in Derrida. Don't push your luck. Look, are you finding the content genuinely uninteresting, or is it just the way it’s being presented? Because there’s a difference. I think it’s both, to be honest. The actual subject matter is… not as riveting as I’d hoped. I thought studying English Lit would be all romantic poets and scandalous Victorian novels. It’s mostly academic essays about the symbolism of spoons. Okay. Right. So, spoons. Let's have a think. Have you spoken to any of the lecturers? Maybe just to say you're finding it a bit tough to follow? They’re usually decent enough. I don't know... Feels a bit daft, doesn’t it? Like admitting defeat. It’s not defeat, it's asking for help. Everyone needs a hand sometimes. Or, you know… maybe we could negotiate a swap? I'll write your next essay if you get me a proper, full-body massage.

Right, nearly ready then. Bit more salt, I reckon. This stew’s smelling alright, wouldn't you say? Better than that microwave muck you lot were eating last week. It does smell lovely, Dad. And don't remind me about the lasagne! It was a necessity, not a preference. You know how hectic things were. Little Leo’s got chickenpox, by the way. Chickenpox? Oh, poor little button! How’s he coping? Is he miserable? He’s being a trooper, actually. Lots of cuddles and cartoons. It's the itching that's the worst. We're just trying to keep him cool and distracted. Sarah's been a saint looking after him while I'm trying to mark these bloody essays. Essays, eh? Always the essays. You were always a bright one, weren't you, love? Never struggled, you. I didn’t, you know. I got by. Didn’t always shine, but I got by. Don’t be like that, David. You were brilliant at your job. Everyone said so. I’ve just been reading about that situation in Calais. Dreadful. Absolutely dreadful. The conditions those people are living in… It is heartbreaking, isn't it? I showed Leo some pictures in a book about different countries and we talked a little bit about people having to leave their homes. He was quite concerned. It's hard to shield them from it all, you know? Shield them? What’s the point? It’s all over the news, isn't it? Terrible, it is. Terrible for them, terrible for us, really. More and more arriving, more and more trouble. They say they’re fleeing war and persecution, but…well, you see what's happening, don't you? Strain on resources, the lot. David, please. It’s a bit insensitive, isn't it? Imagine being in their position. Fleeing everything you know, facing all that uncertainty… I’m not saying it’s nice, I’m just saying… It can't go on, can it? It can’t. They’ve got to sort it out where they are, surely? These countries, these borders… all this nonsense. When I was a boy, it was all… simpler. You knew where you stood. Things have changed, Dad. The world has changed. It's not a simple issue, and demonising people seeking safety isn't the answer. Have you seen that charity, 'Safe Passage'?
