They’re doing some amazing work helping families with their asylum claims… Charities.

Right then, Bryn. Dreadful morning, wasn’t it? Rain hammering against the window all the way in. Makes one appreciate a decent cuppa, doesn't it? Aye, a proper downpour. Luckily, Tredegar wasn't hit as badly as Newport, I hear. My sister phoned this morning, said the River Ebbw was getting quite high. Speaking of houses, you mentioned last week you were thinking about redoing your bathroom, Alistair? How’s that progressing? Don't even get me started, Bryn. It’s been a complete and utter nightmare, the whole thing. I thought I’d done my research, meticulously selected a reputable firm, read all the reviews... You know the drill. "Premier Bathrooms & Beyond," they called themselves. Beyond dreadful is more like it. Oh dear. What happened? I had similar trouble with a roofer a few years back. Said he’d be here at nine, arrived at one, and the bill was double what he quoted. Rotters. Well, the initial delays were bad enough. Promised start date: two weeks ago. Actual start date: yesterday. But it's the workmanship... It’s practically medieval! They’ve managed to tile over a skirting board, for heaven’s sake! And the grout… it looks like a five-year-old did it with a crayon. I had to have a very firm word with their project manager. A firm word, eh? Sometimes that's all it takes, a bit of Welsh steel in the voice. Though, I find often, it's all about documentation. Did you have a detailed contract? Precise measurements? Timelines? I thought I did. I had the legal department at the university look it over. Said it was "robust." Apparently, 'robust' doesn't prevent someone from gluing tiles crookedly. I’m half tempted to just live with it and use the bathtub as a decorative feature. Don't do that, Alistair! Stand your ground. You’ve paid them good money. Are you thinking of getting a second opinion? An independent surveyor, perhaps? I am, Bryn, I really am. I’ve already contacted someone – Mr. Davies down the road. Apparently, he is quite the expert in resolving disputes with tradespeople. Sent him some photos. He nearly choked on his tea, I gather. Good man, Davies. Reliable as they come. Always recommends getting everything in writing, and chasing them relentlessly. It's a national sport, dealing with builders, isn't it? Remember old Mrs. Evans from down the pub?

Right, so, Liam, you were saying about this… feeling. Like, this internal… zing? Was it more like an electrical shock or…? It's hard to explain, Mr. O’Connell. Like... imagine you're touching something metal, but it's not cold, it’s… buzzing. A warm, buzzing pain. But not unpleasant, mostly. It happened when I was trying to eat a spoon earlier. You  ate  a spoon?! Liam, darling, are you alright? What on earth possessed you?! I don’t know! It was just… there. And I thought… maybe if I concentrated hard enough, I could… absorb its properties? Like, become stronger or something. It was silly, I admit. Absorb its properties? Sounds like you’ve been reading too many comic books, lad. Superpowers, eh? What superpower did you think a spoon would grant you? I don’t know, exactly. Super strength? Maybe metal manipulation? I dreamed of making this metal shield defending us all. Metal! Metal! Honestly, the things children come up with. Still, a metal shield… that  is  quite imaginative. Liam, you wouldn't happen to have swallowed anything else interesting today, have you? Like, I don't know, a coin? No! Just the spoon. It wasn't very tasty, by the way. Kind of... dull. Dull? You tried to eat a spoon and you’re complaining about the taste? You’re a strange one, you are. Reminds me of old Fergus down the road, always getting into scrapes. Once, he tried to build a… a catapult out of drainpipes and a rubber band. Near took out Mrs. Doherty's prize-winning roses. Your uncle Fergus sounds like a character. Anyway, back to this… unusual sensation. Does it happen often? And you’re absolutely sure you swallowed the spoon? No, definitely didn't swallow it! Thankfully. Mum made me spit it out. It happens sometimes, but it's usually when I'm thinking really hard about things. Like, when I was trying to understand that truly horrible history book they gave us. It was full of dates and battles and… and  kings . So boring. Aye, history can be a killer. Remember trying to learn the Tudors? My head was spinning. Much prefer a good biography, something with a bit of... life to it. You know, speaking of life... We need to finalise plans for Finn’s birthday. The park event on the 18th? Yes, the park. I've booked the bouncy castle and the face painter.

Cor blimey, look at this weather! Proper beastly, innit? Like a November gale blowin' in early. Reminds me of the time… well, never you mind. Been watchin' 'em Halloween decorations goin' up, though. Always thought it a bit daft, all that carryin' on, didn't I? Never had much truck with fancy dress myself. Too much fuss. Oh, don't be such a grump, Arthur. It's just a bit of fun. The children love it, don't they, darling? And it's a good excuse for a bit of a treat. Remember when we used to take young Emily trick-or-treating? She was a little witch, bless her heart, with a pointy hat and everything. It's wicked, Nan. Everyone at school's planning their costumes. I’m going as a zombie cheerleader. It’s gonna be epic. Mr. Davies, my maths teacher, is going as Voldemort. Apparently, he wants to scare us into doing our homework. A zombie cheerleader? Sounds... energetic. And Mr. Davies as Voldemort? Bold choice. Schools are certainly making an effort these days. Back in my day, Halloween was just buying some sweets and hoping for a few trick-or-treaters. No elaborate costumes or themed nights. Though, I suppose that wouldn't go down well with the parents now. They want everything to be 'special'. Special, eh? Everything’s gotta be special nowadays. Back in my day, ‘special’ was findin’ a whole penny in your pocket. Now it’s, well, all this… . Fancy that. Still, Emily's got more spirit than I did at that age. Always loved a good game, did she? Remember her and her pony, Betsy? Oh, Betsy! That was a lovely pony. Emily spent hours out in the fields with her, didn’t she? I used to worry she’d stay out there all day long. She was a natural, that girl. Always had a way with animals. You remember the County Show, Arthur? Aye, I remember! That was a right palaver. All those folk crowding around, judging the ponies. Emily won a ribbon, didn't she? Little blue one. Near burst with pride, she did. Almost fell over tryin' to show it off to her grandad. Used to be a nice little riding school just down the road from here, you know. Old Farmer Giles’ place. Shame they built them flats over it. Horse riding sounds cool, Nan.

Honestly, this is ridiculous. I thought leaving Maidstone at seven thirty would beat the rush, but look at this! A solid wall of red brake lights. Are we even moving? Well, love, you know what they say. Bank Holiday weekend, everyone and their nan wants to see those big engines. It's always like this. Least we’ve got the radio. Fancy a bit of early Bowie? Radio’s alright, but my ears are already ringing from the lorries. This traffic is something else though, isn’t it? Not ideal when we’ve got Auntie Maureen to think about. She's not exactly a fan of being stuck in a car for hours. Exactly! And she needs the toilet every hour on the dot. I'm worried about getting her to the disabled parking. Last year, it was an absolute nightmare. People just parked wherever they felt like it, and we ended up having to walk ages. There's always bound to be a few chancers, innit? Wanting that prime spot right near the entrance. Mind you, I remember back in the day, when they hadn't even thought about disabled parking. It was every man for himself, practically a free-for-all. Times have changed, thankfully. Although, even with designated spaces, it's often a lottery. It's the same at work, you know. Trying to find parking for the residents at the care home. Some people just don't consider others. It's so frustrating. And it’s not just the fair. It’s everywhere, isn’t it? Finding accessible housing is a miracle these days. My friend, Chloe, she’s been trying to get a ground-floor council flat for three years now. She has mobility issues and living upstairs is killing her. Council housing…don’t even get me started. Blimey. The waiting lists are longer than a Great Western Railway line these days. Back in my youth, if you needed a place, you got one. Didn’t matter if you were working or not. It was a safety net, see? Now…well, it's a postcode lottery and a closed shop. It’s a failing, plain and simple. And with the aging population, the demand for specialist housing, for elderly housing, is just going to keep increasing. They need to build more, and they need to stop selling off council properties to private developers. Exactly! So many older people end up stuck in houses that aren’t suitable, or even  dangerous , just because they can’t afford anything else.

Right then. So, allotment. Honestly, it's a bit bonkers, isn't it? Me, having an allotment. I can barely keep the basil alive on the windowsill. Bonkers in a brilliant way, I think! And honestly, you’re already doing better than I was with houseplants. Remember that fern? It didn’t stand a chance. But seriously, it will be amazing. Fresh veggies, a bit of fresh air…what’s not to love? And you’ll have me to help, of course. That’s what I’m nervous about. You have all this fancy, organic, soil-loving knowledge. I’m more of a 'throw some seeds in and hope for the best' kind of gardener. I'm picturing chaos, really. And slugs. Loads and loads of slugs. Right, well, we can definitely tackle the slug situation. Copper tape around the edges, beer traps…the usual. And don't worry about lacking knowledge. Everyone starts somewhere. It's all about learning and having fun. Have you been looking at which plots are available at the community garden yet? I had a quick look online. There's a waiting list, naturally. They call it 'The Green Patch'. Bit twee, isn’t it? But apparently there are about ten available now. Number 7 seems decent - it’s got a bit of sun, apparently, but also some shade. Which, I gather, is important? Absolutely important. Too much sun can scorch things, too little and they just won’t thrive. Number 7 sounds promising. Do you want me to have a proper look at the map and the plot descriptions? I can spend a bit more time on it tonight. It's helpful to know the position relative to the water source, and if there's been any old rubbish left behind. That would be amazing, actually. You’re a star. I got distracted trying to visualise what to  grow . I was thinking courgettes. Massive, ridiculous courgettes that I'll be forced to give away to everyone I know. Courgettes are a classic! They're prolific. You might want to start with slightly easier things though, while you’re getting the hang of it. Like, lettuce, radishes – things that come up relatively quickly and give you a sense of achievement. And tomatoes, of course. Everyone wants tomatoes. Tomatoes… yes, tomatoes. Truss tomatoes, definitely. But I also saw something about growing pumpkins. Isn’t that… a lot of space?

Aye, it’s dead quiet 'ere, innit? Gran’s at bingo again, bless ‘er. Reckon she’ll win that tenner this week. Though, she'd spend it on Werther’s Originals straight away, she would. It's… calming, actually. Needed a bit of quiet. London’s been a bit much lately. Though, I do miss the constant buzz, you know? The energy. Buzz? Sounds stressful, that. Yorkshire’s got its own energy, just a bit… slower. More deliberate. And definitely more cake. Fancy a biscuit? Got some chocolate digestives. Real proper ones. Please! Chocolate digestives are essential. You know, Leo keeps trying to introduce me to posh biscuits – shortbread, macarons... it's just not the same, is it? Give me a good, solid digestive any day. Leo, eh? Still goin' strong then? You two seemed a bit… flippy-floppy last time I saw you back in August. Everything alright between you two? Yeah, mostly. It’s just… long distance is hard. He’s so busy with his uni stuff and his internship, and I’m trying to juggle everything here and with the open day next week for my new course. It feels like we're living two separate lives sometimes. Aye, I can imagine. It’s like yer both stuck in different planets, innit? Though, I reckon if he's proper about it, he’ll make an effort. You deserve that. What’s he say about coming up to see us for Christmas? Gran's already planning the turkey - she's got a whole spreadsheet dedicated to it. He said he'd try, but he can’t promise anything. He’s got some conferences he might have to go to. Honestly, it’s a bit disappointing. I was looking forward to Gran's Christmas onslaught. It’s a tradition! It is, it is. Don’t you worry, though. She’ll get over it. Probably bombard him with Christmas cards anyway. Right, so, what about this open day? You nervous? Absolutely terrified! It’s a big deal, you know? Getting into that course would be amazing. But there’ll be loads of other people, all brilliant and clever… what if I freeze up and say something daft? Daft? You? Nah. You’re clever, love. Proper clever. And even if you do say somethin' silly, so what? Everyone does. Just be yourself. That’s all that matters, innit? Easy for you to say!

Right, listen to this – I’m tellin’ ya, this boss fight in Elden Ring is having a right laugh at me. Been at it for three hours now, proper rinsed I am. Three hours? Honestly, Liam, you're such a glutton for punishment. It’s just pixels! Have you tried summoning someone? Aye, I’ve tried, love. But everyone's either offline or just as clueless as I am. Plus, summoning ain’t really me. I like the challenge, see? The satisfaction of beatin' somethin' fair and square, even if it takes 'til the cows come home. You'd be the same with your miniature painting, wouldn't you? Hoorin' over every tiny detail. You two are both obsessed. Seriously, Liam, Elden Ring? Still? And Chloe, are you  still  painting those…things? What  are  they even? They’re Warhammer miniatures, Raj. And this is a Blood Elf Sorceress. She’s practically finished. And Liam's not obsessed, he’s… dedicated. Dedicated to repeatedly dying, more like. Anyone want a cuppa? I made some proper strong builder's tea. Needed somethin' to combat the existential dread brought on by trying to understand Liam’s gaming habits. Builder’s, that’s the ticket, yeah. Thanks, Josh. So, Raj, what’s got your nose buried in your phone? Another TikTok rabbit hole? Worse. My mum sent me a picture of my cousin's baby. Seven months old. Honestly, the pressure to become a functioning adult is real. Like, I need to be building a career and owning a house. Not… still living in a student house watching Liam get obliterated by a digital dragon. Oh, stop it. You’re being dramatic. Most people are still figuring stuff out at seventeen, let alone… well, our age. And that baby’s cute, admit it. It’s… fluffy. Look, you wouldn’t understand. Coming from a family where everyone had a business by fifteen… Actually, how's your nan doing, Chloe? Last time I spoke to your mum she wasn't well. She’s a bit better, thankfully. Still slowin’ down a bit, you know? Memory’s not what it used to be. She keeps asking me if I’m married. Like, when I told her I’m studying marine biology, she said, "Why aren’t you knitting scarves for your husband?” Classic. My grandad’s the same. Still thinks I'm destined for a career down at the local steelworks.

Cor, this Cambridge air is a bit nippy even indoors, innit? Not like back ‘ome in Essex. Much warmer, usually. Remember those summers we 'ad, love? Scorching, they were. You could fry an egg on the pavement. They always say that, Nan. I doubt it ever  actually  got that hot. Though, it has been a bit chilly since we arrived. This house is lovely, though, really cosy. Lovely it is. Your Auntie Anon has done a smashing job with it. Though, a bit modern for my taste, if I'm honest. All those straight lines. Give me a bit of chintz and a floral wallpaper any day. Brings a bit of cheer, don't you think? Yeah, definitely. It's just... different. Right, so, Mum was saying you and Uncle Peter were thinking of going to the cinema? What were you planning on seeing? We were. Peter's been on about this new one, "The Beekeeper’s Secret" – sounds a bit daft, doesn't it? But he says it’s got Dame Helen Mirren in it. Can’t argue with Dame Helen, can you? Always puts on a proper show. He keeps going on about the cinematography, the “visuals,” bless ‘im. He fancies himself a bit of a film critic, doesn’t he? He does. It looks like a proper period piece, from the trailers I’ve seen. It's got good reviews, actually. Mum sent me a link. Reviews, eh? Well, that’s promising. I haven't been to the cinema in ages, not since... well, since your Grandad passed. Peter's been nudging me for a while. Says it’s good for the brain. Keeping me sharp, he says. Like I need reminding I’m getting on! It’s good to get out, Nan. And it's always fun. Remember when we went to see "Mamma Mia!" all together? That was brilliant. We were singing along at the top of our lungs. Oh, don’t remind me! Your Auntie Anon nearly got thrown out, she was so enthusiastic! That was a right good laugh. ABBA, you can't go wrong with ABBA. Gets you every time, doesn't it? Even after all these years. Absolutely! They're timeless. Have you seen anything good recently, besides the trailers Peter's been showing you? Not really. Your Auntie Anon got me a DVD of "Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris" last Christmas.

Right, so, spill. How was the interview? You seemed a bit stressed about it earlier. Did you get the position at  Bloom ? Honestly? It was… a lot. They really grilled me on my experience with long-form feature writing, more than I expected. I mean, I  have  done it, but it wasn’t the main focus of my degree. They kept circling back to that article I did on Welsh folklore. Do you think that was a good thing or? Hmmm, folklore? That could go either way, innit? Shows you’ve got a niche, a passion, something that makes you, you. But magazines these days… they're all about reclaiming stories, real people, relatable struggles. Was there a massive emphasis on social media presence? Everyone’s obsessed, ain't they? Oh, massively. They wanted to know my follower count, engagement rate… I felt like they were interviewing me to be an influencer, not an editor! It’s ridiculous, isn’t it? Wanting you to be famous  before  you can even do the job! I think I stumbled a bit on that one. I mean, I have Instagram, obviously, but it’s mostly pictures of cats and the occasional landscape. Not exactly dazzling. Cats are always dazzling, love. Seriously though, don’t beat yourself up. It sounds like a toxic environment, if I’m honest. Trying to box you in like that. Did you get a feel for the team? It was...neutral. There was this woman, Fiona, who seemed quite frosty. Keeps a really tight grip on the style guide apparently. Said my suggested layout for the travel section was “unconventional.” Unconventional! It’s  design , not rocket science! Sounds like a classic. You know, I was thinking, we really deserve a proper spa day after all this stress. Remember that place in Cambridge, the one with the lavender oil and the ridiculous robes? Ooh, yes! That would be  amazing . Although, my bank account is currently weeping. Still waiting to hear back about the  Bloom  job, so I’m trying not to spend anything extravagant. Nonsense! Consider it a mental health investment. We’ve been working so hard. Besides, I was just watching  The Undateables  last night. Absolutely heartbreaking but also inspiring, you know? Reminded me that life's too short to worry about a few pounds. You and your emotional TV. It’s a classic tactic, you know – guilt tripping me into spending money.

Right, this is a disaster. An absolute blooming disaster. The washing machine’s done it again. Done what again, love? Sounds serious. Did it eat a sock? That happened once, didn't it? Worse, Paul. Much worse. It’s…frothing. Like, actual, bubbly, soapy froth coming out the back. I had to mop it up! It looks like a badger had a party in here. Frothing, eh? Sounds like a plumbing emergency. Did you try turning it off at the mains? Aye, of course I did! I'm not a complete numpty, are you? It's still dripping. And it smells strongly of… lavender. I put in the usual detergent. Not the fancy stuff, mind you, the regular Tesco's value stuff. This is baffling. Lavender? That’s odd. Maybe you accidentally grabbed the lavender-scented fabric softener? Honestly, Paul. Do you think I’m that daft? I counted everything before I put it in. This is definitely a machine malfunction. I’m starting to think we need to call someone, and I  hate  calling people about washing machines. It feels so… pathetic. Like admitting I can’t handle basic domesticity. Don't be silly, pet. It's a machine. They break. And you're a Research Manager, crunching data and designing methodologies - hardly a sign of domestic inadequacy. Besides, I’m here to help if I can. Maybe it’s the drain hose? It might be kinked somewhere. Maybe. I’ll have a look later. Right now, I'm starving. I was hoping to actually relax tonight after dealing with… the froth situation. What are we having? I was thinking that Thai green curry I found online. It looked fairly straightforward. Thai green curry sounds amazing! I'm in. We could watch something while we eat? I was thinking that new Wes Anderson film,  Asteroid City . I've heard good things. Ooh, Wes Anderson! Proper quirky, isn't it? I haven’t seen it yet. Mum and Dad were raving about it last week when they rang. Apparently, it's got Jason Schwartzman in it again. They're massive fans. Dad's already got every single film on DVD. He's obsessed. Yeah, he's brilliant in it. And the visuals are stunning. It's like stepping into a pop-up book. You know, my Gran used to collect pop-up books. She’d have them all laid out on the coffee table, tiny little castles and animals leaping out.

Honestly, I still can't quite wrap my head around it all. A whole company…faking emissions tests? It's just… brazen, isn’t it? I mean, the scale of it… you read about it, but to think they were doing it for years… It  is  pretty astonishing, isn’t it? At first, there was a bit of a shrug, you know? “Companies do bad things,” the general attitude. But the sheer financial implications, the environmental impact… it’s more than just a dodgy business practice. And the fact that it took so long to be uncovered... They thought they were clever, didn't they? Clever enough to fool the regulators. Like that bloke at Enron. Same sort of hubris. Thinking they were above the rules. It's always been the same, innit? Big companies thinking they can get away with anything. Exactly, Michael! It just breeds such cynicism. And then you think about the consumers, buying cars believing they were environmentally friendly… it feels like a betrayal, doesn't it? A real slap in the face. All this talk of 'green' technology, and it’s all based on a lie. Definitely. They were practically advertising themselves as being eco-conscious, and it was all a facade. It's the trust element that really stings, I think. Especially now, with everything that's going on. People are already questioning everything they read and hear. Trust is a vanishing commodity, love. Vanishing. Used to be, you shook a man’s hand, that was a deal. Now… …it’s all paperwork, lawyers, clauses. And still, they find a way to deceive you. Happens in planning too, you know. Developers promising one thing, building something entirely different. Using loopholes to get what they want. Speaking of building… are you two still happy with Hunsonby and the move? It’s still so very… quiet. I’m getting used to it, slowly, but I do miss the… the bustle of Dublin, I suppose. I love it here. It’s calmer, less stressful. And the house is perfect, isn't it, Michael? Much more spacious than the flat. Though, remember when we were house-hunting? Honestly, the price of those little cottages around here… it's ridiculous! Southern England prices for Northern England charm. Don't I know it! We did well to get this for this price. Back in Walsall, you’d be paying double for a place half the size.

Cor, this tea’s gone cold again. Don’t know why I bother, do I? Seems everything’s gone cold these days. Even me. Don’t say that, Arthur. You’re not cold. Just… quiet. You’ve been quieter than usual these past few weeks. Something on your mind? Something to do with that letter about the housing development, was it? Aye, it were. More metres of those bloody boxes than you can shake a stick at. They’re wanting to build right on the edge of the fields, Reginald. The ones we used to go rabbiting on, remember? Used to. Seems a lifetime ago, that does. Remember old Mr. Henderson nearly shot himself trying to scare one out of a bramble patch? Oh, I do. Right clumsy bloke, he was. Got more tangled than the rabbit ever did. Still, at least he weren’t upsetting folks like that lot are, with their planning applications and their surveyors trampling all over everything. Upsetting folks is a national sport these days, isn’t it? Honestly, I saw Mrs. Peterson tearing strips off poor young Jamie down at the shops. He’d accidentally knocked over a display of tins. Tins! Like it were the end of the world. People just need something to grumble about, don't they? It’s the modern way. Reminds me of that pension thing, honestly. They change the rules every other week. Keeps us all on our toes, don't it? Like chasing a shadow. Don't get me started on pensions, Arthur. Utter shambles, it is. They promised us the world, used to. Now look at it. Barely enough to cover the heating bills, let alone a bit of decent fish and chips. Speaking of bills, have you two looked at the electricity statement? It's outrageous! I swear, they're metering it by the blink of an eye these days. I tried explaining it to Margaret, my granddaughter, but she just looked at me like I was speaking Swahili. All this computer nonsense... Computers! Don't even get me started on those contraptions. Tried to order a new bulb online the other day. Nearly had a coronary. Too many clicks, too many boxes to tick. Ended up calling the shop. Much easier. Easier for you, maybe. My eyesight's not what it used to be, and those tiny fonts… it's a nightmare. I think I’d rather spend the day in bed.

Honestly, I’m just completely brain-fried. Biology was brutal today. Mr. Davies spent the whole lesson on meiosis, and I swear, I’ve never felt so utterly confused in my life. It's like, why do we even  need  to know this? I’m never going to use it! Relax, Liam. You’ll get it eventually. It’s just a complicated process. Think of it like… Legos! Really tiny, complicated Legos that make… well, you. Legos is a terrible analogy, Zayn. It's more like a bizarre dance where chromosomes have to swap bits and pieces. And it  is  important. It's how genetic variation happens, which is the foundation of evolution! You know, natural selection and all that. Oh, here we go. Another evolution lecture from Ethan. What? It’s fascinating! Did you see that video that went viral of the peppered moths? The industrial revolution, pollution… suddenly, darker moths were camouflaged better against soot-covered trees. Boom! Natural selection in action. Speaking of things going viral, did anyone see that TikTok of the guy who accidentally filmed a squirrel stealing his sandwich? It was hilarious! Yeah, I saw it. That's getting like, millions of views. It’s insane how quickly stuff explodes on the internet these days. Remember that singing cat? That was ages ago, but it feels like yesterday. It’s clever algorithms, man. They feed you what they think you want to see. It's all a bit creepy, isn't it? Like they know more about you than you do yourself. Definitely. It’s weird. And sometimes, it’s just bizarre. Like all those conspiracy theories. Honestly, some people believe the craziest stuff. Well, some of them have a kernel of truth… sometimes. Though most of them are just… well. Okay, okay, let's not go down the conspiracy rabbit hole. I’m trying to eat my chips in peace. So, Liam, are you  really  struggling with meiosis? Maybe I can try to explain it differently? It's not just meiosis, Zayn. It’s just… everything. School feels so pointless sometimes. Like, we’re learning all this stuff, but it doesn't connect to anything real. Plus, there’s all the pressure to get good grades, go to a good university… It’s exhausting. Tell me about it. My sister keeps going on about how she needs to be 'influencer ready' by the time she finishes uni.

Honestly, the hospital appointments are just piling up. I've got this follow-up for the knee operation next week, and then there's the blood tests – they’re worried about a potential infection. Everything feels a bit… much. Aye, hospitals are a right pain, aren’t they? You’re doing well to keep on top of it though. That knee must be playing up something fierce. My Doris next door, she had that operation last year. Took her ages to recover. Was on a dozen different tablets, poor love. Tablets! Back in my day, a cup of tea and a lie-down sorted everything out. Though, to be fair, we didn't have all these fancy operations either. Used to be, if you broke a bone, you just wrapped it up in bandages and got on with it. Nonsense, Elsie. You’d be dodging lorries and horses, not lying down. I remember patching myself up after a shunt with a Ford Anglia once. Just a bit of duct tape and a prayer. Kept me going for weeks. You both have such wonderfully… pragmatic approaches. I'm trying to manage it all, you know? The tablets, the physiotherapy… it's exhausting. I keep thinking about that acupuncture clinic I saw advertised. Apparently, it can help with pain management. Acupuncture? Now, that’s interesting. My Brenda, she swears by it. Says it fixed her back after she tripped over a cat. Worth a try, I reckon, rather than being loaded up with pills. I’ve heard tell of it. Sounds a bit… pokey, doesn't it? Though, anything's worth a go if it eases the discomfort. My arthritis is playing up something awful today. Pokey is right. Gives me the willies just thinking about it. I’m a man who likes mechanics, not needles. Speaking of mechanics, did you get your MOT done yet, Sarah? Just last week. Passed, thankfully. Though they warned me I’ll need new tyres soon. Another expense! I swear, running a car is just a bottomless pit. What about yours, John? Changed 'em last month. Got some decent ones this time, Michelin. You gotta invest, girl. Safety first, eh? Used to drive all over Europe in my lorry – never penny-pinched on the tyres. Memories… So many miles, so many countries. Remember that time in Germany? We were delivering… John, dear, don't get started on the lorry stories again!

Right then, love. So, we were talking about, well, a really long time ago. About people owning other people. Doesn't seem right, does it? No. Why would they do that? That’s a really good question, sweetheart. It’s a hard one to answer properly. A long time ago, some people thought it was okay because they believed some people were… less important than others. They needed lots of people to work on big farms, like sugar or cotton farms, and instead of paying them a fair wage, they made them work as slaves. For nothing. But where did they get them from? Well, a lot of people were taken from Africa, which is a huge continent, and brought over to America. It was a really cruel journey, called the Middle Passage, and it involved terrible conditions on ships. People were treated very badly. Do you remember when we talked about being kind to everyone, even if they’re different? Yes. Like Thomas next door. He’s got funny ears. Exactly. It's like thinking Thomas’s ears made him less of a person. It wouldn't be fair, would it? Anyway, these people who were enslaved, they were clever and strong, but they were forced to work and they weren’t allowed to have freedom. They weren’t allowed to read or write, often. Did they fight back? Some did, yes. Some ran away, called themselves ‘Maroon’ and built secret communities in the forests. It was really hard, always looking over their shoulders, but they were determined to be free. And other people, both enslaved and free, helped them. It took a  very  long time, but eventually, slavery was abolished. It was made illegal. Abolished? What does that mean? It means it was stopped. It was deemed wrong. But... it's important to know that even  after  it was abolished, things weren’t instantly fair. People faced a lot of discrimination, and struggled to be treated equally. They had to fight for it. Oh no! That’s alright, love. We can build it again. It’s a little like… sometimes, even when something bad is stopped, it takes a long time for things to truly get better. It’s like wars, really. What’s a war? Like, roar like a lion? Not quite. Wars are when countries or groups of people fight against each other. It’s really, really awful.

Right then, this is lovely. Proper family get-together, innit? Feels years since we all sat down like this without someone rushing off to something. Tell me about it, love. Work's been a proper whirlwind lately. This department is… well, let’s just say I’ve seen more drama than EastEnders this month. Speaking of which, anyone watching that still? Oh, yeah! I’m totally addicted. Kat Slater’s my spirit animal, honestly. She just gets things done, ya know? It’s a bit ridiculous sometimes, but I find myself glued to the sofa every week. Ridiculous is an understatement. It’s pure, unadulterated chaos. But you can’t look away. It's the same with that  Bake Off  thing. All that gentle baking, then horrifying disasters. Fascinates me. Remember when that Phil Mitchell lot were having all that trouble with the docks? My Elsie – bless her heart – she used to get so worked up! She’d be yelling at the telly, giving them a right mouthful. Oh, Elsie! She was something else. Remember when she chased after that lad who was fly-posting on the new roundabout? Said he was ‘ruining the aesthetics’ of the village. Good times. Trying to keep Kemsing pristine. It was a passionate thing, that. Speaking of aesthetics, have you seen what they’re planning to do with the old community hall? Apparently, some developer wants to build flats. Seriously? That’s awful! Where will the WI have their meetings? And the dog training? The village would lose its heart, wouldn't it? It would, wouldn't it? Council’s got no sense sometimes. All about the money. It's always the same. They'll say it’s progress, but it's destruction really. I saw old Mrs. Higgins down the shops yesterday, in floods of tears about it. It's always the same story, isn't it? They have meetings, promises, consultations… then they do whatever they want anyway. Remember the debacle with the proposed supermarket down by the river? They promised us a lovely little place, didn’t they? Nice and quaint. Ended up a monstrous thing, didn’t it? So much traffic, all down our little roads. Ruined it. It’s just…sad. Everything’s changing so fast. It feels like nowhere’s safe. It’s hard to feel grounded anywhere anymore. I was reading an article the other day about how… Now, now, don’t start preaching about the existential angst, love.

Right, that’s the dishwasher done. Feeling slightly less chaotic now, isn't it? Honestly, it's a wonder we ever manage to keep the house vaguely tidy. Miss Emily, Miss Emily! Did you know Hermione Granger is really clever? Like,  really  really clever! I did, sweetheart. Hermione’s brilliant. She knows loads of spells. But you know who else was clever? A very long time ago, before even your grandma was born… Who? Tell! Well, there was this man named George Stephenson. Now, he wasn't a wizard, but he invented something incredible. What did he invent? A broomstick that  really  flies? Not quite a broomstick, darling. He invented the railway engine! You know, the trains that go ‘choo-choo’? Trains! I like trains! They go  whoosh ! Exactly!  Whoosh ! They’re incredibly fast, especially the modern ones. But George Stephenson, he had to figure out how to  make  them go. It wasn’t easy. People thought he was a bit mad, actually. They said trains couldn't possibly work. Mad? But trains are brilliant! He was passionate. He spent years experimenting, figuring out how to make the engines powerful enough to pull carriages and all the people inside. He even built his first little engine, Puffing Billy, when he was just a young man. It was tiny, but it showed everyone what was possible. Puffing Billy? Like a little dragon? A little dragon, yes. But instead of breathing fire, it breathed steam! He and his son, Robert, they built even bigger and better engines. They built the Stockton and Darlington Railway, which was the first public railway in the world using steam locomotives! Wow! So, no magic then? Just… cleverness? Just cleverness, ingenuity, and a whole lot of hard work. Sometimes, the cleverest things are the ones that aren't magical, you know? Building a whole railway system, that's pretty amazing in its own way. It changed the world, it really did. People could travel much further, much faster, and move goods around the country. Could he build  me  a train? A really big one? Unfortunately, George Stephenson isn't around anymore, sweetie. He lived a very long time ago. But engineers today, they build trains all the time! They’re even working on trains that float on magnets! Can you imagine? Floating trains?! Even better than broomsticks! It is pretty amazing, isn’t it? You know, it's funny, when I was your age, I was obsessed with trains too.

Right, so, I’m thinking this chilli needs a bit more…oomph. What do you reckon, Liv? Bit more paprika? Or maybe some smoked salt? Paprika, definitely. Smoked salt’s a bit much, innit? You'll overpower the beans. And are you  sure  you measured the cayenne properly this time? Last time it nearly took my eyebrows off. Alright, alright, lesson learned. I’m being super careful. It's a really important dinner, yeah? Think Auntie Carol will be alright with the spice level? She's not exactly a fan of a bit of heat. Don't worry about Carol. She'll complain, she always does. But she’ll secretly love it. Honestly, she complains just to have something to do. Speaking of which, did you guys see Sarah’s post about that supper club she’s doing next week? "Flavours of Morocco," she called it. Sounds amazing. Morocco, eh? Bit ambitious for a Tuesday night, wouldn’t you say? Though, Sarah’s always been one for throwing herself in the deep end. Remember that awful attempt at paella she did? Oh god, the paella! The rice was rock solid. And barely any seafood. She’s got the drive, I’ll give her that. Speaking of things that are stressful... I’ve got this absolute nightmare with my housing contract. Landlord’s trying to pull a fast one, hiking the rent by like 30 percent. It’s mental! Seriously? That’s outrageous. Have you spoken to a solicitor? There’s that Citizens Advice thing, they’re pretty good. Yeah, I’ve been looking at stuff online. It’s all so complicated. Like, I know my rights, but actually  proving  something is another ball game. I keep getting drawn into some weird website filled with legal jargon that makes absolutely no sense. Anyone know a decent lawyer who doesn’t charge the earth? My dad knows a bloke, quite good apparently. I can get his number if you want. He does mostly family law, but he might be able to point you in the right direction. Legal stuff's always a headache, isn't it? Just gotta document  everything . Emails, photos, dates... everything. You need a paper trail. I had a bit of a run-in with a customer the other day. Wanted a ridiculously complicated soy latte with oat milk and some other nonsense. Just wouldn’t stop complaining. Had to report it.

Honestly, this coronation chicken is just what I needed after that morning’s rush. Did you manage to grab anything decent from the canteen today, Anya? Nah, the canteen was a disaster, as usual. Just grabbed a sad-looking salad from the shop across the road. Not exactly inspiring, is it? I was thinking of making a big batch of borscht this weekend, though. Proper comfort food. You ever had borscht? Borscht? No, I don’t think so. Isn’t that…Russian? I know a bit about Russian cuisine from a documentary I watched once, all beetroot and lovely sour cream. Sounds rather chilly, though, doesn't it? This weather's been so unpredictable lately. It is Russian, yeah! Beetroot is the star. And sour cream is essential. It's warm and hearty, especially good when it’s cold. You absolutely should try it! Next time I make a big batch, I’ll bring you some. It’s much better than that sad salad I'm having now. Oh, you’re awfully kind! I'd love that. It’s so nice to have someone who actually  cooks  around here. I'm a bit of a disaster in the kitchen, to be honest. Tuna sandwiches for the win, most days. Though little Leo has been wanting shepherd's pie lately. Apparently, all the other kids at school are having it. Shepherd’s pie is good. Simple, but good. Leo must be getting big now, right? Last time we spoke, he was just learning to say ‘cat’. He is! He's five next month, can you believe it? Starts proper school in September. It’s a massive step, isn’t it? I'm trying not to get too weepy about it. He’s absolutely thrilled, though, wants to wear a superhero cape every day. That sounds like Leo! My niece, Sofya, is starting primary school in Moscow this year too. It's always a strange feeling, letting go a little. Are you worried about him settling in? A bit, I lie. It's the social side mostly. He can be a bit shy, you know? Hoping he makes some good friends. Plus, you know how they are with playground politics at that age. Have you kept in touch with your family back in Tomsk? Yeah, we video call every Sunday. My mum is always sending me care packages full of weird and wonderful things I don’t need, but it's the thought that counts.

Are we nearly there yet, Grandad? My legs are killing me after lugging all that baby stuff. Mum’s got some right weird taste in blankets, hasn’t she? That fluffy, pink one… honestly! Nearly, love. Just gotta navigate these Preston roads. They're a nightmare, especially on a Saturday. And honestly, Elara, pink suits a baby. Don't be so grumpy. It’s well worth it. You never know, it’ll be yours one day. Aye, she'll be saying that when she's got kids o’ her own! She’ll be pickin’ out the most garish thing she can find. Remember that orange scarf your Auntie Sheila bought for me? Still got it, I do. Wore it to your mum's graduation. Ew, Grandad! That scarf was truly horrific. Still, at least Sheila has a sense of… something. Mum just likes fluffy. Did you get the survey done on the house, Mum? The one we talked about yesterday? Yes, I did. It came back this morning. Mostly good news, thankfully. Some damp in the downstairs bathroom, needs addressing, and the electrician flagged the wiring in the kitchen needs updating, but nothing major. It’s mostly cosmetic, really - new flooring, a bit of painting, that sort of thing. It did come back a bit worse than I thought though. Damp, eh? Always a worry. Your mum reckons she can tackle that herself? She’s a dab hand with a paintbrush, your mum. Remember when she redecorated the whole kitchen in Bolton? That was a right palaver, though. Paint everywhere! She’ll be trying. She’s convinced she's going to be a DIY expert. I’m placing bets on her needing to call a professional before the weekend. What about the loft? Did they look up there? That's where all the junk is. They did check the loft. It's fine… full of boxes, naturally! Mostly your dad’s old football memorabilia. Speaking of which, he's still humming that tune from that football match we went to last week. Aye, he is! That was a good game, though. Proper drama. Reminds me of when I was a lad, watching Bolton at Burnden Park. Used to get right behind the team. Those were the days. Grandad, stop reminiscing about your youth! I’m trying to concentrate. So, kitchen wiring… that’s going to be pricey, isn’t it?

Ugh, I'm so frustrated with 'Aetherium Wars' right now. Seriously, how can they balance the Valkyrie class like  this ? It's ridiculous. Everyone's using her, and I can’t even get past level 42. Aetherium Wars, is it? Sounds… intense. Is that the one Jamie’s always going on about? The one with the dragons and the sparkly swords? Yeah, that’s the one, Mum. It’s a massively multiplayer online RPG. It’s pretty complex, actually. The Valkyrie's power spike at level 42 is well-documented. The developers are going to have to address it. Exactly, Jamie! Tell her! They just made her abilities completely overpowered. I’ve been trying different builds, different gear combinations…nothing works. It just feels like pay-to-win at that point, you know? It's got some frustrating elements, yeah. The microtransactions are a bit heavy-handed, but the core gameplay is solid. You should try a different class entirely, maybe the Rune Knight? They're a bit slower to level, but they're incredibly durable. I don't know. I’ve already invested so much time into the Valkyrie. It feels like starting all over again. And besides, that's what  everyone  says to do. It won't feel the same. You're rather passionate about your…digital battles. It’s a bit like when I was younger, obsessed with sewing. Spent weeks on a quilt, then the fabric faded a bit, and all that effort felt wasted. You just have to let it go sometimes, love. But it's not the  fading ! It’s the unfairness of it all! It’s like… psychological warfare, almost. They  want  you to feel like you need to spend money to keep up. It’s manipulative. Actually, there's a lot of psychological research into game design and reward systems. They intentionally exploit dopamine pathways in the brain to keep people engaged, and encourage spending. It's not inherently malicious, just… clever. See? Even Jamie understands! It’s business, love. Keeps the game running. Though, I do agree, some of it is a bit much. Remember when Christmas was just about, well, Christmas? Now it’s adverts on telly in October! True. It's just…everything feels so stressful lately. Even things that are supposed to be fun. I'm supposed to be enjoying my holiday, not battling digital Valkyries and feeling manipulated by algorithms.

Right, so, iron ingots are definitely the bedrock of most things in Minecraft, aren't they? You two need a constant supply. But diamond? Diamond's the real treasure. Seriously, remember that time I finally found a diamond vein after hours of digging? I nearly screamed! Did it sparkle, Mummy? Like Ms. Davies’ sequins on the Christmas decorations? Oh, it  sparkled  alright, Poppy. More than anything you can imagine. Like little pieces of starlight. Unlike felt, though. Felt doesn't sparkle. It’s very… fuzzy. Sparkle! Like dragon scales! Leo found a dragon scale, Mummy! Did you now, Leo? A dragon scale? Where did you find  that  little beauty? In the Whispering Woods! The one with the grumpy trees. They told me. The grumpy trees  told  you? What did they say? They said… they said the dragons used to sleep under the roots and they shed their scales. But the gnomes steal them now. They use them to make tiny hats. Gnomes! Are they like the ones in the garden? The ones who eat the strawberries? Well, perhaps they’re distant cousins, Poppy. This is Leo's legend, isn't it? It’s getting quite elaborate! Honestly, you’re turning into a proper storyteller, sweetheart. Much better than me; I just tell boring facts about materials. Iron’s strong, copper’s reddish, gold's shiny… Gold is like my dancing shoes! All sparkly! Exactly! See? You're much better at this than I am. Though, speaking of materials, did you know there’s wool in Minecraft? It comes from sheep! Not quite dragon scales, but it makes nice blankets. Wool is for baby dragons! They get cold. The gnomes knit them little sweaters. Tiny, tiny sweaters. With dragon scale buttons. Oh, you’re incorrigible! Right, well, while we're on the topic of things to keep us healthy, are you both taking your vitamins today? Poppy, have you had your gummy vitamin C yet? Not yet. Can I have one after we finish talking about dragons and gnomes? Absolutely. Vitamin C keeps you strong, like iron! And Leo, you need your Vitamin D. Remember, it helps your bones grow, so you can climb trees to find more dragon scales. I need strong bones for climbing. So I can fight the gnome-hat makers! That’s my brave little knight. So, tell me more about the Whispering Woods. Are the grumpy trees always grumpy?

Honestly, Liam, you're moaning about practice again? It's only been a week since you got that new Strat. Give it a rest, eh? It's not just the Strat, Chloe! It's everything. My fingers are bleedin', I keep tuning it out of key, and I sound worse than that cat that yowls outside Nan's window at 3 am. It’s disheartening, you know? I thought I’d pick it up quicker. You always do this, though. You get all fired up about somethin' – remember that pottery phase? – and then you give up after a week because it’s hard work. You're a whirlwind of enthusiasm, you are. Pottery was different. Clay's messy, but it’s not... unforgiving. A guitar just mocks me. Plus, the neighbours are proper peeved with the noise. Had a right telling off from Mrs. Higgins yesterday. Said I was disturbin' her prize-winning petunias. Mrs. Higgins and her petunias! Right then. She’s always had a bee in her bonnet. Look, you're getting ahead of yourself. Everyone struggles when they start somethin' new. Remember when I first started Uni, I felt like I was completely out of my depth. That's different. You're dead clever. Always have been. I’m just… average. Don't be daft. You’re brilliant. You’ve got that dry Yorkshire wit, and you can remember lyrics to every Oasis song ever written! That’s a gift, Liam. Seriously. And you're getting better. I heard you playing that little riff the other day, the one from “Wonderwall”– it weren’t half bad. It was clunky. Really clunky. Speaking of things that are clunky and unsettling… did you see that article about the… you know… the ones who hurt kids? It's proper grim, innit? Oh, yeah. I saw it. It's awful. Makes you sick to the stomach. Why are there even people like that? Honestly, it’s… it’s beyond comprehension. It just… I don't know. They say it's all about power and control. Makes you want to lock every door and never let anyone in. Proper changes how you see the world, doesn’t it? Aye, it does. It’s just… scary. My little cousin, Millie, she's just started school. It makes you worry, doesn’t it? You know, about everything. You worry too much, Chloe. Millie’s got you and your mum.

Seriously, Mr. Davies is  still  on about the EPQ. Like, I get it, it’s supposed to be impressive for uni, but the constant nagging is… draining. I’m halfway through researching sustainable beekeeping, and it's fascinating, but sometimes I just want to throw the whole thing in the bin. Tell me about it. Mrs. Patel keeps giving me the side-eye because my film proposal isn’t “ambitious” enough. Apparently, documenting the history of Wembley Stadium fans isn’t sufficiently… groundbreaking. I mean, it’s  people , Liam! Real people who are passionate about something. You’re both moaning about your projects. Mine's even worse. I'm trying to write a comparative analysis of Victorian social reform and contemporary food bank usage. It's depressing. Like, brilliantly, academically depressing. Woah, that's heavy, Freya. At least bees are… buzzing and pollen-y. Yeah, yours sounds like a constant reminder of how messed up things are. Seriously though, the food bank thing… it’s crazy, isn’t it? How even in Slough, it’s a thing. It shouldn’t be. Remember when my nan used to tell us stories about when she was a kid, after the war? She said everyone helped each other. Sharing food, looking after neighbours… it feels like we’ve lost a bit of that. Exactly! It’s the whole system, isn't it? The inequality… It feels pointless sometimes, trying to analyse it in an EPQ when the actual problem is so much bigger. I was reading this article the other day about children who are eligible for free school meals but don't claim because of the stigma. That's awful. It makes you think, right? Like, what's the point of stressing about university applications if the world's going to be, you know… well, like that. Don’t go all existential on us, Liam. Although… I did see this documentary about a guy who quit his job to build schools in Nepal. Pretty inspiring, actually. Maybe I should just pack it all in and start a charity. You? Running a charity? You’d probably forget to pay the electricity bill. Hey! I’m resourceful. Besides, think of the Instagram content. #MakingADifference #WembleyCharityKid. Seriously? That’s your justification? Okay, okay, I’m joking. But it did make me think about what I actually  want  to do. Forget film, maybe I’ll become a humanitarian juggler.

Honestly, this electricity bill is  mad . Forty quid? Just for a week? How am I supposed to afford that, let alone everything else? My nan's gonna have a right go at me if I ask her for more. She’s already lent me a fortune. Tell me about it! Mine’s looking worse. I reckon Liam’s been using the hairdryer for three hours straight again. I swear, the man’s got a permanent frizz situation. I’ve left a passive-aggressive note on the microwave, you know? Just hinting. Passive-aggressive notes? Classic. Back home, my mum would just unplug everything without a word. Much more efficient. These noodles are a lifesaver, though. Uni food is… questionable. Reminds me of the school dinners, only slightly less grey. Did someone say noodles? Can I have some? I'm starving! Mr. Davies gave us a massive essay on Victorian poetry. It was brutal. Like, seriously, who even  likes  Victorian poetry? Easy, Finn. Share the wealth. And yes, Mr. Davies is a menace. Honestly, he’s got a face like a slapped flounder. But yeah, noodles are good. Better than this accommodation, that's for sure. This kitchen's the size of a postage stamp! And everything’s always sticky. Stickier than your last relationship, I reckon. Very funny, Liv. That ended for a reason, thank you very much. And this kitchen is just impractical! How are four of us supposed to cook in here without knocking each other over? Last week, I nearly took Finn out with a flying saucepan. I remember that! It was a close one. Speaking of family and chaos, my auntie just got married. To a man she met on a cruise. Apparently, he's a penguin enthusiast. A  penguin enthusiast ? Seriously? Like, he collects penguin figurines? More than that. He has a whole room dedicated to penguins. Photographs, models, documentaries running constantly. My grandma nearly fainted. Oh my god, that’s insane! You’ve got to show me the pictures. Is he, like, rich? Because if he's got a penguin room, he's gotta be rolling in it. Maybe he could pay for our electricity bills. If only! My mum keeps sending me pictures of the Cornish coastline. Says I need to “appreciate the simple things.” As if appreciating the simple things is going to pay my rent. My dad keeps going on about me joining the rugby club.

Honestly, Mum, I’m still reeling from little Leo’s nativity play. He was a shepherd, you know. Not one of the main ones, bless him. He had this permanently confused expression throughout, like he was actively questioning why he was herding cardboard sheep. Oh, Leo! That sounds perfectly like him. He’s always been a thinker, hasn’t he? Reminds me a bit of your Uncle Bryn, actually. Remember when Bryn tried to build that shed in the garden and it ended up looking like a leaning tower? He’d spend hours debating the structural integrity of a single plank of wood. Oh, don't remind me! The whole village was watching, convinced it was going to collapse and bury the rose bushes. Dad was quietly reinforcing everything in the dead of night. Leo’s the same. He'll question the logic of  everything . Yesterday, he asked me why Santa needs reindeer. "If he's got a sleigh, why doesn't he just use petrol, Mum? It would be much faster!" Children! They ask the questions we've forgotten to even consider. Petrol! Honestly. So, are you managing with the teaching? Still in Totnes? Yeah, Totnes is lovely. The kids are...challenging, as always, but mostly good. There’s a real mix - some brilliant little minds, some who are struggling a bit. I've got one boy, Sami, who just  lives  for dinosaurs. He can tell you the scientific name of anything prehistoric, but struggles to tie his shoelaces. It's wonderfully bizarre. And it’s rewarding, you know? Seeing them start to grasp something new, even if it’s just “the” versus “a”. It is rewarding, isn't it? Teaching. You’ve always had a knack for explaining things. I'm glad you found something you enjoy. It's a far cry from what you thought you’d be doing after sixthform, though, eh? Remember all those aspirations of being a journalist? I do. I think I was a bit naive. Living in Torquay then, journalism felt…distant. TEFL felt practical. And honestly, I love travelling. I'm thinking about maybe doing a stint in Spain next year, just for six months or so. Spain! That sounds wonderful! You’d love it. They take their food seriously there. And the weather! Think of all the sunshine. It would be a nice change for you. Are you thinking of taking Jamie?

It’s… it’s really changed, hasn’t it? Crayford. I barely recognise it. Used to be all little shops, remember? Now it's just… chain stores and new builds. Progress, eh? Though I do miss Mrs. Patel’s sweet shop. Best jaffa cakes this side of London. They built a Greggs on that corner. Doesn’t quite compare. Two years, you said? Feels like a lifetime since you were last down. It does. Uni took over, and then the job in… well, everywhere but here, really. I’m trying to get used to the idea of Brighton. It feels so… gentrified. Brighton's not bad. Bit pricey, mind you. Heard there's decent board game shops though? You still playing those? Remember that Scythe obsession you had? Oh God, don't remind me! Still got the board, actually. Still too complicated for you, though. You’d probably be building a little wooden house in a corner while I'm strategizing world domination. Speaking of complicated, did you see that speed camera they put on the A2? Ridiculous. They’re everywhere now, aren’t they? They’ll get you eventually. Speaking of getting caught, did you ever sort out that driving license situation? Renewed it yet? Almost. The online system is a nightmare. Honestly, filling out forms online is less stressful than trying to navigate the DVLA website. It kept asking me if I was a robot. Like  I’m  the one being unreasonable. Technology, eh? Never been a fan. How's the job going? Still teaching English? Yeah, it's good. Rewarding, most of the time. I’ve got a class of mostly Saudi students at the moment. Learning about their culture is fascinating, but it's exhausting trying to explain British sarcasm. They take everything literally! Sarcasm. The British superpower. You alright though? You seem a bit… quiet? Just a bit jet-lagged, I think. The trip to Tanzania with Mum was amazing, though. Absolutely breathtaking. The wildlife... incredible. But the flight back was a nightmare. Delayed for hours. Tanzania, eh? Sounds fantastic. Always wanted to go. Remember when your mum was trying to convince us all we should go on safari? Thought she’d never stop! You put on any weight? All that good food, I bet? A little, maybe. I’m trying to be good. Mum's already started on me about it. It’s always the same with her.

Honestly, the supermarket was a nightmare. Absolute carnage. Did you see they've put the reduced-to-clear avocados next to the organic ones? It's deliberate chaos, I swear. People were practically wrestling over bruised fruit. Wrestling over avocados? Sounds about right for a Saturday afternoon. I managed to avoid the fray. Spent the morning marking those dreadful essays on postmodernism. You wouldn’t believe the interpretations some of them came up with. One student claimed Kafka was secretly a performance artist. Oh, bless him. Performance art! That’s… ambitious. At least the avocados were edible, mostly. Got a few alright ones, hoping they'll ripen properly. Did you hear back from PR about the conference proposal? Actually, I did. Just got the email while I was simmering this Bolognese. They loved it. Apparently, the panel on "Music and Memory in the Digital Age" really resonated with them. They want me to present and even suggested I could invite one of the researchers from Goldsmiths to join me. Seriously? That’s fantastic! Goldsmiths! Who were you thinking of inviting? Professor Davies? She’d be brilliant. This could really put our department on the map. I was thinking of her, yeah. Or maybe Dr. Anya Sharma. She's doing fascinating work on the algorithmic curation of playlists and how that affects collective memory. It’s slightly different, but equally relevant. I need to check both of their availability, obviously. This is rather exciting, isn’t it? I’m almost regretting the avocado wrestling wars now. Don't talk yourself out of a victory. It is absolutely brilliant! We should celebrate. Maybe order in some Thai? Although, knowing my luck, they'll be out of Pad See Ew. Everything’s always out of something these days, isn’t it? We could try. Or I could attempt a Bolognese worthy of a Michelin star. Though, judging by my experience marking student essays, I suspect my cooking might be closer to performance art than fine dining. Oh, I'm sure it'll be lovely! As long as it doesn't have any unexpected avocado chunks. Speaking of which, I saw this amazing concert advert. Phoebe Bridgers is playing at the O2 in November. Phoebe Bridgers? Really? She's good. A bit melancholy for my usual taste, but I appreciate her talent. The O2 though… that's a beast of a venue. Is it any good for a gig?

Honestly, David, I’m starting to think this lentil stew is going to take over the entire kitchen. It’s producing a frankly alarming amount of steam. Are you sure we didn’t accidentally double the recipe? Relax, love. It's a good, hearty stew. Needs to be substantial, especially with how chilly it's been. And no, I didn’t double it. Though, now you mention it, it  does  smell particularly fragrant tonight. Maybe I’m just more hungry than I realised. What about you? Still wrestling with that beanbag cover? Wrestling is the perfect word. The ribbing is a nightmare! I’ve gone through three balls of that chunky cream yarn already, and it still looks… wonky. I swear a straight line is the enemy of my needles. It's supposed to be a cosy, relaxed, boho vibe, but it’s currently radiating intense frustration. Boho is rarely achieved through perfect tension, you know. Embrace the imperfection! Think… rustic charm. Besides, it’s for Anon's reading corner. They’ll appreciate the effort more than the flawless execution. Easy for you to say. You’re dealing with carrots. Carrots don’t judge your knitting. Although, they  do  seem to multiply when you're chopping them. Seriously, where do all these carrots come from? The farmer’s market! Remember? You insisted we buy a huge bag. Said it was important to support local businesses. Right. Well, I’m regretting that wisdom now. At least we'll have carrot cake for days. Speaking of regret… I’ve been thinking about the bathroom. Oh? More renovations on your mind? You're a whirlwind of DIY projects, you know that? It’s just… that shower curtain. It's driving me mad. That seafoam green? It clashes with everything. With the tiles, with the towels, even with the bath mats! It ages the whole room ten years instantly. It's… not awful. A bit dated, perhaps. But not awful. "Not awful" is a very low bar, David. I saw this gorgeous botanical print one online – ferns and wildflowers, muted colours. It would look  stunning . And it would tie in with the little succulent shelf I put up last month. Botanical, eh? So, moving away from the nautical theme? Definitely moving away from the nautical theme! I feel like we’re living in a slightly depressing seaside gift shop. It needs a lift. Something…sophisticated.

Cor blimey, Doris, this rain’s a right misery, innit? Seems like it’s been chuckin’ it down for a week solid. Makes a man feel right damp in the bones, it does. Oh, Arthur, don’t start. A bit of rain never hurt anyone. At least the garden’s having a good drink. And it’s not chucking  that  hard, you’re exaggerating as usual. Do have a biscuit, dear. Digestives, your favourite. Exaggerating? I’ll ‘ave you know I can tell a proper downpour from a drizzle after all these years. And me bones ain't gettin’ any younger, remember? You coddle me, you do. Proper coddlin’. Dreadful deluge out there, wouldn’t you say? Nearly lost my hat on the way up the drive. Hope the gutters are coping. Michael! You’re late, darling. We were just debating the intensity of the rainfall. Arthur, of course, thinks it’s the end of the world. I said it's a misery, Doris, not the end of the world. There’s a difference. And don't you start on me, you know I like a bit of drama. Keeps things lively. Fancy having some tea, Michael? Doris makes a lovely cuppa. Thank you, Arthur. That would be lovely. A rather dry sherry would be even better, though, if I’m honest. The drive was more treacherous than I’d anticipated. Just spent a fortune getting those rhododendrons pruned. Those chaps from ‘Green Thumb’ charged an arm and a leg. Said they were “structural maintenance” – structural maintenance on rhododendrons! Honestly… Oh, Michael, you and your rhododendrons. They’re your pride and joy, aren’t they? You treat them better than you treat me sometimes. Don’t be absurd, darling. You know that’s not true. But they are rather magnificent, if I may say so myself. The bloom this year’s been exceptional. You should have seen the ‘Lady Clementine’ – simply breathtaking. Actually, I was thinking about perhaps extending the patio a bit. More space for the furniture... Patio? More like a moat at this rate, with all this rain. You’ll be needin’ a boat to get to the back door soon. An’ spendin’ even more money, I reckon. Rhododendrons and patios...a man could bankrupt himself keepin' up appearances. Arthur! Don’t be like that. Michael works hard, he deserves to enjoy his garden. And it looks lovely. Besides, a bigger patio would be nice for us too.

Honestly, this is exactly what I needed. Feet up, cup of tea, and no beeping machines for once. Feels like ages since I’ve had a proper relax. Tell me about it. That budget meeting this morning… pure agony. Apparently, we need to find another three percent savings. Where are we supposed to magic that up from, eh? Three percent? That’s brutal! Sounds like my freelance life is looking pretty good right now, less stress, more control. These ginger biscuits are fresh out of the oven, anyone? Ooh, lovely! Ginger's always a winner. Three percent, you say, David? You know, the training course for the nurse practitioner thing is getting expensive. They want me to volunteer extra shifts, which is, you know,  fantastic  experience, but time is money, innit? Exactly, Janice. It’s relentless. Work, work, work. Speaking of relentless, did you manage to get those Christmas lights up in the garden, David? The neighbours are already starting to put theirs up. Not yet, love. Been a bit preoccupied with the budget apocalypse. I was thinking about getting those ones with the reindeer and the snowman. Fancy? Reindeer and snowman are classic, Dad. But maybe a bit… predictable? I saw some fairy lights that change colour – really atmospheric. Could even sync them to music! Oh, don't start, Chloe. My electric bill will be through the roof if you start syncing fairy lights to pop music! Remember last year? The squirrels were completely mesmerised by the flashing disco ball. Nearly took out the bird feeder. Oh, Janice, you and your squirrels! You know, it reminded me of when I was a little girl. My grandad used to put a single string of fairy lights on the holly bush. Just a simple glow. It felt so magical. It’s the simplicity, isn't it? Sometimes, less is more. Although, I did see this amazing Christmas market in Vienna on Instagram… all those little wooden stalls, the mulled wine… Vienna, eh? Now, that’s an idea. We haven’t been anywhere decent for ages. Remember that trip to Southport when we were kids, Chloe? Your mum nearly lost you in the arcades. Oh my god, don't remind me! I was obsessed with the claw machine. Wanted that ridiculously oversized teddy bear. Mum was livid. It's funny how the things you worry about at the time… You’re always reminiscing about your childhood, David!

This is lovely, isn’t it? Such a peaceful Sunday morning. I’m still getting used to the… quiet, I suppose. Dorchester can be bustling, especially on a market day, but this is something else entirely. Aye, it is that. Quiet is certainly a word for it. Took some getting used to myself, after all these years in Watford. Noise, bustle… always something going on. Though I wasn’t always contributing to it, mind. More often observing, really. Observing, yes. I can imagine. So, you’ve been here… how long now, is it? Since February, wasn't it? That’s right. Came in February. Still feels a bit surreal, to be honest. Leaving Blighty… seems like a lifetime ago and yesterday all at once. My wife, bless her, she wanted this. Always talked about the sunshine. Funny, isn’t it? Dreams we have, and then… we just do them. It is. I'm finding that out myself. I kept putting off learning Turkish, thinking “I'll do it when I retire.” Now I’m here, surrounded by it, and it’s far more daunting than I imagined. I’ve managed a few pleasantries, of course – ‘Günaydın’ and ‘Teşekkür ederim’ go a long way. But beyond that… Aye, Turkish. A tricky one, that. Try learning the case endings. It'll bend your brain inside out. I've been giving it a go myself. Had a go, anyway. My wife’s much better. Sarah is. She’s got a real aptitude for languages, you see. Always has. Oh, really? That’s wonderful! I'm more of a history woman, myself. Brings me a lot of comfort, actually, knowing all that came before. Gives things a perspective, doesn't it? I was reading about the Venetian influence here the other day – fascinating. Did you know they controlled this area for quite some time? Aye, I do. Saw some of the remnants of the fortifications further down the coast. Remarkable, really. Considering the state of things back home... We're all so obsessed with the new, aren't we? We forget to respect what’s been here, quietly weathering the storms for centuries. Absolutely. It's something I try to instil in my students. Celebrating the past, understanding how it shapes the present. Although, persuading teenagers to care about Roman pottery is… a challenge. . Have you managed to explore much of the island? I'm hoping to get out and about more, once I’ve settled in properly.

Honestly, I feel like I've swallowed a brick. This air… it's just relentless, isn't it? Worse than yesterday, I think. Definitely. The visibility's dreadful. I could barely see the office building from the taxi. I checked the AQI – it’s off the charts today. Didn't expect it to be this bad so soon after the last rain. Rain seems to make absolutely no difference anymore. Remember when we first moved here, and everyone kept saying, "Oh, a bit of rain and it'll all clear up?" It’s become a cruel joke. Did you manage to get through to Mark about the conference proposal? Yeah, I did. He's still hesitant about sending it to Professor Chen. Apparently, Chen's been rather dismissive of anything that deviates from traditional Marxist interpretations lately. Typical. He’s stuck in his ways. Well, that’s just brilliant, isn’t it? We're trying to push for a more nuanced, contemporary approach, and he wants to stick to dogma. Honestly, sometimes I wonder if academia anywhere in the world is the same frustrating battle. It’s the same principles, I think. Just different battles. Remember arguing with Professor Davies about post-structuralism for three hours straight in Norwich? That felt like forever. Oh, God, yes! He genuinely believed Derrida was a fad. "A passing fancy," he called it. Can you imagine? Still, at least the air was clean back then. I miss… well, I miss proper blue skies. And not having to constantly worry about air purifiers. Me too. It's affecting Lily, I’m noticing. She’s been coughing a lot more in the evenings. We need to look into getting a better filtration system for the apartment, don’t we? The one we have is just… inadequate. Absolutely. And maybe we should think about investing in those face masks with the little fans. The ones that actually cycle the air. They look ridiculous, but if they help… it’s worth it. I saw some at the pharmacy the other day. Good thinking. I'll look into it. I also heard some of the other lecturers are talking about petitioning the university to allocate more resources to air quality research – specifically, indigenous plant species that might have some capacity to absorb pollutants. That's excellent! Anything proactive is good. I'll lend my support to that. Though, frankly, I’m starting to feel a bit hopeless.

Right, nearly got all this carrot done. Honestly, you’d think I was preparing for an army, not just a Tuesday night supper. Where's Liam been hiding? Did he manage to get that bit of coding sorted? He’s been battling with it, apparently. Something to do with the user interface. He says it’s a right fiddle. Just popped out to the shed to grab some tools. Needed a tiny screwdriver, he muttered. Dramatic, isn’t he? Did you manage to look at those photos I sent over from Southport? The ones from Gran’s garden? Nearly! Just finished up a freelance brief. It was a nightmare – client kept changing their mind about the colour palette. Ugh. Oh! Photos, yeah. They're lovely! Gran’s roses are looking absolutely gorgeous. Reminds me of being little and sneaking a petal or two when she wasn’t looking. Remember, Mum? Of course I do, love. She’d chase you around the garden with a watering can! Such a character, your Gran. Southport looks lovely too. Different from Kent, though. Much… flatter. Is that the right word? Flatter, yes. Certainly less rolling hills! It’s got a charm of its own, though. All those Victorian buildings. And the beach, of course. Though the sand's a bit gritty, if I’m honest. Not like Broadstairs, is it? Speaking of which, what are we having with this stew? I was thinking crusty bread to mop up all those lovely juices. Ooh, crusty bread sounds perfect! And maybe some mashed potatoes? I’m starving. That brief really took it out of me. Should have had something earlier, but I was so caught up in trying to appease the client. What about a side salad, Mum? Something with a lemon vinaigrette? Salad's a good shout. Adds a bit of freshness. I’ll throw one together while you two are deciding on potatoes. I’m thinking the jacket ones, yeah? Nice and fluffy. Are you watching that new detective show on ITV? "Shadows of the Past"? No, haven't got round to it yet. Too much telly these days, isn't there? Seems like every channel has a detective show. Liam's been glued to "Galactic Sentinels," though. It’s… not my cup of tea, to be honest. All lasers and spaceships. You haven't seen "Galactic Sentinels"?! Dad, seriously! It's incredible. The special effects are mind-blowing.

Right, so this new bus route… honestly, it’s a right mess, innit? They’ve rerouted the 7 through the science park, which means it takes an age to get anywhere near the city centre now. Used to be a quick hop, skip and a jump to the market square, and now? Forty minutes. Forty minutes! I’m proper knackered after work already. Yeah, I saw something about that. Trying to understand the logic, really. It seems… counterintuitive. The intention was to serve the science park better, wasn't it? Supposedly. But they’ve missed the point entirely, haven’t they? Loads of us who live out there, who rely on the bus to get into town, are stuck. And the people in the science park? They’ve probably got cars. Typical, really. You’re probably right. It's a classic case of not truly understanding the needs of the users. Did you manage to get to the Cambridge University Press bookshop last week? No, I didn’t. Was trying to, actually. Got delayed with work. But I’ve been meaning to. They’ve apparently got a proper good collection of North East history books now, have they? My grandma would be chuffed to bits. I promised to have a look. They do. Saw a few that looked particularly interesting. They’ve really expanded the regional literature section. It's much nicer than it used to be, less…stuffy. Good to hear. Cambridge University Press used to feel like stepping into a museum, didn't it? All dusty leather-bound things and hushed tones. Definitely. Much more welcoming now. Did you hear about the protest yesterday? The one outside the Sidgwick Site? Aye, saw bits and pieces on social media. Something about tuition fees, was it? Sounded a bit chaotic, to be fair. That's right. A few students chained themselves to the entrance of the economics faculty. Apparently, they're demanding a review of the university's investment in fossil fuels. It got a bit… lively. Lively? Sounds like a proper kerfuffle. Reminds me of the demos back home when the mines closed, that did. A lot of shouting and passion, but did it actually change anything? That's the big question, isn't it? I mean, I admire their commitment, their willingness to stand up for what they believe in. But I also worry about whether it's the most effective way to achieve their goals.

That lemon drizzle cake, honestly. Divine. Reminds me of Mrs. O’Malley’s bakery back in Dublin, though hers was always a bit…chewier. This was just perfect. Light, fluffy, a tang of lemon... It's funny the things that trigger memory, isn’t it? Absolutely! Food is the ultimate time machine. I was just remembering my nan used to make these awful sticky toffee puddings, but they were the best thing in the world because she made them. Are the kids driving you mad this weekend, Mum? Thomas was supposed to call yesterday, haven't heard a peep. They’re alright, dear. Liam’s trying to build some sort of elaborate Lego city – it’s taking over the entire living room. And Saoirse is… well, Saoirse is being Saoirse. Currently convinced she's a woodland nymph and demanding I weave her a crown from the rhododendrons. Thankfully, the garden is a bit too prickly for her to actually  live  out there. Oh, Saoirse! Classic. Reminds me of my little Leo. He's decided he’s an astronaut now. Keeps trying to launch himself off the sofa with a pillowcase. It’s exhausting, but also kind of wonderful, isn't it? The sheer, boundless imagination. I had a tricky call with a new client this morning, about restructuring, but that helped reset me. It did. How’s your arthritis behaving, Mary? You mentioned it was a bit sore the other week. It’s… manageable. These damp conditions don’t help, though. Cumbria is beautiful, of course, but the weather can be unforgiving. I do miss the sun more than I thought I would. England is grey, even compared to Dublin sometimes. And I’m finding myself missing simple things, you know? A proper pint of Guinness, a chat with Mrs. Doherty… things you take for granted.
