You need to come down to London soon, Mum. We’ll drag you to a decent Irish pub. Honestly, I’m worried about you being so isolated up here. You’re not feeling down, are you? You always were a bit of a worrier. I remember when I was little and you'd practically have a panic attack before every maths test! Don’t remind me. Numbers were always my nemesis, ironically. Teaching them was easier than understanding them myself. And I  am  lonely, a little. Retirement… it wasn’t quite what I envisioned. I thought I’d be filled with hobbies and a sense of purpose, but mostly I just… exist.

Brr, it’s colder than I thought it would be. You’d think being this close to the water, it’d be more… humid, at least. That’s London for you, love. Damp and delightful, all in one. Right, nearly to the Millennium Dome, are we? Always seems bigger from this side of the river. It does, doesn’t it? They did a good job with it. Remember when it first opened? All that controversy about it looking like a giant inflatable blob. I do! The press were having a field day. Now it’s just a landmark. A rather large, shiny landmark. It's funny how quickly things become normalised, isn't it? Like, we wouldn't bat an eyelid at it now. Exactly. Speaking of landmarks, have you ever thought about how many historical things are clustered around here? Woolwich Arsenal, the Royal Naval College… just down the way is the Cutty Sark. Incredible. Sometimes I feel like I should be narrating a walking tour, just spouting facts. You probably would be a brilliant one! Though I imagine you’d be far too busy questioning the accuracy of every plaque. Well, one has to, doesn’t one? It's my job to be accurate after all. Transcribing historical documents - you see some unbelievable things. Nowadays, you have to check and double-check everything. Speaking of things that are unbelievable... Still can't believe we haven't bought a car. Don’t start. We’ve been over this. It’s simply not practical, with my work and your commute. Besides, it’s better for the environment. And frankly, the cost of parking in this city is obscene. I know, I know. But imagine, just for a second, being able to just  hop  in the car and drive out to the countryside. A spontaneous weekend away… We can manage a spontaneous weekend away on the train. We did go to Brighton last month, remember? True, but trains don’t exactly convey the same freedom as a motorcar do. Where have you been thinking about for our holiday this summer? I was thinking Cornwall, maybe? The kids would love it. Cornwall would be lovely. The beaches are gorgeous. I was looking at a place in Devon actually. Little cottage, near the coast. But the kids want somewhere with a pool. Of course they do. Always something. You know, they keep talking about these American recipes… "a cup of flour," they say.

Honestly, Mum, it’s absolutely chucking it down. Sports day's going to be a washout, innit? Little Leo’s been practicing his egg-and-spoon race for weeks. Poor kid's gonna be gutted. Well, that's England for you, love. Always promising sunshine and delivering drizzle. Remember that summer in '86? Never saw the sun. Leo'll be alright, he’s a tough little one. Did he remember his teddy today? The little blue bear? Yeah, he's got Bluey. He won't leave the house without him. It's ridiculous, really. He's nearly five! I keep trying to persuade him to leave it behind, you know? Like, he's not a baby anymore. Leave him be, Chloe. They cling to those things. Remember when you wouldn’t go anywhere without Barnaby the badger? Barnaby was different! He was a proper adventure badger. Bluey just sits there. And honestly, the amount of fluff! It's everywhere! I swear, it reproduces. I found a tuft stuck to the ceiling fan the other day. Oh, kids and their cuddly toys. It's a phase. You’ll be throwing those Build-a-Bear workshops into the past before you know it. Remember when you wanted one of everything from there? You nearly bankrupted your dad! Oh god, don't remind me! I was obsessed. I wanted a unicorn, a dinosaur, a penguin...each with a different voice box and a sparkly outfit. Dad was working overtime for months to pay for it all. You loved all those sparkly outfits. You used to dress up your dolls in them. Remember Millie's face when you ‘borrowed’ her Barbie's clothes? Don't go there! She cried for a week! I was terrible. But it was just...shiny! Anyway, it’s not just Bluey. It’s the entire toddler phase. Daniel’s still in nappies, you know. Potty training is an absolute nightmare. He just sits there and laughs at me. Oh, they’re clever little devils, aren't they? Don't give up. Positive reinforcement works wonders. Stickers, little charts... I've tried  everything . Stickers, charts, books, songs...He openly sabotages my efforts. Last week, he flushed all his cars down the toilet! Oh, Daniel! He's a little rascal. At least he’s entertained himself. Speaking of which, have you seen my phone charger? It’s gone missing again. Probably swallowed by the sofa.

Right, so, let’s actually  talk  about this, shall we? Beyond just "lovely house, lovely weather." I've been mulling over a few things, spurred on by this… space, I guess. It’s funny how a change of scenery can do that. Mmm, it definitely has a clarifying effect. Dorchester felt a bit… clogged, you know? Too much layered history and ingrained routine. What’s been on your mind, then? Business, I assume? You’ve got that furrow in your brow that means spreadsheets are involved. It’s partly the business, yeah, the tech start-up. I’m thinking about scaling up, properly. Taking on some significant investment. But it’s also… more than that. It’s about  what  I want to be doing in five years. Am I happy just building another successful company? Or do I want to use the platform for something else? Something… meaningfully impactful, you know? Impactful… that's a big word. Sounds like you’ve been having conversations with that life coach you mentioned. You’re right. She’s persuasive. She’s prompted me to think about aligning my values with my work. Trying to use technology to solve a genuine problem, rather than just create another flashy app. There’s a project I've been circling around – leveraging AI for sustainable agriculture practices in developing countries. It’s complex, but… compelling. That  is  compelling, actually. Sounds a rather far cry from your initial idea for a social media aggregator. But it suits you, I think. You’ve always had that… a restlessness to do good, even if you cloak it in entrepreneurial ambition. How about you, professionally? Still enjoying the Year 9 drama? They're a fascinating bunch this year. A lot of untapped potential, a real spark. I was thinking of doing a short course in restorative justice. The behaviors I'm seeing… it’s more than just teenage rebellion. It’s often a response to something deeper. I’ve started a personal reading list, but I want some formal training. It could overhaul how I work with them. That sounds brilliant, love. Very you. You always were the empathetic one. It’s good you’re prioritising your own development, too. We both need to keep learning, don't we? Otherwise, what's the point? Precisely. Speaking of deep topics… have you given any more thought to… well, to the whole ‘family expansion’ thing?

Honestly, I was listening to this podcast the other day, about regional accents, and they were going on about how Yorkshire accents are dying out. Dying out! Like, how can you lose an accent? It's part of you, innit? They say everything’s dying out these days, don’t they? Even Pokémon Go. Remember when that was all anyone talked about? My little cousin used to run around the garden like a mad thing, trying to catch 'em all. Oh my god, I do! I got completely sucked in for a good week. I nearly tripped over the cat trying to catch a Pikachu in the living room. Mum was fuming. Pikachu, eh? We were mostly finding Weedles in Leeds. Proper little creepers, them. And yeah, about accents... my gran, she'll correct your grammar if you say 'seen' instead of 'saw’. Like a linguistic sergeant major. It’s comforting though, you know? Reminds me of home. Comforting? Sounds stressful! My nan used to just give you a look that could wither a rose if you didn't say please and thank you properly. Proper ingrained manners. It was a trial growing up. Tell me about it. My dad’s the same. Still gives me grief if I don't say "good afternoon" to Mrs. Higgins next door. Even when I'm rushing to work! Speaking of rushing, Jamie needs a fag, doesn't he? He's having a right grumble. Yeah, he’s practically vibrating. Honestly, he’s worse than a toddler denied a sweet. Should’ve grabbed one before we came. I’ll pop to the shop for him. Anyone else need anything? I’m going anyway. Could I get a packet of After-Eights? Please? Always a proper treat. Ooh, good shout! I’ll have one too. Reminds me of Christmas at my Auntie Brenda's. We'd always have a massive tin of them. Do you remember that year she ended up arguing with Uncle Barry about whether they were best eaten pointy side up or down? Vaguely! Was that, like, 2015? Near when we went to that disastrous camping trip? Remember that, lads? Torrential rain, soggy tents... Don’t even. Absolutely horrendous. Felt like a real-life fight-or-flight situation. I spent the entire time huddled under a tarp, convinced a badger was going to steal my sleeping bag. Badgers are sneaky. I saw one once, rootling around in a bin in Leeds.

Cor blimey, that was a bit of a match, weren’t it? Norwich put up a good fight, mind you. Though I still reckon that penalty was a bit dodgy. Ref wasn't watching, proper blind as a bat, he was. Oh, come on, Arthur. You always say that about penalties! You’ve been saying it since the seventies. It’s a reflex now, isn’t it? Though, I do agree, it was a close call. Still, a lovely evening, really. ANON did a smashing job with the roast. It really was delicious, ANON. The Yorkshire puddings were perfect – light and fluffy. Dad, you cleared your plate faster than anyone! Well, a fella’s gotta eat, hasn't he? And that gravy...that's proper gravy. Not that watery stuff you get in some places. ANON, you’ve got a gift, you do. A right gift. He says that about every roast, love. It's his standard compliment. I know, I know. It’s endearing, in a predictable sort of way. So, speaking of parties... ANON mentioned wanting to plan something for her birthday. Any thoughts? Oh, a garden party! That would be lovely. In June, hopefully, when the weather's a bit more reliable. We could have some bunting, and maybe a little BBQ. Nothing too fancy, mind. Remember that disastrous barbecue we had at Barbara’s? The sausages caught fire! Don’t remind me! Smelled of burnt rubber for a week. We should stick to sandwiches. And a nice cup of tea. Simple and sweet. Well, we could do a bit of both. Maybe a BBQ for the men, and a lovely tea for the ladies? That's a clever compromise! But who’s going to organise it all? It's a lot of work. ANON will want to be involved, of course. But we can all help. I can do the bunting. Arthur can be in charge of… of keeping everyone entertained! I’ll have you know I can tell a cracking joke! Though some of them are a bit… well, they’re not for young ears. We'll keep the young ears out of it then. So, bunting, BBQ, sandwiches, jokes... It’s shaping up nicely. What about music? Music is vital. Something upbeat, but not  too  loud. And definitely no death metal! What about that Vera Lynn CD I found last year? A bit of a trip down memory lane.

Right then. So, you’re  seriously  thinking about it? Dropping out, I mean. It’s a massive thing, innit? Seriously. Yeah. I've been thinking about it for weeks, honestly. It just…doesn’t feel right, does it? All this. Lectures, essays, the whole shebang. It’s just not  me . I feel like I’m trying to squeeze myself into a mould that isn’t shaped properly. I 'ear ya. Proper, I do. But you’ve only been here a term, love. Give it a proper go, yeah? It takes time to settle, find your feet, figure out which lectures even make sense. Remember when I tried surfing? Spent like, three weeks looking like a beached whale before I even stood up once? Yeah, and you nearly drowned twice. That's a lovely image to conjure up when contemplating academic failure. It’s not just that, though. It's…the subject. I thought Sociology would be fascinating, you know? Understanding the way society works, the power dynamics… but it's just so much theory. And honestly, the readings are drier than the Sahara. Blimey. That  is  rough. I remember Year 11 English. Chaucer? Honestly! Sounded like a cat choking on a hairball the whole time. But did I drop out of school? Nah. I stuck it out, didn’t I. My mum would’ve had my guts for garters if I had. My mum would be gutted, yeah. But she also says, 'A happy daughter is better than a degree.' Which, considering her, is a pretty radical statement. Though my dad... He’s the one who pushed me to apply in the first place. Says it’s 'vital for opportunities'. Oh, the 'vital for opportunities' speech. I recognise that. Mine used to use it about getting a sensible haircut. Still does, come to that. Anyway... speaking of opportunities, what  would  you do if you did leave? I don’t know. That's the terrifying bit, isn’t it? Probably go back to Liverpool, get a job in a cafe or something. Maybe try and save up some money, figure out what I actually  want  to do. It’s just… the pressure. From everyone. Pressure’s a right bugger, innit? My nan used to say, “Pressure makes diamonds, love.” Though she also used to say, “Never trust a man wearing brown shoes," so take that with a pinch of Cornish sea salt. Right. Noted.

Honestly, it’s so lovely to finally be here! Oxford restaurants are always a bit…fancy, aren't they? Feels like ages since we properly caught up. This place looks nice, though. What are you thinking? I’m leaning towards the sea bass – it smells amazing. Fancy is an understatement! My mum would faint at the prices. But yeah, it’s good to be here too. Life’s been a bit chaotic, as usual. Sea bass sounds good. I’m always a sucker for anything with lemon. So, spill! Project coordinating, eh? Sounds terribly important. What are you working on at the moment? Not another supplier drama, I hope? Oh, you know me too well. There's  always  a supplier drama. Right now, it’s about getting the new signage approved for the London office. They want, and I quote, “a vibe.” A vibe! I swear, the marketing team are a different species. Honestly, you'd think they’d understand deadlines. What about you? Pearson marketing, that sounds glamorous! Is it all champagne and social media campaigns? Ha! If only. There’s a  lot  of spreadsheets and internal meetings. I’m heading up a campaign for one of their online learning platforms. Trying to convince students that studying through a screen isn't the worst thing in the world. It’s… challenging. And the office is… beige. Very, very beige. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I’m in a particularly depressing accountant’s office. Beige. The colour of despair. Right, I need something vibrant to counteract that image. Okay, sea bass it is. So, aside from corporate battles, what's been happening? Heard anything from Liam? Still seeing him? Liam… It’s complicated. We broke up, actually. A few months ago. It wasn't dramatic or anything. Just… drifted. We wanted different things, I suppose. He’s really focused on his music, which is brilliant for him, but… travelling around in a van playing gigs to ten people wasn’t exactly fitting into my five-year plan of… well, not quite sure what the plan  is , if I’m honest. What about you and Tom? Still going strong? You guys have been together forever. Nearly four years, can you believe it? And yes, thankfully, we’re still going strong. He’s finally got that promotion he was after at the firm, so things are pretty good. We were talking about potentially looking at a place together – maybe something outside of the city.

Right then, Liam, are you finished haggling over that… thing? What  is  it, anyway? Looks like something out of a science museum. It’s a vintage oscilloscope, Gran. For my electronics project. It's a proper one, not one of those digital simulators they use in school. I can actually see the waveforms. An oscilloscope? Aye, well, I remember my dad fiddling with one of those. Back when TVs didn’t just appear in a box, ready to go. Nowt like learning a thing properly, mind. You gettin’ a good price on it, lad? Don't be getting fleeced. Those Ebay sellers, some of 'em are proper sharks. I think so. The seller’s in Sheffield, says it's been tested and works perfectly. He's knocked £20 off his asking price already. Going to try and get another ten off. Sheffield, ey? Good lads in Sheffield, generally. But keep your wits about ya. Read the feedback, Liam. Always read the feedback. That’s what I tell ya. Never trust a picture alone. Read the small print, too. Returns policies, shipping costs… it’s a minefield, internet shopping is. I have. He’s got 99.8% positive feedback and a load of glowing reviews. Says he’s an electronics enthusiast himself. 99.8%? That’s pretty good, I’ll grant ya that. Still, that 0.2%… that’s where the heartbreak lies, isn’t it? Remember that sewing machine I bought off Amazon last year? Promised to be a Singer, top of the range. Ended up being some cheap Chinese knock-off. Nearly gave me palpitations. Had to argue with ‘em for three weeks to get my money back. Yeah, I remember. You were fuming. You nearly wrote a strongly worded letter to the Prime Minister. I were close, weren't I? Honestly, Liam, sometimes I think it’s easier to pop down to the market in Driffield. You can see what you’re buying, you can shake the seller’s hand, look ‘em in the eye. You know if they’re leading you on or not. Online, you’re just dealing with a profile, a blurb. It feels… impersonal. But you can find things you just can't get in Driffield, Gran. This oscilloscope is really rare. And it’s cheaper than buying one new. Plus, I looked at the same model on Amazon. It was almost double the price. Aye, that’s true.

This coffee’s a bit weak, isn’t it, love? Not like that stuff Doreen used to make. She knew how to brew a proper cup. Strong enough to stand a spoon up in, that was Doreen’s coffee. It’s just instant, Dad. Easier than getting the cafetiere out. You know you don’t need it that strong. Besides, you had a biscuit. Biscuits don’t count, love. They’re just… fillers. Doreen always said, "A biscuit is for between the proper things, Arthur, not  instead  of them." Wise woman, Doreen. Used to run a flower shop down in Brixton. Knew all the best deals, she did. Remember that time she got a whole load of lilies donated for the church fete? Saved us a fortune. I do remember. You were thrilled. Always loved lilies, didn't you? You used to say they reminded you of… what was it? Something about Victorian funerals? Something like that. Always seemed a bit grand, funerals. Though, I suppose everything is, when you’re looking in from the outside, isn't it? Never been much good at… big things, I've always felt. Dad, don’t start. We're here to have a nice, relaxed day. You’re doing brilliantly, by the way. Cambridge is lovely. You seem to be enjoying the gardens. They are, aren't they? Right pleasant. Better than Modern, that’s for sure. Always loved green spaces, I have. Used to sneak off to Tooting Common when I were a lad. Just to sit and watch the people. People watching… that was my hobby, really. Still is, I suppose. You're good at it. You notice everything. I bet you could write a whole story about any group of people you see. Wouldn’t know where to start. Never been one for writing. Always just… observed. Like a… like a distant star, watching from afar. You’re being ridiculous. You've got a memory like a steel trap. Remember all the football scores from the '70s! Ah, the '70s! Now you're talking! Arsenal were on fire then, weren't they? Liam Brady, that was a player. Remember that goal he scored against Tottenham in the FA cup? Blew the roof off Highbury, it did. Of course, you do. You’ve told me that story at least a dozen times. Though, I'm not sure it's entirely accurate… didn’t he slip on the pitch?

Right, so Christmas Day. Proper mad, innit? Flying out on Christmas Day… you sure about that, Liv? It feels so… wrong. Like actively ruining the whole vibe. Ruining it? Don't be daft, Finn. It's brilliant! Think of it, sunshine, minimal family arguing, and I’ll be drinking something other than lukewarm mulled wine. Besides, Mum and Dad are coming to mine on Boxing Day, so they’re sorted. It’s just me and my partner really who are off. Boxing Day? Honestly, that's the  real  Christmas stress. The sales, the crowds… I'm dreading it. At least you're escaping all of that. Me, I’m stuck here, brewing endless flat whites and dealing with caffeine-deprived hordes. Hordes is right! You're a legend, Chloe. I’d lose my mind. Flying on Christmas Day though… Bold move. Bit surreal, isn't it? Like something out of a movie. It is mental. Think about it, you're hurtling through the sky while everyone else is sitting around the fire. Speaking of fire, what are we having for Christmas dinner this year? Mum's still doing the roast turkey, yeah? It's practically a family tradition at this point. Definitely turkey. And all the trimmings – sprouts, roast potatoes, stuffing… the works. Although, I'm thinking of making a proper Yorkshire pudding this year. Mum’s always been a bit rubbish at them. All soggy on the bottom. Oh, Yorkshire puddings? Now you’re talking proper Christmas. I might need to pop over for seconds after I’ve finished serving up my Boxing Day hangover cures. Yorkshire puddings are crucial. Can’t have Christmas without them. I’m just craving some good old-fashioned pavlova. It’s been ages since I had a decent one. Everything here’s a bit… muted compared to back home. Pavlova, eh? That’s a bit fancy for Christmas, isn't it? Though, I can see the appeal. We saw a deer on the way back from the shops earlier, completely flattened. Proper sad, innit? Must have been hit by a car. Oh God, Finn, don't! That’s awful. Poor thing. It’s been mental how many foxes we've been seeing around lately too, though. Bold as brass, waltzing through the garden like they own the place. They do own the place, Liv! They’re urban royalty. I’ve got a couple that regularly sneak into the café courtyard when I'm closed.

Right, this is nice. Actually relaxing for once. London was a madhouse yesterday. Glad we're getting out of it. Tell me about it. Editing late into the night, dealing with a particularly grumpy sub-editor… I needed this Cambridge escape. Thanks for offering the lift, Anon. Seriously. My bus journey would have been a nightmare. Aye, no worries at all. Saves me a fortune on petrol too, honestly. Wouldn’t have wanted to face that A11 in my little hatchback. It’d have been swallowed whole. Swallowed whole’s right. This thing’s a tank, innit? Your dad’s car's got some serious presence. Never thought a Volvo would look… well,  cool . Cool is a strong word, Anon. It’s... practical. And spacious. I’m just glad it's got heated seats. October in Cambridge can get chilly, you know. So, about this drive… you reckon we can swap playlists at some point? My choice of indie bops is probably going to be grating on you both by the time we’re halfway. Indie bops? Don’t worry, I’m immune. I’ve been listening to nothing but 8-bit soundtracks for the past six months developing 'Galaxy Gladiators'. My ears are pretty desensitised at this point. Though, a bit of something different wouldn't hurt, I suppose. I've got a few classic rock albums I could inflict. Nothing  too  heavy, promise. Though, I did find a really obscure German techno track the other day… Don’t say I didn't warn you. German techno? You’re testing me, aren’t you? Right. We'll see how charitable I'm feeling. Speaking of sounds, did you hear that bloke at the pub last night? The one trying to order a pint? He was attempting a… well, it was  something  resembling a Bristol accent. Oh god, yeah! It was atrocious! Like he'd swallowed a dictionary of Bristol slang and was just randomly spitting it out. Proper cringe, innit? You can tell someone's trying too hard. My Nan’s from Devon, and she's got a beautiful accent – subtle, you know? But some people just try to  do  an accent. It's awful. You can hear the straining. Totally. It's like they're playing a character. And badly, at that. It reminds me of my Aunt Carol - she tries to do a posh voice when she’s talking to shop assistants.

Honestly, I'm still reeling from that physics lesson. Mr. Davies was going on about quantum entanglement for like, an hour. It's just… so weird. How can two particles be linked across vast distances? It breaks my brain. Bruv, physics is always weird. You gotta just accept it. It's not meant to make sense. More importantly, did you hear that new track from Central Cee? "Doja"? It’s bussin’. Yeah, I heard it! Proper bop, innit? I was blasting it on the way here. Though, I've been obsessed with Nova lately. Her new EP is insane. The production is top tier. Nova? I don't think I know her. What genre is she? She’s kinda R&B, but with like, a drill influence. It's proper cool. You should check her out, Liam. You’re always listening to that… indie stuff. Hey! There’s nothing wrong with indie. It’s got more substance than a lot of… well, than a lot of what’s popular these days. It's about storytelling, about feeling. Okay, okay, Mr. Music Critic. But sometimes you just need a tune you can dance to, yeah? Especially after that physics torture you just endured. Speaking of which, I still can't wrap my head around the double-slit experiment. Like, how does an electron know it's being observed? See, that’s the physics stuff that  is  interesting. Makes you question everything, doesn’t it? It’s like, if we weren’t looking, would the universe even… exist properly? Don't go there, you two. You'll give me another headache. Quantum mechanics is already enough to contend with. It’s all probabilities and uncertainties. It’s like… like watching a movie where you don't know what's going to happen next, but every possible outcome is simultaneously… happening. That sounds awful. I prefer a good narrative, you know? Something with a clear resolution. Like  Dune . Have you two seen the new  Dune  movie? Yeah, it was alright. A bit long though, yeah? The first one was better, I reckon. More action. I thought it was brilliant. The visuals were incredible, the music was haunting. Hans Zimmer really nailed the atmosphere. The scope of the story is just breathtaking. And the science – even though it’s fictional – felt grounded in some kind of logic. I agree with Liam on the visuals. They were stunning.

Right then, Operation Balanceability is underway! Leo, you nearly took out the cat again this morning, didn't you? But Mummy, I  almost  got it! I was going really, really fast! And Whiskers jumped! It was hilarious! Whiskers didn't like it, Leo. He hissed. He did indeed. Poppy's absolutely right. We need to be a bit more careful, don’t we? It’s brilliant you're trying, love, truly it is, but we don't want anyone getting hurt. It's about balance, you see? Like when you're trying to learn something new, anything really. It’s not about going fast to start. It's about small steps, finding your centre. But I  want  to go fast! Like a race! I know, sweetheart. And you will, eventually. Remember when you were learning to read? You struggled with ‘th’ sounds at first, didn’t you? You used to say ‘think’ as ‘sink’. I did! Miss Davies laughed! She was silly. She wasn't being silly, darling. She was encouraging! But you kept practicing, didn't you? Every single day, a little bit more. And now you can read practically anything. Balanceability is the same. It's practice, patience, and not giving up when you wobble. It’s about getting back up. Okay. But can I have pizza for dinner? Always with the pizza, isn't it? Always thinking about food! Poppy, you’re quiet. What’s been happening at school today? Anything interesting? Amelia's mum got them a new house. It’s really big. Oh, that's lovely! Has she told you about the renovations? Yes! It’s being done up. They are putting in a… a swishy thing! A waterfall? A manmade waterfall? Yeah! And a swimming pool! A really big one! Can we have a swimming pool? Please, Mummy? With a waterfall? One thing at a time, you two! Swimming pools are a bit beyond the budget at the moment. But don't you go thinking about diving in, alright? Diving into water you don't know is incredibly dangerous. Remember what we talked about? Always check the depth, always ask an adult. Yes, Mummy. Good. Now, back to school. Anything else exciting happen? Did you have a good conversation with your friends today? We talked about cats. Cats? Oh, that’s nice. Did you know it's National Cat Day in Japan today? They really love their cats over there.

Right then, so you’re  actually  doing the SoulCycle thing? Seriously? I thought you were just having a laugh when you mentioned it. I am! Well, I was, initially, having a laugh. But then I did a class, and… honestly, it’s surprisingly addictive. It’s like a rave, but with Leg Day. A rave? With Leg Day? Yorkshire lass through and through, I am. Sounds a bit brutal, love. I tried that Zumba thing once. Nearly threw up. Ended up spending the rest of the day on the sofa, wrapped in a blanket, and feeling properly sorry for meself. It’s not  that  brutal. Okay, the first one was… intense. My glutes were screaming for a week. But then you get used to it, and the music’s just… motivational. It distracts you from the fact you’re basically cycling like mad. Plus, it’s beating the January blues. Cambridge is grey as anything right now. Aye, t’grey’s are proper bad here too. Though t’weather’s been a bit milder lately, hasn’t it? Makes a change. Tell you what, though, getting fit and all that… it’s harder when you’re distracted, innit? Like, with… everything. Everything? What everything? Is it… Mark? Well, yeah, a bit. He’s just… he’s being a bit distant, an’ all. Not as affectionate as he used to be. And he keeps working late. Always ‘important meeting’ this, ‘urgent deadline’ that. Makes you wonder, dosn’t it? It does. It really does. But maybe it  is  just work. Mark’s always been career-driven. Remember when he was pulling all-nighters to finish that presentation at uni? Aye, but that was  uni . This feels different. He doesn’t really  talk  to me about it. Just mumbles something about spreadsheets and comes home exhausted. It's like I'm living with a ghost. Have you tried… talking to him? Like, really talking? Not just, “Did you eat?” or “How was work?” But a proper sit-down, deep conversation? I’ve tried. Sort of. But he just gets all… defensive. He says I’m being paranoid. Says I overthink things. Says I need to “just relax”. Typical. Men! They just don’t get it, do they? Look, I’ve been there. With Liam, remember? He used to do that too. Ignore the problem until it exploded. Aye, I remember. That was a right mess, that was.

That was a grand domino drive, wasn’t it, lad? Mrs. Henderson finally managed to get a five-in-a-row! You wouldn’t believe her shriek, would you? Nearly deafened poor Arthur next door. Aye, it were good. Did you see young Liam try and cheat again? He kept shifting his tiles when nobody was lookin’. Aye, I did. Honestly, that boy’ll be at it 'til he's grey. He’s got his grandad’s competitive streak, that one. Speaking of grandads, how’s your Uncle Barry doing? He seemed a bit quiet tonight, didn’t he? He's alright, I reckon. He just wasn't having much luck in the dominoes. He keeps saying he's going to get a new set, like, a really fancy one. With gold trim or somethin’. Gold trim! What a waste o’ money! A domino’s a domino, lad. Doesn’t need gold to fall over. You want fancy, buy a telly! That pizza smells right good, mind. Could eat another slice. Here you go, love. You earned it after that haul today, didn't you? Heard you were up and down to Thirsk all afternoon. Aye, a right rigmarole it were. That gate on Farmer Giles’ field, it’s slipped again. Nearly lost a whole trailer load o' lambs. And the rain… it were comin' down sideways. Right misery. Did you see that goal Newcastle scored last night? Proper screamer! From Saint-Maximin! I did! Thought you’d be chuffed to bits, didn't you? Still, I’m not gettin’ myself worked up about football. It's just a game. Although, I do enjoy a good cuppa and a biscuit while watching it. Just a game? It's a way o' life, woman! Don’t go tellin' me it's just a game. Makes a Tuesday night, anyway. Though I'd prefer a bit o' Wham! while I watch it if I’m honest. Wham!? Uncle Barry, you’re ancient! Everyone listens to drill now. Drill? Sounds like someone's drilling a hole in me head! Give me a bit o' George Michael any day. Reminds me of me younger days down the Working Men's. Do you remember the Northern Soul nights, Maureen? Oh, don’t remind me! My knees ached for a week afterwards. And your dancing, Barry… well, let’s just say it was enthusiastic. Speaking of knees, I need to get my hair cut.

Right, then. Earl Grey it is. Standard, innit? Fancy a biscuit, love? Got some ginger snaps, they're dead lovely. Yeah, ginger snaps sound perfect, thanks. Just let this kettle boil, will you? I’m absolutely knackered. This data analysis is eating me alive. I swear, if I see another scatter plot… Scatter plots, eh? Sounds grim. Me, I’m knee-deep in longitudinal surveys. Not quite as visual, but just as boring, I reckon. Though, I did spend most of yesterday trying to figure out why a bloke in Scarborough thought Brussels sprouts were a type of celebrity. A celebrity? Seriously? What did he say? Aye, dead serious! Said they were “absolutely star quality, like” Apparently, he’d had them roasted with bacon. Full works. Said he was a big fan. I had to explain, very gently, that they were, you know,  vegetables . I nearly choked on my own laughter. Only in this country. Honestly. You'd think people would know a sprout when they see one. It’s a bit like confusing Idris Elba with a potato, isn’t it? Both are undeniably handsome, but… dramatically different. You've got a point there! Speaking of handsome… did you see that Rebecca Ferguson’s been posting pictures of her garden? Proper lush, it is. All wildflowers and bees and whatnot. Makes you want to chuck in your data and become a beekeeper. Ferguson’s gorgeous, she is. But a beekeeper? You’d be covered in stings before you could say 'Royal Jelly'. Besides, someone needs to analyse my data – who else is going to figure out if there’s a correlation between turbulence in the market and people's choices of vegetables? Right, well, that's a conversation for another day then. So, what's this data about anyway? It sounds… ambitious. More ambitious than convincing a man from Scarborough that sprouts aren't famous. It’s about consumer behavior in volatile economic climates. Basically, are people trading down on quality during recessions, and if so, what’s driving that? I'm looking at fruit and veg consumption patterns, mostly. Trying to find out if folks are buying more potatoes and less asparagus, you know? The basics. Makes sense. Though, you'd think something a wee bit posh like asparagus would always be a luxury, wouldn't you? Still, people do weird things when they’re worried about money, don’t they?

Right, okay, I’m officially protesting this round. Rhys, you're cheating! Saying "quixotic" is just… blatant manipulation of the dictionary! Cheating? Don't be ridiculous, Seren! It’s a perfectly valid word. And you’re the one who chose ‘obscure’ as your category. You knew this would happen! Besides, it’s Articulate, not lexicography. A little creative interpretation is encouraged. It  is  a good word, though. Quixotic. Like a tilting-at-windmills sort of thing. A bit like the way you used to chase after those sheep, Gwyn, when you were a boy. Remember? Down by the Taff. Thought you were a shepherd, you did! Oh, stop it, Dad! That was one time. And they weren’t just  any  sheep, they were… particularly fluffy. And I was trying to help. Always helping, weren't you, boyo? Always getting into a flap. Speaking of flaps, did anyone see that robin outside the window this morning? Little thing, bright red breast, chirping away like he owned the place. Rhys, seriously! “Quixotic” is just too clever. It’s designed to trip people up. What about something more… accessible? Like “chair”? “Chair”? Where’s the fun in that? Besides, you got “elephant” in your last round. Don’t pretend you’re not a word wizard yourself. I think we should maybe introduce a rule. No words with more than three syllables? Now who’s being ridiculous? That would completely ruin the game! It needs to be challenging. It’s Articulate! I rather like Gwyn’s idea. Keeps things a bit fairer for the younger generation. Though, I remember when we were kids,  we  didn’t have all these complicated rules. Just a bit of shouting and a lot of arguing. Aye, that was the way. Less fuss, more fun. Though, I do recall your mother, Mary, once getting incredibly upset because someone said "sesquipedalian" and declared it wasn't a real word. Oh, my goodness! That's brilliant! She was convinced it was a made-up word just to confuse everyone! Honestly, she was something else. Remember when she tried to convince everyone that "aardvark" was actually derived from a Welsh word meaning "earth-pig"? She did, didn't she? And insisted on correcting everyone’s pronunciation for the rest of the evening. She had a way of making things… memorable. Strong-willed woman, your nan. But a good heart. Always looking out for everyone.

Right then, everyone settled? Rhys, stop trying to peek! Honestly, you’d think you’d learned by now. I’m merely admiring the artistry of the deck, Seren. A craftsman's work, you know. Can't let a good shuffle go unappreciated. Besides, I’m already planning my strategy. A strategic peek never hurt anyone. Strategy? It’s just Rummy, Rhys. Not a military campaign. Though, knowing you, you’ll treat it like one. Don’t you be getting smart with your cousin, Gareth. He likes a bit of flair. Besides, a bit of competition keeps us all on our toes, doesn’t it? Especially you, Seren, with your fancy postgraduate brain. Don't expect to win easily, love. Oh, here we go. Fancy postgraduate brain! It’s just a bit of extra studying, Mum. And I’m fully expecting Gareth to crush me, he always has. He’s surprisingly cutthroat when it comes to card games. Reputation precedes me, it seems. Though, I’ll admit, I’ve brushed up on my Rummy skills. Remember that trip to the Lake District last year? I schooled you then, Seren. Barely schooled me! I let you win because you kept going on about the amazing view. It was distracting. Anyway, bids anyone? Rhys, are you even paying attention? Nah, just observing the theatrics. I'm going to pass this round, I think. Saving my energy for the endgame. Let you lot tear each other apart for a bit. You and your 'endgame' mentality, Gareth! It's Rummy, not chess. Just play the cards you’re dealt. Right, I'll bid five. Not playing shy, am I? Five, eh? Bold! Rhys, you’re passing? Seriously? I’m a strategist, remember? Patience is a virtue. And I've got a feeling something good is coming. Plus, watching Mum get flustered is always entertaining. Typical. You’re just being contrary. Alright then, I'll go for seven. Let’s see if your passive tactics can withstand a bit of pressure. Hmm, not a bad hand actually. I'll bid six. Let's see who's bluffing. Now, Gareth, your turn. Don't be a wallflower. Fine, fine. Ten. Just to make things interesting. Don’t say I didn't warn you. Ten! You’re having a laugh, Gareth! You’ve got no good cards! You're trying to bankrupt us all, aren’t you? One can only dream, Mum.

Honestly, Bridgerton is getting  so  predictable. Like, do they think we're all that easily fooled? The romantic tension is just… staged. You’re saying? I think it's a bit of fluff, but perfect for December. I needed something easy to watch after those awful care shifts. Mrs. Henderson was particularly grumpy today. Just kept complaining about the sprouts being too small. Can you believe it? Sprouts! Don’t even get me started. My nan makes them with bacon lardons and a balsamic glaze.  That  is how you do sprouts. Anyway, what are you two moaning about now? Mostly just Anya's disdain for period dramas. Though, speaking of moaning, my mum’s convinced I’m spending too much time at ANON’s. Says I need to focus on the Navy stuff and not dilly-dally with… “civilian pursuits.” Seriously? You’re a Combat Systems Engineer! You’re practically saving the world. A few hours spent with your friends isn’t going to derail you, Leo. I know, I know. But she's worried. It’s tough, you know? Leaving home, going off to training… It's a big deal. Especially for a mum. Sorry I'm late! The shop was mental today. Everyone's desperate for last-minute Christmas bits and bobs. Sarah ended up having to wrestle a woman for a sparkly reindeer. No way! That’s brilliant. You sound proper stressed though, Chloe. I am a bit. And I’m still not sure what I’m doing after sixth form. College? Another year in retail? I just feel… lost. You've got loads of time, Chloe. Don't worry about it now. I'm feeling it too, actually. Everyone keeps asking about university, and I’m just… not sure. Accounting sounds dryer than toast most of the time, to be honest. But you’re good at it! You always were. Remember in Year 9 when you helped Mr. Davies with the school budget? Yeah, well, helping with a school budget is slightly different from auditing tax returns for a multinational corporation. Also, my parents are constantly on about Oxbridge. Like, it's the only acceptable path. My dad keeps going on about apprenticeships. Says they’re the way forward. Loads of practical experience, earning money, and no student debt. Makes a lot of sense, actually. It does. I was looking at some care apprenticeships, to be honest.

Right then. That was a proper lovely bit of shepherd’s pie, wasn’t it? Better than anything I could rustle up myself these days. My back's been giving me gyp, you see. Couldn't be standing about for that long. It really was, Nan. Thanks, Anon. You’re a star. I was thinking afterwards, we could go for a walk tomorrow? Weather’s supposed to be decent. Just a little stroll around Grantchester Meadows. Walk? In this weather? It'll be freezing your toes off, that’s what. Better to stay put, watch a bit of telly. There’s that nature programme on later, you know, the one with all the penguins. Ooh, penguins! Do say so, love. I do enjoy a bit of penguin watching. Though a walk sounds alright too. Just a gentle one, mind. My knees ain't what they used to be. Used to be able to walk for miles, back in the day. Remember that trip to Brighton, Tommy and me? Nearly wore out the soles of my shoes! I’ve only heard stories about that trip, Nan. Brighton sounds amazing. You’d love it now though. Loads of shops and vegan cafes. I’ll check the weather forecast properly and we can decide then. Maybe we could cycle part of the way too, if you’re up for it? Cycling? You’re mad! On a bike? It’s dangerous out there! All those cars and lorries. I saw a cyclist get knocked over just the other day. Proper nasty accident. Now, now, don’t go scaring the girl, Michael. A bit of cycling never hurt anyone. Keep you young, it does. Though, I’ll stick to walking, thank you very much. Always preferred me feet on the ground. Less wobbly, see. It's a cycle path, Michael, mostly. Pretty safe. I'd stick to the quieter roads anyway. Besides, the fresh air would do you good. You’ve been cooped up in here far too much lately. Fresh air? It's just cold damp air! I prefer the warmth of the telly and a nice cup of tea. Less chance of catching a chill. Always the same with you, love. A creature of comfort, you are. Remember when you tried to learn to drive? Ended up putting the car through Mrs. Higginbottom’s hedge! Nearly gave her a heart attack, she did. Oh, Nan, don't remind him!

Honestly, I’m just bowled over by the sheer number of people here. Alumni Day – who knew it would be so popular? Feels a bit like a GCSE hall on results day, doesn’t it? It really does! I wasn't expecting this many faces either. I did a quick scan and realised I’ve only recognised maybe three people from my cohort. I’m Elodie, by the way. Language Research Administrator – bit of a mouthful, I know. Chloe. Language Research Co-ordinator. Nice to meet you, Elodie. So, language-y things then? Are you specializing in anything particularly interesting? I’m currently buried in a project looking at the impact of online platforms on dialectal divergence, specifically in rural areas. It's…fascinating, if you’re into that sort of thing. That sounds hugely interesting, actually. I'm mostly focused on data acquisition and analysis for our corpus linguistics projects. Less 'fascinating' in the field, more ‘fascinating’ in the spreadsheet, I suppose. We've got a huge dataset on contemporary Spanish slang. Want to hear a particularly bizarre one? "Ser carne de diván" – to be couch meat. Apparently, it describes someone who’s utterly unproductive and just spends all day melting into the sofa. Oh, goodness! That's brilliant. We need that for our new project on cultural expressions. It's that sort of nuance that gets lost in translation, isn't it? Speaking of Spain, I spent a few summers in the Basque Country a while back. Absolutely stunning scenery, but the language… my word, that’s a challenge. Excuse me, I couldn't help but overhear you two discussing Basque. A truly remarkable language, isn’t it? Completely unrelated to anything else in Europe. Astonishing isolation. Oh, hello! Yes, it is. I attempted it. Keyword: attempted. It quickly became clear my GCSE French wouldn't cut it. I've always been intrigued by the fact it's spoken on both sides of the border between Spain and France. Do you know much about its history? Indeed. Its origins are shrouded in mystery, which only adds to its allure. It’s been through periods of suppression, of course, largely driven by centralisation efforts. They tried to eradicate it during Franco’s regime. A valiant effort by speakers to preserve it, truly. I recall reading a fascinating article on the standardization process… It reminds me a bit of attempts to preserve Welsh in some ways, though the current circumstances are very different.

Honestly, seeing you both is brilliant. Two years! Feels like ages since we properly caught up. Mum's done a smashing job with the house, hasn’t she? A bit...retro, perhaps, but smashing. Retro is a kind way of putting it, Liam. It’s like stepping back into the 80s. Though, I do love this sofa. Remember when we used to build forts on it with blankets and cushions? Oh god, the forts! And the arguments about who got to be the ‘queen’ of the fort. Always you, Chloe, seemingly! Well, I  was  older! And dramatically superior, obviously. . How’s recruitment going, Abbie? Still headhunting for CEOs? Pretty much. It’s manic. But the money's decent. Though, half the time, I feel like I’m just writing really long, repetitive job descriptions. Did you see that video doing the rounds on Facebook about the ice bucket challenge? Apparently, it's raised a fortune for motor neurone disease. Yeah, loads of people are doing it. Mum's been pestering me to nominate some of my uni mates. I’m a bit hesitant though, feels a bit...performative, doesn't it? Especially when people are just doing it for the likes. There’s always that element, isn't there? But even if some are doing it for the wrong reasons, the money's still going to a good cause. We should look into local charities, shouldn't we? There's that children's hospice just outside town… Absolutely. Good shout, Chloe. Speaking of good causes, I’ve been thinking about fostering, actually. Or even adoption, eventually. Really? That’s...wow, Abbie. That’s a big commitment. I know! It's just a thought at this stage. It’s just...seeing my niece and nephew last weekend, and thinking about how much joy they bring to life, you know? It's definitely something I'd consider with Tom. That's lovely, Abbie. Wonderful, in fact. Liam, did you ever think about having kids? Now you're teaching all those bright young things… Not particularly, not right now. Teaching takes up so much time, you know? And I'm still finding my feet a bit, traveling, experiencing things… It’s just not something I’m actively thinking about. Although, correcting student essays all day does make you ponder the mysteries of grammar and potential future generations! You and your grammar! Mum’s been going on about having a family get-together for ages...

Honestly, this coffee machine is driving me mad. It hisses and groans like an old steam train. I swear, it’s rebelling against being stuck in Hunsonby. It's probably missing the familiar rumble of Dublin traffic. It’s just a bit temperamental, Mum. I'll look at the manual later. It's probably just needs descaling. You know, you could get one of those fancy pod machines. Simpler, less fuss. Pod machines? They’re… soulless, dear. Give me the ritual of freshly ground beans any day. Besides, all that plastic waste! The environmental impact alone… it’s just irresponsible. Everything feels so wasteful these days. Wasteful? Tell me about it. This removal company sent me a quote. Fifty quid just to  store  a couple of boxes! Fifty quid! Back in the day, you'd stuff everything in the attic and be done with it. Now, it’s professional storage facilities and exorbitant prices. That  is  ridiculous, Dad. We could probably find you a cheaper option. Aunt Carol’s got a huge shed, remember? Maybe you could just keep a few things there until... well, until things settle down. Settle down. That’s a lovely thought, isn’t it? Settle down in a little village in Cumbria. After a lifetime in Dublin! It feels… disorienting. Don't you start with the melancholy now, Moira. It's a change of scenery. Fresh air. And it’s good to be closer to everyone, isn't it? Though I still can’t get my head around the cost of everything. It's galling. Speaking of which... did you see what Starmer said yesterday? Oh, please, not politics. I'm trying to avoid anything that raises my blood pressure. Go on, Dad. What's got your goat this time? He's talking about fiscal responsibility, isn't he? Saying we need to rein in spending. As if a decade of austerity hasn't crippled the country already! It's the same old song and dance. The man’s a banker, at heart, you can tell. No real fire in his belly, no real idealism. Now there's a point. I always thought he was... bland. Lacking a certain spark. Remember Kinnock, back in the eighties? Now  there  was a man with passion! He  believed  in something. You could feel it. Mum, you’re going back decades! Kinnock was brilliant, but the world's changed. We need… practicality now.

Honestly, Mum, I’m already feeling a bit overwhelmed with Christmas plans. It’s barely November! The school nativity is booked solid, I've got three different Christmas markets I'm supposed to be helping with, and then, you know,  actual  Christmas itself. Oh, love, you always say that. You throw yourself into everything with such enthusiasm. Remember when you were little and you wanted to build a gingerbread village that stretched across the entire kitchen table? You were meticulously icing it for days! Oh god, yes! Dad nearly had a stroke trying to navigate around it. But the nativity...it's just a lot. Little Timmy keeps forgetting his lines, and Mrs. Davies is insisting on tinsel everywhere. Everywhere! It's a fire hazard, honestly. Well, a little tinsel never hurt anyone, did it? And Timmy will remember his lines. They always do, just before they're on stage. It's the tension, you see. Reminds me of Gareth before his exams. Frozen with anxiety. Gareth! How is he? Has he booked his flights yet? I need to confirm numbers for Christmas dinner. I’m thinking of doing a proper roast this year, not just the usual turkey and all the trimmings. Maybe a goose? Gareth’s doing well, dear. He's finished that big project at the firm, so he’s finally de-stressed a bit. He mentioned having a few days off somewhere warm – probably Spain, knowing him. He'll book his flights as soon as he’s decided where, that boy is a last-minute sort. And a goose? That’s a bit ambitious, isn't it? Especially with all the other commitments you have. Don’t burn yourself out, love. I know, I know. It’s just… I want it to be  perfect  this year. Last year felt a bit… rushed. And Auntie Carol and Uncle Dave… well, they're not getting any younger. I want to make sure they have a really lovely Christmas. They will, darling. They adore you. And as long as you’re all together, full of laughter and good food, it  will  be lovely. Carol and Dave are seasoned Christmas veterans, they've seen it all. Remember the year you tried to make those homemade mince pies, and they were completely rock solid? They just laughed and ate them anyway. Oh, that was a disaster! I was so determined to impress everyone.

Right, so, Liam's still going on about Sarah’s snoring. Honestly, you’d think he’d get used to it by now. They've been together for, what, nearly two years? It's like a nightly drama. Aye, he’s a sensitive lad, our Liam. Remembers every single rumble. It's worse when he’s got a cold, apparently. Sounds like a walrus trying to restart a lawnmower. Oh, poor Liam! But Sarah, is she actually  that  bad? I mean, everyone snores a bit, don't they? My granda snored like a freight train. You could hear 'im three rooms away. My nan used to shove earplugs in and pretend she was deaf as a post. My mum’s the worst, though. Like a blocked drain gurgling. She’s bought those fancy nose strips, but they don't seem to do much good. Nose strips! That's a choice. Liam’s suggested she sleep on her side, but she says she wakes up on her back every time. Proper stubborn, she is. Anyway, speaking of food... did you lot get Waterfields' this morning? Aye, got a couple of their cheese and onion baps. Proper hangover cure, those are. I did! And a batch of their Eccles cakes. They're just the best, aren't they? Proper traditional, that bakery. My grandma used to take me there when I was little. Waterfields, eh? We’ve got a proper pie shop near me in Leeds. Now  that’s  a treat. Yorkshire pudding with a proper steak and gravy… beats an Eccles cake any day, I reckon. You’re just saying that! Eccles cakes are legendary. Though… I did get Richmond sausages this morning. From the market. Best I’ve had in ages. Richmonds! Now you're talking. Those are top tier. Got a right good butcher here in Warrington, does a mean Cumberland too. Remember when Uncle Geoff tried to make his own sausages? Ended up with something that resembled grey rubber. Nearly took out poor Auntie Brenda's teeth. Oh my god, I'd forgotten about that! He was so proud of them, too! Said he’d perfected the recipe. My dad tried to make his own bread once. It was like a brick. Seriously, you could’ve built a wall with it. Honestly, men and DIY… they’ll try anything. Speaking of things men do… does anyone still carry handkerchiefs?

Honestly, Dad, that was  exactly  what I needed. Just… proper relaxing. I feel like a new person after that spa day. Aye, well, you looked like you needed it, love. Worked yourself ragged with that Henderson project, haven't you? Always rushing about, stressing over deadlines. A bit of pampering never hurt anyone. Bit of lemon and ginger tea, right? Just like your Nan used to make. Exactly! They had a little aromatherapy room and everything. Lavender and chamomile… bliss. Though, I did have a slight disaster with the seaweed wrap. Seaweed wrap, eh? What happened, did you end up looking like you'd wrestled a giant kelp forest? Almost! They put it on and it felt… cold. Properly cold. Then they told me to wrap myself in foil. I felt like a baked potato! And I kept sticking to everything. My phone, the chair, the poor therapist’s hand… it was mortifying. Oh, lass, you and your dramatic flair. Seaweed’s always been a bit slippery stuff. Remember when your Uncle Barry tried to grow it in his pond? Said he was going to have a seaweed farm. Didn’t last a week. The ducks were having a right laugh, paddling through it. Oh god, I'd forgotten about that! He was so hopeful. Did you go to the farm show on Saturday then? I was wondering how it went. Went, did I? Well, it was the usual mixture. Some good bits, some not so good. The new fertiliser company, AgriBoost, were showing off their latest stuff. Claimed to increase yields by 20%. Sounded a bit ambitious, to be honest. Sounds promising though, if it works. Farmers need all the help they can get, don't they? They do, they do. Though some of them are a bit stubborn, you know? Tried to convince me that manure’s still the best way to go. Said all these fancy chemicals were ruining the soil. Old school thinking, that. Still, can’t argue with results. It's just a different approach, isn’t it? Like, with project management, we’re always looking for the most streamlined, efficient methods. It's not about saying the old way was  bad , just that there might be a better way now. Aye, I suppose you're right. Always something new to learn. Though, some things are best left untouched. Remember that time I tried to install a self-watering system in the vegetable patch?

Honestly, Amy, I don’t know how you do it. Teaching French to teenagers all day - you must be knackered. My little Year 7s are proving quite the handful this term, but at least they’re generally enthusiastic. The apathy is palpable some days with the older ones. Enthusiasm is a rare commodity, isn’t it? My Year 9s are currently obsessed with dissecting Shakespeare, which is lovely, but the sheer volume of marking… it’s brutal. And the behaviour! Don’t even get me started. It’s a different beast entirely from the primary schools I used to work in. How’s the workload looking for you, then? Still manageable? It’s… okay. The school's been pushing extra language clubs again. They're trying to get more students involved, which is great in principle, but it feels like they're just piling it on. They want me to run a conversational French club for Year 10s on Tuesdays and a ‘French film appreciation’ thing for the Sixth Form on Thursdays. Bit much, really. I told them I’d consider it, but… Yeah, I know that feeling. Pressure from above. They always want more, don't they? Sometimes you have to draw a line. Remember when Mrs. Davies at Sheldon tried to get us to run a Saturday detention club for kids struggling with maths? It was madness! Oh god, Mrs. Davies. Don’t remind me! Speaking of languages, are you still dabbling in Spanish? I remember you were so keen to get back to it. I am, actually! It's been slow going, I’ll admit. Little Leo's taken up most of my time, you know? But I've been using Duolingo, surprisingly. It’s actually not horrible, though I do feel a bit silly talking to a cartoon owl. I'm trying to focus on conversational fluency, rather than just grammatical perfection. You know, being able to order a coffee and not butcher the pronunciation. That’s the goal, isn’t it? I've been thinking about brushing up on my German. I used to be quite good, but it’s all slipped away. Perhaps we could do it together, virtually? We could motivate each other. That’s a brilliant idea! We could even try and find a language exchange partner online. Someone who’s a native German speaker and wants to learn English. Definitely! I’ll have a look tonight.

Blimey, look at that, Arthur. A right proper nest. Bigger than last year’s, innit? Must've taken 'em ages to build that. Proper engineering, that is, even if it’s just birds. Bit haphazard, mind you, not exactly to code. Haphazard, you say? That’s the charm of it, George! They ain't got your fancy degrees. Just instinct and a bit o’ mud. Bet it’s full o’ blue tits soon enough. Remember when Mabel put up that fancy wrought iron feeder? They wouldn’t touch it. Said it was 'too formal’ apparently. Oh, don't remind me of that feeder, Arthur! Absolute waste of money. They much prefer the old sunflower hearts in the plastic one. And look, George, you’ve got a bit of bark on your cheek. Right you are, Mabel. Blastin' trees. So, Arthur, you reckon they'll raise more than one clutch this year? The blackbirds were having a right old time in the rose bushes yesterday. Could be. They’re a busy lot, birds are. Trying to make the most of the mild weather we're having, eh? Used to be a proper spring, you know. Now it’s just… confusing. Like my blood sugar. Don't you start worrying about your sugar, Arthur. Have a piece of cake first, that’ll calm you down. It's got a little sugar in it, mind you, but not too much. Just enough to be nice. How’s your toe feeling today, love? Still throbbing? A bit, aye. Still swollen. Doctor says it's just age catching up with me. Age. What a convenient excuse. Used to be able to walk for miles. Now, I'm lucky to make it round the garden without needing a sit-down. You’re doing alright, Arthur. Don’t be so hard on yourself. We all slow down a bit. Remember old Mrs. Higgins down the road? Used to be a whippet of a woman, always pottering about. Now she just stares out the window all day. Proper sad, that is. They say it's hard, being old. No one much cares, do they? Not properly. Just poking and prodding at you at the doctor’s, checking your blood pressure and asking if you’re lonely. Lonely! As if you can just  shake off  loneliness. Exactly! They talk about ‘social isolation’ and ‘preventative measures’. Means nothing to us, does it?

Honestly, John, this place is charming, isn't it? Such a lovely view of the sea. I’m starving though. What are you thinking of having? The grilled octopus looks tempting. It does, doesn't it? Though, I might go for the kleftiko. Lamb, you know. A bit easier on the digestion. This heat does things to you. Reminds me of that summer we spent in Crete... remember the taverna in Elounda? The owner's cat used to steal the olives right off your plate. Oh, I do! That cheeky little thing. And the owner, Yannis, swore it was a reincarnation of his grandmother. Cypriots are full of those sorts of stories, aren't they? Makes you wonder… all that talk of destiny and whatnot. They have a different perspective, that’s for sure. A looser one, perhaps? It’s a lovely thing, though, to believe in something bigger than oneself. Reminds me of old Mrs. Higgins, used to dabble in dowsing, she did. Said she could find lost pets with a stick. Never believed her myself, truthfully, but she was convinced she was on to something. Dowsing? Really? I thought that was all a bit… fanciful. Still, everyone’s entitled to their beliefs, I suppose. Speaking of lost things, have you heard from Emily recently? How’s her chihuahua, Pip? Emily’s alright, I think. A bit preoccupied, as always. Pip's got a terrible habit of escaping. She’s currently trying to teach him Turkish - just numbers, mind you. “Bir, iki, üç…" It’s rather sweet, actually. She’s been quite down lately, though. Still reeling from Uncle Arthur's passing, I reckon. Yes, poor Arthur. It was so quick. Cancer, wasn’t it? Dreadful. I still can't quite believe he's gone. Made me think about… well, about mortality, you know? It’s a silly thing, but I find myself looking at people and imagining their stories. That couple over there, for instance. Middle-aged, quite serious looking... I bet they both work in finance. Probably. Although, the woman is wearing quite a vibrant scarf. Could be retired, enjoying a holiday. Hard to tell. My hearing isn’t what it used to be, you see. These blasted aids don't always pick up whispers. They promised me the newest model. "Crystal clear!" they said. More like slightly clearer. You’ll have to remind me to research some good audiologists when we get back.

Honestly, Mum, this is exactly what I needed. Just… relaxing. Work has been absolutely mental this past month. The Henderson project is threatening to swallow me whole. Oh, love, you always say that. You're a whirlwind, you are. Project Coordinator, eh? Sounds ever so important. More important than marking endless GCSE papers, that’s for sure. Though, judging by the state of your hair, I reckon you've been burning the candle at both ends. Are you eating properly? Trying to. It's mostly grabbing a sandwich at my desk. Dad's roast last night was a lifesaver, though. Seriously, you two make the best roast potatoes. Well, a man's gotta know how to roast a potato, doesn’t he? Keeps the family happy. Speaking of happy, how’s that little flat of yours? Still battling squirrels trying to get into your bird feeder? Don't remind me! It’s an ongoing war, Dad. They're cunning little blighters. I’m starting to think I need to invest in some sort of tiny squirrel-proof fortress around it. But honestly, it’s fine. It's small, but it's mine. I’m just… thinking about space, you know? Space? Oh, are you thinking of finally moving somewhere bigger? You’ve been saying you’d like a garden for years. Yeah, something like that. I was looking at a few places online actually. Nothing serious, just browsing. There's a charming little cottage in Saffron Walden – bit outside my budget currently - but it has a beautiful garden and is proper characterful. The thought of doing it up, though… that’s daunting. Doing up a cottage is a right palaver. Believe me, I’ve got enough experience with that. The farmhouse needed a full rewire when we bought it. Nightmare. But immensely satisfying when it's finished. You know I’d lend a hand, love. Just say the word. I appreciate that, Dad, I really do. But I think I need to be financially stable before I even contemplate something that big. And before I can even  think  about that, I need to finish the Henderson project! It’s got a ridiculous deadline looming. Mr. Henderson keeps adding scope creep. It’s infuriating! Men. Always thinking they know best. Tell you what, love, you looked a bit knackered last time I saw you. Why don't you go for a nice, long walk tomorrow?

Right, so, honestly, this catfish situation… it's proper mad, innit? Like, I still can’t quite believe poor Liam fell for it. Months, Sarah! Months chatting to a girl who didn't even exist. I know! It's just… heartbreaking. Did you see the pictures? The girl he was talking to, “Isabella,” had these perfectly curated travel shots, fancy restaurants, always looked like she was having the time of her life. But then, Liam found out it was just stock photos cobbled together from Pinterest. Poor lad. Honestly, it's a prime example of why you shouldn’t trust anything you see online. Though, I mean, even Jeremy Kyle figured that out years ago, didn’t he? Don’t even start on Jeremy Kyle! That's a whole different level of… well, misery, really. I haven’t watched it in ages, but I remember it was always a train wreck. All shouting and DNA tests. Makes you feel a bit grim, doesn’t it? True, but there was a certain… fascination, wasn't there? Like, you couldn't look away. Pure rubbernecking. It's weird, though, isn’t it? People deliberately putting themselves in that position, on television, for everyone to judge. It's a cry for help, probably. Definitely. And the producers, of course, are loving it. Feeding off the drama. It’s just… manufactured, really. All for a bit of telly. Though, to be fair, Liam's situation with the catfish is proper genuine. He was genuinely convinced. Aye, that’s what’s so grim about it. It’s not for entertainment. He was genuine. He was opening up and trusting someone. And to have that trust completely shattered… it's brutal. He keeps saying he feels like a total idiot. Don’t let him beat himself up about it. It’s clever, what these catfish do. They’re good at it. They build up a whole persona, play on your vulnerabilities. He’s not an idiot; he’s just… kind. Yeah, he's a good lad. A bit naive, maybe, but a good lad. Did he report it to the police? He's thinking about it. Apparently, it's tricky because it’s hard to prove where they’re operating from. It’s probably some dodgy country where they won’t extradite them anyway. Honestly, it’s just infuriating. Knowing there are people out there deliberately doing this to people… it’s disgusting.

Right then, Nana, dig in. Made it pretty much how you like it – not too much garlic, just a touch of chilli. Hope you’re feeling alright today? You seemed a little quiet this morning. Thank you, darling. It looks lovely. And yes, I am feeling… calmer, I suppose. The computer was giving me absolute fits again this morning. Honestly, sometimes I think they’re designed to torment elderly artists. Do you remember when I tried to scan those watercolours I did of the Duomo in Florence? Disaster. Absolute disaster. Yeah, you were muttering about restoring to the Stone Age for a good hour. Did you manage to sort it out eventually? Liam down the street might be able to have a look. He's decent with computers, a bit younger than me, but knows his stuff. No, no. Liam's too busy playing those… computer games. I ended up just giving up and going back to using proper pencils and paper. Much more reliable, you know. Though I do wish I could figure out how to get those scanned images to look right. They always seem so… flat. It’s like losing all the depth. That’s the digital age for you, I’m afraid. It’s not always an improvement. Anyway, so, tell me, you were saying something about Paris the other day? You sounded almost wistful. Paris… yes. I was remembering my youth. It was… a different time. I was studying at the Sorbonne, you know. A whirlwind of philosophy, art history, and rather charming young men. Seriously? You studied at the Sorbonne? Blimey, Nana, I never knew that! French, I assume? Of course, French. And a little German, naturally. Father insisted. He said it was essential for understanding Central Europe. He was a bit… intense about languages, your grandfather. Always drilling us. “A language is a window into a soul, Liesel!” he’d say. Dreadful, really. Although, I do appreciate it now. It opened so many doors. You should learn another language, you know. It’s enriching. Have you thought about picking up some German, considering your Classics degree? I’ve thought about it. Latin and Greek take up most of my brainpower as it is. Trying to cram in German… not sure I’ve got the capacity right now. Classics is keeping me pretty busy, you know? The dissertation is looming, and Professor Davies is being particularly…  demanding  this term.

Honestly, Dad, you were tailgating that bloke like a maniac! Nearly gave me a heart attack. Dorset's supposed to be relaxing, not a Formula One race. Don't you fret, love. Just keeping up with the flow. Besides, that sat nav's been barking up the wrong tree half the time anyway. Should've stuck with a proper map. Remember those? Maps are bulky, George. And unreliable. Honestly, relying on a bloke who thinks tailgating is acceptable… I’m glad I brought my audiobook. It’s drowning out the stress a bit, least. The sat nav  is  a bit wonky, I'll grant you that. Keeps trying to send us through villages that clearly weren’t built for cars. It sent us through Cheddar last week, remember? That was a nightmare. All tiny lanes and sheep everywhere. Honestly, Cheddar's not a place you'd  want  to build anything, let alone live. Cheddar was alright. Bit too many tourists, mind you. Reminded me of Margate in the sixties. Not a place I’d ever set up shop, though. Too… transient. Give me Walthamstow any day. Walthamstow? Really, George? You always were a creature of habit. I’d rather live in a damp caravan than Walthamstow. At least then I'd have a view. Right, well, as long as you're entertained, Mum. Speaking of entertaining, I've got that email from the solicitors. About sorting out Grandma’s will. It’s a right mess, apparently. Solicitors. Rip-off merchants, the lot of ‘em. Always looking for a fiver. Should have just used a nice, friendly solicitor like old Mr. Finch used to be. Finch was lovely, yes, but remember what happened with Aunt Maureen's will? He missed a crucial detail and she ended up leaving everything to that terrible cat lady from down the road! Exactly! That’s why you need someone proper. They're quoting over five grand just to sort it out. Five grand! I’m skint as it is, juggling my studies and that part-time job at the library. Honestly, education these days. All that blimey treasurer you have to learn. Why'd you choose History anyway? Because I  like  it, Dad! And it's not blimey treasurer, it's… finance! And it’s relevant. Anyway, back to the solicitors – I was thinking maybe we could negotiate the fee. Or at least ask for an itemised breakdown.

Cor, me bones are achey today, they are. Rain settin’ in proper, innit? Makes ‘em feel it more, that does. It is a bit grim, isn't it, Arthur? Though, I quite like the sound of it against the window. Reminds me of when we were little, hiding under the covers during a storm. Do you remember storms like that in Costessey? Oh, aye. We copped a fair few gales up there. Flat fields, see? Nothing to break the wind. Remember old Farmer Giles’ sheds flyin' off during '66? Ruptured his whole livelihood, that did. Never did get 'im properly back on his feet. Poor man. Life's so fragile sometimes, isn’t it? Speaking of which, did you see that article in the paper about the new housing development going up on the old orchard? Saw it. Bit of a shame, that orchard. Always smelled lovely in springtime, full of blossom. Used to go pickin’ apples there with me mum, when I were a lad. Proper Norfolk bramleys they were. None of that imported nonsense. I know! It's all concrete and identical houses now, isn't it? No character. And they’re calling it ‘Willowbrook Estate’. Honestly! Doesn’t even reflect the area. Typical. They never do. Always tryin' to make it all ‘modern’ and ‘stylish’. What’s wrong with a bit of tradition? A bit of… Norfolk? You know, I saw young Timmy down at the shops the other day. Said he was lookin' for a proper pasty. Can't seem to find one that’s not full of potatoes and cheap meat anymore. It  is  difficult. Everything's changed. Remember when Mrs. Higgins used to make those amazing meat pies at the bakery? They were the best! Her pastry was like silk. Silk, that's right. Thin as silk. And the gravy… proper gravy. Not that gravy-browning stuff they sell now. That was real cookin', that was. None of this microwave muck. You’re drifting, Arthur. What were we talking about? The orchard, weren’t we? And these… these new houses. They'll be full of folks who don’t know the first thing about Norfolk. Don't appreciate a good bramley apple, or a proper pasty. Well, hopefully, they’ll learn. It takes time, doesn’t it? Though, I suppose, it’s changed so much already, they might not even want to. Do you fancy another cup of tea?

Right, so, I was listenin’ to The Sugarcubes again yesterday. Proper nostalgia trip, that was. Remember when we used to try and play ‘Where Is My Mind’ on that busted keyboard your dad had? Sounded nothin' like the Pixies, let me tell you. More like a cat fightin' with a kazoo. Vaguely. My musical memory isn’t what it used to be, especially when alcohol is involved. Though, I do recall your dedication. You were determined to learn that whole riff, weren't you? Even though it was completely beyond our skill level. Aye, I was! I was convinced I’d be a rockstar. Or at least, a halfway decent bassist. Now, I'm more likely to rock a spreadsheet, aren't I? Still, there’s something about Bjork’s voice, isn't there? Just… otherworldly. What have you been listenin’ to? Still obsessin' over those Baroque composers, are you? Still. Though I’ve expanded my horizons a little. Been exploring some early Romantic stuff. Schubert, mainly. His "Winterreise" is… devastatingly beautiful. It’s remarkable how much emotion he crammed into those simple melodies. Completely different vibe from the Sugarcubes, wouldn’t you say? Completely! Like, chalk and cheese. Though, both proper powerful, in their own ways. Did you hear back from Liam and Chloe about the weekend? Are they finally gonna make it up to Durham? It's been ages since we've all been up north. I texted Liam earlier. They're tentatively yes. Chloe's got a conference on Friday, so she's a bit stressed, but they're hoping to join us Saturday. It’d be brilliant to have them. We need a proper catch-up. It feels like we’re all just existing in separate bubbles these days. Aye, it does. Life gets in the way, doesn't it? Work, studies… you're permanently buried in books, aren't you? Although, I'm not exactly headin’ the charts with my research either. Endless reports and action points… thrilling stuff. It has its moments. The library can be quite peaceful if you can find a corner away from the undergrads. Although, I'm starting to feel the pressure a bit more now. The submission deadline's looming. Fun times. Tell me about it. Speaking of deadlines, did you manage to get those tomato supports in the garden? The ones I asked you about? It’s ragin’ a gale out there tonight, I can feel it in me bones.

Honestly, Liam, I still can't get me head around it. Forty-two! Forty-bloody-two redundancies at the firm in one go. It’s bonkers, isn't it? And all apparently due to “restructuring.” Restructuring me backside. More like they're cutting costs by chucking decent, experienced people out. It is rough, Liv. The climate's just… unpredictable, isn’t it? I’ve been reading about the financial forecasts – it’s not looking brilliant. Academia isn’t exactly booming either, you know. Funding is tighter than ever. Aye, but forty-two! There were folk who’d been there fifteen, twenty years. Proper reliable, good workers. Margaret from accounts – she’s got two kids, just starting uni themselves. What’s she going to do now? It's awful. And that brings me back to the fees, actually. Did you hear about the proposal they're floating around for postgraduate funding? They’re talking about increasing them significantly. Oh, don't tell me! Please tell me you’re havin' me on. Increased postgraduate fees? Seriously? It’s already a financial black hole, isn't it? I'm still payin' off mine, years later. I know! Apparently, the argument is that it incentivizes more private funding. But all it really does is bar a lot of clever people from pursuing advanced degrees. I mean, how are people supposed to dedicate themselves to research when they are desperately trying to pay rent? It's just… rotten, innit? The whole system. Makes me wonder if I made the right choice, spendin' all that money on me masters. Though, to be fair, it did get me this job. Still, it was a huge gamble. It was a good one, though. You're brilliant at what you do. You always were. Remember when you got that top mark in A-level sociology? Miss Henderson nearly fainted! Aye! I were chuffed to bits with that. She said I had a real knack for spotting the underlying power dynamics. I think that’s what I do best – seeing the patterns, the bits everyone else misses. Useful for research, I suppose. Though sometimes I just wish I’d gone straight into somethin' more practical, like hairdressing. Hairdressing? You? Liv, you’d style the Prime Minister’s hair on a whim and argue for a socialist revolution while you were at it. Aye, probably! Although, I do miss gettin' me hair done sometimes.
