My nan’s the same about “innit.” She’ll give you a look that could curdle milk if you say it. And don't even  think  about using "literally" ironically. It's a declaration of war, apparently. My grandma just gets confused by everything. She asked me the other day if 'influencers' were people who worked at the local council. Oh, that’s brilliant! See, it’s not just about understanding new words, it’s about understanding completely new  concepts.  Like, what  is  an influencer? It’s a weird job title, even to me, and I work in publishing! It's fascinating how intertwined language and culture are. Back in Sweden, the concept of ‘fika’… it’s more than just a coffee break. It’s a social ritual, a way of connecting. There’s a specific wordplay and entire phrases associated with it that simply don't translate. My attempts to explain it to my colleagues often resulted in blank stares. We have something similar, don’t we? A roast. Honestly, it's a cultural minefield to an outsider. You've got to be so careful about the line between playful banter and genuinely hurting someone’s feelings. It involves a very specific cadence and facial expression. You're right. We  do . And the passive aggression! Trying to navigate British passive aggression is a course in advanced linguistics in itself. Don’t remind me. My boss’s favourite phrase is, "Just a little tweak…” which translates to, "Completely rewrite this from scratch."

Right, so, I’ve been trawling Gumtree all afternoon. It’s a right mess, innit? Folk trying to flog anything and everything. Found one bloke offering to 'facilitate' visa applications for, like, a grand. Absolutely mental. A grand? Seriously? That's daylight robbery. Don’t even entertain that. We’ve got the official gov.uk site, haven’t we? Just gotta be patient and fill everything out properly. Did you manage to scan your passport like I asked? Aye, scanned it. And I've started on the application form. It's all a bit… overwhelming, to be honest. They want every detail of me life, don't they? Like they're expecting me to list every chip I've ever eaten. Yeah, a bit. But it's just standard procedure, I reckon. You just gotta be thorough. Have you got your passport photos sorted yet? The ones I took last week were a bit dodgy, apparently. Post office said I blinked. Blinking! They didn’t tell me that when they took my driving license photo. I’ve got a proper squint in that one, lookin’ like I’m trying to solve a riddle. Need to get some fresh ones done, then. Probably tomorrow, I reckon. Think I’ll pop to Boots, they’re usually alright. What about you? I’m going to try a professional studio this time. Worth the extra few quid, I think, to make sure they're spot on. Can’t be messin’ about with visa applications. Speaking of which, how's the donation drive coming along? Any luck with getting that local garage owner to sponsor us? Nah, he said he’s already pledged to another charity this year. Bit gutted, that. He was a good shout. I did try the baker down the street, Mrs. Higgins. She offered us a load of pasties for the rally! Said she’d even bake some extra special ones with a Mongolian twist. Mrs. Higgins is a legend! Pasties are a brilliant idea. We need to promote that – "Fuelled by Higgins' Mongolian Pasties!" - catchy, innit? Have you put up the adverts on Gumtree yet? We need to get some volunteers, especially for driving the support van. Aye, I put 'em up last night. Got a few people asking about it, mostly people offering to sell dodgy satellite dishes. So far, no takers for driving the van, though. Do you think we should widen the search?

Ugh, I’m proper knackered, innit? Like, bone-tired. Feels like I haven’t slept in weeks. Tell me about it. Still aching from lugging you around A&E last night. Seriously, you massively overestimated your strength trying to impress that lad from your history seminar. He seemed alright! And it wasn’t  all  my fault. That climbing frame was treacherous, yeah? Like, a death trap for a short person. You're both being ridiculous. ONE scraped elbow deserves a trip to A&E? You practically had the place shut down with your drama. You looked like you were auditioning for a soap opera, ANON. It swelled up, didn't it? And it was throbbing! Plus, I was freaked out. You know I’m a bit of a wuss when it comes to doctors. You’re a wuss about everything remotely medical. Remember that time you cried because you had a splinter? That splinter was massive! And it was right on my thumb! It felt like I’d caught a bit of wood from a haunted house. Anyway, the point is, I'm tired, and my arm's a bit sore, and I’m pretty sure the fluorescent lights in that hospital are responsible for half of my exhaustion. Speaking of things that are exhausting... how’s the essay going, Liv? You looked like you were about to spontaneously combust in the library yesterday. Don't even. It's awful. Just… awful. I’m staring at the screen and the words just aren't connecting. Like, the topic makes sense in my head, but translating it into coherent academic prose is proving impossible. I think I've hit peak student overwhelm. Need chocolate. Seriously. Like, a family-sized bar. Come on, let's raid the kitchen then. I’m starving. And maybe there's some decent tea… that hospital tea was… questionable. Good plan. I'll make a pot. And Liv, seriously, step away from the essay for an hour. Go for a walk, listen to some music. You’re just spinning your wheels at this point. Right, found some biscuits. Not chocolate, sadly. Just digestives. Will that do, Liv? Digestives are acceptable in a crisis. Thanks. You know, that lad from history – what was his name, Finn? – he actually seemed quite nice when we were waiting for the doctor. He offered me his cardigan when I was shivering. Finn! Yeah, he’s alright.

Right then, love. That was a grand do, wasn't it? Though I'm absolutely knackered now. My feet are screaming. Yeah, it was alright, Gran. A bit… loud, maybe? Uncle Barry kept trying to get me to play darts with him. You know he cheats. Oh, Barry. Aye, he does. Always has. Though, he’s just being friendly, isn’t he? Trying to engage the young’uns. It’s nice to see everyone together though, isn't it? Especially after the year we've had. Your Auntie Carol was beaming, bless her. She was. She kept showing everyone pictures of the new cat. Like, for twenty minutes. Twenty minutes, Gran. Just photos. Well, she’s proud of Mittens. They’ve been wanting a pet for ages. You did seem a bit bored though, didn't you? I noticed you mostly stuck to your phone. It was a bit… repetitive. All the reminiscing. All “Remember when you were this high, son?” and “Did you ever think you’d be here today, lass?” It’s all a bit much, innit? Aye, it can be. But it's important, love. It's grounding. It reminds us where we come from, and who we are. Fifty years of marriage for your dad and your Auntie Carol. That’s something to celebrate, isn't it? It’s not every couple that manages that. Yeah, I guess. It's just… all the talk about the past. I'd rather talk about, you know, what's  going  to happen. Future stuff. Like, I'm thinking about applying for that apprenticeship at Siemens next year. Oh, really? That's excellent news, love! Siemens, you say? That’s a good, solid company. What sort of apprenticeship? Electrical engineering, apparently. It’s a four-year thing, with college and work. It’s quite competitive, I think. Well, you're a clever lad, aren't you? Always good at your maths. Speaking of which, how's your A-Level studies going? Mr. Harrison seemed pleased when I bumped into him at the supermarket the other day. Said you were doing well in calculus. It's alright. It’s a lot of work. I'm trying to pace myself. This party took a lot out of me. I can imagine. Long day for everyone. Your mum was in the kitchen all afternoon, making that fancy lemon drizzle cake. She does go all out, doesn't she?

Are we nearly there yet, Dad? My bum’s numb. Seriously, this is taking forever. Now, now, Elara. Don’t be like that. We’ve barely been driving six hours. Cornwall's a fair trek, lass, even in this motor. You’ve got your water bottle, haven’t you? Don't want you getting dehydrated. Yeah, yeah, I’ve got it. Though I’m going to need a refill soon. And could you maybe stop moaning about Yorkshire puddings? I’m starving. Are we having lunch soon? I’m thinking a pasty. A proper Cornish pasty, not one of those shop-bought things. Right you are. We'll aim for around Plymouth. See if we can find a decent cafe. I was thinking a bit of a pub lunch actually, roast dinner. Proper Yorkshire puds included, mind. Got to represent the North! You and your puddings. Honestly. Did you pack any pens? I need to do a bit of revision, just in case. Examiners are wicked this year, apparently. They've changed the syllabus again, haven't they? It’s just not fair. Pens? Aye, got a whole bag of ‘em. Why do you need to revise on holiday? You deserve a break. All those Latin verbs… I know, but… it's just in the back of my mind. Plus, I want to be ahead for next term. It's A-Levels, Dad! It’s serious! Remember that time Mrs. Davies made me dissect a frog? I still have nightmares. Aye, I do recall that. Poor frog. Speaking of nightmares, the traffic was horrendous around Bristol, wasn't it? Like rush hour, but at two in the afternoon. Makes you wonder what people are doing. Probably all on Amazon, buying stuff they don't need and getting it delivered. Probably. Or watching DVDs on their tablets. I've been wanting to watch Jurassic Park again. Remember going to see it at the cinema when I was little? That T-Rex… terrifying! Aye, that it were. Changed the game, that film. Thinking about things changing, we've still got to sort out the movers for the new house, haven’t we? I need to ring them tomorrow. Trying to find somewhere with a decent washing machine is proving surprisingly difficult. And a cat flap! Definitely need a cat flap for Marmalade. Marmalade trying to escape through a closed window again, I bet.

Honestly, David, this is just…heartbreaking. Look at her, beaming. She seemed so full of life then. That’s your sister, isn’t it? Eleanor? It was quite a graduation, if I recall correctly. You all drove up in that dreadful Volvo of your father’s. Dreadful is an understatement. It smelled permanently of damp dog and disappointment. And yes, that’s Eleanor. Before…everything. Do you remember how proud she was? Top of her class, scholarship to Oxford… Eleanor was a marvel. A bright spark, that girl. A proper scholar. I remember interviewing her for the bursary. She had such fire in her eyes. Such…ambition. You were so good to her, Aunt Margaret. You really believed in her. More than anyone, I think. One recognised talent when one saw it, dear. And Eleanor had talent to spare. Dash it all, she was meant to do great things. Such a waste. A dreadful, dreadful waste. Tell me, are you all keeping up with the legal proceedings properly, Susan? As much as one can. It’s a shambles, frankly. They keep shifting the goalposts. The defense is arguing diminished responsibility, claiming…well, claiming everything but the obvious. It's barbaric to trawl through these details. Right. Er, I brought that cable you asked for, Susan. For the telly. Needed a bit of fiddling, but I’ve got it sorted now. Anything else I can do? Oh, thank you, Gareth. That's lovely, really. I… I don't know. I'm a bit preoccupied at the moment. Gareth, good to see you. Did you manage to get that replacement hinge for the kitchen cupboard? I’ve been meaning to mention it. Aye, no bother. Got it this morning. Just need a quiet hour to slot it in. Been a bit hectic lately. Orders are up, you know. People actually want bespoke furniture again. It's mad, really. Bespoke furniture? Good heavens. That's a pleasant change from the particle board monstrosities they sell these days. Though I wouldn't mind a decent sideboard myself. Mine's seen better days. Oak, you know, properly seasoned. Not that modern stuff. Aunt Margaret, please. Not the sideboard. Not right now. Eleanor’s case is…it’s draining, Susan. You need to try and detach. Gareth's right, focusing on something practical can sometimes…helps. Even a hinge. Detach? How can I detach, David? My sister… She’s the one in court, facing charges that… it's beyond comprehension.

Right, so, plans for Mother’s Day are… percolating. Still percolating, actually. I was thinking, we could do the Forest School thing again? Remember how much they both loved building dens last time? Dens! Yes! And finding sticks! Big sticks! Can I find the biggest stick ever, Mummy? Can we make a fairy house this time, Mum? Not just a den. A tiny house with… with moss and flowers. Absolutely, darling. A fairy house sounds brilliant. We could even gather some sparkly things. It’ll be much more magical than a den. Though, Leo, you  do  need to remember those sticks are for building, not for whacking each other, alright? I know, Mum! I wouldn’t. Alright then. So, Forest School it is. I'll check the weather tomorrow morning and book a slot. Do you two want to choose what we have for lunch? I was thinking something simple, maybe sandwiches and fruit? Squeezy cheese sandwiches! And strawberries! Lots and lots of strawberries! Can we have those little cocktail sausages? The ones with the pineapple rings? Cocktail sausages? Alright, alright, you’ve twisted my arm. Little sausages it is. And maybe we can decorate cupcakes later? I found that lovely icing. Cupcakes! With sprinkles! Pink sprinkles! Pink sprinkles it is. Right, let's see… Forest School, sausages, strawberries, pink sprinkles... I’m feeling a bit like a plate spinning act at the moment, aren’t I? What's a plate spinning act, Mum? Well, imagine you're trying to keep lots of plates spinning in the air at the same time. It's hard work, isn't it? You have to concentrate really hard, or they all fall! Wow! Can we learn to do that? Not today, sweetheart, but maybe when you're older. It's a bit tricky. Speaking of tricky, I was trying to explain that idiom 'break a leg' to a student today. They were completely baffled. Break a leg? Why would you want to do  that ? It sounds really bad! Exactly! That's the funny thing. It doesn’t mean you actually  want  to break someone's leg. It's a way of wishing them good luck, especially before a performance. It’s a bit of an old theatrical thing. Like saying "good luck" but in a silly way. So, if I was going to do a really good dance, you'd say “break a leg?”

Honestly, Sarah, I just don’t know what to do. Mum’s been… distant. Ever since the appointment. She won’t talk about it properly, just keeps saying “it’s being managed.” Managed! Like a leaky tap. Managed how, love? Has she told you what they said exactly? I know she tends to downplay things. Remember when she broke her wrist and said it was just a "bit of a twinge"? Exactly! That’s her. The consultant said… well, it’s secondary breast cancer. It’s spread to her bones. They’re starting chemo next week. She keeps saying she’s fine, that it’s “just a blip.” A blip! It’s devastating. And she's hiding it from Dad. Oh, love. That's… that’s awful. I’m so sorry. You’re right, the denial is strong with her. Staffordshire women, eh? We bottle everything up. But keeping it from your Dad… that’s cruel, isn’t it? Even if he’d be upset, he deserves to know. He’d be… a mess. A complete mess. He's always been so reliant on her. They practically breathe the same air. I tried to gently suggest she tell him, but she just waved me away and said, "Don't you worry your pretty little head about it." As if I'm still a teenager! Classic Mum behaviour, then. Always trying to shield you. Look, you need to be strong for both of them. Have you spoken to your brother, Tom? I texted him. He said he’s busy with work, which I understand, but he always seems to be busy these days. He's so focused on his promotion, it's all he talks about. I half expected a 'thoughts and prayers' emoji. Don't be like that about Tom. He's probably just… overwhelmed. It’s a lot to take in, even from a distance. Has he even visited recently? Not properly. Last Christmas. He claimed he was working, but… well, we all knew. It's always an excuse with him. Makes me feel guilty, but also, frustrated. Mum always did favour him, you know that. Always praising him, letting him get away with things. It used to drive me mad as a child. I remember. You were always the ‘sensible’ one. But don’t let that bitterness cloud things now, love. This isn’t about childhood rivalries. This is about supporting your mum.

Right, okay. That last lecture on comparative phonology absolutely drained me. My brain feels like a damp sponge. Fancy a cuppa? Please! Desperately. I think Professor Davies is actively trying to break us with his enthusiasm for the International Phonetic Alphabet. Seriously, who needs to know the exact placement of the tongue for the velar nasal? It's crucial, apparently! He went on for fifteen minutes about the subtle differences between Korean and Japanese articulation of /ŋ/. Did you manage to follow along with his explanation of Korean vowel harmony? Lost me around the first plosive. I’m starting to think my Linguistics degree was a monumental mistake. Although, I did find that bit about the sociolinguistic implications of dialect shifting in Kent interesting. See! There's  something  you enjoy. Speaking of Kent, Mum texted. She wants to know if we’re coming for Sunday dinner. She's making her famous roast. Oh, God. The roast. Last time I had that much gravy, I felt like I was swimming. And let's be honest, Dad will invariably start a lecture on the proper way to carve a joint. I’ll bring the oatcakes, at least. They may distract him. Good thinking. Oatcakes are a strategic food group. I was thinking, actually, about that Korean cooking class I saw advertised online. Really? Kimchi everything? I'm tempted, but the thought of fermenting anything for days on end is… unsettling. Though I do enjoy bibimbap. We should try making that. Exactly! And bulgogi, maybe? We’ve got loads of veg in the freezer, thanks to the last supermarket run. Should we hit Aldi later? Their prices are insane. Aldi is a battlefield. I went last week and nearly got trampled by a pensioner wielding a cabbage. But yes, good point. I need more lentils and that weird Italian cheese my mum bought me. Did you see that article about the ethics of factory farming? It's been keeping me up at night. I did. It's… bleak. I'm trying to be better about buying less meat, honestly. It’s just so convenient, you know? I saw a game on Marketplace, too. Grand Theft Auto, apparently. Looks pretty cheap. Thought you might be interested. GTA? Really? Which one? I've been craving a proper gaming session. That's brilliant! Do you think it's legit? Seems so. Says the bloke lives just around the corner.

Honestly, this pepperoni is doing wonders for my mood. Physics is trying to actively destroy me right now. Like, why does it  need  to be so complicated? Tell me about it. I'm battling with vectors. I swear, they're just moving around taunting me. At least pizza doesn't move around and taunt you. Proper grub this is. Reminds me of my Nan’s cooking, bless her. She used to make the best cheese and onion pasties. Vectors taunting you? That’s brilliant, Liv! You’ve got a talent for that kind of description. Anyway, talking about destroying moods… did anyone else see those pictures of Lancaster Quay? The flooding is unreal. I’m genuinely worried about the campus – will lectures even be on next week? It's awful, isn't it? Proper heartbreaking. My Mum sent me a text saying they're just bracing for more rain. Thankfully, we’re up on the hill a bit, so we're safe. Though I’m starting to get a bit paranoid about leaking roofs. Want to move some important stuff upstairs, just in case. Speaking of things getting wet... remember that camping trip to the Lake District? Oh god, don't remind me. The tent collapsing at 3 am, getting eaten alive by midges... and Sarah’s new sleeping bag ending up soaked through. Sarah did look a bit peak that morning. I still think we should’ve packed those waterproof trousers. Remember how we joked about needing Noah's Ark for that trip? Speaking of needing things... I’m still trying to find my sports kit tops. I’m convinced they’ve been abducted by the washing machine monster. Anyone seen them? Nope, haven’t seen them. Though, I did find that weird fluffy thing behind the sofa the other day. Pretty sure it was part of one of your jumpers, Chloe. That's probably it! Thanks. Right, back to suffering. I'm stuck on this problem about projectile motion. It's referencing  Cloud Atlas  in a way that feels deeply unfair. Like, I need to understand sentient clones AND quadratic equations at the same time? Honestly, the degree courses these days... it's mad, innit? Have you read  Chaos Walking  trilogy? It's got loads of mad physics going on, but in a much more entertaining way than a textbook. Oh, I loved  Chaos Walking ! The whole "noise" thing was brilliant.

Right, so, you're  sure  this is a good idea? Like, really, really sure? Because I’m already feeling a bit… frayed, to be honest. The indexing on the Dickens corpus went mental again this morning. It’s like the man deliberately wanted to trip me up. Come on, Beth. Relax. It’ll be brilliant. You need to get out of Sunderland for a bit. Fresh air, new scenery… it’s good for the soul. And it’s my mum’s birthday, so it’s not just a random trip, is it? Besides, you've been stuck in front of those digital pages for weeks. You’re practically glowing with LED light. Glowing with stress, more like. And it's not a “bit” of fresh air, is it? It’s a four-hour drive to the Cotswolds! My backside’s gonna be numb. And I still don’t understand why we’re having a full-blown country house affair for your mum’s 60th. Couldn't we have just done a nice pub lunch? With actual, you know, Yorkshire puddings? She’s always wanted a proper garden party. And your mum’s got a soft spot for you, you know that. Plus, it's a chance to see all the family that's scattered around. Uncle Richard’s coming over from Australia, remember? You haven't seen him since you were, what, ten? Australia… spiders... no thanks. And I’m pretty sure last time I saw Uncle Richard, he tried to teach me how to whittle miniature kangaroos. Ended up nearly losing a finger. Look, it’s just… posh. I’m not really wired for ‘posh.’ I’d rather be at the Seaburn amusements, eating fish and chips. You'll be fine. Just don't try to start a conversation about the nuances of chip shop vinegar. Trust me. And it's not  that  posh. It’s a lovely old house, no stuffy airs and graces. Think less Downton Abbey, more… slightly overgrown country manor. Slightly overgrown, yeah. That still sounds terrifying to me. Actually, speaking of terrifying… remember that time at school, when Mrs. Hawthorne made us do that presentation on the French Revolution? Oh, please don't remind me. My voice cracked  constantly . It was mortifying. I swear I lost a year of my life right there and then. Aye, but you were alright, weren't you? I nearly had a full-blown panic attack.

Cor blimey, this drizzle ain’t lettin' up, is it? Reminds me of a proper Costessey autumn - grey as a badger’s bottom. Used to be you could rely on a bit o’ sunshine, even in November. Not anymore, mind. All this climate change, they say. Don't make a jot o' sense, does it? Used to be predictable, this weather. You could set your clock by it. Don’t start on the weather, Arthur. You'll only get yourself worked up. It’s just a bit of rain. At least it’s not snow, eh? Remember that winter of '78? Couldn't get out for a week. The kids were delighted, of course – snowball fights and everything. Though I was run ragged trying to keep them entertained. Mum's right, Dad. It's cozy inside. And at least the garden's getting a good soaking. My hydrangeas were starting to look a bit peaky. Speaking of which, how are your knees today? You were limping a bit yesterday. Oh, they’re the same, love. Always the same. A bit creaky, a bit achey. Doctor says it’s old age catching up. What can you do, eh? Should’ve taken up knitting instead of… well, never you mind what I should’ve taken up. The football’s been the only thing keepin’ me going, really. Did you see Norwich's game on Saturday, Arthur? Absolutely dreadful! They were playing like they'd never met before. I honestly don't know what the manager's doing. Bringing on Williamson in the 70th minute? Madness! Complete madness! Oh, David, you always get so worked up about football. It's just a game. Though I do agree, they weren’t playing well. Still, it's nice to have something to talk about, isn’t it? Especially with this weather. It  is  nice to have something to talk about. Though I'm a bit overwhelmed by the football chat, I admit. I'm more interested in how Nan's feeling. You mentioned she's been having trouble sleeping, Mum? Yes, dear. It’s been a bit of a bother. Keeps her up half the night. Says she can't stop thinking. I told her to try listening to some music, but she just stubbornly insists she'll be fine. You know your grandmother. She's a headstrong one. Strong as an ox, that one. Never did complain much, even when times were hard.

Honestly, the seating plan is driving me insane. It's like a giant Sudoku puzzle made of family drama. Aunt Carol  absolutely  cannot sit next to Cousin Brian. You know that, right? It's a recipe for disaster. Seriously? Still on that? You've been wrestling with it for days. Just put them on opposite ends of the table and be done with it. It's a wedding, not a political summit. Easy for you to say, you don’t have to deal with the fallout if Carol starts loudly accusing Brian of stealing her prize-winning marrow at the village fete twenty years ago. Oh god, remember that marrow? It was massive! It looked like a small child was living inside. Exactly! And don't even get me started on trying to place Liam and his girlfriend. They've been together, like, six weeks. Is it too soon to put them next to each other? Will everyone think I'm suggesting they're rushing things? Six weeks is definitely rushing things for a wedding! But truthfully, they're probably already planning on spending most of the time glued to their phones anyway. Don't stress about it. Let the chaos unfold. Honestly, your face is permanently creased these days. You need a break. She does. We all do. This wedding planning obsession is a bit much, even for me and I’m usually all about aesthetics and clever colour palettes. I'm currently wrestling with finding the perfect shade of blush pink for the napkins. It’s crucial, apparently. Crucial, apparently! See? You get it! It’s a domino effect. Pink napkins lead to pink table runners, which requires a specific floral arrangement, which… you get the picture. Speaking of weddings, have you heard anything about Chloe and Mark? Are they still on for October? Last I heard, they're still planning. Mark’s been super stressed with work though. Apparently, the new marketing campaign is a nightmare. He's practically living in the office. Poor thing. Though, knowing Mark, he's probably just enjoying the attention of his team. He’s a charmer, that one. He is. Remember that time he convinced Mrs. Davies at the ice cream parlour that he was a food critic just to get a free waffle cone? Oh my god, yes! I'd completely forgotten. That was brilliant. He's always been one to avoid paying for things.

Cor, this brew’s a bit weak, innit? Not like Mrs. Higgins used to make. She could brew a cuppa that’d put hairs on yer chest. Proper strong. Now, Arthur, don't you start complaining. It’s perfectly decent. And Mrs. Higgins, bless her, added a spoonful of molasses to everything. A bit much, even for me. At least ANON remembered the biscuits. Chocolate digestives, my favourite. Molasses, though? That’s a flavour I’ve only ever encountered in treacle toffee. You wouldn’t get that in Birmingham, not unless you were deliberately trying to recreate your grandma’s cooking. Everything's a bit more… refined these days. Though refined doesn't always mean  better , does it? Tell me about it. Used to be, a proper cuppa was a proper thing. Now it’s all fancy coffee machines and… and… those things that froth the milk! What's the point of that? Looks like a rabbit’s been sick in your mug. You’re terrible, Arthur! But he’s got a point. It’s all become so complicated. Remember when a game of cards was all we needed for an afternoon? None of this online gaming nonsense. My grandson, Liam, he’s glued to that screen all day. Says he’s ‘leveling up’ or something. Don’t even get me started on the technology. I teach ICT at the secondary school, and honestly, half the kids can barely turn the computer on. They’re experts at gaming, yes, but ask them to write a simple email, or research a historical event… it’s a challenge. It's brilliant in some ways, access to information like never before, but it's creating a generation utterly dependent. My daughter, Sarah, she wouldn't know how to use a map if her life depended on it. Blames the sat nav, of course. Sat navs! Another thing. Got us lost in Swaffham last year. Led me straight into a field full of sheep. Sheep, I tell you! Couldn't get the thing to recalculate. Ended up have to ask a farmer for directions, lookin' a right fool. You and your sheep, Arthur. You always manage to find some sort of trouble. Remember when you tried to train that pony, Jasper? Jasper was a stubborn beast, that's what he was. Should've sold him when I had the chance. Cost me a fortune in carrots and farrier bills.

Honestly, Arthur, it’s been ages! It feels like forever since we last properly chatted. How are you keeping? Alright, alright. Can’t complain, Annie. The bones creak a bit more these days, you know, but the sun's been shining, and that does wonders for a fella. Lovely tea, by the way. Strong, just how I like it. You’ve a good hand with a kettle, you do. Thank you! Glad you like it. So, what have you been up to? Still pottering about in the garden, I hope? I remember you had a prize-winning marrow last summer. The marrow was a thing of beauty, it was. Beaten it was, though. Elsie next door, she always has a trick up her sleeve. But yes, the garden keeps me occupied. Though the slugs are having a right field day this year. You wouldn't believe the size of 'em. Oh, the slugs! I know the feeling. I had a disastrous attempt at growing courgettes last year – completely decimated. I’ve decided to stick to herbs and flowers this year. Less heartbreak, you see. Tell me, are you still going to the bowls club? Trying to, yes. My back's not always cooperating, mind you. Used to be a sprightly bowler, I was. Captain of the team, even. Now… well, I mostly watch. Enjoy the company, that’s the main thing. What about you, Annie? Still teaching languages? Yes, still plugging away! It’s busy, but I love it. I’ve got a new class starting next week - a group of adults learning Italian. They’re incredibly enthusiastic - a real mixed bag of ages and backgrounds. Always fascinating to see how people approach a new language. Italian, eh? Always fancied learning a bit of Italian myself. Sounded lovely, all that rolling 'r's and gesturing. Never got around to it, though. Too busy with… other things. Never too late to start! It’s surprisingly accessible, actually. A lot of Latin roots, which you might remember from school. You always were a clever lad, Arthur. Managed to run a whole company, didn't you? That’s impressive. Oh, that. It was a job. A lot of fuss for a lot of money, if you ask me. Stressful, much too stressful. Wouldn't trade my quiet retirement for all the managing director titles in the world. Though, I did miss it something fierce for the first few years after I left.

Honestly, Chloe, Valentine's Day. What a load of… well, you know. Tell me about it! Felt like every shop was plastered with hearts and roses. It was a bit much, innit? Like, aggressively romantic. Aggressively is the perfect word. Like they're  forcing  you to feel something. And the price of chocolates! Don't even get me started. I went to Boots to grab a card for my nan, and it was like robbing a bank. Yeah, it’s all a bit manufactured, isn’t it? My mum was saying the same thing, moaning about how much she spent on flowers for my dad. She says it's just another way for businesses to fleece people. Proper Midlands logic, that. You always let your mum's logic shine through! Makes me miss a proper cuppa. This canteen tea is… well, it’s canteen tea. So, did you end up doing anything for the night? Anything exciting involving overpriced roses? Nah, nothing like that. Just watched a film at home with my little brother. He's been obsessed with  Everything Everywhere All at Once  - apparently, it's blowing his mind. Ooh, I've heard about that one. Everyone's raving about it. Is it actually any good? I need something to pull me out of this Valentine’s slump. It's brilliant! Properly bonkers, but brilliant. Loads of clever stuff going on. Seriously, give it a watch. We could go to the cinema sometime next week to see something, if you fancy? There’s that new Wes Anderson film out,  Asteroid City  – looks right up our street. Asteroid City? Yeah, I saw the trailer. Looks gorgeous, all retro and quirky. Sounds perfect. We could grab some Nandos afterwards, yeah? I'm craving a peri-peri chicken fix. Nandos always does the trick. Although, last time I went they were completely out of lemon and herb! Absolute chaos. It’s the little things that ruin your day, right? Tell me about it! You know, I had a right disaster trying to do some shopping yesterday. Went to Primark to look for a new jumper – ended up wandering around for an hour and a half, getting pushed and shoved by hordes of people. And then I found  nothing  I liked. Just felt defeated. Oh, Primark on a Saturday… suicide mission. I swear, they design the layout to be as confusing as possible. You need a survival kit just to navigate.

Right, so you’re saying Patel's speech really landed with a thud, even amongst  his  supporters? I mean, the blatant dog-whistling was… audacious, even for him. Honestly, it’s exhausting. Every few months it's back to this, isn’t it? “Strong borders,” “controlling immigration” – all code for "othering" people. It wasn’t just a thud, Elara. It was a sonic boom. You had people actively questioning  him , on Twitter, tagging him. And not the usual suspects, either. More… the carefully curated, patriotic types. They're starting to see, I think. Or at least, they’re nervous about the optics. The backlash from the BAME community was immediate, obviously. Did you see that thread by Fatima on Insta? Absolutely devastating. I did! Brilliant analysis. Though, honestly, sometimes I feel like screaming into the void, you know? Like, we’ve been saying this for years. It's not  new . It's just… relentless. And the cycle just keeps spinning. Yeah, it's a broken record. But maybe a little crack is starting to show. It’s the cognitive dissonance, I reckon. People want to believe in their leaders, in the system. But when that system is actively, visibly, harming people... it’s tough to ignore. Plus, this housing crisis is absolutely fuelling that tension, isn’t it? Every time someone gets evicted because of rising rents, it's another layer of the injustice. Absolutely. And it’s all intertwined, isn’t it? The immigration policies, deliberately manufactured scarcity of housing, the whole drive towards… well, towards maximized profit for a tiny elite. It’s capitalism at its most brutal. My mum was saying the other day, about how her parents could actually  buy  a house in Watford in the 60s… a decent one! With a garden and everything. Now, the thought is laughable. Ludicrous. I’m still living with my parents in Kensal Rise. It’s fine, don’t get me wrong. They're great. But it’s… squashing my dreams a little, isn’t it? The freedom of having your own space, your own life… it just feels further away with every passing month. I’ve been looking at places in Walthamstow, but even there, it's bonkers. Overpriced shoeboxes with shared bathrooms. Tell me about it. I've been looking in Richmond, thinking a bit further out might be doable. But even then… the competition is insane. Every viewing is a zoo.

Honestly, love, I’m a bit of a nervous wreck about little Leo starting nursery next week. It feels… momentous, doesn't it? Like a real chunk of my life is changing. I keep picturing him all alone, you know? Surrounded by strangers. Yeah, I get it, Mum. But honestly, he’ll be fine. He’s a little chatterbox, remember? He’ll make friends in five minutes. And it's good for him, getting used to being around other kids. School's not that far off after all. Think of the stories he'll come home with! I know, I know, you're right. It's just... I’m going back to work full time too, isn’t it? It's been lovely having him home all this time, even with the exhaustion. Suddenly going back to the office feels a bit like, well, a shock to the system. I miss him already just thinking about it! Mrs. Davies at the nursery seems lovely, though. She did reassure me about the settling-in process. She did seem really nice when I went with you. And you’ve got a good job, Mum. You deserve to go back and do your thing. It’s not like you’ve been sat around doing nothing! And think about it, a bit more money for holidays! We need to start planning something proper. Holidays… yes. We do. I’ve been looking at Greece, actually. Kos, maybe? Nice beaches, not too far to fly. Remember that trip we did to Crete when you were little? You were obsessed with the sand. Oh god, I remember! I built the most enormous sandcastle, and then a wave just completely destroyed it. I was devastated. Greece would be brilliant, though. More appealing than Butlin’s, that’s for sure. Remember that disaster?! Oh, don't remind me! The rain and the seagulls… Never again. Though, you did seem to love the high ropes course. I did! I was fearless. Now I get vertigo just looking at a ladder. Anyway, back to Leo. What about weaning? He's nearly six months, isn’t he? Are you sticking with purees, or are you thinking of finger foods? That’s another thing I’m stressing about! I’ve read so many conflicting articles. Some say purees until they're practically a year old, others are all about letting them explore food themselves.

Right then, everyone dig in. It’s not quite Mum’s, but it’ll do. So, Anon, how was the police station? You look like you’ve seen a ghost. Aye, you look right drained, love. Giving a statement can't be easy, especially about something like this. You alright? Need a cuppa? Is everything okay, Anon? You didn’t have to do that, you know. We could have handled it. Absolutely. Letting the police get involved… risky. Did they put any pressure on you? Don’t get ahead of yourselves. It’s just standard procedure, apparently. They wanted a formal account. Honestly, the questions… it felt like I was the one on trial. They kept circling back to the timeline, wanting absolute confirmation of exactly where I was at what time. As if I'd conveniently misplaced a few hours. They’re just covering themselves, lass. Can't fault them for that. Best to be thorough. Did you tell them about the… the incident in the car park? I… I mentioned it. Briefly. I didn’t go into all the details. Honestly, reliving it… it's awful enough without having to lay it all out for a room full of suits. And the questioning about Mr. Davies’ whereabouts… it’s all a bit unsettling. He’s been avoiding me all week, the slippery fox. That’s proper creepy, Anon. You should definitely keep your distance. Did you mention the CCTV footage to them? The one from the shop across the street? It might help corroborate your story. I did! But apparently, the quality isn’t great. They said it's “difficult to discern.” Typical. It's clear as day to me! You can see the bloke pushing him. Honestly, bureaucracy. Bureaucracy's the lifeblood of it all, isn’t it? Right, moving on from that gloomy business. Anyone seen my EE bill? It's gone walkabout again. I swear, they're charging me for talking to the wall these days. It’s robbery, pure and simple. Honestly, twenty quid for a few texts and a couple of calls to Doreen about the raffle tickets. Daylight robbery. I think I saw it on the kitchen counter earlier, David. Underneath that pile of takeaway menus? Blast! You’re right, Sarah. Twenty-seven pounds! And what's this charge for "premium data services"? I haven’t downloaded anything premium in my life! I mostly just look at cat videos.

Right, so you’re saying his gladiatorial training was  brutal ? I mean, I know the Romans weren't exactly known for their gentle methods, but Spartacus… the details are grim, aren’t they? I watched that show, of course, the Starz one. Andy Whitfield, brilliant. Shame about him, though, wasn’t it? Such a waste. Brutal’s an understatement, mate. They’d break your back just for looking at the wrong person. And Whitfield… yeah, proper sad. I’d been following him a bit, thought he had serious potential. Cancer, right? At his age? It's mad, innit? Makes you think. Makes you appreciate a good cuppa. This Earl Grey’s decent. Much better than that stuff Mum buys – tastes like dishwater. Mum's tea is a... specific experience. This is a decent blend, yeah. I’m trying to get into herbal teas myself, branching out. Got a load of dried herbs from that little shop in town. Rosemary, thyme, even some saffron – a bit extravagant, I know. Thinking of making some proper spiced chickpeas. I’ve got some lovely pitta bread too. Fancy some? Chickpeas, yeah, sounds good. Need a proper mortar and pestle though, to really get the spices in, you know? Blending them in a food processor just doesn't have the same... oomph. My Nan had one, solid granite. Used to make the best pesto with it. I’ve been meaning to get one. Probably end up spending a fortune on something I use once a month. Exactly! It’s the logic, isn't it? Like, you look at somethings and think, 'This is essential!' Then you never actually use it. Remember that ridiculous tat I bought in China? That little ceramic panda playing a flute? Vaguely. You dragged that thing out every Christmas for years. Was terrible. Though, I remember you were obsessed with getting it. Something about cultural significance? I was young and impressionable! And desperate for a souvenir. Anyway, what are you up to besides, you know, wrestling with rhododendrons and battling slugs? Any good music? Anything new you’re into? Been listening to a bit of Fontaines D.C. – good stuff. Gritty, you know? Reminds me a bit of The Strokes. And I discovered this Cypriot band - Evdokia. Proper atmospheric. Their singer’s voice is… haunting. My Grandpa listens to them non-stop. Says it reminds him of his childhood. Cypriot, eh? I’ve always wanted to go.

Honestly, this English test felt like a personal attack. Like, why did Mrs. Davies have to pick  that  poem? “The Raven”? Who even  likes  Edgar Allan Poe? Everything was just… bleak. Tell me about it. I spent half an hour just trying to figure out what a "bleak December" even meant. Ms. Harding kept saying we needed to analyse the symbolism, but all I saw was a sad bird. Exactly! Symbolism? I’m trying to pass, not write a PhD thesis. And the essay question! "Discuss the role of atmosphere in creating a sense of unease." Seriously? She’s setting us up to fail, innit? She does love a bit of drama, doesn't she? Remember last year with the Dickens one? Everyone was sobbing about Tiny Tim, and she was all, "Excellent emotional engagement!" It's just... exhausting sometimes. It is. I need a serious sugar rush after that. Fancy sharing some of those biscuits your mum made? The ones with the jam and coconut? Definitely. Mum went a bit mad this week. Made too much, she said. They’re still warm. So, did you at least manage to do the ‘macabre’ bit in your answer? Like, the spooky stuff? Sort of. I wrote something about the raven being a harbinger of doom and a symbol of lost love. Sounded a bit cliché, even to me, but it was all I could think of. What about you? Did you try and be clever? I tried. I wrote something about the darkness mirroring the narrator’s inner turmoil or something. It sounds way more impressive when you say it out loud. I’m proper worried though. I used a thesaurus for, like, half the essay. Now I’m scared Ms. Harding will think I’m trying to sound all fancy. Oh god, yeah. The thesaurus risk. Classic. I just stuck to basic words. Played it safe. Actually, speaking of playing safe, are you still thinking about auditioning for the wind band? Yeah, but I’m still nervous. Mrs. Peterson said I have potential with the flute, but… you know. Stage fright. What about you? Are you still considering the clarinet? I think so. I quite enjoy it, actually. It's nice to do something that isn’t about analysing some old dead poet. It’s just… fun. No pressure. Plus, Liam's in it. That's a bonus. Liam, always a bonus!

Och, look at that rain, love. Proper miserable it is this afternoon. Reminds me of a November day back in Darlington when I were a lass. Everything grey and dripping. Aye, it’s chucking it down. Makes you want to just stay in, doesn’t it? Playing FIFA. FIFA, eh? Still addicted then? You’ll be forgetting how to talk proper if you spend all your time shouting at a screen. Leave him be, Brenda. He’s just a lad. And besides, at least he’s not spending all day watching those dreadful reality shows like some people I know. Now, Elsie, don't you start. "Love Island" gives me a good laugh. It's a bit of a laugh, like, and something to take your mind off things. You’ve been moaning about your pension statement again, haven’t you? Don’t remind me! It's a pittance, Brenda, a pittance! Used to be able to treat myself to a nice bit of seafood, now I’m lucky if I can get a packet of frozen peas. All this talk of inflation, it's scandalous. Grandad says the government’s messed up the economy, because of… something. He was ranting about it last night. Something about a flag and a brand. Oh, he'll be on about Brexit, won't he? Your Grandad’s got a strong opinion on that one. Honestly, you can’t mention the word “Europe” around him without expecting a full-blown debate. He always was a proper staunch one, your dad. Remember when he argued with Mr. Henderson at the cricket club about the cricket whites? Said they weren't Yorkshire enough. Oh, I do! He spent a good hour ranting about the colour being too pale. Made Mr. Henderson’s face go redder than the whites themselves! You wouldn't catch him wearing anything that wasn’t proper Yorkshire, would you? He's the same with accents. Keeps telling me to drop the ‘th’ sounds. Says I sound like a Geordie, not a proper Yorkshireman. And you're letting him, are you? Don’t you go changing your accent for anyone, lad! It’s part of who you are. Besides, a good Yorkshire accent is the best accent there is. It is, isn’t it? Strong and proud. Though, mind you, my Mam used to say I sounded like a Hull trawler when I were a kid.

Right, so Dad, you were saying about the new exhaust on Brenda’s Vauxhall? It sounded like a proper saga. Saga is right, love. Right proper kerfuffle. The bloke at the garage, young lad, barely out of his teens, insisted it was a catalytic converter fault. Said I’d need a new one, cost me near on six hundred quid! Six hundred! I told him, "Look here, son, I've been sniffing petrol fumes for fifty years, I know a dodgy exhaust when I hear one." Turned out, it was just a loose clamp. A loose clamp! Men! Always fiddling. Should’ve just let me have a go. I once fixed a lawnmower engine with a bit of string and some chewing gum. Mum, you fixed a lawnmower with chewing gum? Really? Don't you give me any cheek, Daniel. That was back in '78. Things were different then. Everything broke down, and you had to make do. And back then, people weren’t all concerned about their BMI and whatnot. You ate what you wanted and you were right as rain. These youngsters... all obsessed with scales and calories. Honestly, it's a wonder anyone manages to enjoy a Sunday roast. Well, there is a lot to be said for moderation, Mum. And it's not  just  about weight, it's about health, isn’t it? There’s definitely a genetic component too, you know. My cousin, Sarah, she can eat a whole cake and not put an ounce on, while I have to look at a biscuit and my jeans tighten. That’s your mum’s side, isn’t it? All that fancy academic talk. Genes, shmenes. It's what you put in your belly, that’s what matters. And a bit of exercise, though I haven't done much of that lately. Knees aren't what they used to be. Speaking of health, how’s your knee after the operation, Grandad? Are you still having phantom pains? Phantom pains are a right nuisance, Daniel. Gets ya in the middle of the night. Like there's a dentist tryin' to drill into ya. But the surgeon said it was a success, didn't he? Best he could have hoped for, given the state it was in. Years of crawling under cars, you know. Takes its toll. It must be awful. Are you taking the medication regularly? Dr. Davies said it’s crucial, especially for the inflammation.

Honestly, Ben, I’m pulling my hair out. Moodle is actively trying to sabotage my lesson on Boolean logic. It's just… infuriating. Boolean logic, eh? Sounds delightfully complex. What’s Moodle done this time? Don't tell me it’s decided to randomly shuffle the quiz questions  again . Worse, actually. I’ve spent the afternoon building this tutorial – a layered approach, you know, starting with simple examples, gradually increasing complexity. I even included some interactive elements using that… what’s it called… H5P. H5P? Right, the thing you were raving about last week. Thought you were quite pleased with it. I  was  pleased! It’s brilliant for visualising logic gates, really helps the students grasp the concept. But apparently, Moodle hates H5P and decided to render half of it as blank boxes. Blank. Boxes! And now I'm wrestling with embedding another video, and the player keeps defaulting to 144p. I’m trying to get them to understand binary, and they’re getting a pixelated mess! Pixelated binary. That’s a new one. Have you tried clearing your browser cache? Sometimes that sorts out the rendering issues. Of course I've tried clearing the cache! I’ve tried every browser, every device, I even restarted the router. It’s Moodle’s fault, I tell you. It’s inherently resistant to anything beyond the most basic text assignment. Remember last term when I tried to upload a PDF with embedded hyperlinks? It turned it into a series of images. Right, okay. Let’s take a breath. It’s just Moodle. We all know it's a monster. What did you have in mind to fix the H5P issue specifically? Did you try manually updating the plugin? The plugin's up to date. I've gone through the troubleshooting guide three times. It’s… it's like it's  choosing  to be difficult. I'm half tempted to just abandon H5P and tell them to draw their logic gates on paper. Can you imagine? “Students, please illustrate AND and OR gates using coloured pencils and rulers.” That’ll go down well. It'll be a talking point, certainly. Though perhaps not the kind you want. Look, why don't you show me the H5P code? Maybe a fresh pair of eyes can spot something you've missed. I’ve been working with Javascript a bit more lately, maybe I can pick up on something.

Oh, goodness. My brain feels like a bowl of porridge. Did you manage to sleep at all last night? I think I was awake for a good two hours just staring at the ceiling, convinced I could hear the neighbours arguing about garden gnomes. Garden gnomes? Seriously? My jetlag manifested as an insistent need to alphabetize the spice rack at 3 AM. It wasn’t quite as dramatic as your neighbourly feud, but equally pointless. I think I managed about four hours scattered throughout the night. The little one seemed to sense we were both running on fumes and decided to join the party around 5:30. The little one. Right. Leo's timing is impeccable, isn't it? Always knows when we're at our most vulnerable. Did he at least give us a cute smile while he was demanding breakfast? He did, actually. A proper gummy grin, showing off a new tooth. Made the 5:30 wake-up call almost bearable. Though followed swiftly by a demand for my phone and a surprisingly accurate impression of a teething lion. Sounds about right. So, are we human enough to discuss anything other than the offspring’s current needs and our collective exhaustion? Absolutely. I was thinking about that production of  The Importance of Being Earnest  at the Playhouse. Tickets are still available, apparently, for Saturday evening. Fancy it? I know you’ve been wanting to see it. Oh, clever you! That's rather perfect timing. It would be absolutely lovely. It's been ages since we’ve actually done something just for us, hasn't it? The last theatre trip involved strategically positioned snacks and constant vigilance against rogue balls launched by nearby children. Exactly. A rogue-ball-free evening sounds divine. We could even have a proper dinner beforehand. Perhaps that new Italian place, 'Bella Notte'? I've heard good things. Bella Notte… that does sound tempting. Though, logistically, are we even capable of arranging a babysitter? It feels like a Herculean task these days. Aunt Susan's no longer keen, and you know how Sarah feels about leaving Leo with anyone other than her own parents. True. We could try Mum and Dad; they’d love to spend an evening with him. I’ll give them a ring later. If that falls through, maybe we could look at a reputable agency? It feels a bit mercenary employing someone for one night, but desperate times... Let's give Mum and Dad a shot first.

Right then, Omar, tell us more about your niece. You were saying she’s trying to get out, yeah? To…Canada, was it? Yeah, Layla. She's… ambitious. And, frankly, a bit worried. Not just about the economy, you know? The whole atmosphere in Erbil is getting tense. It’s not like the old days. Too much…expectation. Too much reliance on the KDP and their…connections. Aye, I can imagine. Difficult for young people, isn’t it? Trying to build a life when the ground's shifting under their feet. My cousin’s lad, Ben, he’s desperate to get out of Liverpool altogether. Says there’s nothing for him here. Wants to go to New Zealand, can you believe it? Builds model airplanes, the lad, and thinks he'll be a mechanic fixing them in bloody New Zealand! It’s a common dream, isn’t it? To escape. Canada’s proving difficult for Layla though. The visa process is a nightmare. She’s got a good education, a skilled job in IT, but... the paperwork. And the background checks. It's always the background checks, isn’t it? Being Kurdish, having family who… well, let’s just say they’ve had dealings with various factions over the years, doesn't help. No, not at all. Bureaucracy at its finest. It's a shame, really. It's like they're penalising people for wanting a better life. Reminds me of my own father, struggling to get settled here in England after the war. Constant paperwork, constant questioning. Never truly felt at home, you know? Always looking over his shoulder. Exactly! And it’s not just the Canadian process. My brother’s son, Karim, he wants to go to Germany. He’s fluent in German, got a degree in engineering… but the whole visa situation is a minefield. It’s all tied up with… well, with oil, isn't it? And who controls it. Don’t get me started on oil. It's the root of so much misery, isn't it? The geopolitics of it all... Libya, Iraq, Syria… It’s a constant game of chess with real lives as the pieces. You read about it, you hear about it… but truly understanding the complexities… it’s frightening. Frightening is an understatement. You know, the whispers… the influence of Wahabi ideology spreading, particularly amongst the younger generation. It’s very subtle, but it’s there.

Honestly, that was divine, Alistair. The lamb was cooked perfectly. You’ve really outdone yourself. Just followed the recipe, love. Though I did throw in a little extra rosemary, you know how I feel about it. Glad you enjoyed it, Fiona. It seems a shame to be eating such a lovely meal in front of the telly though, doesn’t it? Nonsense, Alistair! It’s perfectly acceptable. These days, are we going to be sitting around in silence after a hearty meal? A bit of  Escape to the Country  never hurt anyone. Comfort watching, that’s what it is. And besides, it's  her  house. Exactly, Mum. It’s a bit of a treat to have the TV in the dining room. Usually, we're crammed into the living room like sardines. Though, I do worry about the landlord. He’ll probably complain about the electricity bill soaring. Landlords. Don't get me started. Mine keeps sending passive-aggressive emails about the state of the garden. As if I have time to be weeding between reports and, you know, everything else. They're all the same, aren’t they? Just looking for an excuse to raise the rent. When I was Headmistress, the only landlords I dealt with were boarding house mistresses, and they were a different breed altogether. Dedicated. Hard-working. Speaking of hard work, are you still keeping up with those workouts, Mum? You mentioned something about joining a Pilates class. Pilates? Oh, it’s a delight! Keeps the old joints moving nicely. My back's thanking me for it, I can tell you. Though, it's more social than anything else, really. A good natter with the ladies while stretching. It’s better than being cooped up in this flat. You should try it, Fiona. You're always desk-bound. I've been thinking about it. Maybe I’ll look into something after this transcription project wraps up. It's been a monster, honestly. Hours and hours of squawking interviews. My brain feels like mush. It does sound dreadful. Perhaps a holiday is in order. We were talking about that cruise, remember? The Norwegian fjords? Oh, yes! That would be lovely. A bit of fresh air, some stunning scenery… and absolutely no transcription. A cruise! Splendid. I’ve always wanted to see the Northern Lights. Though, I am a bit wary of those huge ships. So many people!

Aye, this is reet grand, isn't it? Feels like I've lived here for weeks. Which, I suppose I 'ave. Still no word from the job centre, though. Just that automated thing, you know? "Your claim is being processed." Right, like I can’t tell that already. Stop moanin', Liam. You’ll scare the bairns. Dinner's nearly ready. It’s just a lentil stew, mind. Not exactly Michelin star quality, but it'll stick to your ribs. Honestly, you'd think the job centre would have something, anything, for a lad with a degree. Linsen? Really, Amelia? That’s your exciting dinner tonight? I’m starving just looking at you stir that. Can’t you make something with, like, actual vegetables? Sorry I’m late, Mrs. Henderson kept me back helping a kid with his phonics. Honestly, you wouldn’t believe the things they don't know by Year 3. Anyway, what are we ‘avin’? Smells… hearty. Lentil stew, Ethan. It’s better than it sounds. And Mia’s complaining, as usual. Mia, everything’s bland to you. It’s not  bland , it’s just... predictable. Like Whitehaven. No offense. I miss proper food, you know? Schnitzel, Spätzle… not this…brownness. Brownness? You're priceless, lass. Look, at least someone’s cookin' a proper meal. Better than another tin of beans for me. Still can’t believe you’re living here, Mia. That's a bit posh for us, isn’t it? Posh? My dad’s in the army, Liam. We’re not posh. We're… transient. And it’s temporary, anyway. I'm going to try applying to universities in Frankfurt next year; it's more interesting than sticking around here. Plus, the food's better. Don't get your hopes up too much, Mia. It's competitive. And university isn't all sunshine and roses, you know. Loads of debt, loads of stress. Ethan's been telling me all about it – he’s been helping me with my UCAS application. UCAS is brutal, yeah. Don’t let them fool you. They make it all seem shiny and exciting, but it’s just a spreadsheet of stress and rejection. I'm applying for primary education, hopefully at Lancaster. It’s not the world, but at least I’ll be doing something useful. Lancaster, eh? Fancy. That's miles away. Proper city. You'll be scoffin' all sorts of grub up there, won’t you?

Right, so the sugar’s in, butter’s softened… this Victoria Sponge needs to be perfect for Year 3, doesn't it? They’ve never made anything like this before. I’m a bit nervous they’ll all get covered in flour. Will there be sprinkles, Mummy? Lots and lots of sparkly sprinkles? Of course, sweetheart! Sprinkles are essential for a Victoria Sponge, aren't they? Though, I might have to hide them. Last time I let them loose with sprinkles, it looked like a glitter bomb went off in the classroom. Can I lick the spoon? Please, Mummy, please? Absolutely not, darling. That’s for a teacher, not a little gentleman. And it's raw batter, remember? Bad for tummies. But... Just a tiny lick. Yum! Right, so, back to the lesson. I was thinking, after they've mixed the ingredients – which is always chaotic, by the way - we’ll do it in pairs. One mixes, one folds in the sugar. And then… the grand reveal! Then we'll spoon the batter into the tins. What do you reckon? Can I help you with the tins? I’m really good at filling things! You are, aren’t you? You're a star. Maybe you can be my "tin assistant." But you have to promise to keep the flour on the counter, not on your face! Face flour! Exactly! Now, the most important thing is explaining why we're baking for our half birthday celebration. I want to explain a little about fractions, how we need half a cup of sugar, half a teaspoon of vanilla… Do you think I'm being too ambitious? Half birthday? Is that like when you’re not quite a whole year old? Precisely! It's a little celebration to mark halfway through the year. We're having cake on Friday, remember? Can we play Tomodachi Life after cake? Please? Possibly. If everyone’s been a good baker and kept their faces clean. Tomodachi Life is pretty addictive, isn’t it? I’m still trying to get Park to marry Naomi. It’s proving tricky. Park wants to marry Amy! He keeps giving her flowers! Oh, does he? Well, that throws a wrench in my plans, doesn’t it? Right, I need to pop to Morrisons later. I was hoping they'd have that Julia Donaldson book I was looking for. "The Gruffalo’s Child," was it?

Honestly, James, I don’t understand this obsession with electric cars. It’s all the rage now, isn’t it? Everyone's suddenly gone green. It's a bit more than a "rage," Elara. It’s a necessary shift. And honestly, I'm quite taken with the Polestar 2. Sleek, Scandinavian design... and the performance is surprisingly good. Have you driven one? Driven one? No! I'm barely keeping my battered Mini on the road, let alone considering a £40,000 electric vehicle. It's all a bit… aspirational. Plus, the range anxiety! What if I’m stuck halfway between Norwich and the coast and the battery dies? I envision myself being rescued by a very smug breakdown van driver. They've improved dramatically, Elara. Most have a good 300-mile range now. And there are charging points popping up everywhere. You’d be surprised. Think of the environmental impact, though. The reduction in emissions… I do think about it. I really do. But it feels performative sometimes, doesn’t it? All these people virtue-signalling on Facebook about their new Teslas, while simultaneously flying off to Dubai for the weekend. The hypocrisy is staggering. You’ve got a point there. It’s a complex issue. Social media definitely amplifies that. Everyone wants to present the best version of themselves, even if it's a distorted one. I saw something on Facebook earlier about a local farmer posting a picture of his electric tractor, but then there were comments pointing out he still uses intensive farming practices that are, let’s say, not exactly eco-friendly. Exactly! It’s all about perception, isn't it? It’s like, ‘Look at me, I’m doing my bit!’ without actually addressing the bigger picture. Do you ever feel overwhelmed by the sheer volume of information online? It’s endless outrage and doom-scrolling. I tried to detox from Facebook for a week… it lasted about two days. I can relate. I attempted a full digital cleanse once. Lasted a similar amount of time. It’s addictive. The algorithms are designed to keep you hooked. It’s clever, in a sinister way. I’ve been trying to be more mindful though, limiting my time on it. Primarily academic research now, hopefully. Less cat videos and political arguments. Easier said than done. It's like a reflex now, isn't it? Bored for a minute?

Right then, this is… surprisingly engaging. I wasn’t expecting to get so absorbed in  Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs . It's bonkers, innit? It's brilliant! I like the gummy bear rain. And the spaghetti! Imagine if it rained spaghetti! I'd never need dinner again! Exactly! Though I reckon you'd get a bit sticky, wouldn’t you? Anyway, my day was… chaotic. Honestly, the shop was rammed. Apparently, it’s "Bank Holiday weekend shopping madness" now, every Saturday. I’m starting to think they deliberately advertise the sales a week early just to torture the staff. Did Mrs. Higgins try to make you give her extra discount again? Don't even mention Mrs. Higgins. She tried the "oh, I’m a pensioner, I deserve a bargain" routine  again . I explained that discounts are applied automatically at the till, and she gave me this look like I'd insulted her family. She does that! She does it to everyone. Did you remember to put the new stock of crisps away? Yeah, mostly. I got distracted by a bloke trying to use a loyalty card from five years ago. Apparently, he thought it still worked. These people… Honestly. All this thinking about customer service… makes me want a proper cup of tea. Fancy one? Please! With sugar. And a biscuit. Is there any Hobnobs left? Nope, devoured. Unless you want a Digestive? Nah, Digestive’s are boring. Wait, why is he building a giant catapult to launch the food into space? See, that’s what’s interesting, isn’t it? It's not just silly fun. I think – and this is probably reading way too much into a kids’ film – it’s about consumerism, about producing so much stuff that we end up with mountains of waste. Throwing it all into space is a ridiculous visual for that, you know? Waste? Like…throwing things away? But if he throws the food away, people won't get to eat it. Exactly! That's the bit that's kinda messed up. There’s a huge disparity, innit? Loads of food wasted while people are starving somewhere else. Bit heavy for a film about flying burgers, but… Can you press the button to make it louder? I can't hear properly over my crisps. Sorry! I’m rubbish with this thing. It’s one of those modern clicky ones. Give me a good old-fashioned button any day.

So, you were saying about the government, weren’t you, Barry? Something about them being all the same, regardless of what they promise? Aye, that’s right, Karl. Same faces, different haircuts. Same bleedin’ song and dance. Remember New Labour? Tony Blair? Promised the world, didn't they? "Cool Britannia" and all that rot. Thought things were finally gonna change. I do recall the media fanfare. It was quite the cultural moment. Though, from my perspective, observing from across the channel at the time, the initial optimism felt… slightly manufactured. A very strategic rebranding, wouldn't you say? Strategic? It was a con, Karl, a straight-up con! Look at what happened. Iraq. The mess that left us in. Wars built on lies. And for what? Oil? Political point-scoring? It’s a right disgrace, it is. Still rippling through society, the fallout. The repercussions are undeniable, Barry. The erosion of trust in institutions, the rise of populism... It's a complex web of causes and consequences. Though, I think it's important to acknowledge Blair did some good things too. The minimum wage, for instance. Some investment in public services. It wasn’t all doom and gloom. Aye, a crumb thrown to the working class to keep us quiet while they lined their own pockets. Don't make me laugh. Minimum wage? Barely enough to feed a family these days. And the investment in services? It was smoke and mirrors, Karl! Outsourcing, private companies running the NHS… It all funnels money to the already rich. Don’t kid yourself. I'm not attempting to 'kid myself,' Barry. My point is merely that history is rarely a matter of purely black and white. Nuance is crucial. Remember the devolution of power to Scotland and Wales? That was a tangible, positive legacy. Devolution? More like passing the buck! Shifting responsibility while Central Government still pulls the strings. Look at the mess they’ve made of Brexit. Promised us back control, didn’t they? And what have we got? Chaos! Food shortages, rising prices… It’s a bleeding nightmare. And don’t even get me started on the cost of living crisis. Brexit… yes, a truly divisive issue. And one with far-reaching consequences. Regarding the cost of living, I believe it's a confluence of factors, not solely attributable to Brexit. Global supply chain disruptions, the pandemic… Always got an excuse, don't you, Karl?

Right, so I’ve been listening back to some of the BNC recordings – honestly, you wouldn't believe some of the slang people used back then. It’s fascinating, but also a little… jarring. Found one specifically about a bloke complaining about the price of chips, and he’s using phrases I’ve never even  heard  before. Makes you realise how much language shifts, innit? Chips, eh? Can’t go wrong with chips. Though, prices  are  ridiculous now. Listen, I’ve been meaning to ask you about this LinkedIn thing. You’re always going on about it. Is it genuinely useful, or just a massive time suck? I’m supposed to be updating my profile, but the thought of it just... paralyses me. Oh, LinkedIn! Absolutely useful. It's the modern networking, darlin’. Think of it as your online CV, but with a bit more personality, you know? You can follow people in your field, see what they’re up to, connect with potential clients… or, you know, find out what your ex is earning. Seriously though, it's good for keeping track of industry trends. Create a profile already! It takes like, an hour, tops. Trends… yes. Interesting. The algorithms… fascinating. Algorithms are  not  fascinating, ANON. They're terrifying! Honestly, the whole social media thing scares me. I deactivated my Instagram a while ago. Too much comparison. All those perfect holiday snaps… feels fake. Like everyone's living a better life than you are. I get that. The comparison trap is a killer. I’ve been trying to curate my feed a bit more, follow accounts that genuinely inspire me, rather than just make me feel inadequate. Speaking of holidays... have you ever thought about the Maldives? It looks absolutely bonkers. All that turquoise water... Maldives? Way beyond my budget, I'm afraid. Unless I win the lottery. I’d rather go back to Spain, honestly. A little villa in Andalucia, sunshine, tapas… simple pleasures. Although… I did see something incredible online the other day. Footage of whales breaching in Iceland. Absolutely breathtaking. Whales! Oh, I love whales! I saw a documentary – blue whales, weren't they? Absolutely massive. Makes you feel tiny, doesn't it? Being out in the ocean, watching those giants… I’m wishing I wasn’t so petrified of flying right now. Tell me about it. My knuckles are white every single time. My mum tried to convince me hypnotherapy would work, but I just ended up laughing at the suggestion.

Right, so, I’m thinking about getting another one. Another what, darling? Another dodgy takeaway? Because I’m drawing a line there. Last time’s vindaloo nearly set off the smoke alarm. Nah, not vindaloo. Tattoo. Another tattoo. Oh, honestly, Liam. You’re covered already! What would you even get? Another geometric shape? Are you collecting them like Pokémon cards? Something a bit more... meaningful, I think. Been looking at some traditional Japanese stuff. Koi fish, y'know? Symbolise perseverance and all that. Bit deep, innit? Deep for you, maybe. You spend most of your time arguing about Fortnite. But, alright. Where are you thinking of putting it? Don't you dare go anywhere near your neck again. I’ll disown you. Yeah, yeah, learned my lesson. Probably on my forearm. Got some space there. Think it'll go well with the little fox. The fox was a good choice. It was a bit impulsive, though, wasn't it? You got it after that…incident at the pub. Don’t remind me! Right, pass me the chorizo, yeah? Gotta get some protein in me before I go and get inked up. How's the tiling coming along, by the way? Still a disaster zone in the bathroom? Don’t even ask. The builders are hopeless. They promised they'd be finished last week. I'm starting to think I’ll be bathing in the kitchen sink by Christmas. At least the paella’s smelling good. You hungry? Starving. Seriously, you always make the best paella. Beats anything I can rustle up. Speaking of Christmas…have you thought about it much yet? It seems so far away. Chloe: Hello! Sorry I'm late, the traffic was absolutely mental. Smells amazing in here! Paella, you say? Chloe, darling! You made it! Just in time for chaos. Liam’s contemplating permanently altering his body, and the bathroom’s currently resembling a demolition site. Hey Chloe! So, you’re thinking Koi fish, serious stuff. Chloe, give me some advice – don’t let her do it! Chloe: Liam, you’ve got more tattoos than a biker convention! And Eleanor, promise me you’re not relying on those builders again. They’re notorious, aren't they? Tell me about it. I'm honestly starting to contemplate doing it myself. It’s just… time. Chloe: Well, a glass of wine will definitely help with that. How's work been?

Honestly, I’m surprised you made it here after that absolute nightmare on the train. Birmingham New Street was chaos, wasn’t it? I saw the reports – signal failure, delays everywhere. Tell me about it. I’m still twitching. They announced a 45-minute delay, then an hour, then… well, it was closer to two and a half. And the overcrowding! Honestly, I felt like a sardine. I was wearing my new skirt – the floral one from & Other Stories – and I'm pretty sure someone stepped on the hem. It’s completely creased now. Oh, that's awful! The floral one’s lovely though. I’ve been meaning to get something from there, but their prices are a bit steep, aren’t they? I'm sticking with my trusty M&S range for now. Practical and reliable. Like this curry, hopefully. Very practical indeed! Smells amazing, by the way. Are you using coconut milk? I’m trying to be better about dairy, you see. My digestion has been playing up something chronic lately. Yes, all coconut milk. And a fair bit of turmeric, which is supposed to be good for… everything, apparently. Anti-inflammatory, antioxidant… the whole shebang. I started going to that Pilates class down the road after my back started complaining. You should try it! It's surprisingly good for you, and a nice way to de-stress. Pilates? Hmm. I'm tempted, but the thought of contorting myself into unnatural shapes makes me slightly apprehensive. I've been trying to get to that yoga class Sarah recommended - the one with the candlelight and chanting. Sounds far more relaxing. Although, fitting it in is proving difficult with work. We're gearing up for the new travel supplement in October, so it's manic at the moment. We're focusing on 'off the beaten path' destinations, which is exciting, but means endless research. Off the beaten path travel – sounds fascinating! Where are you looking at? I’ve been dreaming of going to Georgia – the country, I mean. Not the state! I saw a documentary about the food there. It looked incredible. Khachapuri, khinkali… I'm drooling just thinking about it. Georgia! That  is  on my list. We're also looking at places like Albania, and some of the smaller Balkan countries. Trying to find somewhere that feels authentic, you know? Not swamped with tourists. I went to Santorini last year, and it was beautiful, of course, but you couldn't move for selfie sticks.

Brr, it’s colder than I thought it would be tonight. Honestly, after that lecture hall, I was sweating buckets. Did you manage to get the projector working okay? It was threatening to give up the ghost halfway through my bit on Ming Dynasty ceramics. It was dodgy, yeah. Giving me the usual static and flickering. I swear, that building's electrical system is held together with hope and a prayer. But yes, I wrestled it into submission. You were brilliant, by the way. The students were really engaged – you can just tell when they're absorbing things. Unlike some of my philosophy lectures, which are clearly just a warm place to nap. Oh, come on. Your philosophy lectures are fascinating! They just require a bit more... intellectual effort. Though, I did notice a few faces nodding off during the Kant section. Poor things. Though, thinking about it, I’m rather needing a good nap myself. I forgot just how draining it is teaching three back-to-back seminars. Tell me about it. Marking essays consumes my very soul. Speaking of consuming... did you manage to trim your toenails? You were complaining about them this morning. Don’t remind me. I tried. I really did. But the lighting in the bathroom is abysmal, and I kept snagging myself on the edge of the bath. It’s a disaster. I'll have to tackle them properly this weekend. Honestly, it wouldn't surprise me if I end up with a miniature bloodbath. You’re a disaster with a nail clipper. It's endearing. Right. Anyway, did you hear back from Liam about that weekend trip to Guilin? Not yet. I sent him a message this afternoon, but no response. He’s probably just swamped with work – that new legal case he's working on is apparently a beast. Though, knowing Liam, he's probably just lost in a particularly engrossing video game. Remember that time he spent three days straight playing that space strategy game? Vaguely… it involved a lot of frantic gesturing and stressed muttering about resource allocation. It was quite the spectacle. He completely forgot about our dinner reservation! He did! And blamed it on a ‘critical galactic alignment’. It’s just brilliant, isn’t it? That he can argue the intricacies of international law and completely fail at remembering basic human appointments. It’s wonderfully Liam. Still, I was hoping we could all go.

Honestly, Mark, I still can't believe you actually  bought  into that whole 'birds aren't real' thing. Come on, Eleanor. Don't tell me you haven't dabbled in a good conspiracy theory now and then. It's a bit of fun, isn't it? Keeps the mind sharp. Plus, the evidence is surprisingly compelling when you actually look at it. Government drones disguised as pigeons...it's brilliant! Brilliant? It’s absurd! Where did you even hear about this? It’s obviously satire. A meme! I saw a documentary on YouTube, naturally. Very thorough. Apparently, every bird was systematically replaced in the 1950s. Keeps track of our movements, collects data… all the usual stuff. Typical. You, falling down a YouTube rabbit hole. You’re supposed to be a director of a major company, not researching avian espionage. Speaking of work, how's things at 'Innovate Solutions' going? Still burning the midnight oil? Pretty much. Big push this quarter to secure the Henderson contract. It’s massive, Eleanor, could be a real game-changer. I've been practically living in the office. Sarah’s not exactly thrilled, bless her.
