She keeps hinting I need to reconnect with the ‘real world’ and stop ‘golfing with spreadsheets.’ Sounds about right. Sarah sounds wonderfully pragmatic. She always did keep you grounded. Are the kids alright? Did Leo pass his A-Levels? He did, thankfully! Physics was a killer, but he pulled it off. Heading off to Durham next year to study Engineering, can you believe it? Time flies, doesn’t it? Seems like only yesterday I was teaching him to ride his bike. And Chloe’s thriving at drama school. She’s got an audition for a showcase next month – terribly exciting. That’s wonderful news! Durham is a brilliant university. I'm so pleased for him. It's hard to believe they're nearly grown up. I’ve got a group of Year 10s prepping for their GCSEs right now. It’s exhausting, but rewarding when they finally get it. I'm trying to introduce some creative writing exercises – they're shockingly resistant to anything other than essays, though. Ah, teenagers. They're a world unto themselves. Remember being that age? So convinced you knew everything, yet completely clueless. Don’t remind me! Although, I did fancy myself quite the intellectual, I seem to recall. Did you ever watch that new BBC drama, 'The Seafarer'?

Dad, are we nearly there yet? It's taking ages. And this road is just…grey. All grey. Grey road, grey sky, grey hedges. It’s depressing. Now, now, Elara, don’t be like that. We've barely been driving for three hours. And it’s not  all  grey, love. Look! There’s a field of wildflowers over there, bursting with yellow and purple. See? Can’t be  all  grey. Oh, yeah, I see them. They're nice, I suppose. But everything else is just... monotone. Makes me think of the Wicked Witch of the West in The Wizard of Oz. All green skin and everything. You always did have a vivid imagination. Remember when you were little and convinced the postman was a sorcerer because he delivered telegrams? He  did  look a bit like one. All serious and official. Telegrams! Can you imagine? Sending a message like that. It would cost a fortune now. Do you think people even know what a telegraph is anymore? Some do. I remember my grandad used to tinker with them. He could read Morse code, you know. Proper flick of the wrist and everything. He used to try and teach me, but I never had the patience. Now, there's a skill lost to the ages. Like Braille, almost. It's amazing how people can communicate using just dots. I read a bit about Braille last year for a project. It's so clever. It makes you appreciate how much we rely on seeing. It’s just like in a Lewis Carroll story, isn't it? Everything is skewed and backwards. You always did have a head for books, Elara. Better than your old man, that's for sure. Speaking of books, did you finish "The Hound of the Baskervilles"? You were saying you were halfway through last week. Nearly. Sherlock Holmes is brilliant, isn't he? Although, I'm not sure it’s as good as the films. Benedict Cumberbatch is just… epic. Aye, he is. But there's something special about reading the original stories. The detail, the language… it's different. Reminds me of those old fairy tales my mum used to read to me. Simple stories, but full of magic. They always led you somewhere. Like this holiday will, I hope! Are we still stopping at Jamaica Inn tonight? That’s the plan. We booked a room weeks ago. It’ll be a bit spooky, what with all the Daphne du Maurier vibes.

Honestly, Grandad, this roast is champion. Proper champion. You’ve outdone yourself, you really have. Better than that woman down the street, Mrs. Henderson, and she fancies herself a cook. Aye, well, a bit of practice, lass. Been doing it long enough, haven’t I? You’ve got a good appetite though, you do. Just like your great-aunt Elsie. Remember Elsie? Always scoffed down everything in sight. It is excellent, honestly. The gravy’s particularly good. Did you use beef stock this time, Anon? Aye, I did, love. Real proper beef stock, not that watery stuff you get in the supermarkets. Makes all the difference. Liam, put your phone down for a minute and tell us something interesting. You've been glued to that thing all afternoon. Sorry, just checking on a project deadline. Big presentation next week. All about sustainable bridge design. Quite fascinating, actually. We’re looking at using bio-concrete for the pilings. Bio-concrete? What in the name of… is that made of seaweed? Not quite, Grandad. It incorporates bacteria that essentially ‘grow’ the concrete, making it stronger and more sustainable. Less carbon footprint, you see. It’s complicated. Blimey, that sounds right clever. My job’s nowt like that, you know. Just moving bits of data around for a linguistics project. It's all about recording how people talk. Proper boring, that is. Though, sometimes you hear some right gems. Like the other day, this fella from London, he kept saying "innit" after everything. It's wild to see how language changes and spreads. 'Innit'? Sounds like something you’d hear down at the market. Speaking of market, remember the price of petrol back in '63? You could fill your tank for next to nothing. Now, it’s robbery, pure and simple. Absolutely robbery! I used to drive my Morris Minor all over the place for a pittance. Petrol prices  are  ridiculous. I'm seriously thinking about switching to an electric car. Though charging infrastructure around here is still patchy, isn't it? That’s what I keep saying! It's a nightmare. Though, I’ve recently been trying to be more active. Started going for a run round the park a couple of times a week. Keeps you sane, that does. You should try it, Grandad. A bit of a gentle walk, even. Run? At my age? Don’t be daft, lass. I used to swim, though.

Right, okay. Jet lag is  real . I feel like I've been living in a perpetual twilight zone. Mum, thanks again for having me. This roast smells incredible, honestly. Could eat a horse. Don't you start, Daniel. You’re a growing lad, even if you are hovering around twenty-seven. Eat up. And don’t talk with your mouth full. Enfield manners, remember? Enfield manners. I’m trying, Mum. It's just... everything's so familiar, so comforting. It's a nice change from trying to explain the subjunctive mood to a class of teenagers who mostly want to know about TikTok dances. TikTok? Good heavens. Well, you’re doing a grand job, dear. Your father was telling me just yesterday – he's been going on about how well you're doing. He adores you. He does, doesn't he? It's good to hear. Right, back to the house hunt. I’ve made a start on the list. Obviously, we need to sort out the furniture – sofa, bed, dining table. And then all the small stuff...blinds, lamps, kitchenware... it’s endless. Endless, it is. You know, your Auntie Carol is still got that lovely antique dresser that she’s never really used. It wouldn't suit her modern place, and she’s been hinting she'd like to see it go somewhere it'll be appreciated. Really? The one with the inlaid flowers? Wow, that would be brilliant! Absolutely gorgeous, and it would fit perfectly in the dining room. I’ll give her a ring, shall I? Anything else I should ask her about? Just tell her I said hello, and that I'm missing her. And remind her to take her blood pressure medication. She forgets sometimes, bless her. Will do. Speaking of forgetting things…you know Sarah from university? The one who studied archaeology? Sarah... Sarah... oh, the girl with the bright pink hair! Vaguely rings a bell. What about her? She's getting married! Invitation just arrived. We’re going to Italy! Florence, can you believe it? Italy! Oh, that’s wonderful! Florence! Absolutely gorgeous. You must take lots of pictures. And I do remember Sarah, now you mention it. Lovely girl. Bit eccentric, but lovely. I hope you'll give me a chance to see the photos after. Of course! It's in October, so hopefully the jet lag won’t be quite as brutal as it is now.

Honestly, this documentary's plant life is just breathtaking, innit? Like, the resilience of these desert succulents - mind-blowing. I've been trying to get my aloe vera to thrive, but it's proper sulky. Sulky aloe vera. That’s a new one. It probably misses the humidity of Sunderland, doesn’t it? Cambridge air's a bit… dry. You ever thought about misting it regularly? I’ve tried! But then I end up with powdery mildew. It’s a constant battle. You know, reminds me a little of trying to get A-Level results up in some schools – a constant uphill struggle. Did you see that article about the reformed A-Levels? It sounds even more brutal than when we did them. I did. It’s a mess, isn’t it? Narrowing the syllabus so much… It feels like they're actively discouraging critical thinking and lateral learning. The whole point of education shouldn't just be about regurgitating facts for an exam. It’s about… well, developing a mind. Aye, exactly! And the pressure on the students… it’s gotta be awful. They’re being judged on so much earlier too. Remember feeling relieved when those results came out and you knew where you were going? These kids barely have a chance to breathe. It’s compounding the existing inequalities, too. Kids from disadvantaged backgrounds, the ones who might need a bit more support to navigate the system… they're getting squeezed even harder. It’s just… frustrating. Frustrating is an understatement! And on top of all that, this petrol crisis - madness, right? I was trying to get to Leeds last week for a conference, and the queues were ridiculous. I ended up having to cancel. Cost me a fortune, really. Tell me about it. I drove to see my mum in Birmingham last weekend and it was a nightmare. People are getting so stressed and aggressive. It feels… unsustainable. Like the whole system is starting to creak. It is, isn’t it? It makes you think about the NHS too, doesn't it? All this pressure on everything… they're already struggling. How are they supposed to cope when people are stressed and rationing their petrol to get to appointments? It's a vicious cycle. We need systemic change, not just band-aid solutions. Easier said than done, of course. Speaking of which… …did you see that fella’s beard?

Right, so, Chloe's proper leggit this week, innit? Didn't even bother showin' up for the study group. Reckon she's still stressed about that essay? Probably. She’s been a wreck about it. I saw her in the library, looking like she wanted to burrow under a table. Honestly, the pressure they put on us at this uni is ridiculous. And the grading… don't even get me started. Aye, tell me about it. I nearly had a meltdown tryin' to understand the lecturer's point about post-structuralism the other day. It’s like he’s speakin' a different language entirely! And then there’s the cost of livin’ here. Leeds is bleedin’ expensive! You lot are talkin’ about stress? Try workin’ a ten-hour shift at the pub  and  tryin' to write a ten-page essay on the socio-economic impact of the Black Death. Seriously, how is anyone supposed to concentrate on the bubonic plague when you're clearing glasses and dodging grumpy drunks? Proper grim, that sounds. Goin' back to the plague, though… it’s mad, innit? Like, everyone just accepted it. They didn’t have the medical knowledge we’ve got now. Imagine just… dyin’ like that. It's terrifying, isn't it? Thinking about the sheer scale of it. It puts all our modern anxieties into perspective, doesn't it? But I do wonder, were women often blamed for the plague back then? You know, the whole scapegoating thing? Aye, I’ve read somethin' about it. Sometimes blamed for witchcraft, wasn’t it? To try and explain somethin' they couldn't understand and were afraid of. It's just... horrible. Similar mindset to how some people treat women with periods, really. Exactly! Same sort of fear-based ignorance. It’s the same pattern. Blaming a group because you don't have the answers. Which links back to university, doesn’t it? We’re expected to know all these answers, and when we don’t… It’s mad pressure. And the finances are awful. I'm swearin', I'm barely managin' with me part-time job at the bakery. Mum's been helpin' out, bless her, but she's got her own bills. You two gettin' by alright? It’s… okay. My dad’s been giving me a bit of a top-up, which is good, but I'm trying to get a summer internship sorted so I won't need to ask.

You know, this is gorgeous. Truly. But it’s also making me think… about things. About what kind of things? The best route to Santa Barbara? Because honestly, I think we should just stick to the 101. This coastal route is lovely, but it’s taking forever. No, not about driving. About…people. Specifically, friendships. Oh? What sparked that? Don’t tell me you’re having a mid-life crisis and suddenly questioning everything? You’re barely thirty-eight! Hardly a crisis. Just…realizing some friendships, you know, they don’t… nourish you anymore. And I’m finding it surprisingly difficult to navigate letting them go. Especially the ones that have been around for ages. I get it. It's not like you're breaking up with a romantic partner. There’s less societal script for it. It’s just…awkward. I went through something similar a few years back with Chloe. Remember Chloe? From uni? Vaguely. Blonde, always wore enormous scarves, right? And into…fairtrade everything? That’s her! Yeah. We’d been friends since freshers’ week, shared a flat for three years. But then she got really… intense. Constantly needing to vent, always making everything about her. I felt drained after every conversation. I started making excuses not to meet up. Exactly! That's precisely how I feel sometimes with Sarah. It's not  her  fault, I don’t think. She’s just… going through a lot. But honestly, every phone call ends with me feeling emotionally wrung out. I feel guilty even thinking about distancing myself. It's been years! Guilt is a monster, isn't it? I felt awful about Chloe. Like I was abandoning her. But then I realised that being a genuine friend doesn't mean being a dumping ground. It's okay to prioritize your own wellbeing. But how do you  do  it? Like, cold turkey feels brutal. And gradually fading out… I've tried that. It just seems to create confusion. She texts me, asking what's going on. It's tricky. With Chloe, I just started being more…selective. Less available. I’d message back saying I was busy, suggesting alternatives that were less frequent. Little things. Eventually, the frequency just… decreased naturally. No big declarations, no dramatic showdowns. So, gentle attrition? Sounds remarkably dull, but possibly a good strategy. I’ve been trying to avoid her favourite topics of conversation – the latest drama with her boyfriend, her ongoing battle with the council over planning permission...

Right then, Gran. This Earl Grey’s a bit strong, innit? Mum’s usually got a better blend. Nonsense, dear. It’s perfectly acceptable. Strong tea is good for you. Keeps you alert. And your mother’s blend is far too fruity for my taste. A bit like eating jam, really. Tell me about this essay you were fretting over last week. Is it finished? Yeah, finally. Handed it in yesterday. Felt like it was taking over my whole life. It was on Post-Structuralism in contemporary British theatre – proper head-scratcher, that. Loads of Derrida and Foucault. My tutor, Professor Davies, kept dropping hints about Lacan. Sends shivers down your spine, just thinkin’ about it. Sounds frightfully dense. You young people, with your academic jargon. Back in my day, we read Shakespeare and called it a day. Though, I suppose, even Shakespeare can be Post-Structuralist if you squint at it hard enough. Did you get a good mark, I hope? I think so. He said it was ‘insightful’ which, according to uni grading, is practically top marks. He did mention needing to work on my… clarity of argument, though. Apparently, I ‘get lost in the theoretical weeds.’ Charming, innit? Yes, well, that's what happens when you spend too much time in those weeds. Sometimes you need to step back and look at the whole garden. Like painting. You can obsess over a single brushstroke, a single shade of blue, and completely miss the composition. Exactly! That’s what I was tryin’ to tell Professor Davies! He just gave me this look... Anyway, what are you working on at the moment? Still doing those landscapes? Yes, yes. A new series, actually. I'm trying to capture the light in Tuscany. I went there last spring. The colours… utterly breathtaking. Olive groves shimmering in the sun, the cypress trees against that intense blue sky… It's proving quite challenging to translate onto canvas. It’s far more inspiring in real life. Tuscany, eh? You should’ve taken me! I could have used a break from Derrida. Always wanted to go; seen loads of pictures in magazines. We'll go, darling. Soon. I've been looking at flights. Your cousin, Elsa, says they're having a particularly good vintage this year. We could stay with her and her husband near Florence. She’s promised to give us a tour of the local vineyards.

Honestly, I’m starving. Should have had something more substantial than that biscuit earlier. Are you sure we can't stop at somewhere for a proper bite to eat before we hit the gym in Tarnów? My energy levels are rapidly diminishing. We're pushing it, Rach. It’s nearly quarter past. Remember we talked about getting there no later than four to get decent slots with the trainer? And you know how he gets if you’re late. He’s got that… intense thing going on. Intense is an understatement. He practically radiates disapproval. Still, a girl needs sustenance! I was thinking something with protein, maybe a chicken salad sandwich? Or even just a handful of nuts. Anything to ward off the inevitable collapse. There’ll be food in Tarnów, I promise. We can grab something quick after the gym. Though, thinking about it, maybe a small banana now wouldn’t go amiss. Got any? Nope, ate the last one this morning. Honestly, this journey is highlighting my lack of planning skills. You're much better at that sort of thing, aren't you? Always prepared. It's a northern thing, I reckon. We practically come out of the womb with a packed lunch and a survival kit. Being prepared is just… sensible. Look, there's a lay-by coming up, we can pull over for five minutes. Stretch our legs, have a quick look at the map, and you can mentally prepare to negotiate with the gym trainer. Thank you. You’re a lifesaver. Driving’s exhausting, isn't it? I can’t imagine doing this for very long. You're exceptionally good at it though – proper steady. I get anxious behind the wheel for some reason. It’s alright. You just need to relax. And keep your eyes on the road. It's easier than I thought it would be, to be honest. The roads are… manageable. Though I’m dreading city driving. Poland is certainly a revelation. It’s so… different. It makes you think, doesn’t it? About everything. You know, I was reading something the other day about how many people still haven’t quite grasped the whole gender fluidity thing, and it just reminded me of some of the nonsense I had to put up with at university. Oh really? What sort of nonsense? Oh, you know. The constant assumption that I’d be interested in marriage and babies.

Right then, Nana, fancy a top-up? Milk or no milk in yours? Just a splash o’ milk, lass. Not too much. You know I don’t like it overly milky. Beautiful morning, isn’t it? Though a bit nippy still, mind. I’ve got me shawl on. Didn't expect it to be this cool in May. Aye, it’s a bit changeable, isn't it? One minute it’s sunshine, the next a right chill in the air. Think we’ll get that festival in alright this year though, don’t you? Saltaire? I've been looking at some of the artists exhibiting… some lovely hand-thrown mugs, actually. Proper chunky ones. Reminded me of some you used to buy from that fella down the road from your old flat. Oh, aye, Harold! Good lad, Harold. Made the best mugs. Solid as a rock, they were. You could warm your hands on ‘em in winter. Always said he’d learned from his grandad, who was a potter in Barnsley. Used to bring ‘em over for a cup o’ tea sometimes. Remember that time he dropped one? Right mess on the carpet! Oh, I do! Your old Persian rug. You were livid, but Harold was mortified. Made you a whole set as an apology, didn’t he? He did. Bless him. Moved away a few years back, didn’t he? Heard he was doing well, selling his pottery online. Still, nothing beats having a proper chat over a mug of tea. Speaking of which, did you see that big spider in the bathroom this morning? Nearly gave me a fright, it did. Big and hairy, it was. Oh, don’t even mention spiders! I saw one dangling from the rose bush this morning. Proper beastly thing. I shooed it away, but I'm half expecting it to be back. You know I'm not good with 'em. Though, honestly, I shouldn’t complain. They eat all the aphids, don't they? Good for the roses. Aye, good for the roses. Everything’s got its place, I suppose. Still, I hate 'em. Makes me think of that power cut we had last week. Couldn’t even find a torch straight away. Felt like being back in the war! Tell me about it! The whole street was plunged into darkness. And the birds! They went absolutely mad. Chirping and squawking like anything.

Honestly, Mum, Blackpool? Really? It's like, the tackiest place ever. Now, Maisie, don't be like that. Your Grandad’s been talking about going back to Blackpool for ages. It’s sentimental for him, you know. And it's not all just kiss-me-quick hats and donkey rides anymore. They’ve got that new SEA LIFE Centre, and the Pleasure Beach has got those crazy rollercoasters… Yeah, but everyone goes to Blackpool. It'll be rammed. And full of… well, you know. Loud people. And seagulls. Loads of seagulls. I’d rather go to Cornwall. Actual beaches, proper surfing… Cornwall? Darlin', you'd freeze your timbers off. Blackpool’s bracing! Gets the blood pumpin’. Besides, I haven’t been back proper since... well, since your Grandma and I used to go on the Golden Mile, spending every last penny on candy floss and arcade games. Seriously, Grandad? All that sounds… dusty. He has a point, love. It holds a lot of memories for him. And practically everyone offers an affordable trip. Look, here’s a nice little flat near the Tower. It’s got sea views - well, partial sea views – and it’s close to everything. Partial sea views? What does that even  mean ? You can see a bit of the sea? Like, between a chip shop and a car park? Now, now, Maisie. Be polite. Don’t be lookin' a gift horse in the mouth. Blackpool's got character. It’s lively. Remember that show we saw there a few years back, with all the Elvis impersonators? You were laughin' so much your face hurt. Okay, okay, that was funny. But it was a  one-off  funny. I’m thinking about Chloe and Liam, though. They were saying they were thinking about going to Skegness. Maybe we could meet up? Skegness? That's even further north than Blackpool! And probably even more… industrial. Honestly, darling, let’s stick to the plan for now. We’ve already booked everything. And your Grandad is really looking forward to it. He’s even started polishin’ his lucky bowling shoes. They're a wee bit knackered, but don’t you go tellin’ her that! I always bowl a strike when I’m wearin’ 'em. Used to impress your Grandma somethin' fierce. Fine. Blackpool it is. But I'm  not  buying a kiss-me-quick hat. And I'm holding you both personally responsible for any seagull attacks.

Ugh, that film was  long . But like, in a good way, innit? Heath Ledger was proper dreamy. Dreamy? He was a menace! Absolutely infuriating at first. I was proper annoyed with him, winding Kat up like that. But then... yeah, okay, dreamy. A little. Especially when he was reading poetry. See! I told you! And Julia Stiles? Don’t even get me started. That whole scene where she’s just… lecturing Patrick about poetry and life? Give me chills every time. Proper powerful. It was good. Really good. But honestly, I’m more stressed about Mr. Davies’ English test next week than I was about Kat Stratford ever finding true love. Oh, don’t even mention Mr. Davies! He’s like, deliberately trying to make us fail. All that Shakespeare… I still don't understand  Hamlet . Why is everyone being so dramatic? Tell me about it! It's like, okay, your dad died and your uncle snatched the throne, we get it. But then all the moping and the ghost sightings? Bit much, isn't it? Exactly! And he's got like, three girlfriends and then he goes all crazy about Ophelia. Honestly, the man needs a therapist. What’s he even asking us to learn? Besides how to feign a mental breakdown? Good point. Mrs. Peterson said it’s about exploring complex themes of revenge and morality. But all I'm exploring is the depths of my boredom. I keep picturing Hamlet going to McDonald’s and complaining about the fries. Oh my god, that's brilliant! He’d be all, “These golden tubers are an inadequate representation of the ephemeral nature of joy!” Totally! And then the cashier would be like, "Next!" Anyway, back to the misery. I’m pretty sure I spent most of the last lesson staring out the window, thinking about that London trip. Oh my gosh, yes! Mum said we could look at hotels online tonight. I’m thinking somewhere near Covent Garden. All those shops... and the theatre! Imagine seeing a proper show. Covent Garden’s good. Or maybe somewhere in Notting Hill? I saw a documentary about it once, and it looked so cute, all those colourful houses. Plus there's Portobello Road market! We could get vintage clothes and stuff. Ooh, yeah! That would be amazing. Do you think we could convince our parents to let us go to that Harry Potter exhibition?

Honestly, I don't understand why everyone's so obsessed with Facebook. It’s just… endless scrolling. And people sharing the most bizarre things. Did you see Brenda’s post about that pigeon she rescued? Three photos, all blurry, and a ten-paragraph saga about its heroic journey to freedom. Well now, pigeons are alright, aren't they? Bit of a nuisance in the garden sometimes, mind you. Pecking at the bird feeder. But Brenda’s a good soul. Always lookin' out for the little critters. Facebook… I've ‘ad a little look, Sarah’s daughter showed me once. All them pictures movin' about, makes me head spin, it does. Like a right circus. It's a wonder anyone gets anything done. I tried it for a bit, you know, after I finished minding the children. Felt pressured to join. All my friends were on it. But it just made me anxious. Comparing myself to everyone else, you see. Pretending their lives are perfect. I deleted it after a month. Better to stick to a good book, wouldn't you say? There’s a curated reality element to it, definitely. People only show the highlights. It’s almost performative. Though, it  is  useful for keeping in touch, particularly with people who’ve moved away. I use it mainly for groups related to my field, actually. Sharing articles and discussing research. Much more productive than blurry pigeon photos. Exactly! Although, I do enjoy seeing pictures of my niece. It’s just… the negativity, sometimes. People arguing about everything. It’s exhausting. It just feels like a breeding ground for anxiety. And my OCD hasn't been very helpful with it - thinking about how to organise the feed neatly and ending up spending hours on it. OCD, eh? That’s a tricky thing. My sister had a touch of it, she did. Always needin' things just so. Line of cutlery aligned perfectly, cushions plumped just right... it drove her husband mad sometimes. Says it’s the devil’s work, though I wouldn’t go that far. It must be awful, dear. Sarah, are you getting help with it? Have you spoken to anyone? Yes, Mum. I’m seeing a therapist. It’s… progress is slow. It impacts everything, even something as simple as deciding which tea bag to use. It has to be a certain brand and a certain number of dips. Sounds ridiculous, I know.

Right then, who’s feeling hungry? I've put a roast on, should be ready in about an hour. Bit of Yorkshire pudding too, just how Dad likes it. Ooh, roast! Yes, please! I'm starving. Been mad busy at the salon all day, colour transformations galore. Honestly, some people want neon pink one week and then natural brown the next. The drama! Neon pink, eh? Back in my day, if you wanted a bit of colour, you just got a perm. That was daring enough! Dad, you’re sounding ancient. And honestly, a perm? The horror! Speaking of ancient, I was just looking at some old photos for a client’s website. They had pictures from a family holiday in Germany, like, the 70s. The cars! Absolutely enormous. All these boxy, brown things. Germany, you say? I was over there last year for a craft fair in Dusseldorf. Lovely city. Proper efficient, wasn’t it? Trains ran on time, everyone spoke perfect German… or at least, they tried to hide it when they realised I didn’t understand a word. Oh, you and languages, love. You tried to order a coffee in Italian once and ended up asking for a small dog. Nearly caused a riot! It was a misunderstanding! And they do look rather similar, coffee and ‘cane’ in Italian… anyway! They were fascinated. Anyway, back to Germany. What were you thinking about, love? The cars? Yeah, the cars mostly. It's wild to see how much things change. And the clothes! Brown flares for everyone! It just makes you appreciate things now. Though, I do miss a good, solid, reliable car. Everything feels so… flimsy these days. Speaking of changes, anyone remember that awful Ford Sierra Dad used to drive? The one that coughed and spluttered its way up Kemsing hill? Don't remind me! That thing was a menace. Remember how Dad used to try and fix it in the driveway, using more swearing than tools? That was a grand old car. Reliable as anything, it was. Just needed a bit of attention. And a lot of swear words, apparently. Though I do admit, it wasn’t exactly stylish. Your mother used to call it the 'mobile dustbin'. Mobile dustbin! That’s brilliant! Honestly, the stories you lot tell. My mum used to tell me stories about her grandparents. Apparently, they used to drive to Southport for holidays, from Ashford.

So, you're  still  slinging pans then, eh? Last time I saw you, you were talking about opening your own place. Any closer to that dream? Nah, not really. The restaurant scene in Exeter's…competitive, to put it mildly. Landlords want the Earth, inflation’s chewing up everything. At the moment, I’m happy enough at 'The Golden Anchor'. It’s a decent pub, good clientele, and the head chef’s surprisingly relaxed. He lets me run with a few ideas in the specials. That's good, isn’t it? Still getting the experience in. Remember when you were obsessed with that weird avant-garde fusion place in London? Thought you were going to become a molecular gastronomy genius. Oh god, don't remind me. That internship… that was a  year  of my life. Tiny portions, horrifyingly pretentious clientele, and a chef who treated you like you were less than dirt. I’m sticking to proper pub grub for now, thanks very much. What about you? Still buried in those dusty books at Uni? Pretty much! Dissertation's looming, though. It’s…a slog. I’m doing it on the influence of Northern Soul on Britpop. Sounds niche, I know, but I'm really getting into it. Have you heard of ‘The Upbeats’ lately? Their new album's phenomenal. It's got that raw, authentic energy that everything else seems to lack. 'The Upbeats'? Vaguely rings a bell… are they the ones Liam was raving about last summer? He kept playing that one track at every barbecue – something about a rainy Tuesday? Yeah, that’s the one! “Grey Skies, Good Times.” Liam loved it, obviously. But you need to hear the whole album. Seriously. It’s not just that one song. It’s the drumming that gets you, you know? Proper driving beat. It makes you want to dance. You know I appreciate a good drummer. Remember when I was trying to convince everyone I was the next Keith Moon? My poor mum… the noise I was making on that kit. Oh God, yes! The entire street complained! You were a menace. Still playing now? Occasionally. Mostly just banging out a few beats in the kitchen when things are quiet. Helps keep me sane. There’s this new band playing at The Cavern Club on Friday – ‘Lunar Echoes’. Apparently, they’re incredible live. Heard their drummer is a beast. Fancy a trip down to Exeter next weekend?

Right then, Thomas. This is nice, isn’t it? A bit of peace and quiet. Feels like ages since we’ve just…sat. Could barely hear meself think with all that racket earlier, could I? Sounds like a school dinner hall in here, honestly. Aye, it's alright. Bit loud, though. What was that about Durham though? You said something about going? Aye, Durham. I were thinking, now. We've not been in ages, have we? With you being so busy with football and everything. I thought we could make a day of it in the summer. See the cathedral, the castle…maybe a wander along the river. A proper day out. Could get some nice cream there, remember that lovely little shop we found a few years back? Cream's good. But what about the summer holiday? Are we still thinking Spain? Spain’s still on the cards, love. But Durham could be a little something  before  that. A warm-up, you could say. We need to get the sleeping bags out and check 'em – don’t want a soggy tent in Spain, do we? And beds! Need to make sure the caravan’s got proper beds. You’re getting too big for that old inflatable mattress. Yeah, that’s true. It's like sleeping on a paddling pool these days. Did you see that article about obesity in the news yesterday? Apparently, kids are getting heavier, faster than ever. Aye, I did. Dreadful, isn’t it? Part of it’s food, of course, but it's also the lack of activity. All glued to their phones, like you. Don’t get me wrong, I love a bit of telly meself, but it’s all about balance, isn’t it? You need to get out and run about. Like you used to. Remember those domino drives we used to have with your grandad? You were a dab hand at ‘em. Those were good. Remember he always cheated? Said it was a strategy. He did, didn’t he? A right crafty one, your grandad. Speaking of crafty, I need to make a shopping list before we leave. Milk, bread, sugar… Honestly, it's a constant battle keeping the cupboards stocked. And I need to remember to look into those loyalty promotions at Boots. Got that voucher for the shampoo. What about the people in the drive-through at McDonald's earlier?

"So, what do you reckon, Liam? Bit of a fixer-upper, yeah? Still feels a bit... echo-y." “Right proper echo, yeah. Sounds like a bowling alley in here. Sussex's a bit quieter than Brum, isn’t it? Though, I’m enjoying the peace, to be honest. Much better than listening to the office drone on about spreadsheets all day.” "Tell me about it. Though, the spreadsheets are probably more interesting than marking essays on the passive voice. Speaking of interesting, did you bring that recording equipment? I want to get some proper examples of your accent, you know, for the linguistics project. It's fascinating, the way you say 'bath' – it's almost a diphthong disappearing entirely!" "Always the linguist, eh, Finn? Right, got it here. . 'Baths', alright. What sort of words are you after? Don’t want to be sounding like a right eccentric for your notes." "Just natural conversation, really. The more casually you talk, the better. Actually, before we do that... how’s Sarah doing? I heard she's... well, you know." "Yeah, she is. Quite a lot bigger now, actually. Can barely fit into her usual jeans. She’s a bit tired but excited, naturally. Doctors reckon it'll be around November. Got the midwife appointments booked, all the scans done. It's a lot, isn't it? Suddenly, all that assurance work feels pretty irrelevant compared to... well, childbirth." “It is, isn’t it? Huge life change. Are you thinking about joint bank accounts and all that? We're looking at that at the moment, with rent and bills and everything. Getting a handle on the budget is a pain.” "Definitely. Sorted that out ages ago, actually. Turns out having a good salary – mine’s… well, let's just say it's comfortable – makes things a little easier. Joint account for bills, separate ones for spending money. It works for us. You’re finding Sussex is as expensive as they say, then?" “Even more so! Council tax is a killer! I was working out the other day, just with rent and utilities, I’m eating into almost all of my salary. Teaching's not exactly a get-rich-quick scheme, you know. Remember that awful stint at the call centre after uni?” "Oh god, don't remind me! 'Please smile while I’m telling you your internet isn’t working!' The worst. Seriously though, you should consider looking at another teaching position.

It’s just… relentless, isn't it? The phone calls, the visits… all lovely, bless them, but it's just  constant . Poor Mark. He’s trying to be strong, you know, for the kids, but I can see it wearing him down. He hasn't slept properly in weeks. Absolutely, love. It's a marathon, not a sprint. And losing your mum… there's nothing like it. It rewrites your entire world. Is he eating properly? Mark’s a terrible one for neglecting himself when things are tough. That’s exactly it. I went round yesterday and offered to make him a shepherd's pie – he loves my shepherd’s pie – and he just shrugged and mumbled something about having 'grabbed a sandwich'. A sandwich! With everything he’s going through. I practically wrestled a plate of food into him. Oh, you’re a good friend, Fiona. A really good friend. My Janet would’ve done the same. Remember when Dad got sick? I swear, Janet single-handedly kept me afloat with her constant casserole deliveries and just… listening. She’s got this knack, hasn’t she? Of just  being  there. She does, doesn't she? I admire that so much. I tend to... well, I tend to flail. I offer solutions and organize things. It’s my default setting. But sometimes, people just need someone to hold their hand and say, “This is awful.” Exactly. And sometimes, solutions aren't what's needed. It feels like we’re all just navigating this minefield of grief and responsibility. Honestly, with Ethan’s university fees looming and Jess struggling with anxiety… it's hard to know where to focus. Jess’s anxiety... I keep thinking about it. Have you noticed a shift in her? She’s always been a bit… sensitive, bless her. But lately, it seems more than that. She’s isolating herself. She mentioned it last week when she popped in for a cuppa. Said she felt like she was constantly disappointing people. Said she felt like a burden. My heart just sank. It’s a common feeling, I know with grief adding a layer... It is. And the expectations! Everyone expects you to be ‘fine’ or ‘strong’ or ‘helpful’. It’s exhausting. I had a phone call with my aunt yesterday. She kept saying, “Well, at least she lived a long life.” As if that makes it any easier!

Right then, so, Finn, how was your tennis match on Saturday? You seemed a bit quiet about it earlier. It was alright. Lost the first set, won the second. Then I choked in the third. Proper choked. Choked, eh? Happens to the best of us. Remember that penalty I took in the five-a-side back in '98? Missed completely. Humiliating. Really? You were a footballer, Mr. Kim? I didn’t know that! Briefly. Just a hobby. Anyway, Finn, choking happens. It's about how you bounce back. Did you actually enjoy playing? Yeah, the playing was good. It’s just… I wanted to win. Especially against Leo. Leo's a good player, love. Don't beat yourself up about it. Have you been going to your coaching sessions with Mrs. Davies regularly? She’s really impressed with your forehand, you know. Yeah, they’re okay. Bit boring sometimes, though. All drills and no actual playing. I’d like tennis coaching. My school only has a badminton court. Well, we could look into it for you, Daniel. It's good exercise. Although, I’m not sure you'd be keen on all the drills Finn’s complaining about! Speaking of plans and things, I was reading about apprenticeships the other day. Seems a rather solid route for some people, especially in technical fields. It’s a shame it’s not pushed more. What do you two think? Any interest? Apprenticeships? In what? All sorts. Engineering, IT, even some business administration roles. You get paid while you learn, and often end up with a qualification at the end of it. Better than just racking up student debt, arguably. My cousin’s doing an apprenticeship in plumbing. Seems alright, he gets to go on site and actually do stuff. It’s definitely worth looking into. I remember when I was trying to decide what to do after university. It felt like so much pressure, you know? Everyone expected me to go straight into a ‘proper’ job. What about you, Mum? What would you have done differently? Ooh, tough question. Perhaps taken a gap year. Travelled a bit more. But honestly, I think ending up self-employed has served me well. Had to be a bit resourceful, certainly. Although a bit of investment at the start would have made things a lot smoother. Exactly! That’s what I’ve been pondering. Thinking about putting a little bit into a friend’s new business – a craft brewery just outside Birmingham.

“Right, so, Lancaster. It's been ages since I’ve been up north. Feels a bit…different from Aylesbury, doesn't it? Less rolling hills, more, well, bricks.” “Definitely. Though I've only ever driven through, never actually  been  to Lancaster itself. Auntie Carol’s house is just outside, in Bolton-le-Sands, wasn’t it? Apparently, it’s lovely. She’s going on about her roses again, says they’re blooming beautifully.” "Bolton-le-Sands, that's the one. Honestly, the woman could talk about her roses for hours. I’m mostly looking forward to a proper walk along the coast. We haven't done a seaside trip in ages, have we? Remember that awful cockle disaster down Weston-super-Mare? That was, uh, memorable." “Oh god, yes. The news reports were just…horrendous. I'd almost forgotten about that. Still, makes you appreciate fresh seafood, doesn’t it? I'm positively craving fish and chips after this. Auntie Carol makes a mean mushy pea fritter too, apparently. Have you ever tried one?” "Only once, at a fair. It was... interesting. Not horrible, just very, very beige. But I’m willing to give Auntie Carol’s a shot! Speaking of things that are interesting, are you still thinking about applying for that Masters in Linguistics at Lancaster University? I know you were looking at their program.” "I am. I really am. I just… the dissertation part terrifies me, you know? It’s such a massive undertaking. And thinking about needing to justify it to Mum and Dad... they're still not entirely convinced a Masters is 'necessary' when I've got a perfectly decent job." "Tell me about it! My parents are the same. They just keep saying, 'You're earning well, aren't you? Why spend more money on books?' I’m arguing that research experience will be invaluable for career progression, but it’s hard to get them to see the bigger picture. What's your proposed topic, anyway? You mentioned something about sociolinguistics and online communities?" "Yeah, that's what I’m leaning towards. Examining how online slang and meme culture shapes identity formation. It sounds ridiculous when I say it out loud, doesn’t it? But there’s actually a lot to unpack there. It's just… daunting." “Not ridiculous at  all , it's fascinating! Seriously. It's current, relevant, and you clearly have a passion for it.

Nah, seriously, have you heard Arctic Monkeys’ new stuff? It’s… different, isn't it? Proper different. Not like the Sheffield days at all. Different’s a mild word, lass. It's like they've gone full-on… desert rock. I swear I heard Alex Turner trying to channel some Nick Cave vibe at one point. It’s a bit much, innit? A bit much, aye, but I’m liking it! It’s got that… that atmosphere, you know? Makes you wanna be driving through the Mojave Desert or summat. It’s not the stomping, shouty stuff we grew up on, but it's grown on me, it has. What d'you reckon of "Body Paint?" "Body Paint" is… something else. The video's weirder than the song, though. Honestly, what  was  that about? Did anyone understand what was going on there? My mum just kept asking if they were advertising something. She probably thought it was a shampoo advert! I didn’t understand it either, to be honest. All those spiders! But the song's got a proper groove. Speaking of strange videos, did you see Liam's latest one? Oh, don’t even start me on Oasis and their videos. They were always bonkers, weren't they? Remember "Roll With It?" The chickens! Absolute madness. But in a good way. Anyway, back to Arctic Monkeys... do you think they'll ever go back to the older sound? I doubt it, to be fair. Alex seems pretty committed to this new direction. Keeps things interesting, though, doesn't it? It’s not like they’re churning out the same old tunes. What about you though? Been getting up to any mischief with your photography lately? Still stalking pigeons in the town square? Guilty as charged. The pigeons are remarkably photogenic, you know. Got some good shots of a fat one the other day, practically posing with a discarded chip. But yeah, I’ve been trying to get into long exposure stuff. Been down by the river a few times, trying to get the lights blurred and dreamy. It’s a right pain trying to get the tripod level on that uneven ground. Aw, you’re getting arty! That sounds proper good, though. You should show me some of your snaps. Maybe we can go down there together sometime? I've been wanting to get out and about a bit more. Been stuck in the library mostly, studying for that history essay.

Right, okay. So, Rhys, you’re still insisting on prioritizing Atlanta? Seriously? We’re hemorrhaging cubes in Europe! Now, now, Elin, don’t get your knickers in a twist. Atlanta's a crucial hub! If it goes, the whole southeastern US collapses. Strategic thinking, that's what it is. You’re just panicking because you haven't cured a single disease yet. Easy there, Rhys. Nobody's panicking. Elin’s just… passionate about global disease control. And technically, I cured the yellow fever in South America. Don’t forget that, love. Passionate? I'm trying to prevent a global apocalypse, Jamie! And a single cure doesn't exactly offset the fact that we’re about to lose Brussels. Kevin, are you even  paying  attention? You just keep building research stations everywhere! Well, somebody’s gotta do  something . You two are arguing again. And besides, more research stations mean more chances for cures, right? It’s simple logic. Reminds me of the time I was trying to organize a fundraising gala in Singapore. Absolute chaos. Everyone had their own ideas. You’d think saving humanity would be less stressful than getting a raffle ticket printed. Honestly, you’d think a group of teachers would be better at cooperation. It's just a game, girls. Don’t get yourselves in a proper state. I’m just worried about running out of tiles. We need to ration these. Ration tiles?! Bronwen, darling, try worrying about my rapidly deteriorating stress levels! Rhys, seriously. Atlanta can wait. We need to contain the red cubes in Scandinavia  first . But if Atlanta falls… it’s a domino effect! Think about it, Elin! Think about the logistics! You’re a teacher, you should appreciate the importance of a well-structured lesson plan. This is just like managing a classroom, only with more… deadly viruses. Comparing Pandemic to his classroom? Rhys, that's brilliant. Absolutely brilliant. You know, I've been thinking, maybe we should try a different approach. What about focusing on preventing outbreaks instead of just curing diseases? Less reactive, more preventative. Like, bolstering the cities at risk. Yeah! That's smart, Jamie. We could use those event cards to our advantage, anticipating where the outbreaks will hit next. That... actually isn't a terrible idea, Jamie. Preventative medicine, right. Restricting movement, implementing quarantine zones... alright, okay. I'm tentatively on board. But Rhys, if Atlanta collapses because we prioritized Scandinavia… Don't look at me!

Right then, little ones. Mummy’s had a proper cuppa. Let's talk birthdays, shall we? Poppy, darling, you’re turning six in… what month is it again? June! June, Mummy! Like strawberries! Strawberries are red. Like Mr. Tumble's shoes. Exactly! And Leo, you’re turning five in… July, isn't it? We need to start planning, don't we? I was thinking, given how much you both love it, we could try and get tickets to that CBeebies pantomime they're doing at the theatre in Cambridge. Panto! With the Bluey characters? Pleeeease, Mummy? Is there a superhero panto? With a cape? I don’t  think  there's a superhero one this year, sweetie. But Bluey would be brilliant. We’d have to book quickly though, they sell out ages in advance. It'd be a proper treat after half term. What do you think, Leo? Okay. But can I have a superhero biscuit? Of course, you can. Always a superhero biscuit. Speaking of treats, Poppy, we need to have a think about your party. Any ideas? Remember last year when you were adamant you wanted a mermaid party? I still love mermaids! But maybe… a fairy party? With lots of glitter! And a sparkly cake? Glitter and a sparkly cake, got it. We’ll need to stock up on fairy wings then. I’ll have a look online later. But before we get lost in glitter and fairies, remember that story Officer Popcorn told on CBeebies yesterday? About the little lost duckling? He went 'quack, quack, where's my mum!' And then the big duck showed him the way! You remembered! That's right. It reminds me of something my Nan used to say – "Every duckling finds its way home, love." It’s a lovely little saying, isn't it? My favourite story on CBeebies is still Hey Duggee. Because Duggee gives out badges! He does, doesn’t he? He really does. I wonder what the badge would be for this week? Maybe... "Best Biscuit Tower Builder"? I could build a  really  tall one! Higher than the ceiling! Let’s not get too ambitious, darling. Though, I'm impressed with your enthusiasm! Okay, quick change of subject. It’s nearly World Book Day, isn’t it? Have you thought about what you want to dress up as? I'm going to be Princess Belle from Beauty and the Beast!

Right, this is actually quite decent, Anon. You've outdone yourself. Proper posh bread, this isn’t it? Didn't think you were the sourdough type. It's from that new place down the road, 'Artisan Loaves'. Bit pricey, I admit, but worth it. You’re always moaning about my cooking being bland, so I thought I’d splash out a bit. How's the engineering life treating you this week, Liam? Still battling rogue algorithms? Aye, still at it. Spent half of Tuesday trying to convince a program that north is  not  south. You wouldn't believe the hoops you have to jump through sometimes. Ridiculous, honestly. It's a constant battle against… well, the inherent illogicality of computers. Makes you appreciate a good, solid sandwich, doesn't it? You’re a ray of sunshine, Liam. Always so enthusiastic about your frustrations. I’m glad you like the bread, Anon. Smells lovely in here. Honestly, I'm exhausted. Marking essays all morning – A-levels, you know? Such pressure on those kids. They're basically writing their entire futures in three hours. Tell me about it. My brother's doing his A-levels this year. He’s melting down over physics. Thinks he’s going to fail and his whole life is ruined. Dramatics, honestly. It's the same pressure, isn't it? Everyone makes such a big deal of the results. Remember when I was stressing about my postgraduate dissertation? Like the world hinged on it. Now it’s just a dusty document somewhere. Absolutely. Perspective is key. Although, I do feel for them. I’m seeing a huge difference in the language skills of this cohort compared to previous years. It’s worrying. People just aren’t reading as much, are they? Stuck on their phones. It’s the internet, isn't it? Everything's bite-sized. Instant gratification. It’s terrible for attention spans. Actually, speaking of the internet, I’ve started trying those dating apps again. Oh, really? Back on the market then? I thought you were happy being single. I  am  happy! But… you know. It’s nice to have someone to share a Netflix night with occasionally. The apps are horrific though. So much swiping, so little substance. And the photos! Half of them are clearly five years old and heavily filtered. Oh, you've ventured into the digital dating abyss! It’s a perilous journey, love.

Honestly, this book was a bit of a slog, wasn't it? All that descriptive prose about the wildflowers - I nearly nodded off three times. But the biscuits are excellent, Sarah. You’ve outdone yourself. Oh, thank you, Claire! Glad you like them. It's my mum's recipe; she always made them for book club back when I was a kid. Remember those afternoons at her place? All those little girls huddled around, arguing about who got the most sprinkles on their fairy cakes. Sprinkles! And remember those plastic ponies? The ones with the incredibly tangled manes? I’m pretty sure I spent most of my childhood trying to detangle Princess Sparkle’s hair. It was a losing battle. Princess Sparkle! Good heavens, I’d completely forgotten about her. I had one too, a dreadful shade of pink. I think I named mine…Gloria. Utterly ridiculous. My mum used to threaten to throw them all in the bin if we didn't behave. She did that to us too! My nan, I mean. Always threatening to “chuck the lot of ‘em.” Bless her, she was a bit of a firecracker. Always talking about “putting your foot down” - never quite understood what she meant, to be honest. Speaking of things you don't understand, have you two ever tried to decipher my mum’s Essex accent when she's really got going? It’s like a completely different language. Like, I’ll be on the phone with her, and I’ll be nodding along, pretending I understand, and then suddenly she’ll say something and I’m utterly baffled. Oh, I know exactly what you mean. My dad always used to tease my mum about her Lincolnshire accent. He'd mimic her saying “clart” instead of “cart,” just to wind her up. He'd claim he liked the 'rustic charm' of it all. Oh, you know how men are! My husband does the same with me. He'll pick up on my ‘eastern vowels,’ as he calls them, and exaggerate them until I'm practically shouting. It's good fun, though. Keeps you on your toes. Honestly, you can't get rid of it, can you? My kids, they started picking it up too. Little Alfie keeps saying “bung it in the bin,” which is a bit worrying! It’s so fascinating, isn’t it? How language gets passed down. My gran used to say things like “oo-sh” for ‘it is’ and “a right kerfuffle” for a big argument.

So, you’re actually saying you spent a whole week birdwatching in Norfolk? Dad, seriously? That sounds… intense. Intense is one word for it, love. Peaceful is another. You wouldn’t believe the colours, the variety. Binoculars glued to my face for hours, I was. Mum kept threatening to swap them for a plate of chips. Mum always does. Did you see any of those rare ones you were hoping for? The… what were they called? The Stone Curlews? Aye, the Stone Curlews! And the Bittern, didn’t you see the Bittern, Arthur? Proper elusive blokes those, they are. Moved so quick! I did! Briefly. A flash of brown across the reeds. Nearly missed it entirely. That was the highlight, though. Mum was a lot less impressed. Said it just looked like a 'big, noisy heron'. Classic Mum. Anything else exciting happen? Did you catch any fish? Nope. Tried my hand at a bit of fishing in the Broads, but came away empty-handed. The locals, they were pulling ‘em out left and right. Turns out, I’m not quite the angling prodigy I thought I was. You never have been, Arthur! You’ve got two left feet and clumsy hands. It's a wonder you didn't hook yourself rather than a fish. Very funny, dear. It was still relaxing, even if I didn't catch anything. Just being out in the fresh air, away from… well, away from everything. Sounds like you needed it. Work’s been pretty hectic, hasn’t it? Launching that new phase of the project put everyone on edge. Tell me about it. I’m practically living off coffee and sheer willpower these days. Although, maybe I should take your Dad's approach and embrace… birdwatching. It does sound rather calming. Don't you start, lass. You'd get bored within five minutes. You'd need chasing after some handsome young ornithologist, you would! Mum! It's not all handsome ornithologists, you know. There’s a real community of birdwatchers. Proper friendly lot. They swap stories, share tips… and argue passionately about whether a certain sighting was actually  that  rare. Sounds… nerdy. In a good way, I think. Are the places you went really touristy? A bit, in some areas. But we focused on the quieter reserves, the less-trodden paths. Found a lovely little pub in a village called Horning. Proper good fish and chips, too.

Right, that’s more like it. This instant stuff is just… insulting, really. Shouldn’t be allowed to call it tea. You’re being dramatic, Ben. It’s early on a Saturday. Give the poor stuff a chance. And, FYI, I made a massive batch of that lentil soup yesterday. There’s loads in the fridge if you’re feeling peckish. Way better than instant anything. Morning, you two! Lentil soup sounds amazing. I practically lived on that during uni. Remember those ramen noodle nights, Chloe? We were a mess. Don't remind me! We thought we were being so clever, surviving on next to nothing. Though, realistically, we were just glorifying cheap carbs. Clever is a strong word. I was spending most nights trying to debug some frankly ridiculous piece of software after a 12-hour shift. Didn't have the energy for culinary experimentation. Though, modularity back then… Christ, the spaghetti code! It makes me shudder even now. Speaking of shuddering, did you see this article about the proposed changes to the tax system? Another mess. They’re going to hit freelancers and small businesses hard. I’m trying to find a contact at the Treasury to get some clarity, but it's like pulling teeth. Ugh, typical. Everything seems designed to make life harder. I'm honestly starting to resent my phone. I spend more time doomscrolling through depressing news than actually connecting with people. Tell me about it. I was reading about that AI thing, the one that's generating images. It’s remarkable, really, the processing power. But then you think about the implications for artists and designers…feels a bit… precarious, doesn’t it? Definitely. It’s the same with journalism. AI can churn out basic news reports, but it can’t do the investigative work, the nuanced storytelling. That's where the human element comes in. That’s why I'm no rushing to get replaced. Though, on a lighter note, have you seen pictures of Harry Styles at that charity gala? That suit… chef’s kiss. Seriously, he’s nailed the whole timeless, effortlessly cool vibe. Harry Styles? I thought you were more into…well, you know, obscure Czech poets. A girl can have varied interests, Ben. It keeps things interesting. Besides, don’t tell anyone, but I’m starting a pottery class next week. Need to find a creative outlet, apparently. Stress relief, they say.

Honestly, I still can’t quite believe you’re going, Reg. It feels so… sudden. Like yesterday you were complaining about needing to fix that leaky tap in the downstairs loo. Aye, lass, time flies, doesn't it? That tap's still drippin', by the way. You sorted it out then? No, Dad. Chloe’s been meaning to. She's got bigger things on her mind, hasn't she? Like, leaving England for…Saudi Arabia. Bit of a jump, that. It’s a fantastic opportunity, Liam! Don't be flippant. It's a three-year contract, solid pay, and a chance to really build something. And it's good for my career, you know. Three years is a long time to be away. You’ll miss Christmas. Of course I will, Josh. But we’ll FaceTime every day. And you guys can come out and visit! Imagine, sunshine and camels! Camels, eh? Proper holiday that would be. Mind you, I'd want a good satnav. Remember that time I got lost in Wales trying to find Auntie Maureen’s? Ended up in a sheep field. Oh god, Dad. You were halfway to Cornwall! Everyone was on about it for weeks. And you blamed Google Maps. It was your fault for not paying attention. Google Maps is unreliable, I tell you! Give me a proper map any day. You can’t trust those digital things. They’ll lead you astray. Should’ve got a Garmin, like Chloe did. She's smart that one. It's very reliable, actually. And I’ve downloaded offline maps. So, no sheep fields for me, thank you very much. I even programmed in all the best coffee shops in Jeddah. Gotta have my caffeine fix. Coffee in Saudi? Is that allowed? Yes, Josh, coffee is definitely allowed. They practically invented it! It's a whole culture. They’ve got these amazing coffee houses. So, what's the decorating like out there then? Are there different styles? I'm thinking of finally getting around to painting the living room. Mum keeps nagging me. Apparently, it's very traditional. Lots of ornate details, rich colours… It’s very different from what I'm used to. I’m taking some pictures of the living room, and maybe I’ll recreate the style in my apartment. It’ll be a talking point. Talking point, is it? Back in my day, a talking point was whether you could get the telly working after a power cut.

Stunning, aren’t they? Absolutely stunning. I’ve never seen such a deep crimson. It reminds me a little of the rata flowers back in Wellington, though the scale is just… different here. They are lovely, darling. Though I am slightly peckish. I’m regretting not grabbing a pastry before we came out here. All this floral beauty is making me think of crumble and custard. You always tie floral appreciation to baked goods, don’t you, Eleanor? It’s a defining characteristic. Anyway, I’m feeling pretty drained. Not the best energy levels today. I think this Stockholm air is getting to me. It’s so…clean. Almost aggressively so. Clean is a good thing, isn’t it? I feel invigorated! Although, I did have a bit of a rough night. My sinuses decided to throw a party. Think I’m slightly allergic to something here. My nose has been playing up something awful. Reminds me of when I was little, Mum would get a sneezing fit whenever she came near the lilac bush. She blamed the pollen, of course. Oh, poor love. Allergies are the worst. Have you tried those nasal sprays? The saline ones are usually quite good. And are you drinking enough water? That often helps, you know. I had a terrible sinus infection last winter, felt dreadful for weeks. My doctor put me on some really strong antibiotics, and a humidifier. Made a world of difference. I have some nasal spray, yes. Not touched it yet, feeling a bit too lazy. Water...that's a fair point. I’ve been mostly on coffee, if I’m honest. And a surprising amount of Swedish fizzy water – it's everywhere! Right, I just got an email from the conference organisers. They’ve moved the evening reception to a different venue. Apparently, there's been a catering issue. A catering issue? That doesn't sound promising. Last time there was a “catering issue” at one of these conferences, it turned out the chef had simply lost the entire order of canapés. Mid-event. Chaos ensued. Oh dear. I hate being hungry at these things. Remember that conference in Edinburgh? The only food they offered was stale biscuits and lukewarm coffee. I nearly fainted. This one's at the Grand Hotel, apparently. Upmarket. Hopefully, they've sorted something decent out. It’s a shame, really. I was planning on having a proper chat with Ingrid from the sustainability collective.

Honestly, Mum, it’s just… frustrating. My phone keeps misinterpreting me. It's like, I’m saying “book” and it thinks I said “look.” It’s a nightmare when I’m trying to send a quick message. That’s technology for ya, innit? Always trying to outsmart us. Remember when they first brought out those mobile phones? Massive things they were, like bricks. Couldn’t believe anyone would carry one around. And the cost! Don't remind me, Arthur. I remember saving for months just to get a basic one. Though, I’ll admit, it’s handy now. Especially with work. Though I still find it odd, the way younger people talk to 'em. Like they're a person themselves. It’s the accent, isn’t it? It messes with the software. My mate, Darren, same problem. Lives up in Manchester, proper northern accent, and Siri thinks he’s ordering takeaway half the time. See? It’s not just me! And it’s not just the vowels, it’s the whole drawl, you know? Like the way we say "bath" – it’s a whole different sound. People from up north say it completely different. Aye, the South East accent is a tricky one. It's changed a lot over the years. Used to be much stronger, you know. My Dad, born in the East End, he had a real Cockney accent. Couldn’t understand half of what he said sometimes. Your dad? Wasn't he always complaining about how posh everyone was getting? He used to grumble about how kids weren't speaking properly anymore. Sounding all…Americanized. He did. Used to say, "They’re losing the spirit of London, they are." Though he could be a bit of a grumpy old man, bless 'im. Remember that time he got into it with that delivery driver about the pronunciation of 'chorizo'? Oh god, yes! Mum was mortified! He was going on and on about how it wasn’t ‘chor-ee-zo’ like they think, it was ‘chor-eeth-o’! He was always a stickler for proper pronunciation. Though I do worry about young people these days. Heard Sarah's been having a terrible time with Mark over custody. He's…difficult. Mark's always been difficult. Remember when he used to steal my biscuits when we were kids? Thought he was being funny. That's awful about Sarah, though. I wish there was something  I  could do.

Right, nearly there. Just needs a bit more seasoning. Honestly, these boys eat like horses. Did you manage to grate all that cheddar, Leo? My arms are aching! Yeah, finished it. It was a lot. Why do we need  that  much cheese anyway? It’s just chips and burgers. It’s not  just  chips and burgers, darling. It's a "Supper with the boys" extravaganza. And you know how much Tom likes his cheesy chips. Speaking of extravagance, I was thinking about that Baked Alaska we saw that chef make on that cooking show… remember? Vaguely. It was showy, wasn't it? All ice cream and meringue. Bit ridiculous. Ridiculously delicious, I think. I was toying with the idea of attempting one for Halloween. It would be a bit of a statement, wouldn't it? Halloween’s just about pumpkins and scary masks, Mum. Not fancy desserts. Are we even having a proper party this year? Last year’s was a bit… lukewarm. Oh, believe me, this year we’re going all out. I've already started recruiting volunteers. Mrs. Peterson next door is making spooky cupcakes. And I'm hoping to get Liam, from school, to help with the music. He's brilliant with a DJ set. Liam? He's a bit… intense. Remember when he tried to convince everyone the pumpkins were government surveillance devices? Yes, I do! A rather creative interpretation of conspiracy theories, wouldn't you say? Still, he's enthusiastic. It's good to encourage that. You know, it reminds me of your Uncle David when he was your age. Absolutely obsessed with science fiction. Uncle David? He was a bit weird, wasn't he? Always talking about… things. What did he actually  do  again? He was a research scientist, actually. Worked on some pretty groundbreaking stuff, though it was a bit above my head. Sadly, he faced a lot of… pushback. They claimed his ideas were too radical, that he was destabilising the accepted scientific norms. There were whispers of discrimination, of course. Often minorities of thought don't fare well, do they? Discrimination? Like, people weren't nice to him because of his ideas? That’s messed up. It is. It’s a constant battle, isn’t it? Fighting for acceptance, for being heard. Even now, in our supposedly enlightened times. It’s something I’ve had to contend with in my career, too.

Cor, this is lovely, this is. Proper Welsh breakfast, innit? You’ve outdone yourself, love. Though, honestly, I still think a proper Yorkshire fry is unbeatable. None of this fancy smoked salmon, you know. Give me a black pudding any day. You and your black pudding, Bronwyn. It’s a wonder you don't turn into one. It’s good to have you here, though. It’s been ages. Feels like forever since we last properly caught up. How was the journey down? Aye, it were alright. A bit choppy on the train, mind. And that conductor kept giving me the eye! Cheeky bugger. But I got here safe and sound. This place is lovely, your kitchen. Much bigger than mine. I’m crammed in like sardines in Shipley, you know. Still love it though, wouldn't swap it. You could always move! Though I imagine the idea of leaving Yorkshire… Well. Anyway, I was thinking about you the other day, actually. Remember how we talked about potentially going to New York together? New York? Oh, aye! That were a grand idea. We’d have a right laugh. Though the flights… crikey. They’re getting awful expensive, aren’t they? And the jet lag! I’m not as young as I used to be. I know, it’s a bit daunting. I was looking at some deals, and a long weekend could actually be manageable. We could hit the museums, see a Broadway show… It'd be brilliant to go back. Remember that little jazz club we stumbled upon in Greenwich Village? Oh, bless me, aye! That were a result, that were. Tiny place, packed to the rafters. Don’t think I’ve ever danced so much in me life. Speaking of things that put a spring in your step… how's the flying lessons going? Last I heard, you were still terrified of take-off. They're… progressing. Slowly. I'm starting to get used to the controls, I think. The instructor’s a patient man, thankfully. But that initial feeling of leaving the ground… it’s still pretty intense. You should try it! It'd be a laugh to see you yelping. Me? Flying? Don’t be daft, love! I've got more sense than that. I’ll stick to the trains, thank you very much. Though, you know, sometimes I think about how different me life would be if I’d stayed in Japan.

"Double word score! 'Quixotic'! Honestly, where do you even  find  these letters, Liam?" "Just luck, I suppose. You’re moaning, but you just played a seventeen-letter word. Don't pretend you're not enjoying massively dominating me." "Dominating is a strong word. I’m merely… slightly ahead. And it’s ludicrous. This board is clearly biased towards obscure words. Remember last week when I couldn’t find a single vowel? It's a conspiracy, I tell you!" “Oh, stop being dramatic, Finn. It’s just Scrabble. Besides, you were half an hour late getting here! You nearly ruined the whole evening.” "I was  not  half an hour late! More like, twenty-five minutes. And that was entirely the fault of the bus! It decided to take a scenic tour of Cardiff Bay before finally deciding to deposit me here." "Sounds about right. Cardiff buses have a mind of their own. So, are we still arguing about the origins of 'scent' versus 'cent'?" “Yes! Finn was insisting that 'cent' came from the same root as ‘century’ which, ironically, doesn't explain why 'scent' has a 'c' and not an 's'." "I maintain it's a linguistic anomaly! It throws the whole thing into chaos! It's just… wrong. Shouldn’t it be ‘sente’ or something? Like, related to sense?" "It’s Latin, Finn. ‘Scent' comes from  sentire , to feel or perceive. 'Cent' comes from  centum , a hundred. See? Perfectly logical, in a ridiculously convoluted Latin way." “Fine, fine. You’re the linguistic genius. Still doesn't make the Scrabble board any easier." He looks at his rack. "Urgh. Two 'Q's'. Utterly useless." "You know, thinking about words and their origins makes me want to revisit some of my childhood favourites. Remember 'The Gruffalo'? Julia Donaldson is just brilliant. The way she uses rhyme and rhythm to structure the story..." “Yeah, good shout. My niece absolutely loves that one. I read it to her every time I see her. Though, sometimes I think  I'm  learning more than she is." He pauses, then a thoughtful look crosses his face. "Speaking of children's books, did anyone ever tell you why 'A' is for Apple?' It's just...arbitrary, isn't it? Why not 'A' is for Ant?" “It’s because ‘apple’ starts with ‘A’, isn’t it? It's the most basic, iconic example! I bet it’s all to do with reinforcing memory and association.

Cor, it's blowin' a right gale out there, isn't it, Brenda? Sounds like the wind’s tryin’ to blow the shed down again. Might ‘ave to get round to fixin' that later, if me back allows it, mind. It is rather fierce, Arthur. I was worried about the roses. They’re bending double. Should have pruned ‘em back a bit sooner. You did mention it, didn’t you? I just...well, you know how I are. Always put things off. Aye, you do. Like a magpie collectin’ worries, you do. Don't you fret about the roses, Brenda. They’ll weather it. They always do. Remember that storm back in ‘86? Blew half the apple tree over, it did. Yet, it still gave us apples the year after, didn’t it? Oh, goodness, yes. And you were so cross about that tree! Woke up at five in the mornin' to survey the damage. Made a right fuss, you did. Well, it was me apples, weren't it? Always were fond of a good Bramley pie. Though, me digestion ain't what it used to be. Doctor says I need to be careful. Says I should cut back on the processed stuff. Everything’s "processed" these days, Arthur. It’s hard to avoid. Even the carrots come pre-peeled sometimes! Did you see that article in the paper about the price of eggs? Ridiculous, absolutely ridiculous. Nearly three pounds a dozen! Three pounds! Blimey. That’s daylight robbery, that is. Remember when you could get ‘em for tuppence and a smile? Mind, they weren't always the best then. Often had a funny taste, like dust and feathers. That’s right. My mum used to say it was because the chickens were eating too many grit! She’d mix some breadcrumbs in the feed to try and improve the flavour. Aye, those were simpler times, weren't they? Less fuss, less bother. No internet, no mobile phones...people talked to each other. Actually talked. Not just pokin' at little screens. You’re getting melancholy again, Arthur. Don’t go down that road. We have each other, don’t we? That’s something to be thankful for. And we've got this lovely little house, and the garden, even with the wild roses currently bending over... Aye, you’re right, Brenda. You always were the sensible one. Just thinkin' 'bout old times, that's all.

These are absolutely cracking, Annie. Honestly, you’ve outdone yourself. Better than my Doris used to make, and that's saying something. She was a dab hand in the kitchen, my Doris. Always had a roast on a Sunday, rain or shine. That's high praise, Dad. It’s just a simple roast, really. Though, I did try a new trick with the potatoes. Soaked them in cold water for an hour before roasting – makes them extra crispy, apparently. Worth a try, I thought. It certainly is, love. They are beautifully crisp. I've been reading a lot about those potato soaking techniques – apparently, it draws out some of the surface starch, which is what leads to that golden, crunchy exterior. Clever tip! Though, I’m always terrified I’ll oversoak them and they’ll just be soggy. Soggy potatoes are a tragedy, that’s a fact. Doris wouldn't have stood for it! You know, I’ve been trying to get into this fitness lark, you both have been on about it for ages. Bought myself one of those apps – “FitLife,” it’s called. Seems a bit daft, really. Telling me to do step counts and…meditation? It’s alright, Dad, don't knock it till you’ve tried it. It can be motivating. Is it tracking your steps? Are you getting out and about more? Well, I walked to the shops the other day. That's something, isn't it? It kept nagging me, that app. "You need to move more!" Honestly, felt like a nag! Though, the reminders to drink more water have been useful. Hydration, they call it. Doris always said a good cup of tea was the best hydration. Tea is definitely essential! And FitLife does have some lovely guided meditations. Honestly, even ten minutes can make a difference. Speaking of things changing, have you both seen the news about the station? They're finally saying they're going to open it! Really? The Exmouth station? After all this time? I thought it was just a pipe dream. Apparently, they've sorted out some of the signal issues, and they're saying it should be operational by next month. Can you believe it? It'll be brilliant for getting to Exeter without having to drive. Means I can finally ditch the car for school trips! About time. Been saying they'd open it for years, haven't they?

Right, so, stag do ideas. We’re officially in brainstorming territory now, aren't we? Ben's getting married, and we need to make it legendary. No pressure. Legendary is a bit much, isn’t it? Just… memorable. And, crucially, doesn’t massively bankrupt us. My parents are still hovering about, wondering when I'm going to start contributing to the household income, you know? Fair point. Legendary  and  financially responsible. That's a challenge. I was thinking… paintballing and then a curry? Classic, reliable fun. Paintballing? Seriously? That's the best you've got? Feels a bit… 14th birthday, doesn’t it? Remember Mark Henderson’s paintballing party? He spent the whole time hiding behind the inflatable castle. Okay, okay, you've got a point. Poor Mark. Alright, scratch that. What about… Prague? We could do a weekend in Prague. Cheap flights, loads to see, plenty of pubs. Prague's not bad. But it’s a trek. And Ben gets motion sickness. Remember that boat trip we took to Cornwall? He spent the entire time looking green. Oh God, I'd blocked that out. Right. So, staying within the UK… what about Cardiff? Close enough, decent nightlife, and we could potentially sneak in a brewery tour. Cardiff’s alright. There's that Escape Room place we talked about. Remember, the one based on ‘The Lie’? The historical fiction one? The one Sarah swore was going to give her a panic attack? Yeah, I remember. Bit intense for a stag, isn’t it? Though, it  was  surprisingly well researched, from what she said. The detail about the clothing, the politics of the time... It was. But Sarah's a drama student. She sees conspiracies and historical inaccuracies everywhere. I thought it was captivating, actually. Have you read Hilary Mantel's Cromwell trilogy? I’ve started  Wolf Hall . Found it a bit dense, to be honest. I’m more of a Shakespeare man, myself. Did you see that recent BBC adaptation of  King Lear ? Ian McKellen was phenomenal. Yeah, that was pretty good! Although, I’m a bit of a purist, you know? They changed a couple of scenes which, while I understand they were trying to modernize it, felt a bit… pointless. It lost some of the power, I think. I agree. They always do, don’t they? Trying to appeal to a wider audience. Speaking of wider audiences, did you catch the United game on Saturday?

Honestly, Greens is always a good shout. It's just… reliably nice, isn't it? Especially when you’re meeting someone you haven’t seen in ages. Less pressure than trying to find some trendy, new spot. Totally! You know me, I'm all about consistency. And these scones are  divine . Did you have the sausage bap? They’re pretty decent too. It's brilliant being back in Cambourne. Feels quieter than Oxford ever did. It really does. So, tell me everything! Oxford life, Pearson life… spill! Last time we spoke, you were stressing about that big campaign launch. How did it go? Ugh, don’t even remind me. The launch itself was fine, decent engagement, sales numbers were… okay. But the  lead-up  was a nightmare. Everyone was working like crazy, barely sleeping.
