My boss kept changing his mind about the colour palette! Seriously, one day it was teal, the next it was mustard. Mustard! For luxury skincare. Mustard? That sounds… disastrous. You must be gutted after all that work. I am, a little. But you know what? I think I'm finally getting used to the corporate roller coaster. It's less intense now. And I'm actually enjoying the strategy side of things a bit more - figuring out  how  to reach the target audience, rather than just stressing about the visuals. What about you? How’s the Project Co-ordinating life treating you? Still drowning in spreadsheets? Don't even joke. The Henderson project is… well, it’s Henderson. The client has  opinions  on everything. And they change them approximately every five minutes. It's brilliant for my stress levels. I think I've aged about three years in the last month. Oh, I feel you. Difficult clients are the worst. Do you remember Liam, from uni? Sarah's brother? Vaguely… the one who tried to convince us all that cryptocurrency was going to solve world hunger? That’s the one! He’s back in town, apparently. Sarah ran into him at that farmers’ market last week. Apparently, he's trying to sell some "revolutionary" organic fertiliser now. Seriously? From crypto to fertiliser? That's quite the pivot. Is he... single? Just asking for a friend, obviously. Wouldn't you like to know? Sarah said he looks… different. Apparently, he's been spending a lot of time in the garden. Which, I suppose, is a step up from obsessing over blockchain technology.

“Aye, that’s proper loud, isn’t it? Thought you’d’ve gotten used to it by now, livin' here. Still makes me jump every time.” She reaches for the kettle, carefully pouring the boiling water into a teapot filled with loose leaf tea. "So, did your mum call today? About Nan's birthday?" “She did. Apparently, she's already drafted a list of potential presents. Fifteen items, including a 'heated foot massager' and a ceramic gnome. The gnome is non-negotiable, she insists.” He chuckles softly. “She said you’d find that amusing, knowing your history with garden ornaments.” “Oh, don’t remind me! Remember that flamingo I got her for Christmas? The one with the ridiculous pink feathers? She hid it in the shed for three years. Said it ‘clashed with the rhododendrons’.” She adds a splash of milk to her tea. "She's a card, our Nan. Seriously though, is she doing alright? Mum sounded a bit… worried.” “She’s fine, all things considered. A bit stiff in the morning, but booked a physiotherapy appointment. Mostly, she's just bored, I think. Misses having you around more, especially. She keeps talking about those scones you made last time. Says she’s been trying to replicate them, but 'something's missing'." “She’ll never manage! It’s the clotted cream, that’s what. You can't get proper clotted cream outside of the Northeast, you know. It’s a geographical anomaly. Right, let’s get some biscuits out. Do you fancy a ginger nut? Got a lovely tin from Fortnum & Mason, surprisingly affordable actually.” She rummages in a cupboard, pulling out a decorative tin. "Ginger nut sounds perfect, thanks. You know, I was reading about the history of tea the other day – fascinating stuff. Apparently, the Dutch were the first to really popularise it in Europe, importing it in the 17th century. Before that, it was exclusively a Chinese thing." He pauses, biting into a biscuit. "Although, of course, they latched onto the British obsession with it quite quickly, didn’t they? Smart move on their part." "Always tryin' to muscle in on our things, the Dutch. It's like with the chip shops. Everyone's got ‘em now, but it all started with Belgian immigrants in the north, didn’t it? Proper tasty they were too, back then. Better than most of the ones you get nowadays. All mushy and greasy!"

Morning, Rhys. Dreadful weather we're having, isn’t it? Reminds me a little of Cairo, actually, that oppressive humidity. Though, of course, without the sunshine. Morning, Alistair. Aye, it's a dreich one, alright. Typical for October, I'm afraid. Cairo, eh? You never strike me as someone yearning for the desert heat. Thought you were a man of English gardens. Well, one appreciates variety, don’t you? Spent most of the weekend trying to wrestle the bindweed under control in my rose garden. A losing battle, I suspect. How was yours, Rhys? Did you manage to avoid the downpours? Managed, thankfully. Spent a fair bit of time in the shed, getting things ready for winter. Drove over to see a bit of football, too. Newport County. Not exactly the Premier League, but good to see the lads giving it a proper go. Football. Yes, I caught a bit of Man City's match. The youngsters they're bringing through these days are incredible, aren’t they? Did you see that boy, Liam… something or other… scoring? Astonishing skill. Seems like every Premier League club is churning out these exceptionally talented kids. Liam Cullen, you mean? Aye, a bright spark, that one. Though I wonder, do these lads have a proper upbringing? Nowadays, they're practically groomed for it from the time they can walk. Not like my generation, mucking about in the fields and playing street football. Less pressure, I reckon. It's certainly a different landscape. Speaking of skill and pressure, did you see Ronnie O'Sullivan’s performance in the Championship League? Blistering! He’s still got it, even at his age. Though I do find the commentary sometimes… relentless. Ronnie’s a marvel, no doubt. Though I’ve always preferred Mark Selby. A bit more understated, and just as lethal. Gives me a good reason to put the feet up on a Sunday afternoon, mind you. Actually, reminds me, I need to get the snooker table out of the garage. Haven't touched it in months. Dustier than a tomb in there, I'm sure. You should. It's wonderful exercise, actually. Keeps the mind sharp, you know. Keeps you out of trouble, too. Which reminds me, have you seen the number of applications for those police recruitment drives? It’s quite remarkable. Seems like a lot of young people are looking for a career in law enforcement.

Right then, let’s have a proper look at this Christening budget. It’s creeping up, isn’t it? I thought we'd agreed on a limit of £800? Is Teddy coming to the Christening, Nana? Of course, sweetheart. Teddy can come. He'll be right next to you, keeping you company. Though, he might get a bit bored watching everyone else get blessed. Are you excited? Mmm-hmm! Will there be cake? A big cake? With pink frosting? Yes, darling, a big cake with pink frosting, especially for you. Your mum's ordered it – apparently a unicorn is involved. Can you imagine? Hey! Sorry I'm late, the library was rammed. What’s the war about? Is it cake-related? Oh, hello, love. Just trying to rein in the Christening spending. It’s all getting a bit out of hand. And trying to convince your cousin that a bouncy castle  isn't  essential. A bouncy castle? Seriously? Who needs a bouncy castle at a church? That’s a recipe for disaster, isn't it? Especially with all the little ones running around. Exactly! Your Auntie Carol is adamant. Says it'll keep the children entertained. I said, "Carol, we have a garden! And cake!" Classic Auntie Carol. You know she firmly believes glitter fixes everything. Right, let me see this budget. . Okay, £800... where's the money going? Oh, the photographer is eating a significant chunk. I know! I didn't realise how much they charged for an hour's coverage. But your mum insisted on getting professional photos. Said she wants to capture every precious moment. I tried to explain I’m perfectly capable of taking photos with my phone, but… Mum’s Mum-ness shining through. It's unrelenting, isn't it? Still, lovely to have good quality photos. What about the venue hire? Is that in line? Venue's fine. It's the little extras that's adding up. Favours, decorations... that sort of thing. I was thinking, maybe we could ditch the personalised chocolates? They’re £2 a pop. No chocolates? I like chocolates! Don’t worry, sweetheart. You’ll get plenty of chocolates. We’ll buy you a whole bag afterwards. Just not for the guests, alright? Honestly, ditch the chocolates. No one really  needs  a favour at a Christening. They’re coming to celebrate. They’re not expecting a parting gift.

Honestly, this rain is just relentless, isn’t it? Been chucking it down all morning. Makes you want to just curl up with a good book and forget the world. Tell me about it! I had to sprint from the car to the shop this morning, soaked to the bone. Luckily, we've got a decent amount of umbrellas behind the counter, which saved a few customers. It's not exactly sunshine and rainbows for retail, is it? Though Mrs. Higgins did comment that the rain made the petunias look particularly vibrant. You can't win, can you? Dinos like rain! Roar! Of course they do, darling. Dinosaurs love rain. Smart dinosaur. So, about this New York trip… I was just looking at flights again last night. Direct flights are surprisingly reasonable if you book a bit further out. But hotels... the hotels are proper eye-watering. I know! We need to prioritise, don't we? Statue of Liberty, definitely. Central Park, of course. Maybe a Broadway show? But the hotel… maybe we could look at something a little further out, with good transport links? It’ll still be exciting, just... easier on the wallet. That’s a good shout. I was looking at this one near Times Square, looked lovely in the photos, but the reviews mentioned it being a bit noisy. Not ideal with a little one needing her beauty sleep. Remember that hotel in Spain, eh? The one with the dodgy plumbing? Still makes me shudder. Don’t remind me! The shower head practically fell off. And the breakfast… well, let’s just say I’m glad we found that little bakery nearby. At least  that  started the holiday off on a positive note. It's funny, isn’t it? You can have the most amazing scenery, but one bad hotel can really put a damper on things. Rawr! Bad hotels scary! Very scary indeed. Now, thinking about holidays… Your mum's been going on about that Caribbean cruise again. You think we should entertain it? She has, hasn't she? It does sound lovely. Sun, sand, unlimited cocktails… But with you and me working, and someone having to look after Little Miss Dinosaur here, it's just so complicated. Plus, I think she secretly just wants to swan around with her friends on deck. You're probably right. Though it  would  be nice to just…  relax , wouldn't it?

Right, so, this is… this is the current state of affairs. Don't mind the mess, yeah? It’s been a bit hectic. Crikey, that  is  a mess. Looks like a paper snowstorm. What's all this then? You’ve got more sheets than the Ritz. It’s the dissertation proposal. Officially. Unofficially, it’s a monument to my procrastination and a constant source of anxiety. See, I've got the initial outline here, the literature review draft, and then… well, then there’s this. That looks like… a spreadsheet? Filled with numbers and… citations? Right. That's my attempt at a systematic literature search. I’m trying to track all the articles I’ve read - which is, you know, hundreds at this point - and categorize them by theme, methodology, relevance… It’s supposed to help me identify gaps in the existing research. It mostly just makes me feel inadequate. Sounds… ambitious. Is it working, though? Nah, not really. Honestly, I'm starting to think I’ve bitten off more than I can chew. My supervisor – Professor Davies – she’s brilliant but… she’s got expectations, yeah? She really wants this to be groundbreaking, original, the whole shebang. I'm just trying to avoid accidentally plagiarizing someone, that’s the level I’m operating at. Groundbreaking is a tall order, innit? Especially for a dissertation. Most people just want to pass. Have you spoken to Davies about this feeling? About maybe scaling things back a bit? I tried. Last week. It didn’t go great. She said something about “pushing boundaries” and “intellectual courage.” And then she told me to read Foucault again. Foucault! I’ve read  Discipline and Punish  twice already. It’s practically seared into my brain. Ouch. Davies sounds… intense. Look, is the core idea solid at least? You’re still interested in the impact of digital media on local community identity, right? That's what you were buzzing about a few weeks back. Yeah, that’s the… the spark. I still think it’s a worthwhile topic. It's just… how do I  prove  it’s worthwhile? Everyone’s doing something with digital media. It feels like shouting into the void. Maybe you're looking at it too broadly? You could narrow the scope. Focus on one particular community, one specific platform… something that feels more manageable. Like, instead of 'digital media' in general, maybe focus on how TikTok impacts youth culture in Lancaster?

Right, so I had the weirdest dream last night. Honestly, you wouldn't believe it. Oh? Do tell. Was it one of those where you're falling endlessly, or being chased by something ridiculous? Worse, I think. I was… presenting. Standing on a stage in what looked like a gigantic biscuit tin. A biscuit tin? What on earth were you presenting? That’s the thing! I had no idea. I was just… lecturing. About…hedgehogs. Serious, academic-looking notes about hedgehogs. And the audience was all squirrels, wearing tiny glasses. They kept throwing acorns at me. Acorns! Did they hit you, Daddy? They did, darling. They tickled, actually. It was all very strange. What did you dream about, love? I was flying! With a sparkly unicorn! And we landed on a giant cupcake! A cupcake? That’s much more appealing than hedgehogs and squirrels, isn't it? You're getting better at dreaming than your dad then. His dreams are always about work, or something equally dull. Hey! Hedgehogs are fascinating creatures! And besides, that was a particularly bizarre one. What about you? Any dream adventures? No, sadly, nothing quite so entertaining. I dreamt I was marking essays… endless essays. And they were all written in Klingon. Seriously? That's awful! Perfect for a teacher, though, I suppose. Prepared for anything. Exactly! Always ready for the unexpected linguistic challenge. You know, it got me thinking... we were talking about weird dreams, and wouldn't it be amazing to just… win the lottery? Just once? Enough to buy a little place with a garden, maybe. Don't I know it. A garden big enough for a dog. That's all I really want. A Labrador, you know? Big, clumsy, happy. Running around in the sun. Doggy! Doggy! Yes, darling, a doggy. But dogs cost money, don't they? Not just the initial purchase, but food, vets… it all adds up. Hence the lottery pipe dream. I bought one this morning. A silly little scratch card. Didn't win anything, obviously. But it’s nice to imagine, isn't it? Just for a moment? It is. Imagine… no more Prospect Research. No more spreadsheets. Just… peace and quiet, a cup of tea, and a Labrador snoring at my feet. Or teaching Shakespeare to a class full of truly engaged students who actually read the plays before class. No disruptions, everyone’s listening… And no Klingon essays?

Och, it’s mingin’ in here, isn’t it? Proper stuffy. And me head’s still hammerin’. I swear, I've got a wee headache brewing, right behind me eyes. It is a bit warm, yeah. I’ll crack a window. And are you alright? You look a bit pale. Seriously, how’s your wrist? You didn’t tell me properly earlier. Just said you “banged it.” Banged it is an understatement, love. It's like someone’s put a brick in it. I can’t move it much without a proper yell. Doctor said it’s “likely a sprain, possibly a minor fracture.” Lovely. Just lovely. A minor fracture. Like that makes it better, doesn’t it? Right. Well, the A&E experience couldn't have been fun. You sounded…stressed on the phone. What was it like? Honestly, I've heard horror stories. Horror stories don’t even cover it. It was absolute chaos. Worse than Christmas Eve at the Metrocentre. People everywhere, crying babies, folk shouting. And the smell! Like disinfectant mixed with damp socks. I were sat for near four hours, you know? Four hours! Just waitin’ to see someone. Four hours?! That’s outrageous. Did they even triage you properly? I mean, you said it looked pretty swollen. Aye, they had a look. Got a quick poke, a quick "does it hurt here?" and then told me to wait. I kept trying to explain about the wrist, and how I couldn’t really grip anything, but it were all just a blur of noise and stressed-out nurses. I felt like I were shoutin’ into the void, genuinely. One nurse kept asking if I’d taken any paracetamol. Like that were gonna fix a potential fracture! Seriously? That’s ridiculous. I'm so sorry, love. That sounds awful. Did you see a doctor eventually? A proper one? Aye, eventually. A young lad, looked about your age, actually. Seemed alright, though a bit tired. He did an X-ray, sent me home with a bandage and some painkillers. Said to come back if it got worse. Like  that’s  helpful. What’s “worse” supposed to look like? Glowing green and startin' to hum? Okay, yeah, that’s a bit vague. He could have been clearer. Did he give you any advice on resting it? Or what to do if the pain increases? He mumbled somethin’ about elevation.

Honestly, Bernard, did you see that piece on the BBC about the situation in Sudan? Absolutely appalling. Makes you wonder what the world’s coming to, doesn’t it? All those displaced families… it's just heartbreaking. Aye, saw it. Dreadful, truly. Though, the BBC always paints it a bit… dramatic, doesn’t it? Still, there’s no sugarcoating the fact folks are suffering. It's difficult to reconcile the scale of the human tragedy with the complexities of international politics, isn’t it? Trying to get a clear picture? Clear picture? Bernard, we’re lucky to be sitting here, sipping tea, discussing it over scones. Clear isn't the point, is it? It’s just… overwhelming. Makes you appreciate a bit of peace and quiet, doesn't it? Reminds me of that trip we took to Bosnia back in… '98, was it? Still gives me the shivers thinking about it. '98! Good Lord, that  was  a while ago. You remember that little cafe we stumbled upon in Mostar? Best coffee I’ve ever had. Though, the shadow of the bridge being destroyed… the weight of the history… it clung to the air. I’ve been thinking a lot about those times lately. Yes, quite. It did. Speaking of history, have you heard from Margaret and David recently? I tried ringing them last week, but I got their answering machine. Margaret called me yesterday, actually. They’re off to Greece next week. A bit of sunshine, she said, to chase away the grey skies. Said David’s been a bit under the weather, but nothing serious. Still misses his gardening, apparently. Good, good. Glad to hear it. Gardening is a man’s solace, isn’t it? Now, about this idea of yours… this “Artisan Ales Emporium,” you called it? Right, yes! It's been percolating, you see. I've networked, I've done some preliminary research... There's a real gap in the market in Hove, I'm certain of it. People are craving something beyond your mass-produced lagers, you know? Craft breweries are booming, and I thought, why not curate the best of Sussex and beyond? Local, small-batch, interesting brews... Sounds ambitious, Bernard. Quite ambitious. The initial investment alone... Have you secured any funding, beyond your savings? It’s a significant outlay, isn't it? Setting up a retail space, securing the right licenses... it all adds up.

Honestly, this place is…charming in a slightly chaotic way, isn’t it? Like a Victorian museum threw up and decided to serve pints. Those mismatched chairs…and look at that wallpaper! Chaotic is a good word for it. Definitely not minimalist. Reminds me a bit of some of the student halls we used to live in at Edinburgh. Remember that one on Bristo Place? The floral wallpaper that was peeling everywhere? Oh, god, yes! And the communal kitchen that always smelled vaguely of burnt toast and disappointment. I’d almost forgotten that era of my life. Did you ever think we'd end up in a pub that feels like a flashback to those days? Life's funny like that, isn’t it? So, about dinner… are we still thinking Thai down the road? Or are we feeling something more… Guardhouse-y? They do a decent shepherd's pie, I think. Shepherd's pie is tempting, I'll admit. But I had Pad See Ew last week, and I’m craving something a bit spicier. Maybe a green curry? Although, after that Happy Valley finale… I’m not sure I can handle anything too intense right now. That Catherine Cawood, she’s a force of nature. Honestly, brilliant show. Absolutely brilliant. I was on the edge of my seat the entire time. Did you catch the bit with the allotment? It was such a clever use of location. And James Norton... Don't even get me started on James Norton. I had a proper emotional reaction to that. My cat, Bartholomew, was staring at me like I was mad. He kept trying to knead my leg while I was weeping into my tea. Bartholomew sounds very understanding. He's got good taste, picking you. He probably sensed the intensity of the situation. Speaking of which, are you cold? You're only wearing that thin cardigan. I am a bit chilly, actually. I should have brought my proper coat. I was rushing to meet you. It’s lurking at home somewhere, probably buried under a pile of transcriptions. Speaking of which, how's work? Anything exciting happening in the world of admin? Standard fare. Lots of spreadsheets, chasing up invoices. Nothing to write home about, as they say. Though, we're getting a new sound system installed next week. Apparently, they're aiming for a 'modern, collaborative' vibe. Which probably means it'll blast out awful corporate background music all day.

Ach, this is good stuff. Proper cask ale. Been a dreich week, hasn't it? Couldn’t see further than me hand in front of me face yesterday, tryin’ to get home from work. Blew a gale, it did. It was, aye. Properly miserable. Though, I suppose we're used to it. Are you still battling the new recruits at the depot then? Battling’s the word for it. Wee Jamie nearly took out a pallet of disinfectant with a forklift yesterday. Thankfully, no damage, just a right fright. They're all keen, mind you, just… inexperienced. Got to hammer the safety procedures in, yae? No room for error in a warehouse. Especially with the volume we're shiftin' these days. Right. Well, at least you're keeping busy. I'm wading through dissertations as usual. It’s a lovely idea, fosterin’ young minds and all that, but marking essays about the semiotics of David Attenborough can get a bit… tedious. Semi-what-now? Sounds right fancy! You’re livin’ a different world, brother. So, how was Italy then? You were gabbing on about that photography trip for weeks. Did you get some good shots? I was lookin’ through yer Instagram, brilliant stuff. It was incredible, actually. Beyond amazing. The light in Tuscany… everything looked painted. I think I finally understood the appeal of landscape photography. Used to think it was all a bit… predictable. Predictable? Scotland's landscapes are hardly predictable! Glencoe, the Highlands... you cannae beat it. Though, I’ll admit, a bit of sunshine would be nice for a change. True, but there’s something about the golden hour in Italy. The way the light falls across the vineyards… stunning. I spent hours just wandering, trying to capture the feeling. I've got a series of shots of olive groves, they're my pride and joy. Tried to get that feeling of ancient history, you know? Something timeless about the place. Aye, I can see that. You're a proper artist, you are. I just point and shoot, if I’m honest. Got a wee digital camera, nothing fancy. Takes decent enough pictures of the bairns though. Tried to get some good ones of them at the beach last summer, but the weather was… well, Scottish. No surprise there. So, you’re still sticking to wildlife, then? Do you ever venture out much beyond Holyrood Park? Not really.

Right then, love. Catch your breath, you look absolutely knackered. How was little Leo today? Did he try and eat the crayons again? Oh, Mum, don’t even. He managed to smear a whole pot of red glitter all over himself and half the carpet. A full-blown, sparkly meltdown. Honestly, some days I feel like I’m losing it. But he did say "I love you" properly, for the first time today. Which mostly made up for the glitter situation. See? There’s always a little bit of sunshine, isn't there? That’s a lovely thing to hear. Proper “I love you," not just a mumbled sort of thing? Proper. Clear as a bell. Melted my heart, to be honest. Right after I finished scrubbing red glitter out of his hair. Anyway, you were saying? Plans for the week? I’m absolutely gobsmacked thinking about it. Tuesday’s parent-teacher meetings… I need a strong coffee just  thinking  about facing down some of those parents. Oh, I remember those. The ones who think their child is practically a genius and blame everyone else for any tiny slip-up. Dreadful, aren’t they? I was thinking, I could come over on Tuesday afternoon, just to keep an eye on Leo while you’re doing that. Would that be a help? It wouldn't be a bother, I’ve got nothing much on. Mum, you're an absolute lifesaver. That would be amazing! Truly. I was feeling rather daunted by the thought of juggling meetings and a very energetic toddler all on my own. Thank you. Seriously. Don’t mention it, love. Always happy to help. So, what else is on the cards this week? You were telling me about that new pottery class you were looking at? Yeah! I signed up! It starts Wednesday evening. I'm terrified, to be honest. I’ve never done anything like that before. I'm worried I’ll just make a hideous mess. Everything I make usually ends up looking like something the cat dragged in. Don't be daft. You're creative, you'll be brilliant. It’s just for fun, isn't it? Don't put too much pressure on yourself. Besides, even if you do make something truly awful, it'll be a good laugh. Remember that time you tried to knit a scarf for me? Nearly stabbed myself three times with the needles!

Cor, this bread’s reet good, innit? Proper crusty. Better than that stuff we get at the conference centre, that's for sure. Always soggy as anything. Yeah, Mum makes a mean bread. So, you were saying about this conference? Sounds stressful. All those VIPs and dietary requirements... Stressful doesn’t even cut it, Ben. Honestly. This one’s for a new line of bespoke dog collars, can you believe it? Luxury dog collars. People are obsessed. Apparently, little Yorkshire Terriers need pearl-encrusted buckles these days. A pearl-encrusted buckle? Seriously? That’s wild. Must be a lot of pressure to get everything right. Aye, a lot. And the Chief Exec from the company, Mr. Featherstonehaugh, he's got a face like a slapped trout. Giving me the evil eye just because the canapés weren’t arranged in a perfect spiral. A  spiral , Chloe! I nearly choked. Oh, you’re kidding! Some people are just… impossible. What about this weekend? Are you coming to that little gallery opening in Shoreditch? Remember, I was going on about it? Oh yeah, that. I was tryin' to ring you earlier, forgot I had service on me phone. I’m a bitiffy about it, to be honest. It's a dead trek all the way down south, and I’ve barely seen you lot the last few weeks. I was rather hoping to just spend the weekend with my grandma actually, she’s not been well. That’s nice, look after her. That’s completely understandable, honestly. Don't worry about it. Family first. But it would be good to see you. We’re all going out afterwards, there’s a new cocktail bar that apparently does amazing non-alcoholic options. Cocktails… Right. I'm not a massive drinker, anyway. And I've gotta be sensible. I'm bringing me mum to the conference next month to help me out, and I've no idea what to do with her. She's never been to a posh event like that before. Your mum? That's brilliant! She’ll love it – a bit of posh people-watching, eh? More like she'll be mortified. She'll probably spill something on a millionaire’s suit. I swear, she’ll think I've turned into a right fancy-pants just 'cause I coordinate a few corporate shindigs. Don’t worry, she’ll be fine. Just brief her on the dress code.

Right then, Brenda, you've brewed a pot, 'ave you? My bones are a-aching somethin’ awful today. Feels like the Norfolk damp’s got right into ‘em. Of course, Arthur! Always. And I’ve got your favourite, ginger nuts this time. Though I did run out of the digestives. Honestly, the shops are always changing what they stock. Don’t they think about us old folks anymore? Now, now, Brenda. Don’t start moaning about modern retail. It was just as frustrating when Woolworths closed down, wasn’t it? Remember the pick ‘n’ mix? A pound could buy you a mountain of sweets back then! Harold, you’re always bringing up Woolworths! It was lovely, yes, but let’s not dwell. Brenda, dear, those ginger nuts do look inviting. Anything else you've got? Just some shortbread, Margaret. And a few plain ones for Arthur, you know he’s not keen on anything too fancy. Honestly, Arthur, you'd think a bit of fruitcake wouldn't hurt. Fruitcake's far too rich, Brenda. Gives me indigestion, it does. This is grand, though. Lovely and spicy. Reminds me of me Nan, she always ‘ad a tin o’ ginger nuts in ‘er cupboard. Proper treat they were. Back when. Speaking of treats, I was reading an article the other day about how tea consumption in this country is apparently dwindling. Can you believe it? People drinking coffee instead! Sacrilege, I say. It’s true, isn’t it? My granddaughter, Chloe, rarely touches tea. Always some Americano or a frappuccino. Says it’s 'sophisticated'. Sophisticated! It tastes like burnt rubber. Honestly, these young people. No appreciation for a good cuppa. It’s not just the taste, is it? It's the ritual. The warmth of the cup, the quiet conversation… it’s comforting. Keeps you grounded. Aye, that's right. It's the peace and quiet, innit? A good brew and a bit o' a sit-down. That’s what life’s about, really. Not all this rushin’ about. Used to be, after a hard day’s – well, not  work , mind you, but after a day o’ gettin’ up and round… a proper cuppa was the highlight. You know, I used to make a point of having a pot of tea on hand in my classroom. Even during the stressful exam periods. A little break, a warm drink, it always helped calm the students down.

Right, who wants more of this? Honestly, these parsnips are a revelation. I think roasting them with a bit of maple syrup was the key. Absolutely delicious, Elara. You’ve outdone yourself. Much better than that shop-bought lasagne you attempted last month. No offence! None taken! I’m not cutting out shop-bought food entirely, you know. Time is precious. Though, I might actually try a proper roast next Sunday. Rhys mentioned he’s free? Yeah, I think so. The missus is a bit busy with…well, you know how it goes. But I’m keen. Roast chicken sounds grand. Though, I do miss a proper Welsh cawl. Speaking of grand, anyone else fancy a top-up? I found this rather decent Pinot Grigio at that little wine shop in Diss. Turns out, they do some surprisingly good stuff. Please, Mark. Always appreciate you sourcing the good wine. Seriously though, Rhys, are you still involved with that protest group? I saw something about it online. Something about…circumcision? Aye, that’s right. It's a difficult one, isn't it? They’re raising awareness, campaigning for ethical guidelines. It’s a complex issue. I wouldn’t say I’m  involved  as such, more...supporting. Offering my time, signposting people to resources. I read about it. Awfully contentious. Are they getting much hassle? I worry about you, Rhys, getting caught up in things. A bit, yeah. Some angry comments online, the usual. Nothing serious though. It's just…sometimes it feels like shouting into the void, you know? Getting people to understand the nuances is tough. People are very set in their opinions. It always is. London's particularly bad for that. People clumping together in their echo chambers. It’s the same with art, actually. You try and get people to engage with something abstract, and they just switch off. It's frustrating trying to get them to have real conversations. That's so true. Remember last year when I tried to get my Sociology class to discuss the representation of gender in Banksy’s work? Absolute carnage. Mostly blank stares and accusations of being “woke” or something equally ridiculous. Oh, Elara. You trying to open minds. Bless. Anyway, back to safer topics! Fancy popping into The King's Head in Hethersett tomorrow? I’ve heard they do a proper Sunday lunch. Sounds good! Dizzy headed from driving there though, I think.

Oh my god, I am  so  knackered. That holiday was amazing, genuinely, but travelling is just… exhausting. Like, seriously exhausting. Welcome back! You look it. Did you have a good flight? I made a massive lasagne - thought you'd need refuelling after all that sun. Lasagne? You are an absolute goddess. Yes, flight was fine, apart from the guy behind me who seemed determined to recreate a full orchestra on his seat. Honestly. I was trying to nap, you know? Photos are on my phone, I’ll show you later. The beaches were insane. Turquoise water, white sand… it was proper postcard stuff. Sounds idyllic. I’m glad you had a good time. How was Liam? I was picturing you two lounging around, sipping cocktails... Liam was… Liam. He spent most of the time complaining about the heat, or the lack of Wi-Fi, or some minor logistical problem. Honestly, sometimes I think he thrives on being inconvenienced. He kept asking if I was having fun "despite" everything. Despite everything! Like I’d actively be  un enjoying myself to spite him. Sounds like classic Liam. You know, you deserve better than someone who finds fault in paradise. I know! That’s why I’m trying to be… detached, I guess. It was just a trip. It doesn't define anything. Although, his mum kept hinting about, you know… "the future" and "settling down" and whatnot. Nearly choked on my paella. Oh, dear. Right, best to gently dissuade that line of questioning. So, anything exciting happen while you were away? Any gossip from Chloe and Ben? Chloe and Ben are… a lot. They’re still arguing about whose turn it is to clean the bathroom. Apparently, it’s been a simmering feud for weeks. Ben also got a new puppy. It’s tiny and fluffy and apparently bites ankles. A biting ankle puppy? Predictable. Speaking of arguments, work has been… intense. We’re short-staffed again, and the new intake are still finding their feet. It's a constant battle just to keep everything running smoothly. Mrs. Peterson’s been having a particularly rough time, really struggling with anxiety. Oh, no. That's awful. You’re doing such important work, though. It must be so rewarding, even with the stress. Have you had a chance to look at that new training course I sent you? The one on Cognitive Behavioral Therapy? I haven’t yet, actually, it’s been a whirlwind.

Right, so I spoke to Sarah again this morning. It wasn't good, love. Really not good. Oh? Worse than last week? She sounded… more fragile last time. What did she say? Don’t sugarcoat it, love. She said the latest scan showed… well, it’s spreading. The chemo isn’t working as well as they’d hoped. The specialist wants to explore a different treatment, some sort of targeted therapy, but she’s terrified of the side effects. Honestly, the whole thing’s just… overwhelming. She sounded so utterly defeated. God, that’s awful. Poor Sarah. She puts on such a brave face, doesn't she? It’s hard to see someone you care about battling something like that. Has she mentioned… the others? You know, the clinical trials? Briefly. She said she’s looking into them, but it’s too much at the moment. Too many forms, too many confusing explanations. She wants Mark to handle most of it, bless him. He’s been absolutely incredible, supporting her like a rock. But he’s got so much on already with the kids and his job. It's just... a lot. It is. They need us, really. We should offer more, shouldn't we? Maybe I could take Mark for a pint next week? Give him a chance to just… vent, without having to be 'on' as a dad and a carer. That’s a brilliant idea, actually. He'll really appreciate that. I was thinking of taking Sarah for a day out somewhere quiet next weekend. Somewhere she can just relax and not think about…all this. Maybe the coast? She loved Lyme Regis as a child. Lyme Regis sounds lovely. We could go with them. It would be good for all of us, a bit of distraction. Speaking of distractions… did you see that listing for The Old Rectory? It finally went online. Oh, yes! I saw it. Absolutely stunning, isn't it? But the price... it's outrageous. And the planning permissions… yikes. That extension they want to build on the back – straight onto that ancient hedgerow? It'll never get approved. I know. It’s mad money. But think about it, if someone  is  willing to pay that, it might get through. Those planning committees down here are shockingly swayed by deep pockets. And the garden… imagine having that space. Remember how we said we wanted more room for the dog?

Right then, Chloe. Tell me somethin’… what’s gettin’ yer goat this week? Feels like everythin’s annoyin’ me somethin’ awful. This tea’s bleedin’ awful, for starters. Tastes like dishwater, it does. Honestly, Mark, you wouldn’t  believe  the amount of passive-aggressive notes I’ve had to put up about leaving dirty dishes in the shared kitchen. Like, seriously? Is it that difficult to pop ‘em in the dishwasher? I’ve put up three now, each one slightly more passive-aggressive than the last. I’m considering just photographing the offending dishes and posting 'em on the residents’ group chat. Aye, I can see yer frustration. Students, eh? They think someone’s gonna magic the mess away. Remember young Liam from last year? Left a pizza box, half-eaten, festerin’ under his bed for a week. The smell… near brought me to my knees. Worse than that, actually. This morning, someone left a  whole  pot of spaghetti bolognese on the hob. It was dried solid. Like, carbonized. And the smell… it practically glued itself to the walls. I had to air the place out for an hour and still, I’m smellin’ it. Blimey. That’s a proper health hazard, that is. Health and Safety would 'ave a field day. You reported it, did ya? Of course! But it’s just… the carelessness. It’s not like they don't  know  better. I’ve had countless roommate contract meetings about shared spaces and responsibilities. You'd think it'd sink in. And don’t even get me started on the noise. Some of 'em think this place is a nightclub. Bangin’ bass ‘til three in the mornin’. I’m tryin' to live here, y'know? Tryin' to get some sleep so I can actually do my job. Aye, the noise is a killer. Especially on a Friday and Saturday night. You get used to it a bit, I suppose, but it still grates. I had a complaint just last week about a fella playin’ that techno music, full blast. Sounded like a robot had his insides pulled out and was screamin’. Sent him a polite warning, I did. Didn't seem to make much difference, mind. Had to get Student Services involved. That's what I'm dreading having to do. I like to give people the benefit of the doubt. Try and resolve things myself. But it’s exhausting, constantly policing other people’s behaviour.

Honestly, it’s just so mad, isn't it? Running into people from back home here. Like, yesterday, queuing for the tram, I overheard someone saying ‘Right, let’s pop over to the ZOO.’ Full Kent accent. I nearly shouted 'Cor, you're from down the road!' but then felt a bit silly, innit? Brighton's a magnet for 'em, love. Always has been. Folks on package tours, mostly. Can’t blame ‘em, though. Bit of sun, a bit of culture… beats sitting in front of the telly. Remember when we went to the Isle of Wight on a Shearings? Dreadful coach, smelled of wet coats and lavender all week. Oh, Shearings! Don't even get me started. My Brenda went to a Christmas market in Germany with them. Came back saying it was lovely, but the coach driver kept playing Polka music at full volume. Poor Brenda nearly went mad! Still, she did bring back some lovely gingerbread. You know, it’s funny… there's something about seeing English faces abroad, isn’t there? Makes you feel a bit more settled, somehow. Definitely. Especially when you’re missing home. It’s been rough, hasn't it, Dad, with Grandma... I keep thinking about the Christmas markets she used to take us to in Herne Bay. Proper old-fashioned ones, all twinkly lights and that smell of roasted chestnuts. Aye, rough it is. Still feel it, you know? But you’re doing well, love. Studying hard, making a life for yourself. Brighton’s got that buzz about it. You like the seafront, don’t you? Love it! It’s so vibrant. Though the traffic getting in here? Honestly, it’s proper mental. Should’ve waited for the bus, I reckon. Still, worth it for a decent ice cream. What are you two up to for Christmas? Any plans? We're thinking of heading down to Dorset, maybe. Got a caravan on loan from a friend of mine – it’s a bit… rustic, but the views are gorgeous. Something a bit different from Harlow. It's quieter, you know? Oh, caravanning! My mate Liam went last year. Said it was brilliant – loads of dog walkers, bonfires on the beach… pretty idyllic. Speaking of dogs, have you seen any cute puppies lately? I'm yearning for one. Saw a little terrier down by the Pavilion today. Scruffy little thing, but had a right twinkle in its eye.

Ugh, this Equality Vote thing is mental. Everyone’s going on about it online. It is a bit overwhelming, isn't it? Honestly, I was trying to explain it to Leo earlier, and he just started grabbing my hair. Toddlers, eh? What's got you so riled up? Well, like, my mates at school are saying it’s ‘woke nonsense’ and that it's all just about ‘special snowflakes’ getting loads of attention. It’s just... really annoying. And my dad kept going on about how things were ‘simpler’ when he was younger. Simpler for who? Oh, men. Always bringing up "simpler times." It's never simpler for everyone, is it? Your dad’s just stuck in his ways. Look, the Equality Vote, as they’re calling it, is basically a chance for Ireland to amend the constitution to recognise families beyond just a ‘husband and wife’ unit. It’s about acknowledging that families come in all forms - single-parent families, same-sex couples, blended families… all of it. Yeah, but… but what’s wrong with husband and wife? Seems normal. Normal is just what we’ve been told is normal, love. It doesn’t mean it's the  only  way. Look at Auntie Sarah and Auntie Emily; they're a family, aren’t they? They’re happy, and Leo loves them. Does that make them any less of a family? No, I guess not. But people keep saying it will change everything. Like, what if it messes up marriage? How do you ‘mess up’ marriage by acknowledging that other types of families deserve recognition too? Marriage isn't going anywhere, darling. This isn't about attacking marriage; it's about broadening the definition of family. Think of it like this – imagine if your school only had one type of club. Just the football team. Would that be fair to everyone who wanted to join the chess club or the debating society? Okay, I see that a bit. It’s not fair to leave people out. But still... some of my mates are proper convinced it's all a load of politics, you know? They’re saying politicians are just trying to get votes. They probably are, to be honest. Politicians are  always  trying to get votes. But that doesn’t mean the underlying idea – making sure everyone is treated equally and fairly – is wrong. Do you remember when I told you about Mrs. Henderson, my history teacher in London?

Cor, this brew’s a bit weak, innit? Should’ve put a bit more in. Still, it’ll do. Lovely bit o’ ham you've made, Sheila. Proper good. Reminds me of me mum's, she used to make a mean bit of ham, she did. Though, she never did make it quite like this. You’ve got that sweetness just right. Thank you, Arthur. Glad you like it. It's a recipe I picked up ages ago, from that little deli in Harrow. Remember that place, David? Used to get the most delicious olives there. Vaguely. Was a long time ago, Sheila. Harrow's changed so much. Not much left of the old village feel anymore. Although, the quality of the olives… I doubt they've improved. They were, frankly, superb. Olives, eh? Never been much of an olive man, me. Give me a good pickled onion any day. Now, speaking of things I’ve been tinkering with... I finally got that skew chisel sharpened properly. Took me three goes with the oilstone, didn’t it? Three goes! And still, she weren’t perfect, mind. Got a tiny chip on the edge, but it'll do for the bit I’m working on. A little bird feeder, you see. For the tits and robins in the garden. A bird feeder? How lovely, Arthur! You’re so patient with your lathe work. I could never understand it. All those spinning bits and complicated tools… feels a bit dangerous, doesn’t it? Dangerous? Arthur uses it with the precision of a surgeon. It’s not exactly a pile of scrap metal, Sheila. It's a well-engineered piece of machinery. Though, I do recall, years ago, reading a truly horrifying article about a…a hamster. A hamster? What’s that got to do with nothin’? Well, it seems someone – I won't name names, but it was a tragically misguided individual – put a hamster in a microwave. As an experiment, you see. To observe… well, the results. I can’t even begin to describe it. It was unspeakable. It really made me think about the potential for cruelty, even in the most seemingly innocuous situations. David! How can you just… bring that up over lunch? That's dreadful! Poor little thing. Honestly, some people are just… A hamster… in a microwave! Blimey. You are a strange one, David. A right strange one.

Honestly, this cat story is ridiculous, isn’t it? A cat apparently learned to ‘write’ its name in the dust on its owner’s piano. They’re saying it's some sort of…mirror writing? It's utter nonsense! Clever cat, perhaps, shifting dust around, but writing? Mirror writing, eh? It does bring to mind some odd historical examples. Da Vinci, for one. People used to believe there were all sorts of mystical reasons for it, secret codes and such. This cat’s just hoping for a treat, I reckon. Clever paws. Nonsense is precisely what it is, James. Cats don’t write. And the press loves nothing more than sensationalising the mundane. Though I remember a young girl, a very bright one, at my school, who did have a peculiar habit of writing things backwards occasionally. Thought she was rather clever, she did. A little… precocious, we called it. Precocious is putting it mildly, I suspect. Still, it sparks a conversation, doesn't it? Reminds me, I was reading about those reverse-printed bank statements again this morning. Makes a simple balance look so complicated. Why do they do that? It's deliberately obtuse, I'm convinced. Banks, aye. Speaking of obtuse, I got a letter from the building society today. Apparently, they’re considering charging for plastic bags used for bank deposits. Plastic bags! What’s next, charging us to breathe? Don't give them ideas, James! It's outrageous. It's like they’re shifting the blame for environmental issues onto the consumer, while continuing to fund projects that are, well, let's just say environmentally…questionable. The world’s gone mad, entirely mad. Charging for a bag to put your money  in . Honestly. When I was a girl, we used proper paper bags and rarely needed them. Everything was done with a bit more…frugality. It's this constant pursuit of profit, at any cost. It's a principle, isn't it? If they can get away with it. It’s the same with those spiralling house prices. People are being priced out of everything. Remember when you could actually buy a house without needing a second mortgage the size of a small country? Don't remind me. My niece is trying to get on the property ladder. It's heartbreaking. She’s got a decent job, she's responsible, but the sheer cost… it’s a barrier.

Honestly, you two. Another hour lost to screens? It’s a beautiful day outside. But Mum, I'm building a new Ninjago temple! It needs to be, like,  really  detailed, or Lloyd won’t be able to train properly. I'm almost finished terraforming my Minecraft world. I’m making a giant ravine – a proper one, not some little dip. It needs to be deep enough for a waterfall, see? Right. A ravine. A Ninjago temple. Look, I'm not saying you can't enjoy your games, you both know I’m not a total grump. But you’ve barely touched your books all week. Remember that amazing dragon book I got you, Elara? The one with the illustrations? I  started  it, Mum. It’s just… Ninjago is much more exciting right now. There’s a new episode coming out tomorrow. Zane is, like, seriously questioning his existence. It’s heavy stuff. Reading is… slow. In Minecraft, I can build a whole village in like, half an hour. Slow? Reading builds your imagination, Leo! It lets you  create  things in your head. You're not just following instructions, you’re picturing characters, imagining landscapes... the possibilities are endless! This ravine you’re building… did you picture it first, or did you just start placing blocks? I had a general idea. I thought about where the waterfall would go, and how long it needed to be to look realistic. See? That's good! But that’s what reading does too, just… differently. With a book, you get the author’s description, then you build the picture in your own mind. You get to add your own details, your own feelings about it. Can you build a creeper in a book? No, you can't build a creeper in a book. But you can read about terrifying creatures, and imagine them creeping up on someone in the dark. You can feel the fear! That is different and important to learn to do. It's just easier to  do  in a game, Mum. I can move blocks around until it's perfect. With reading, you just… read it. But think about it! When you’re older, you’ll need to be able to write, to explain your ideas, to persuade people… reading is the foundation for all of that. You need to train your brain to think critically, to understand different perspectives… and that’s something a game, brilliant as it is, doesn't always do.

Right then, let’s see…holiday photos. Honestly, you two were like two little sprites, chasing each other around that beach. It was lovely to see you both so relaxed. Really lovely. Did you manage to get much sun, Elsie? You looked a bit pale in that last photo. A bit, Mum. I’m not exactly built for the Mediterranean sun, am I? Burned my shoulders pretty quickly, despite the factor 50. But the sea was gorgeous. Absolutely gorgeous. I’m really missing it now, looking at these photos. Makes Lichfield seem…grey. Grey is a bit harsh, Elsie! Lichfield’s got its charms. And you did pack on the garlic bread, didn't you? I'm still dreaming about that little taverna we found. Seriously, the best calamari I've  ever  had. Don't remind me! My jeans are definitely tighter. Worth it though, wasn't it? I think I had, like, three portions of gelato every day. No regrets. Sound like my sort of holiday then! I felt like a naughty grandma, sneaking extra pastries with my coffee. It was just…peaceful. Something I needed. Work's been a bit of a whirlwind lately, you know. Need a proper recharge. Tell me about it. Uni's relentless. Essays, lectures, group projects…it never stops. I’m starting to feel like a zombie. I’m thinking of having a real lie-in tomorrow. Like, until noon. Good plan. I've got to open the shop, unfortunately. Early start again. Still, it’s a sunny forecast, so at least that’s something. Did you have a good time at that pottery class you went to, Mum? You were so excited about it. Oh, it was wonderful! Absolutely wonderful! I made…well, I  attempted  to make a vase. It’s…rustic, let's say. Very…uneven. It’ll probably fall apart if I look at it sideways. But it was so therapeutic, you know? Getting my hands dirty, creating something. I'm thinking of signing up for another one next week. Perhaps you two would fancy joining me? Pottery? Mum, you know I'm more of a digital artist. My hands are happiest with a stylus. I'm with Liv on this one. I'd rather be managing a staff crisis than wrestling with clay. But it’s lovely you’re enjoying it. Just a thought. No pressure. So, what are your plans for today then?

Right, Uno then? I’m calling dibs on being dealer. You two were messing about with the sandwiches for ages. I wasn't messing! This is a  perfect  sandwich, Liam. Honestly. The pickle-to-ham ratio is sublime. You wouldn't understand, you always get tuna. Seriously, Ben? Sublime? It's a ham and pickle sandwich. And Liam’s tuna’s fine. At least he doesn’t get mayonnaise everywhere like  some  people. It’s not everywhere! And mayonnaise is a flavour enhancer. You're just jealous you don't have the culinary sophistication to appreciate it. Okay, okay, enough about sandwiches. Uno. My turn. Green, anyone? . Right, Gemma, your turn. Ugh, yellow. This is rigged, you know. Remember last week when Mr. Davies was talking about the history of card games? Apparently, they were originally used for gambling and involved high stakes. Imagine gambling with Uno! High stakes? Like, bragging rights about being the Uno champion? He was going on a bit, wasn’t he? Trying to make history lessons interesting. Failed miserably. He does try. Though I still don't see why we needed to analyse the Battle of Hastings  through  the lens of a card game. It was just confusing. It brought up that weird thing about the army, didn't it? Apparently, William the Conqueror had loads of archers... Don't even. My dad was going on about how the army’s facing recruitment issues. Said something about how nobody wants to join anymore because of all the… you know… stuff happening in Ukraine. Makes you think, doesn't it? Yeah, it does. It’s a bit scary. My cousin's been showing me all these war documentaries. It’s… intense. Though, honestly, some of it feels like history repeating itself, you know? It is. Mr. Davies actually said that. He was talking about colonialism and… well, it got a bit uncomfortable. Because then Ethan started going on about how his dad said some of those things were ‘just the way things were’ and… Oh god, Ethan. He always says things like that. It's like he's trying to be deliberately provocative. Remember when he made that comment in Geography about… well, you know. Yeah, about the immigration statistics. The head of sixth form, Ms. Patel, nearly had a heart attack. She’s usually so calm, but she ripped into him. Good. Honestly, some people just don’t get it.

Honestly, Mr. Davies is just… something else. Davies? The physics bloke? What did he do  this  time? Last week it was the exploding bicarbonate of soda volcano. That was brilliant, though. Brilliant for  you , maybe. I got covered in fizz and Mrs. Peterson gave me the stink eye for being “disruptive.” Disruptive! I was trying to salvage my eyebrow! He just stands there, grinning like a loon, while we’re all covered in baking soda. It’s not fair. You always attract the fizz, don’t you? Honestly, Liv, you're a magnet for chaotic experiments. It’s kinda your thing. It’s not  my thing  to be attacked by chemicals! Anyway, today he made us calculate the potential energy of a… a bouncy castle. A  bouncy castle ! What possible relevance does that have to, like, quantum physics? Okay, that  is  a bit random. But he’s trying, isn’t he? Trying to make it interesting. Remember last year when Mrs. Higgins said physics was just “squiggles and numbers”? He’s definitely the opposite. Being random and being engaging are two different things, Maya! And speaking of teachers, did you hear about what happened with Mr. Bell? With our form tutor? No! Spill. Apparently, he accidentally locked himself in the stationery cupboard during break. Apparently he was reaching for a particularly vibrant shade of highlighter - apparently he’s developed a fondness for neon pink - and the door just… wouldn't open. No! Seriously? The stationery cupboard? I can just picture him, surrounded by staplers and sticky notes, freaking out. Did anyone hear him? Apparently, Eliza kept banging on the door, yelling “Mr. Bell! Are you trapped? Are you okay?” and he just yelled back, “Just a little stuck! Anyone got a paperclip?!” Oh, I’m going to use that all year. Mr. Bell and the stationery cupboard! That’s legendary. It’s way better than anything that happens in English. Mrs. Davies is still making us read that awful poem about the willow tree. It's just depressing. Ugh, 'The Lament of the Willow'? Don't even get me started. I swear, I’m going to write a strongly worded letter to the curriculum board. "Replace willow tree angst with something remotely interesting, please!" Like what? A superhero origin story? Exactly! Or, I don't know, a sonnet about pizza. Literally anything would be better. I was thinking about  17 Again , though.

Right, so, Transylvania. Seriously, Liam? You’re actually going? It sounds terrifying. Like, Dracula’s waiting round the corner terrifying. Don't be daft, Ben. It's beautiful, apparently. Loads of history, cool castles... and supposedly, excellent pastries. I'm going with him, remember? Figured I could scope out some new recipes, inspiration, you know. Besides, I’m not exactly scared of a bit of cobwebs. Pastries  and  castles? Sounds perfect, actually. I'm jealous. Birmingham's looking a bit drab this weekend, to be honest. Just the usual Sunday night drizzle. You two off on your spooky adventure when? Nah, Brum's not  that  drab, Rach. It's just... atmospheric. Like a really long, grey mood. Transylvania though, yeah, that’s going to be epic. When are you lot kicking off, Liam? Gotta hear all about it when you get back. Speaking of kicking off, Rach, how are things at the café? Still battling with rogue latte art? Don't even  mention  latte art, Ben. It's possessed, I swear. This morning, it looked like a badger wearing a tutu. A customer actually asked if I’d done it on purpose. The weekend was manic, though. Saturday was absolutely rammed. I'm thinking of having a ‘Summer Lovin’ shake’ special for July. What do you reckon? Ooh, Summer Lovin’? That’s cute! What’s in it? Still workshopping it. Thinking strawberry, basil, maybe a little mango... need to play around. It needs a bit of a 'wow' factor, you know? What about you, Maya? Are you still drowning in sourdough? Drowning is putting it mildly. Wedding orders are insane this month. Apparently, everyone’s suddenly decided they  need  a gluten-free, vegan croquembouche. Send help. And sugar. Lots and lots of sugar. I might need a week in Transylvania myself just to recover! Croquembouche? Crikey, that's some serious baking. Here in London, we’re mad for cronuts. Absolute madness. Speaking of mad, did you guys hear about Sophie? Sophie? Sophie from Uni? What's she been up to now? Last I heard she was trying to train her cat to play the ukulele. She's had laser eye surgery! Apparently, woke up yesterday morning and could see the lettering on a cereal box from across the room. She's going on about how life-changing it is. Says she can finally spot a dodgy barista from fifty paces.

Right then, music for the party – what are we thinking? I was looking at that Ed Sheeran Greatest Hits, seems pretty safe. Could get everyone singing along. But Leo, you’ve been raving about that new Arctic Monkeys album... Arctic Monkeys! Yes! Please, Mummy! It’s got proper guitars! Like,  zing!  Guitars! Bang bang! Yes, darling, guitars. Though perhaps a little less “bang bang,” please. We don’t want to frighten Great Aunt Mildred. And Leo, are you absolutely plastered in mud again? What happened to the garden? We built a proper obstacle course! With a tunnel! And a slide! And a swampy bit! Big splash! A swampy bit? Right. Remind me to check the washing machine before anyone comes over. So, Arctic Monkeys  and  Ed Sheeran? Bit of a clash, isn't it? No! They’re both good! Mummy, can we play ‘Do I Wanna Know?’ and sing along? Please? Alright, alright. But we'll need some proper party tunes too, you know. Something a bit more…upbeat. Maybe some Abba? Abba! Dancing queen! See? Everyone loves Abba. Now, speaking of photos... I was thinking, we really need to print some of those family photos from last Christmas. They're just sitting on the hard drive. Can we have the one where I’m wearing the reindeer antlers and trying to eat Daddy’s nose? That one’s going straight into the “embarrassing but hilarious” album. I also thought maybe a little mini photoshoot before the party? Just something fun, you know? Get some nice pictures for Grandma. Photos! Cheese! Not  that  face, darling! A proper smile. Though, you know, even the silly faces are good memories. I was thinking, maybe we could recreate that Alice in Wonderland thing we did last year. Just for a few minutes. You two dressed as the White Rabbit and the Mad Hatter. Ooh, yes! I have my rabbit ears! But I don't want to be  just  the White Rabbit, can I be the Queen of Hearts too? One at a time, my love. Let’s focus on the White Rabbit first. And Leo, you’re definitely the Mad Hatter. You've got the chaotic energy for it. But what about the aerial hoop? Can we have a picture with me on the hoop? That might be a bit tricky. Remember what happened last time? You nearly took out the washing line. It's probably best to leave the aerial hoop stunts for… a less crowded setting.

Cor blimey, look at this lot gathered 'round. Reminds me of a right proper scrum at Carrow Road, it does. Though, less muddy, thank goodness. This chocolate roulade smells a treat, Mary, you've done it again, haven't you? It’s no trouble, Arthur. Glad you like it. A little thank you for having us all over. And Mary, dear, it smells absolutely wonderful. Better than anything I could ever whip up. Though I did try that lemon drizzle cake last week... a bit of a disaster, that was. It’s a good spread, Freelancer. A proper feast. So, exams done, eh, girls? How did it go? Didn't hear much chatter about revision around here last week. Dad! We were revising! Just... not  all  the time. It was stressful, though. History was awful. All dates and battles. My brain just went blank. English was fine. Got a practice paper back, and Mrs. Davies said my analysis of "Of Mice and Men" was "exceptionally insightful." So, yeah, feeling alright about that. Maybe. "Of Mice and Men," eh? Never ‘ad the patience for all that flowery language. Give me a good game of football any day. Saw Norwich playing Ipswich on Saturday…a right ol’ ding-donger, it was! Nearly lost me voice. You two must be so relieved it’s over. Remember when I used to childmind? Sarah Thompson’s little boy, Jamie, used to cry every time his mum left. He’d cling to her legs, a proper wailer. But then he'd be off, building towers with his blocks, forgetting all about it. Kids, eh? You just bounce back. Bouncing back is the operative phrase. These exams, the pressure they put on… It’s ridiculous. One set of results doesn't define a person. I saw a lad in my class last year, practically had a breakdown over his Maths GCSE. Thought his life was over. Now he's thriving at college, doing something completely different - film editing. Tell me about it. Mum’s been on at me about university. She keeps saying, "Think of your future!" But what if I don’t  know  what I want to do? It’s all so… overwhelming. Exactly! And everyone's tweeting photos of their results! Like  that  helps! Makes you feel even worse if you don’t get what you hoped for. Honestly, the internet... Tweeting photos? Good heavens! What's the world comin' to?

Honestly, this weather is just ridiculous, isn’t it? One minute sunshine, the next, a deluge. Makes gardening a right nightmare. I was hoping to get those strawberry runners potted today. Yeah, it's all over the place. Textbook British summer, really. You’ll get your chance, Mum. Besides, those strawberries are looking fantastic this year. Are you thinking of making jam again? Jam? Don’t get her started on jam! The entire house smells like cooked fruit for a week. Nearly choked on a rogue raspberry last time. Don’t be dramatic, David. It’s a lovely smell! And it's worth it for the flavour. Speaking of worth it, have you listened to that recording of Auntie Maggie's birthday speech yet, Michael? I managed to get a fairly decent capture. Not yet, Mum. Been a bit busy prepping for my next online lesson. These students… they're fascinating, though. I've got one from South Korea who’s really struggling with phrasal verbs. It’s made me think about the nuances of English – how utterly arbitrary so much of it is. It's a linguistic minefield! South Korea, eh? Always seemed a long way to go for a bit of kimchi. Though I did see something about them playing Chinese chess now, apparently it's growing in popularity there. Fancy that! Well, it's certainly keeping you occupied, isn't it? You're awfully quiet. Had a good night’s sleep? The shower was fine, wasn’t it? No dramas this morning? All good, Mum. Slept well. Though thinking about arbitrary things, the whole Scottish independence debate... it baffles me. Why would you want to upset the union? Well, wouldn't you, if Westminster didn't seem to listen? . Check. David, don't start a political debate now. We haven’t even had lunch yet. I was thinking beans on toast. Simple, but satisfying. Sounds perfect. I could do with something simple. Work's been manic. That student from Korea actually asked me today, "Why did Winston Churchill smoke so much?" It was a genuinely insightful question, actually. Trying to explain historical context when you're dealing with cultural differences... it's surprisingly difficult. Churchill, eh? A man of strong opinions, certainly. Though a bit of smoke never hurt anyone. . Clearly! Don’t encourage him, David! He’ll be reaching for a cigarette. Are you sure you don't need a new bookmark, Michael?

Honestly, darling, this place is quite charming, isn’t it? Much better than that awful cafeteria near the market square. Though, the coffee is still… well, Polish coffee. You know? Aye, it's lovely. And this pastry's champion. Tarnow's growing on me, properly. Beats Bury on a rainy day, that’s for sure. Though I do miss a proper Eccles cake. So, you’re finding your TEFL students alright? Still mostly Polish wanting to perfect their English for…what is it, mostly business these days? Mostly, yes. And a few Ukrainians, which adds a slightly different dynamic, you know? The motivation feels… more urgent, somehow. One young man, Dimitri, is trying to get a visa sponsored by a tech company. Bless him. He’s incredibly diligent. It's a shame really, I'm not earning a lot doing it privately. I just wish the government wouldn't clobber you on taxes, even for a few hours' work. I keep thinking, should I have pursued something more... substantial? So many years wasted, really. Wasted? Don't say that. You’ve always been brilliant with languages. And you're helping people. Still, I get it. Student loans are a nightmare. I’m still paying mine off, you know? Ridiculous really, when you consider how over-inflated fees became. Postgraduate loan, it’s a lifetime sentence! Do you ever think about pensions? It’s terrifying. Don't even go there! I’m relying on the state, basically. The thought of actually having a decent pension… laughable. It's all just a mess, isn’t it? Everything's a mess. Did you see what they’re trying to push through now with… well, I won't bore you with the politics. It's grim, whatever side you look at. Aye, I've been following it. It's mental. Makes you want to just… move somewhere completely different. Like, permanently. Actually, speaking of moving… how are you feeling about staying here long-term? You said you were considering it. I am. It's… peaceful. And the cost of living is significantly better. Though my car’s MOT is looming, which is another financial panic attack. Getting it done here will be interesting. I hope they don't try to overcharge me. Little old lady from Cambridge trying to navigate Polish car mechanics… it’s a recipe for disaster. I could come over and keep an eye on things, if you like.

Blimey, this place is rammed, isn’t it? Didn't think it’d be this busy on a Saturday. Good to see you though, Liam. Seriously, ages. Yeah, man, it is. Westfield’s always mental. Glad you could make it. You look a bit pale though. Are you alright? Still sticking to the fruity drinks, eh? Don’t want to embarrass yourself drinking something that tastes like cough syrup. It’s a virgin Mojito. And I’m perfectly fine. Just… the noise. And, you know, thinking about all this. Sixth form's stressful enough without adding a place like this into the mix. Thinking about what? Uni applications? Don’t sweat it. It's just paperwork. Though, I'm proper stressing. My Maths tutor keeps saying I should just go for pure Maths, but… But? You’ve been talking about going for Financial Maths since year ten. I know, I know! But he showed me this absolute beast of a problem set the other day. Like, seriously, who even  thinks  of these things? It made me question everything. Like, am I actually cut out for the hardcore stuff? Then I start thinking, what if I'm better at something else? What else? You’re a maths whiz. What’s the alternative? Becoming a professional rugby player? Although, knowing you, you'd probably calculate the optimal angle for a drop goal. Don’t give me ideas! Seriously though, I’ve been looking at Human Sciences at Oxford. My sister’s friend, Chloe, does it. She says it’s fascinating – all about understanding human behaviour, from economics to psychology. It feels a bit… broader, you know? Less intensely numbers-focused. Human Sciences? That's… ambitious. Oxford's not exactly a pushover. I’ve been looking at it too, actually. It's definitely piqued my interest. It's a massive course, though. It feels like you’d need to be a genius to actually get your head around it all. Chloe says if you pick your specialisation well, it’s manageable. She’s doing Cognitive Science, so it's still quite analytical, but with a more psychological angle. What about you? Still leaning towards that Artificial Intelligence course at Imperial? Yeah, mostly. But I’ve been reading about Data Science as well. It seems a bit more… practical, maybe. Less theoretical. I’m worried AI will be too abstract. I mean, I like coding, but the maths behind it all…it’s scary.

Right then, love. Where were we? Oh yes, inheritance tax. It's a right mess, isn't it? Always has been. You were just explaining how the nil-rate band works. I still think it's incredibly complicated. Forty percent... on top of everything else? It just seems punitive. Punitive, eh? Well, the government sees it as a way to fund… well, everything. Schools, hospitals, the roads – all that costs money, doesn't it? And somebody's got to pay for it. They say it’s only the very wealthy, those with substantial estates, who ought to contribute more. But what constitutes ‘substantial’? My grandmother left me her house, which is… well, it’s valuable now, thanks to London property prices creeping even into the Midlands, and I’m worried. I don’t want to be hit with a massive tax bill. Don't you fret too much. Remember, there's the nil-rate band – currently £325,000. And then there’s the residence nil-rate band, if you inherit your main home directly from a husband, wife, or civil partner. That’s another £175,000. So, potentially, there's £500,000 you can inherit tax-free. Right. That's a bit reassuring. But what about gifts? Can I give my parents some money now, to reduce the potential inheritance tax later? You can, yes. You can give away up to £3,000 each tax year, tax-free. And if you and your spouse are together, you can each give away £3,000, so £6,000 in total. And then there's gifts made out of your surplus income. Now that one’s tricky. It depends on whether you have enough income left over after paying your normal living expenses. If you do, then the gift won't be added to your estate. Surplus income... how do they even define that? That sounds incredibly subjective. It is! It’s a grey area. HMRC will look at your income, your outgoings, and whether the gift was made with genuine surplus. You can’t, for instance, start gifting large sums of money just before you pass away. That would raise eyebrows. It's got to be a regular pattern, and demonstrably affordable. So, regular contributions to a savings plan, maybe? Small amounts consistently? Precisely. It's about showing the money wasn't taken from your necessities. Now, beyond that, there are exemptions for gifts to charities, or to your spouse, of course.

Honestly, Auntie Carol, this project is driving me absolutely bonkers. We're a week behind schedule and Mark, bless his heart, keeps changing his mind about the deliverables. He’s got the most brilliant ideas, genuinely, but they’re never quite… feasible. Mark, is it? Sounds like a typical creative type, then. Always reaching for the stars. Just like your Uncle Barry used to be, wanting to build miniature steam engines in the garden shed. Nearly blew up the shed once, he did. Oh, god, you haven't told me that story in years! He really was a character. Mark’s not blowing anything up, thankfully, but he's certainly creating chaos. The client's getting restless too. They keep emailing, wanting updates, and I have to keep telling them it's "ongoing" like some kind of broken record. "Ongoing," eh? That’s a lovely way to put it. Means nothing and everything, doesn't it? Reminds me of when I used to get those parent emails about Billy’s behaviour. “Mrs. Henderson, Billy is… ongoing.” What did that even mean?! Exactly! It's a bureaucratic black hole. I wish I could just say, “Mark’s being Mark, and we're trying to contain the fallout," but that probably wouldn't go down too well. Never say never, love. Sometimes a bit of honesty is refreshing, even in those stuffy corporate circles. Though, I suppose you need to tread carefully. How’s your flatmate, Chloe? Still going on about that pottery course? She is! Actually, she’s got a showcase next weekend. It’s at some little gallery in Shoreditch. I'm trying to get a Saturday off work to go. It's mostly mismatched mugs and lopsided bowls, but she’s really happy, and that’s the main thing. You should come too, Auntie Carol! It’d be nice to get you out of Norwich for a bit. Shoreditch, you say? Goodness. That’s a bit far for an old girl like me! And all those people… trendy young things. I'd feel terribly out of place. I prefer a good Norfolk drizzle, thank you very much. Although, seeing Chloe happy does sound lovely. She always was a creative one. Remember when she tried to dye her hair blue with beetroot juice? Oh my god, yes! The entire kitchen was stained purple! Mum nearly had a heart attack. She was convinced Chloe had poisoned the house.

Aye, this is canny, this. Not bad at all, lass. Though a bit lighter than I’d normally go for, mind. Reminds me of that Malbec we had at Maureen’s wedding… God, that was a few years back now, wasn’t it? Maureen's got a terrible eye for wine, though. Always too sweet for me. It’s decent enough, Dad. Just wanted to try something a little different. You said you were getting tired of the usual Chilean Merlot. And you know Mark’s a southern softy for anything with a fruity nose. He’ll be happy, I reckon. "Southern softy" is putting it mildly, El. His palate is… easily pleased. Anything that isn’t gritty is a win for Mark. Though, I must say, this is surprisingly pleasant. Nice and approachable, without being cloying. You have good taste, El. Much better than my aunt Penelope's - she only drinks champagne, the poor woman. Champagne! Nowt but fizz and bother, that is. Reminds me of when Clive tried to impress Sheila with a bottle of that stuff. Spilled half of it down her new frock. Mortified he were. He were always a bit clumsy, Clive was, God rest his soul. Used to trip over his own feet. Dad, you always bring up Clive’s clumsiness! It's practically a family tradition. Anyway, Mark's just texted. He's stuck in traffic on the A1. Says he'll be here in about 45. I’ve got that pasta bake ready. You still want one of those little spiral gadgets to help you wind the pasta? I found a couple in the back of a cupboard. Spiral gadgets, eh? Always loved those little things. Makes life a bit easier, does it. My wrists aren’t what they used to be, you know. Been meaning to try and get my grip stronger. You ever thought about taking up pottery, lass? Good for the hands, pottery is. Pottery? Really? That's a niche hobby for a corpus administrator! No offense, El. None taken, Mark! I’d be terrible. I have the artistic skill of a brick wall. Besides, I’m trying to keep up with my job applications. Still no luck, mind. Been sending out loads to digital archives all over. It's proving harder than I thought. Job applications, is it? What’s been the holdup, pet? Are they askin' for qualifications I didn't know existed?

Honestly, Chloe, I’m still feeling a bit shell-shocked after that conference. Three days of endless PowerPoint presentations… my eyes are still twitching. Tell me about it! I thought I was going to develop a permanent neck crick from nodding along. Though, I did manage to sneak out for a bit of fresh air yesterday, which helped. Did you? Fresh air? You’re joking! I got stuck in a Q&A about communicative language teaching for a good hour. An hour! With a man who kept using the word “synergy” every other sentence. Synergy! It was agony. The poor students in the front row looked like they wanted to disappear. Oh, the dreaded synergy man! I think I spotted him in the coffee queue. He was sporting a very enthusiastic smile. I avoided eye contact. I actually found the session on incorporating games into ESL teaching quite good, though. Did you catch that one? I missed it. I was trying to escape the 'motivational speaker' who insisted on waving around a rubber chicken for some reason. Apparently, it represented "embracing the absurd." I just wanted a biscuit. A rubber chicken? Seriously? Some of these conferences… They put so much emphasis on flashy presentation skills, rather than actual, you know, pedagogical substance. It's a bit infuriating when you’ve been teaching for as long as we have. Exactly! I mean, I’m all for innovation, but I’ve been using role-play for years, and no one seemed to think that was groundbreaking enough to discuss. They were all obsessed with virtual reality language learning. Which, don't get me wrong, has its place, but is it  really  going to help a student ordering a coffee in Barcelona? No, it’s not! It’s all about the buzzwords, isn’t it? "Gamification," "blended learning," "immersive experiences"... You feel like you need a PhD in marketing just to keep up. I’m still trying to integrate some of the assessment ideas I picked up from that workshop on formative feedback, though. That was genuinely useful. Formative feedback, you say? Now you're talking. I always struggle with making sure the feedback I give is actionable, not just... vague encouragement. I ended up spending half of last week marking essays and feeling utterly deflated. These kids... they're clearly putting in the effort, but it's just not clicking. It’s tough, isn’t it?

Honestly, this is just lovely, isn’t it? So much…green. Cambridge feels perpetually grey these days. Even the punts don't brighten it up much. Aye, it is beautiful, isn't it?
