It’s watered down, like they’ve been livin’ down South for too long. Well, accents change, don’t they? People move about, pick up bits and pieces. I mean, my nana always said my accent sounded “a bit posh” when I was little, even though I grew up right in Chester. She said I picked it up from school. Posh? Chester accents aren't posh. They’re… diluted. You get a bit of that Liverpool bleed-through, a bit of the Welsh inflection. It's nice, mind you. Just not… strong. Like a weak cup of tea. Ooh, burn! Diluted, eh? At least it's not all flat vowels like you, Derby! Oh, shut it, Wakefield! You lot just yell everything, don’t you? Doesn't make it any more articulate. And don't even start on the dropped 'g's. “Singin’”, “dancin’”. Honestly, it’s a wonder anyone can understand you. It’s called efficiency, love! Saves time. Besides, everyone understands us just fine. Look, he’s started cryin’! Proper blubberin’. You know what I reckon?

Right, right. Honestly, this ref is having a right mare, isn't he? Never seen so many fouls called on one team. Makes you wonder if he's got a wager on, doesn't it? He’s definitely a bit… enthusiastic. But you know how it goes with these big games. Pressure, high stakes. They tend to overcompensate. Relax, Liv, it’s just a game. Though, I must say, their midfield is looking a bit shaky today. Easy for you to say, you’re not from Newcastle! It’s torture watching this. We’ve got decent players, but they’re not clicking. Remember that time at St. James’ Park when… oh, never mind. You wouldn't understand the atmosphere. Try me! Tell me about the atmosphere. I've been to a few games, you know. Admittedly, not as many as I'd like to. My thesis kind of eats into my leisure time. Aye, well, it's just… it's something else. A feeling, you know? The whole city stops. Everyone's talking about it, planning their outfits, arguing over who’s starting. It's more than just a football match; it’s part of the city’s soul. Anyway, back to this ref. He’s winding everyone up. Fair enough. It sounds pretty intense, actually. Speaking of intense… have you made any more progress on that blanket for the baby? The Olympics were rather distracting, weren't they? All that athletic prowess! I was glued to the swimming. Adam Peaty is… well, he's something else. He is, isn’t he? A right powerhouse. Aye, the Olympics did pull me away for a bit. But I've got a few rows done. It’s just… I can’t seem to settle on a colour scheme. I was thinking something muted – grey and cream… but then I saw this gorgeous teal… Teal's nice. Very calming. What about a combination? Grey as a base, with little pops of teal? It'd be beautiful. We haven’t really settled on a name yet, have we? Still bouncing around ideas? Aye, bouncing is the right word. My mam’s got a list longer than my arm. 'Eleanor', ‘Florence’, 'Penelope’… Honestly, they're all a bit posh for us, aren't they? We’re not exactly royalty. I was leaning towards something simpler, more… me. Like 'Maisie' or 'Poppy'. Maisie’s lovely. Poppy's a bit… common, perhaps?

Right, so Barry’s insisted on watching  The Bee Movie  again. For the… what, tenth time this month? Honestly, these two are obsessed. Bees! Bees make honey! Buzz, buzz! And they talk! Like Jerry Seinfeld! He’s funny, Mummy. Really funny. He is, isn’t he? It’s a bit ridiculous, a talking bee trying to sue the human race. But, fair enough. At least it’s not  Frozen  for the hundredth time. Although, you know, I’m still not entirely sure what the moral of  The Bee Movie  is. Exploitation of worker bees? Capitalism gone mad? They give people honey! And flowers! And they fly! Zoom! Exactly! You get it. It’s… complicated. Speaking of complicated, remember we were talking about visiting Hampton Court Palace last week? It cost too much, didn’t it, Mummy? It did, sweetheart. A fortune, really. And for what? To wander around some rooms Henry VIII slept in? Honestly, sometimes I think it's all a bit… silly. All that money going into these royal residences. Why do we have kings and queens anyway? That's a very good question, love. Well, historically, they used to rule the country. Now they're more… symbolic. You know, waving at crowds and opening hospitals. I want to be a queen! I’ll have a really sparkly crown! And lots of ponies! You certainly would. A very glamorous queen. Or perhaps you'd like to be a politician, like your Uncle Mark? No! Politicians are grumpy! Sometimes. But they do try to make things better, in their own way. You know, I was reading something the other day about how some people think we should be a republic instead of a monarchy. No King or Queen. No sparkly crown? No sparkly crown, darling. But maybe more money for things like… vitamins! You both need to take your Vitamin D today. It’s chilly outside. I don't like vitamins. They taste like… lemons. I know, sweetie. But they’re important. Like eating your fruit. Did you know apples were once considered “royal fruit”? Kings and queens used to get them specially grown? Like Granny’s orchard? Precisely! Granny’s old house had the most wonderful orchard. Remember the plums? The smell of them ripening in the summer? We should try to go back there soon. It feels so… peaceful. Can we see the bees there? Perhaps. But we'll have to be careful.

This Earl Grey… it’s not quite right, is it? Bit weak. Reminds me of that time your Uncle George tried to make tea with dandelion roots. Thought he was being resourceful, he did. Ended up tasting like pond water. Oh, George. Bless him. Resourceful is one word for it. Remember the time he tried to build a shed out of pallets? Nearly took out the whole hedge. Still, he had good intentions. Right, well, that was a proper clear-out at the tip, wasn’t it? More junk than I thought we had. Did you find the old PlayStation, Mum? The one with Crash Bandicoot? Nope, love. No ancient gaming relics today. Though I did almost throw out a box of your old Lego. You were  obsessed  with that pirate ship. Honestly, the sheer volume of  things  we accumulate. It's frightening. Your brother, Mark, wants me to clear out the attic at the old house before he puts it on the market. Says it needs to be spotless. As if anyone’s going to be peering up there, looking for dust bunnies. Mark's always been a stickler for detail. Remember his wedding? He had colour-coded name tags for the guests. Even for the canapés! Don't remind me! I spent days arranging those minuscule sandwiches. And the table settings! Honestly, the man had a vision. Slightly mad, but a vision nonetheless. Speaking of weddings… Sarah’s brother’s having a stag do in Thirsk. Apparently, there's some sort of medieval-themed weekend going on. Medieval? Like, knights and dragons and stuff? Can I go? Not quite, love. It's more like… people dressed up in chainmail drinking copious amounts of ale. It's not really your scene at eleven. Weddings are all so extravagant these days. Back in my time, a simple buffet and a bit of music was quite enough. Though, of course, we didn't have these fancy reality TV shows influencing everything. It's all about the “experience” now, isn’t it? It's the curated online persona, really. Everyone wants to  show  they had a good time, more than actually  having  a good time. I’m trying to avoid social media completely at the moment, honestly. Too much noise. It's affecting my writing. Finding it hard to focus. Tell me about it. I’m getting bombarded with invitations for every hen party under the sun.

Oy, Beth! I’m knackered. That parking was a right mare today. Absolutely mental down by the docks, you wouldn’t believe. Spent twenty minutes circling like a pigeon, just trying to find a bleedin' space. Welcome home, love. Twenty minutes, eh? You’re lucky. I saw someone get ticketed for being two inches over the line. Honestly, it's a money-making scheme, that parking down there. How was teaching? Same as always, really. Little Liam’s still convinced ‘the’ is a luxury item you only use when feeling fancy. Had to spend half an hour explaining the difference between ‘I am going’ and ‘I’m going’ again. He’s a good kid though, Liam. Proper bright. What about you? Did you have a stressful day with the patients? A bit. One of the younger ones was having a real wobble. But we got there in the end. It’s rewarding, you know, when you finally see a shift. I was thinking, we should actually go to the Walker Art Gallery this weekend, de-stress a bit. Fancy it? The Walker? Alright, sound idea. Needed a bit of culture to counteract all the ‘I’m going’ and ‘I is going’ that’s been swirling around me head. But parkin’s gonna be a nightmare, innit? Maybe we should get the bus? You and parking! Let’s assess the situation. Right, moving on to slightly less stressful topics… Auntie Maureen’s wedding is officially booked. The invites have gone out. Auntie Maureen? Blimey, she's finally doing it, is she? After forty years with Barry? Good for her, I suppose. Though I bet Barry’s having a bit of a meltdown, the sly dog. He's definitely not thrilled, but he's playing it cool. We need to book time off work. Mid-July, remember? It clashes a bit with your summer school, doesn't it? Aye, it does a bit. I might need to ask Mr. Davies if I can swap a couple of days. Not ideal, but hopefully he'll be alright about it. Speaking of work... that Masters interview went well, didn't it? You seemed confident. I think so, yeah. They seemed really interested in my research proposal. They asked about the practical applications which was good. Fingers crossed! It’s a serious investment, though, isn't it? The fees alone... Aye, it is a bit of a drain, but it’s worth it, love.

Honestly, I’m proper knackered. This essay on Victorian literature is draining the life outta me. Like, who even  cares  about Dickens after all this time? You're always moaning about essays, Liv. It's a student thing, innit? Besides, Dickens is alright. I did a presentation on  Great Expectations  last year. Not bad. This pizza’s actually decent though, right? Better than that slop they served last Monday. Decent, yeah, but it’s still canteen pizza. It'll never compare to Papa Luigi’s. Remember that pizza we had there after the cinema? With the extra pesto? Oh my god, yes! That was heaven. We should go again this weekend. Are you free Saturday? Me and Chloe were thinking of heading to that vintage market down Brick Lane. Saturday's looking a bit hectic, actually. Grandma's birthday, you know. Family stuff. Big roast dinner, awkward questions about when I'm gonna “settle down.” The usual. Ugh, tell me about it. My Nan’s obsessed with finding me a boyfriend. Last week she showed me a picture of her neighbour’s grandson. He looks about 50. No way! Did you say yes to a date? Are you mental? I made up some excuse about having to help my mum. Speaking of which, she’s been going on about Jamie Redknapp. Apparently, he's "still a catch." Right. My mum's obsessed with Ryan Reynolds. Thinks he's just the perfect man. I'm starting to think mums just collectively lose their minds when they see a vaguely attractive celebrity. Probably! Have you seen that new series on Netflix,  Shadow and Bone ? It’s proper good. All fantasy and magic, like a grown-up Disney movie. Nah, haven't had time. Been scrolling through Instagram all week, trying to find inspiration for this bloody essay. It’s a rabbit hole, isn’t it? One minute you’re looking at cute puppies, the next you're comparing your life to some influencer’s perfectly curated holiday. Gets you feeling a bit down. Totally! Honestly, I deleted the app for a week to give myself a break. Felt so much better. Spent the time actually reading a book. Remember how much we used to love Disney films when we were kids? Cinderella, Sleeping Beauty… total classics. Absolutely! We used to stay up all night watching cartoons on VHS. Remember trying to record  The Little Mermaid  and it always came out all glitchy?

This is taking ages. Can we Skyping Grandad after dinner? I wanted to show him my new Charizard card. It's holographic! Of course, love. After you finish your greens, alright? Oisin's having a right time with that carrot, isn't he? A little warrior, attacking the orange beast! 'Rrot! 'Rrot! He's obsessed with carrots. He tried to give one to the dog earlier. Poor Buster looked so confused. Anyway, Grandad will  love  the card. He used to collect Pokémon when he was a kid, remember? I do, yes. He'd tell you all about Mewtwo, wouldn't he? Though I doubt even he's got a holographic Charizard. You're doing brilliantly in that league, aren’t you? Beating everyone? Almost! I lost to Liam last week, but I've got a new strategy. I’m using my Snorlax as a tank now. It's super effective! He keeps trying to use his Jolteon, but Snorlax just shrugs it off. Sounds clever. Maybe you should write it down, a little strategy guide. Could teach it to Oisin one day when he’s old enough. Although, he seems more interested in chewing things at the moment! Yeah, he is. It’s weird, though, isn't it? How Pokémon is still a thing. It's been around forever. Some things just stick around. Like good music, and a good cup of tea. And sometimes, questionable fashion choices. What do you mean? Those jeans, darling. Honestly. You look like you can't breathe. And they’re practically climbing up your legs. They’re fashionable! Everyone wears them. “Fashionable” doesn't mean comfortable, love. And I’m not sure  anyone  can breathe in them. I saw your cousin Millie wearing some the other day, lookin' like a sausage in a casing. Millie’s got different legs. And I like them. Alright, alright. It's your legs. Just please don't complain when you can’t sit down properly. Also, are you still planning on taking guitar lessons? Mr. Davies said you have potential. I don’t know… It’s expensive. And I’m busy with Pokémon training, obviously. It’s an investment in yourself, sweetheart. A skill you’ll have forever. And think of how good it’d be to play along to  your  Pokémon theme tune! 'Cweam! 'Cweam! He’s heard you talking about ice cream, hasn't he? We can have some after dinner too, little man.

Honestly, this place is a monument to procrastination, isn’t it? I swear, I’ve been meaning to tackle this cupboard for… well, I've lost count. It's like a portal to every phase of my life, crammed in here. Don’t be dramatic, dear. A little clutter never hurt anyone. It just means you’ve lived a life. Though, you’re right, we do need to actually  get  to it. I'm just not sure where to start. It's overwhelming. I know! That's why I thought we’d tackle the toys first. Get the emotional baggage out of the way. At least then the tins of Christmas decorations won’t feel quite so potent. Oh look! Remember this? Our 'gardening set'! Oh, heavens! Absolutely! We were convinced we were professional gardeners. So serious about it, too. Remember trying to grow those giant sunflowers in Mrs. Peterson’s flowerbed? She nearly had a fit! I'd completely forgotten about that! She tripped over the hose, didn’t she? A very unfortunate incident for everyone involved. We thought we were doing her a favour, enriching her soil with our…our experimental compost. Experimental is putting it mildly. Mostly mud and grass clippings, if I recall correctly. Though, I do remember you were particularly proud of that one, rather pathetic-looking daisy you managed to coax into existence. It was  magnificent  at the time! Right, let’s move on before we spend the entire day reminiscing about floral misdemeanours. What about the Bako set? I think I saw a box lurking somewhere down here. Bako! The best! That was  serious  building stuff. Those interlocking plastic pieces… we could build anything! Castles, spaceships… I was particularly proud of my giraffe. It was a bit lopsided, but it was a giraffe, you know? Oh, yes! The giraffe! I remember you insisting it had to have a purple neck. Your reasoning was… questionable, as I recall. Something about giraffes admiring sunsets. They do! It was perfectly logical! It’s funny, isn’t it? How fiercely we defended those creations. They were our whole worlds for a while. And look at them now, covered in dust and… what  is  that stuck to this piece? Glue, I think. Probably from some ill-fated attempt to attach glitter. You were obsessed with glitter. Everything had to sparkle. It adds a touch of magic! And glitter is essential for a proper castle.

Honestly, Liam, I’m starting to think we’ve created a mosquito paradise in our garden. Little Elsie’s been covered in bites already, despite the repellent. Did you remember to empty the birdbath? It's practically a breeding ground, isn't it? I did, yeah. Just before we left. They’re persistent little blighters this year, aren't they? Global warming, probably. Everything's getting worse. I’m really hoping we can get away for a week in September. Somewhere hot, somewhere with  no  mosquitoes. Fingers crossed. A week in the sun would be bliss. Although, thinking about travel, the traffic getting here was horrendous. Did you hear that awful screeching on the A11? Sounded like someone had a complete breakdown. I did, yeah. Absolutely gridlocked for a good twenty minutes. I was just thinking, what’s the point of investing in a fancy electric car if you spend half your life stationary in traffic? It’s a bit ironic, isn’t it? All that effort to be eco-friendly, then you're just pumping out fumes while waiting to move an inch. Tell me about it. Still, it was worth it to get Elsie out. She seems to love the fresh air, even if she  is  attracting every mosquito within a five-mile radius. Did you manage to sort that gig ticket situation? I know you were trying to get tickets for that new band, "Static Bloom." Nearly. Missed out on the initial release, of course. Everyone and their dog was trying to get tickets. But I managed to snag two on resale. Slightly overpriced, but worth it, I think. They’re playing at The Scala, aren't they? Should be a decent venue. Oh, brilliant! I’m really looking forward to that. Remember that time we saw 'Echo Vista' at Brixton Academy? That was amazing. The energy in that place was electric. How could I forget? Elsie was just a little bump then! And you spent half the gig trying to fend off a rogue sweat-soaked scarf. Don't remind me! It was a sticky situation, literally. Though, I wouldn’t trade it for anything. It’s nice to have those memories to look back on. Before… all this. Absolutely. We’ll make plenty more. Static Bloom will be just the start. We'll be taking Elsie to gigs before she can even properly walk, I reckon.

Blimey, that was a day. Honestly, Mrs. Higgins was having a right go at my putting today. Said it looked like I was trying to spoon-feed a pigeon. A pigeon, can you believe it? Oh, really? That’s… poetic, I’ll give her that. At least she’s not boring. How was the rest of the round? Did you beat young Liam again? Nah, he pipped me at the post by one. Cheeky sod. He kept going on about needing that win to boost his confidence. As if he needs any! The lad’s a natural. Anyway, I’m starving. What’s for grub? I was thinking maybe we could do that butternut squash risotto you like? I was wandering down the high street earlier and saw they had some gorgeous squashes at the market. Although, I did spend most of the time dodging people glued to their phones. It’s ridiculous. Honestly, you can’t walk ten feet without someone bumping into you because they’re staring at a screen. Tell me about it! I had a chap nearly trip over me on the 7th green. Muttering about a TikTok. TikTok! On a golf course! The world’s gone mad. Did you get the post, by the way? That thing I ordered from Amazon? The new golf shoes? Yeah, it’s on the kitchen counter. And speaking of things on counters, you wouldn’t believe the state of the loo. Seriously, I’m not exaggerating, Leo. It looked like a small tornado had gone through. Right, noted. I’ll sort it later. Promise. You’ve been working hard, haven’t you? Still battling with the recruitment agencies? Ugh, don’t even get me started. Sent off another twenty applications today. Mostly for marketing roles. It feels like shouting into the void sometimes. I had one rejection email that was so generic, it could’ve been for applying to be a paperclip. "We received a large number of applications…" Honestly! That’s rough, love. Don’t let it get you down. You're brilliant, you know? Uni was tough, but you smashed it. You'll find something amazing. Remember that theatre workshop you were talking about? Have you looked into that? Might be a good way to do something creative while you're job hunting. I’ve had a look, yeah. There's a beginners' scriptwriting course starting next month.

Jaysus, that was a grand feed, Sarah. Fiona really outdid herself tonight. Roast beef, potatoes, gravy... the works! Little Liam seems to have enjoyed it too, look at him, belting out 'Twinkle, Twinkle' with all his might. Yeah, it was good, Dad. Really good. Mum’s gravy is epic. But I’m stuffed. Honestly, I could barely move after that second helping of potatoes. He's got enthusiasm, that's for sure! And I’m glad you both enjoyed it, Ben. It's nice to have everyone together, even if it’s just for an evening. Liam, darling, maybe a bit quieter now, eh? We need to hear ourselves think. Twinkle, twinkle, little... SPLUT! He’s a right character, that one. Right, so, about that cloud storage issue at work... it's driving me mad. The entire system's been playing up for days. Think it might be a corrupted sector. We’re practically running on a knife edge. Cloud storage, yeah. Sounds complicated. Is it like… where all those videos I upload to YouTube live? Sort of. It's just everything’s in somewhere else, like a big digital warehouse. Businesses send their data there instead of keeping it all on their own servers. It’s meant to be safer, easier to manage, but... well, as you can imagine, when it goes wrong, it’s a right carry-on. Oh, Ben, you always sound so stressed when you talk about work. Can’t you just… delegate? You carry everything on your shoulders. Delegate? Sarah, you know I can't. If I don't keep a tight grip on it, things'll fall apart quicker than a pot of porridge left out in the rain. Besides, who else is going to sort it? It's down to me, plain and simple. I could try and look something up online. I'm pretty good with computers, you know. Are you now? What sort of things have you been doing recently? Beyond gaming, mind. I helped my Nan set up her email the other week. And I fixed her printer when it jammed. That was quite tricky, actually. Well, maybe. Don't go poking around in anything you don’t understand, mind. You’ll make it worse. Just… see if you can find anything on best practices for recovering from a corrupted sector. Mention it’s a Windows server environment, though. That’s important.

Honestly, I still can’t believe it. Little ANON in his pants. Right there on the sofa. Like a tiny, disgruntled gnome. It was a sight, wasn't it? He said he was "too hot" for pyjamas. Too hot in Suffolk in July. A classic. Did you see the look on his face when I told him it wasn't appropriate sofa attire? Pure drama. It's comfy! It is comfy, love. But not for wearing while the adults are around, is it? Especially not in…well,  those . You're embarrassing him now, Liam. He’s a sensitive soul. Sensitive enough to find the temperature unbearable and resort to underwear as sleepwear. Right. Anyway, enough about the sartorial choices of our offspring. I was thinking about something. You know, once we're back in the real world, when we get back to reality... Let me guess. You’ve been sketching out plans again? Last time it involved a glass atrium and a moat. Okay, the moat might have been a bit ambitious. But the general principle stands. This house…it's lovely, it really is. But it’s a bit…cozy, isn’t it? Especially having two rapidly growing mini-humans. Cozy is a polite word for ‘slightly cramped’ when you're battling over bathroom space in the mornings. I'll grant you that. I was actually looking at some architects’ websites the other day. There’s this one, called ‘Coastal Spaces,’ they do really interesting extensions. Coastal Spaces, eh? I’ll have a look. I was thinking a side extension, mainly. Knock through the dining room and kitchen, make one big open-plan living area. And maybe…just maybe…a small conservatory off the side of that. Somewhere with lots of light. I like the open plan idea. It would be so much nicer for entertaining. And the conservatory… imagining it filled with plants and light… it’s quite lovely. Where would the children's bedrooms go, though? Well, that’s the tricky part. We could lose the study. It's hardly utilised anyway, is it? I mostly file paperwork in there. And… we could go up. A small loft conversion. Two extra bedrooms. Wouldn't need to be massive, just enough. No study! Where will you hide your important papers? Very funny, sweetheart. Your father will sort out somewhere to hide his important papers. Probably under your bed. Don't even joke about that.

Honestly, Alun, this coffee is dreadful today. They’ve changed suppliers again, haven’t they? It tastes like dishwater. Remember that lovely Ethiopian blend we had last month? That was proper coffee. Aye, dreadful it is. The university budget, you know. Always squeezing pennies. They're probably trying to save 30 quid a month. Tredegar used to have a brilliant little café, "The Miner's Rest." Now  that  was coffee. Strong stuff, guaranteed to wake you up after a long shift down the pit. I can imagine. My upbringing in Cairo was, shall we say, rather different. The coffee culture there is… intense. Espresso rituals, cardamom, thick Turkish coffee. You wouldn’t find a lukewarm cup like this anywhere. Speaking of different, have you seen the wife's been going on about redecorating the sitting room? Apparently, beige is "out" now. Beige is  always  out, David. It's the colour of institutional drabness. What’s she thinking of going for? Something vibrant, I hope? My daughter, Bronwyn, she's got a real eye for colour. Just finished renovating her cottage in Pembrokeshire. Used shades of teal and ochre. Looked like something out of Tuscany, it did. Tuscany, ironically enough, is what she wants. Apparently, that's the height of chic now – a sort of rustic Italian farmhouse feel. Think distressed wood, linen curtains, terracotta pots… It's rather overwhelming, to be honest. And expensive. Don’t I know it! Speaking of expensive, have you heard anything more about the funding for the project? My application for phase two of the Hadron Collider data analysis seems to be stuck in a bureaucratic black hole. Dreadful, isn't it? I’ve put in for a grant for my work on X-ray crystallography and I'm facing the same issue. They keep demanding more justification for every single expenditure. As if understanding the structure of a protein is… frivolous. They want a detailed breakdown of how many paperclips we'll use. Paperclips! Good heavens. You'd think with all the money being thrown at things like, I don't know, fracking and new motorway schemes, they could spare a bit for genuine scientific research. It's ridiculous. Reminds me of trying to convince the council back in Tredegar to invest in the library. Endless red tape. It's infuriating. You’d think with the advances in computing power, the data analysis would almost be automatic.

Right, Operation Lego Sort is officially underway. Honestly, I think this pile has grown overnight. Are you two even  helping , or just contributing to the chaos? I'm helping, Mummy! I’m finding all the pink ones! They’re for Princess Sparkle’s castle. I’m building a spaceship! Pew pew! But it keeps…falling. A spaceship, that's brilliant, love. But maybe a slightly wider base? See, like this… . And yes, you're both helping! Princess Sparkle needs a fabulous castle, absolutely. Though, realistically, we need to separate the bricks by colour, not just 'pink'. That'll make building much easier. But pink is a  very  important colour, Mummy. Like,  super  important. Like… like Harry Potter’s cloak! A good comparison. Okay, pink is vital. But what about blue bricks? Do we have enough for a swimming pool for Princess Sparkle’s castle? Can we watch The Simpsons later, Mummy? Bart's spaceship is way better than mine. Honestly, the influence of television! We'll see, sweetheart. There's Lego to sort first. And after that, we need to make some decisions about Granny's place, that needs to be discussed. Granny’s place? Are we finally getting a new kitchen? The old one is  so  creaky. We're hoping! Dad’s getting some quotes for the renovations. It’s a big job, isn't it? New kitchen, new bathroom… maybe even try and get that leaky roof sorted. Can we go to the cinema soon? To see the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles movie? Mikey said it's got loads of pizza! Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles… Pizza… Right. We'll definitely see about the cinema. But remember, priorities. Lego first, Granny's roof second, Ninja Turtles and pizza third. Honestly, it's a constant negotiation. You two are masters of it. . I got a chocolate bunny! A really big one! You little chocolate fiend! Have you been at that already? Easter only just started! I want one too! A really, really big one! With sprinkles! Okay, okay, calm yourselves. We’ll have  some  chocolate later, but only after we've made a dent in this Lego mountain. Look, why don’t you two build something while I sort these yellow ones? Princess Sparkle needs a golden carriage, doesn't she? Yes! With a unicorn pulling it! And lots of… sparkly things! And a jetpack for the unicorn! So it can fly really fast!

Oh my god, it’s  good  to be back. Smells like actual food in here! I was living on croissants and slightly stale airport sandwiches for a week. Honestly, the food in Rome… it was good, don’t get me wrong, but it wasn't  home  food, you know? Hey! Welcome back! You look absolutely knackered. Croissants and airport sandwiches, really? That’s a recipe for disaster. I made you a proper shepherd’s pie. Thought you’d want something hearty after all that Italian exploring. Shepherd's pie?! You are an actual angel. Seriously, best welcome home ever. How long have I been gone? Feels like a lifetime. Did I miss anything important? Apart from obvious things, like the entire world continuing to spin. Just the usual, really. Liam's been complaining about his knee again after that football match – you remember, the one he was so insistent on playing in despite his dodgy joints? Classic Liam. And Mum called, wondering when you were back to take your Nan to that bingo night. She's getting really keen. Oh god, bingo night. That’s going to be… an experience. Liam's knee, though, that’s no surprise. Honestly, he's a walking medical case study. Did he at least win the match? Apparently, they lost spectacularly. And he pulled it. Again. He’s taking it surprisingly well, moaning in a very dignified, slightly limpy way. Speaking of sports, did you catch any of the Women's World Cup while you were away? A little bit! I tried to, but the Wi-Fi was patchy. It’s absolutely brilliant, isn't it? The energy’s been incredible. I was gutted I couldn't watch the whole thing. It's been amazing! Seriously inspiring. Right, pie's nearly ready. How was Rome, properly? Tell me  everything . Did you see all the historical stuff you wanted to? Did you get harassed by pigeons? Pigeons, definitely. They are relentless! I saw the Colosseum, obviously, and the Vatican. It was… a lot. Overwhelming, in the best way possible. But honestly, the best part was just wandering around, getting lost in the little side streets, finding those tiny trattorias. I think I gained about five pounds. Five pounds is worth it if you had pasta and gelato every day, right? So, no handsome Italian men whisking you away? I had bets with Chloe and Maya. Chloe’s convinced you would’ve fallen head over heels for a charming barista.

Right then, love. Grandparents due any minute, aren’t they? Did you get the biscuits out, Ben? Chocolate digestives, like Gran likes? Aye, Nana. Got 'em. And the shortbread for Grandad, too. Did you remember to put the heating up a bit? He’s always moaning it’s nippy. Course I did, lad. Wouldn’t want him catching a chill. Malton’s a bit colder than Hull, you know. Used to grumble about the cold myself when I were a lass visiting my auntie up 'ere. Not like our nice, sheltered East Riding. Speaking of sheltered, did you tell your auntie Sheila not to bring that blasted wind chime again? Last time it nearly drove Grandad mad! Told her. She said she’d leave it in the car. But you know her, she’ll probably ‘forget’. Oh, my goodness, is that telly blaring already? Can scarcely hear myself think! All this modern technology… back in my day, we had the wireless and we were grateful for it! Don’t you start, Elsie! Always moaning. It’s only a bit of background noise. More noise from those blasted tractors down the road these days, I tell you! Scaring the livestock. Now, now, you two. Elsie, be nice. Ben's just trying to find something on for you. Grandad, you want the news? Or maybe a bit of Antiques Roadshow? You were saying just last week you thought you’d spotted a valuable teapot. Nope, neither of you are interested in that stuff. How about a bit of that wildlife programme? Got some amazing footage of owls. Owls? Hmph. Owls are just big, feathered rats. Always causing mischief, they are. Remember that one that used to roost in the apple tree outside our kitchen window in Hedon? Kept me awake all night with its hooting! Aye, and it crapped all over the washing line! Elsie used to go mad. Used to threaten to shoot it with her grandmother’s air rifle. Your father! Elsie, you never! Don't go wishing anything bad on the wildlife. Ben, turn it down a bit, love, will you? My ears are ringing something awful. And Elsie, sit down. You'll be wearing yourself out standing about. My knees aren’t what they used to be, that's for sure. Back in my day, I could dance all night at the Paragon Ballroom. Now? A trip to the shops leaves me breathless.

Right, so, little ones, are you two excited for tonight? We’re having a proper movie night! Yes! Peter Pan! Can we have popcorn, Mummy? Lots and lots? Flying! I wanna fly like Peter! Pew pew! Of course, lots of popcorn. And flying is brilliant, isn't it? That's the magic of Neverland. You know, Peter Pan is a really special story. It’s been told in so many ways. Not just the films, but also in a play originally – a play by J.M. Barrie. He wrote it a long, long time ago. A play? Like at the theatre? Exactly! Though, the Disney film is probably what you’re most familiar with. It's just so lovely, isn't it? All the colours and the music... But it's based on that original story. Who’s Captain Hook? Is he scary? He  is  a bit scary, isn’t he? He's Peter's arch-nemesis. He lost his hand to a crocodile, you know! A very hungry crocodile. That’s why he’s always so grumpy. A crocodile ate his hand?! Ewww! Yes, a rather large, clever crocodile. It's rather sad, really, when you think about it. He’s trying to get revenge on Peter. And what about Tinkerbell? She's your favourite, isn't she, sweetheart? She’s sparkly and she can fly! And she’s tiny! She helps Peter. She does indeed. And you know, Tinkerbell’s story has been explored a lot in more recent films. Those Disney sequels, you know? They really emphasize her feelings and how important she is to Peter. It's quite touching. We were thinking about donating to Great Ormond Street Hospital, haven't we? They do a wonderful job, you know. It's what those films are partly about, remember? Thinking about children who need help. Great Ormond Street? What’s that? It's a hospital, darling. A special hospital for children who are very poorly. They need lots of help and kind people to look after them. Peter Pan is such a magical story because it reminds us to think of children. And sometimes, even when things are tough, there’s still room for magic and believing. So, we give them money so they can be better? That's right. So they can get the best care and feel a little bit better. Even a little bit of magic can help sometimes.

Right then. Nearly there, is it? Feels like we’ve been on the road for an eternity. Southend feels a lifetime ago, doesn't it? Can't believe I'm saying that. Don't be daft, Dad. It's only been a couple of hours. Longer than I’d like, admittedly. Traffic was dreadful getting out of Exeter. You alright back there? You look a bit…melancholy. He's just feeling the goodbye, love. It’s always hard, isn’t it? Even short trips feel significant when you know it's a while before we see him again. And you're not helping with the "eternity" comment, Nigel! Just saying, it's a bit jarring. Moving back to the coast after…well, after all these years inland. Taunton wasn’t bad, you know. Nice place. Always felt a bit…contained though. Like a well-kept secret. Not like Southend. The openness, the sea...it gets in your bones. Taunton was lovely, though. Remember the garden? You were so proud of those roses. We should have taken some photos. And honestly, the peace was brilliant. Remember those early mornings when you’d just sit on the patio with your coffee, reading? Yes, well, peace has its drawbacks, doesn't it? Too much time for thinking. Too much time to dwell on… things. Remember that house we had in Brixham, though? That was something else. Right on the harbour. Oh, Brixham! That was chaotic! The seagulls, the fishing boats, the smell… utterly wonderful. And your attempts at sailing – hilarious! Remember when you nearly capsized? Don't remind me. Nearly ended up fish food. I was never cut out for sailing, I’ll admit. Too much wind and water. I prefer a nice, predictable garden. Though I suppose this Devon air will do me good. I’ve felt…stuck, you know? You will love it, Dad. You'll be pottering about in the garden, reading your books... Just need to get you settled in. Are you sleeping alright these days? You seemed a bit tired last weekend. Sleep…it comes and goes. These days, it’s more like sporadic naps. The neighbours in Taunton were very quiet, mind you. Too quiet, perhaps. Woke up one morning feeling like I’d been buried alive. Do you wake up early for teaching, Amelia? Ugh, don’t even. The kids are like little tornadoes before 9 am.

Right then. Creeh-st-Michael to… well, anywhere that isn't here, really. This track work's a bit of a trial, isn't it? Been waiting nearly an hour. Tell me about it, miss. They said “short delay,” didn't they? Short for them, maybe. My rheumatics are protesting something fierce. Been standin' about all mornin' with the workin' party. Oh, I do sympathise. These old bones don’t appreciate being stood about neither. I’m Penelope, by the way. Penelope Ashworth. Arthur Penhaligon. Pleased to meet ya, Penelope. So, you 'ere for the ME event next year, are ya? I hear it's a proper do. The ME? Oh, you mean the Model Engineering one? Yes, I’m a regular. Always have been, really. Though, I must say, I’ve noticed a distinct lack of women involved lately. Heavens, used to be a few dabblin' in the past, didn’t there? More sketching than building, naturally. Aye, it's mostly blokes, innit? Though, they’re makin' an effort this year, apparently. A special workshop, somethin’ about encouraging younger participants - lads and lasses alike. My granddaughter, bless ‘er, fancied havin’ a go last year, but everything was far too complex for a nine-year-old. It’s important, isn't it? Encouraging them. Whether it’s engines or, well, anything really. My daughter, she runs a lovely little nursery down in Frome. Fantastic with the little ones. Always pushin’ for equal opportunities, she is. Proper advocate for female equality, my Elsie. Good for her. My wife, bless ‘er soul, she always said the same. A right firebrand, she was. Didn’t take any nonsense. Head of the ladies' committee at the Nationwide. Championed equal pay for years, she did. Got some proper battles. Bless her. It’s so important, those battles. Though, sometimes... sometimes I worry things haven’t changed as much as we’d like to think. Honestly, you wouldn’t believe the blokes I have to deal with when I'm trying to acquire a piece for the gallery. They think a woman can’t possibly know the provenance of a Chippendale chair. Men! Always thinkin' they know best. It’s the same in the gardening club. They get all flustered when I offer a suggestion about the dahlias. “Arthur, you wouldn’t know a chrysanthemum from a carrot!” they say. Oh, dear. Reminds me of a chap I met recently, offering me a "Swedish massage" to "help loosen up" a particularly stubborn antique cabinet.

Right, so, Santorini. It really is stunning, isn't it? All those white houses clinging to the cliffs… It’s just… wow. But I’m still a bit… apprehensive, I suppose. Apprehensive? About Greece? Love, what on earth have you got to be apprehensive about? Sunshine, beautiful scenery, delicious food… it's hardly a recipe for disaster. I know, I know. It’s just… it’s a bit far, isn't it? Ten flights from Totnes! And I’ve never really done a proper holiday alone before, not like this. It's me, you, and Finn. Just the three of us. You know I always feel a bit safer with you around. You're thirty-five, Elara. Not fifteen. You’re perfectly capable of looking after yourself and Finn. Besides, you’re a teacher; you handle twenty little terrors every day. A holiday is a different ballgame entirely. Think of it as a chance to recharge, to experience something different. And Finn will absolutely love it. Imagine him splashing in the Aegean Sea! I’m picturing him melting down in a taverna because he’s ‘starving’ and only wants chips. Which, let’s be honest, is a very likely scenario. Adapt and overcome, darling. Learn to say "chips" in Greek. There's probably a perfectly lovely translation. Look, I understand the feeling of… well, being adrift a bit without someone familiar to lean on. But you're not adrift. You're embarking on an adventure. And you’re taking your son. That’s more than enough reason to be excited. Have you looked at the hotel reviews properly? I’ve skimmed them. It seems lovely, a small family-run place overlooking the caldera. But it mentioned a lot of steps. A  lot . Finn's not exactly a champion stair climber at the best of times. Right. We’ll have to factor that in. Perhaps request a room on a lower level? Most hotels accommodate requests like that. You need to be proactive, love. Don't just accept whatever they give you. Good point. I’ll email them. I’ve also been looking at tours. There’s a sunset boat trip that sounds incredible. And a wine-tasting tour in Santorini – obviously, not  with  Finn. I'm thinking maybe you could watch him for a few hours? You'd love it, wouldn’t you? All that sunshine and good food. Now you’re talking.

Morning, Uncle Rohan! Didn’t realize you were up so early. Thought you’d still be dreaming of cricket scores. Morning, Liam. Early bird catches the worm, boy. And yes, still processing England’s performance yesterday. Painful, absolutely painful. Shoulda, coulda, woulda… you know how it is. Didn't expect it from Root at all, honestly. Tell me about it! I was screaming at the telly. Reckon Stokes would’ve made a difference, though. He’s got that… fire, hasn't he? This new-look team needs a bit of that. So, you managed to sort those online payments out then? Mum was fretting about it last night. Aye, sorted it. Took a bit of wrangling, mind you. This new banking system is a nightmare. Everything's online, no face-to-face service anymore. They want you to do everything on yer phone. Tried to pay the electricity bill online, nearly ended up transferring funds to someone in Nigeria! Thank goodness I double-checked. Blimey! That’s dodgy. Mum always says she prefers paying in person, just for that reason. She doesn’t trust all these digital things. She still calls and makes appointments. Crazy, innit? She’s not wrong, though. Being careful never hurt nobody. Anyway, it’s all sorted now. Got the confirmation emails, paid the mortgage, and even managed to top up Auntie Shirley's phone credit. She'll be thrilled. She's been complaining she can't call me to nag about her garden. Always will be. So, how’s work going? Still battling with the new inventory system? You were pulling your hair out last time we spoke. Don't even remind me. It’s a constant struggle. They promised it would streamline everything, make things easier. It’s just… complicated. Lots of hoops to jump through, and the training was rubbish. I'm practically teaching myself. Some of the younger ones are picking it up quicker though. They're digital natives, you know? Born with a phone glued to their hand. Me? I still remember dial-up internet. I can imagine! My Nan still complains about streaming services buffering. Gets proper frustrated. Speaking of which, did you see what Beyoncé’s doing now? Country music? Who'd have thought? Beyoncé? Doing country? That's a right surprise. I haven't been following her music as close lately, to be honest. I’m trying to give myself a break.

Right then, Sharon, can you hear me alright? This Skype thing’s a bit fiddly, innit? Keeps cutting out. Reminds me of the old wireless we 'ad back in the day. Fuzzy as anything. Perfectly fine, Arthur! Just a bit grainy, dear, but that’s to be expected. Lovely to see you both! How’s your leg feeling today? Still giving you gyp? Aye, still giving me gyp. Getting worse, I reckon. The doctor’s wanting me to go and see some fella in Norwich. A ‘specialist’ he calls ‘im. Not fancying that, not one bit. Hospitals… all those corridors and beeping machines. Gives me the willies, it does. Specialists aren’t always bad, Arthur. They just know more about, well, ailments. And Norwich isn’t so bad. Got a decent cathedral, I hear. Cathedrals! What use's a cathedral to me with a dodgy leg? I just need to be able to get down to the shops for me bread and butter, that's all. Speaking of which, Doris made a lovely Victoria sponge this morning. Had a bit, of course. Can't resist a good sponge. Oh, Arthur, you're such a glutton! But a Victoria sponge does sound lovely. Shame I can’t have a slice. Honestly, Michael, stop messing with the lighting! You know I like to see what I’m looking at. Sorry, love. Just trying to brighten things up a bit. It’s a bit gloomy here today. It’s raining, you know. Typical Birmingham weather. Gloomy weather! Reminds me of that trip we took, Doris and I, to Yorkshire. Years ago now, must’ve been… sixty-five years? Always raining cats and dogs up there! But the scenery… well, the scenery was something else. Those moors... vast as anything. I remember that trip! We stayed in a youth hostel in the Lake District, didn't we, Arthur? Slept in a huge dormitory with a snoring champion! I never slept a wink. Ah, youth hostels! Proper rough and tumble, weren't they? Though, mind you, I'm not sure I’d fancy it now. My back wouldn’t allow it. Used to be good for a wander though. Remember young Timmy? He did a project on globes at school. Painted one himself, he did! Took ages. All those little countries… A globe project? Fascinating! I had a student do one on the impact of the London Underground system on urban sprawl.

Right, this is reet good, isn't it? Proper lush. ANON's cooking is champion, honestly. Never thought I’d find Bolognese this good so far north. It is amazing. Seriously. ANON’s obviously been practicing. Though, I still think mine's slightly better… don’t tell her I said that! Aye, you’re always goin’ on about your Sunday roasts. I’ll give you that, you do a mean gravy. But pasta? This is top tier. So, flights… did you manage to find anything decent to Newcastle? I’m trying not to pay a fortune, you know? Mum’s been gettin’ on a bit, want to see her for the weekend. I did a right deep dive this morning. Honestly, it's a minefield. EasyJet were being, well, EasyJet. Ridiculously inflated prices. I found something with British Airways though, a bit more pricey, yeah, but the timings are decent and they include baggage. Plus, you know, a bit more legroom. So, about £140 return? Blimey. That’s a bit steep, innit? Last time I flew with BA I felt like I was payin’ extra for the air itself. Is there nowt else, even if it's a bit… unorthodox? Like, a stopover somewhere? I had a look. There’s one with Ryanair that goes via Dublin, but the layover’s like, six hours. Seriously, who wants to spend six hours in an airport? You’d be lucky to get a decent cuppa. Besides, I remember that Ryanair flight to Malaga with you, remember? The one where they lost your bag? Don’t remind me! I spent half the holiday wearin’ that awful souvenir t-shirt from a market. It was covered in llamas. I looked a right fool. But seriously, six hours… that’s brutal. Okay, BA it is then, I reckon. Just gotta bite the bullet. Send me the link, will ya? I’ll book it before the price goes up again. Will do. Right, speaking of bullets, that documentary we were watchin' earlier… the one about the Arctic explorer? That was intense. Honestly, the conditions they were in… completely bonkers. Aye, it were proper bleak. Makes you appreciate a bit o' central heating, doesn’t it? Still can’t believe they did that all on foot and relying on sled dogs. Had to be some grit involved in that lot. Do you think modern equipment would have made it easier or just changed the dynamic?

Right then, so you’re saying Barclay's are charging you  extra  for… what was it again, Sarah? For international transfers, Dad. It's ridiculous. I transfer money to my sister in Spain, just to help her out a bit with the kids, and they’ve suddenly slapped on this hefty fee. It’s like, five pounds just to send fifty! It’s a blatant money grab, isn't it? They all are, love. Don’t you dare give them a good word. Barclay’s, Lloyds, HSBC… the lot of 'em. Just lining their pockets. I’ve seen it firsthand, working within the system. You wouldn't believe the bonuses some of those chaps get. Makes my blood boil, it does. Well, you know, margins are margins. Banking’s a business, isn't it? Though, five pounds... that  is  a bit steep. You could always look at Wise, Sarah. TransferWise, they used to call themselves. Much better rates, usually. I looked into it! A while ago. It seemed complicated, all that verification and stuff. Plus, I felt a bit uneasy sending money through a… a different provider, you know? Stick with what you know, I suppose. Even if it’s being fleeced. Don’t be daft, love. Complicated? It's a website! And safer, probably. These banks, they're tempting targets for those chaps online. I’m having to deal with more and more fraud cases at court now. The scammers are getting cleverer. Speaking of the police, did you hear about that poor fellow down the road? Had his car nicked. Right in broad daylight! No! What? That's awful. Was anything else taken? Just the car, thankfully. They think it was a chop shop job, apparently. Officer said they’re seeing more of those. Used to be a rare thing, you know, car theft. Now… constant. It’s the price of progress, I suppose. Though, progress doesn’t help when you need to get to work. Progress? It's a breakdown, that’s what it is. Everything’s breaking down. The roads, the hospitals, now car theft on the doorstep. And the weather! Don't even get me started. This summer’s been a washout. Remember summers when we were kids? Proper sunshine! It's climate change, Auntie Maureen. It's been explained a million times. Don't you start with that climate change malarkey! We had terrible summers when I was a girl, too.

Right then, so we’re clear, we're doin' our favourites, yeah? Like, favourite holiday, favourite animal…and the vital one – favourite food. 'Cos that's the important stuff, innit? Aye, dead right, Maisie. Priorities first. Let's start with holidays. Mine’s gotta be Greece. Santorini, specifically. The whitewashed buildings, the blue domes…it’s just  stunning . And the gyros are to die for. Greece sounds lovely, Chloe! Mine’s got to be Ireland, obviously. But specifically, the Aran Islands. It's where my granny's from, and there's just somethin’ magical about the rugged coastline, the ancient stone walls, the feelin' of the sea air...and the fresh seafood! Oh, the seafood. You’ve never tasted anything like it. Aran Islands! Sounds wild. For me, it’s gotta be Cornwall. Bit cliché, I know, but the beaches are gorgeous, even if the weather’s always a bit unpredictable. And proper cream teas! Scones, clotted cream, jam…makes me practically swoon. What about you, Maisie? Where's your dream holiday spot? Dream holiday…hmm. It wouldn't be a sunshine and sand kinda thing. Give me somewhere cold, like Iceland, any day. All that volcanic landscape, the Northern Lights…it just looks proper amazing, doesn’t it? I’d love to see the glaciers. And I reckon the food would be adventurous, right? Not just chips and mushy peas. Iceland! Seriously, Maisie? You’d pick a freezing cold country over a beach? You’re a strange lass, you are. My favourite holiday’s always been Blackpool. Classic, I know, but it’s got everything. The Pleasure Beach, the arcades, the fish and chips on the prom…and it’s right on our doorstep. Can't beat it, can you? Blackpool! That’s a holiday alright. Full of noise and flashing lights. Though, I haven’t had a decent fish and chips in ages. Proper, battered, not that frozen stuff. Speaking of food, what’s everyone's  absolute  favourite food? I’m struggling to pick just one. Probably my mam's Sunday roast. Proper Yorkshire puddings, crispy roast potatoes… it just tastes like home, you know? It’s comfort food on another level. Sunday roast is good. My nan used to make the best. But for me, it's gotta be welsh rarebit. Cheesy, garlicky, toasted bread… perfection! Warm and gooey, especially on a rainy day. Rarebit?

Right, okay, so I’ve been thinkin’. Proper thinkin’, not just the ‘need-to-eat-chocolate’ thinkin’. Dangerous, that. Proper thinking usually leads to existential dread in my experience. What’s it about this time? Old age again? You were fretting about wrinkles earlier. That was just a momentary wobble. This is bigger. It’s… what do we  do  with all this? All this… stuff. The art, I mean. What happens to it when we're, like, eighty? Stuck in care homes, probably, forgetting we ever held a pencil. Dramatic much? Eighty’s a long way off, Elara. And realistically, you're horrifyingly talented. Someone will want your work. Grandchildren, maybe. Or a particularly discerning retirement home art therapist. See, that’s what I mean! A retirement home art therapist! It’s a bit bleak, innit? I don’t want my legacy to be pastel landscapes for bingo nights. I want… I don’t know. Impact. Something that lasts. Impact’s a big ask, even for the greats. Most artists are forgotten, you know. But that doesn’t mean the  making  isn’t important. The process, the joy, the frustration… that’s the point, isn't it? Not necessarily the lasting fame. I suppose. Still feels a bit… pointless sometimes, when I’m staring at a blank canvas and convinced I’m going to produce something utterly rubbish. Like this essay. The one on Surrealism? You were buzzing about Dalí last week. Said he was your new inspiration. Was! Now I'm just… stuck. It feels forced. Like I’m trying to  be  Surrealist instead of, you know, actually  feeling  it. I keep trying to write about melting clocks and lobster telephones, but it’s all just clichés. You need to stop  trying  to be anything. Honestly. Just… describe something. Anything. Something you saw today. Don't worry about making it ‘Surrealist’. Just describe it with as much detail as you can. Okay… Right. There was this pigeon. On the way to the library. It had, like, this weirdly iridescent sheen to its feathers. And it was just… staring at me. Properly intensely. Like it was judging my life choices. There you go. Write  that . The pigeon. The iridescent feathers. The judgemental stare. Forget Dalí for a bit. Let the Surrealism come from the observation itself. It'll be far more interesting than trying to mimic him. That’s…actually a really good point.

Honestly, I’m knackered. This Henderson project is  eating  my life. I swear, if I have to look at another Gantt chart, I might scream. Tell me about it. My shift was a right old rollercoaster today. Had a patient, Liam, really struggling with anxiety. Took almost two hours just to get him to talk about what was triggering it. Poor Liam. You’re amazing, you know. I can barely handle sorting spreadsheets, let alone dealing with that kind of stuff. What was it this time? Just a build-up, really. His mum’s been putting a lot of pressure on him to move back home and get a “proper job.” He's trying to be a musician, remember? You know his vibe. Oh, the musician thing. Right. Poor dude. His mum sounds like a nightmare. My mum’s been on at me about finding a "serious" boyfriend. Like, she doesn’t understand that I’m perfectly happy being single for now. Oh, mums, eh? They just want what they think is best. Although, sometimes, their 'best’ is completely bonkers. Speaking of which, did you hear back from Chloe about Saturday? Are we still on for that rooftop bar? Not yet. I texted her earlier, but no reply. She’s probably just swamped with work – she’s been pulling extra shifts at the gallery. Honestly, sometimes I worry about her. She burns the candle at both ends, doesn't she? Remember that time she collapsed at Sarah's birthday? Yeah, I remember. We need to tell her to slow down. We’ll all be there for her, if she listens. Right, almost ready for you to taste this curry. I went a bit rogue with the spices, added a pinch of fenugreek. You fancy it? Fenugreek? You’re brave! I’m a bit of a spice wimp, you know. Last time you did something adventurous with the curry, I spent half the night clutching the toilet bowl. That was  one  time! And you said you loved it afterwards! This is milder, I promise. It's got butternut squash in, so it's nice and creamy. Plus, you need something comforting after dealing with Gantt charts all day. Okay, okay, you’ve convinced me. But if I end up spontaneously combusting from spice, I’m blaming you. Actually… that’s really good! You've actually outdone yourself. It’s not even remotely spicy.

Right then, let's 'ave a proper look at this consent form, shall we? Seems a bit… thorough, doesn't it? All this GDPR guff. Makes you wonder what they’re expecting to go wrong, doesn't it, Sarah? It’s just standard now, isn’t it, Margaret? They’ve got to cover themselves. Honestly, the legal departments these days… I skimmed it, but I did notice the bit about sharing anonymised data for research purposes. Are we happy with that? Particularly with the international elements of the seminar. Aye, I’m alright with it, Sarah. Anonymised data, that’s fair enough. It could be useful for future course development, couldnae it? Especially considering we're dealing with so many different cultural nuances in international communication. I've been thinking about that, actually. We really need to emphasise the non-verbal cues. It's the bit they  never  get taught, is it? True enough, love. Words are important, o’ course, but a shrug or a raised eyebrow can derail a deal faster than you can say “international trade agreement.” I was thinking, though, about the structure. We agreed on the ‘cultural iceberg’ analogy, didn't we? I’m still a bit unsure about devoting so much time to Hofstede’s dimensions. It's a useful starting point, but it can feel a bit… prescriptive, can’t it? I agree, Margaret. It feels a little dated now, doesn’t it? We don't want to pigeonhole cultures. Perhaps we could broaden it out a bit? Incorporate some more recent research on intercultural communication - maybe Schein's work on tacit assumptions? It's a bit heavier going for undergraduates, but it’s also more reflective of the complexity of real-world interactions. Good shout, Sarah! Definitely. And could we weave in some practical exercises? I was picturing a role-play scenario maybe – something with negotiating a contract with a client from… let’s say, Japan. Knowing their level of formality and indirect communication styles. It could highlight the pitfalls perfectly. I’ve found that sorts of interactive elements really engage the students. Less lecturing, more doing, eh? Aye, that’s the ticket, love. Less of me lecturing, more of them engaging. Roll plays sound brilliant. But we need to be really careful about sensitivity. We wouldn't want to unintentionally offend anyone. It's a fine line, innit? Making the exercise impactful without being patronising or stereotypical.

Honestly, I’m freezing. I thought October in Beijing would be a bit milder. This wind is cutting right through me. You always say that, love. You're never acclimatized. It's perfectly normal October weather. Besides, we're nearly home. Just another five minutes. Did you manage to sort out that scheduling conflict with Professor Li? Almost. He claims he absolutely  needs  to use the lecture hall on Tuesday afternoon for his calligraphy club. Calligraphy! Really? It’s a vital lecturing space, and he wants to practice brushstrokes. I tried to explain we have a guest speaker lined up, but he was… resolute. Very politely resolute, I’ll grant him that, but resolute nonetheless. Sounds like a classic Professor Li. You know, you could try offering him an alternative space. The smaller seminar room, maybe? It's a bit cramped, but… Tried that. Apparently, the acoustics aren't right for "the proper flow of creative energy," or some such nonsense. Honestly, sometimes I think academia attracts people who've spent a little too long inside their own heads. Now, now. Don’t be too harsh. They’re just passionate about their subject. Though, I admit, the level of dedication to calligraphy is… noteworthy. How did the students react to your lecture on post-structuralism today? Mixed, as always. Half glazed over, half furiously taking notes. I think I lost about three of them completely when I brought up Foucault. You could practically see their brains short-circuiting. But that’s the risk, isn't it? Pushing them beyond their comfort zone. Exactly. It’s our job to challenge them, not just to spoon-feed them facts. Speaking of comfort zones, have you had a chance to look at those estate agent listings I sent you? I glanced at them. Mostly just rows of identical apartment blocks, weren't they? All grey concrete and tiny balconies. I’m not sure any of them really “sang” to me. They're a start. It's the market, darling. You know we need somewhere with a bit more space. The current flat is lovely, but both of our offices are overflowing into our living space, and I'm pretty sure the cat is starting to think he owns the kitchen. He practically does. And I agree we need more space, but I’m not convinced we need to move to some soulless box. I was thinking… what about trying to find something a bit further out, maybe in one of the hutongs?

Honestly, this is lovely, Liam, but I feel like I’m going to be battling food waste all week. We made  far  too much Bolognese. I swear, I’ll be reheating pasta for the next five days. It's good though, isn't it? Mum’s recipe is legendary. And honestly, a little leftover Bolognese never hurt anyone. We could freeze some. We could, but the freezer is already crammed with your experimental sourdough attempts. Remember that brick you tried last month? Still haven’t dared throw it out. It  was  a little dense, I'll admit. Engineering principles don't always translate to bread-making, apparently. Anyway, freezing is a good idea. Makes me think of Grandma’s house, doesn’t it? Always a massive freezer full of things she'd made. Pickled onions, marmalade, enough stewed apples to feed an army... Oh, absolutely. And the pantry too. Jars and jars of everything imaginable. I miss that, actually. The feeling of abundance. So different from now, where everything feels so...calculated. You know? We barely buy things unless they're on special offer. It’s gotten so stressful. I’ve started feeling guilty about throwing practically anything away. It’s the plastic bag charge, isn’t it? That really shifted something. Remember when we used to just grab bags without a second thought? It did good though, reduced the plastic waste. Speaking of things shifting, did you see that documentary on urban farming initiatives? Seriously impressive how much food they’re growing in disused railway arches. I did! It was brilliant. Imagine if every school had a proper allotment, not just a sad patch of dirt. We could teach kids so much more than just maths and English. Skills they could actually use. I’d love to incorporate some basic gardening and cooking into my lessons, but… funding, you know. Always funding. It’s the same in engineering. Trying to get innovative projects off the ground… It’s like some industries are just… closed off to new ideas. Private sectors often seem a bit better, though. Less red tape. Do you think so? It always seems so impenetrable to me. My niece is thinking about careers and she's interested in robotics, but I just don't know where to steer her. The careers advice at school is… let’s just say it's not exactly cutting-edge. I know!

Right, so the initial data from the mindfulness intervention… it’s… intriguing, to say the least. The anxiety scores are dipping, definitely, but the reported sense of ‘well-being’ is… lower than expected. Lower? How so? I thought the point was reducing anxiety  leading  to improved wellbeing. Shouldn’t they be linked? Precisely! That’s what I find puzzling. Participants are reporting less anxiety, which is fantastic – we’re seeing a really measurable change in physiological markers too, heart rate variability improving, cortisol levels slightly down. But when asked directly about their overall happiness, their contentment… it's plateaued, or even slightly decreased in some cases. That's weird. Maybe they’re just… uncomfortable with the vulnerability? Mindfulness, like, explicitly asks you to sit with uncomfortable feelings, right? Maybe recognising the anxiety is subsiding makes them feel... emptier, somehow? That's a possibility. I’ve been leaning towards that, actually. It’s almost as if confronting and managing the anxiety is a worthy achievement in itself, a tangible goal. Now that they've arguably achieved it, they're struggling to define what comes next, what they  should  be feeling. It's a bit like reaching the top of a mountain and then realising… there's nothing particularly exciting at the summit. Sounds a bit existential, doesn’t it? Like, we chase after the thing we  don't  want, and then when we get rid of it, we have to figure out what we  do  want. Remember Grandma Doris always saying, “A busy mind is a happy mind”? Though that was usually followed by a complaint about how busy  her  mind was. She wasn't exactly a paragon of mindfulness, was she? You know, I’m half tempted to add a component assessing existential needs – purpose, meaning – into the follow-up questionnaire. Good idea. See if there’s a correlation. What about work, then? Still battling with the SEN paperwork? Little Liam's assessment is proving tricky, isn't it? It is. Honestly, it's a minefield. The parents are understandably anxious, and rightfully so. They just want the best for him, but the system…well, the system is designed to gather data, not necessarily to support children. I'm trying to navigate it with as much empathy as possible, but it  is  exhausting. I feel like I’m writing the same thing repeatedly, just with different student names. Needs a touch more salt.

Cor blimey, this rain’s somethin’ else, innit? Proper miserable. Makes a body ache just lookin’ at it. Reminds me o’ Costessey marshes, right enough, on a proper dreary day. Damp seepin’ into your bones, it does. It is a bit gloomy, dear. But at least we're inside, warm and dry. Fancy a biscuit? I made shortbread this morning. It’s a bit buttery, but it’s cheering. You’ve been quiet today, Arthur. More than usual, even. Is everything alright? Alright? Well… alright's a strong word, Mary. Just… feelin’ a bit lost, I suppose. Like a buoy adrift, you know? Not anchored to nothin’. Used to be, even when I wasn't workin’, I felt… useful. Lookin' after the garden, mending things round the house. Now… just feelin' like I'm takin' up space. Lost, Arthur? That’s a heavy feeling. Sorry to barge in, Mary. Just needed a top-up of that lovely tea you make. What’s all this about feeling adrift? Sounds a bit bleak. He’s just having one of his days, David. Feeling a bit down. All this thinking about retirement, I expect. It's harder than they tell you, isn't it? After all those years, suddenly… nothing to  do . It’s more than just retirement, David. It's… it’s everything, really. Sarah’s been on at me about downsizing, you know. Said the Council Tax is killin' her, and the house is too big for just the two of us. Downsizing? Where were you thinking of moving? Somewhere near the coast, perhaps? You always did talk about wanting to be near the sea again. That's what she suggests, but the thought of it... unsettling. This house… it’s been my life, hasn’t it? All me and Margaret had. Selling it… feels like sellin’ a bit of her too, you know? And finding somewhere… I can’t imagine being away from Costessey. Even with the rain and the marshes. Honestly, Arthur, don’t think like that. It's just bricks and mortar. Memories are in your heart, not the wallpaper. And Sarah’s got your best interests at heart. Money is tight, we all know that. She's right, Arthur. Practicality has to come into it, doesn't it? Though I understand the sentimental attachment. We’ve got that with the old house in Birmingham. Mum kept it full of memories, every nook and cranny.

Honestly, Chloe, this new lash serum is just not doing it for me. I was so excited, all the reviews were raving, said it'd give you natural length without extensions. Three weeks in, and I've got… practically nothing. Just a bit stickier than usual, really. Oh, no! Which one was it? The 'Luminous Lash Bloom' one? I saw that advertised everywhere. Everyone on Facebook was going on about it. That's the one! See? Even Facebook couldn't save it. I'm starting to think the reviews were all fake. And expensive fake, at that! Nearly fifty quid! Ridiculous. I’m going back to my trusty Boots own-brand volumising mascara, I think. At least I know what I’m getting. Boots own-brand is surprisingly good, isn't it? I’ve been using their nail polish remover lately, the one with the cuticle softener. Absolute game changer. My nails were always so brittle, especially after using gel. Oh, I need to try that! My nails are a mess. I was trying this ‘luxury’ remover – you know, the one with the sparkly bottle? – and it felt like I was stripping away my actual nails, not just the polish. Urgent re-evaluation needed. Honestly, sometimes I think the more expensive something is, the worse it is. Tell me about it! I bought a fancy face cream the other week, supposed to be all organic and whatnot. It made me break out! I ended up slathering on some E45 and that sorted it out quicker. Proper pot of gold stuff, that. E45! The unsung hero of skincare. You’re right. Speaking of heroes, have you seen Sarah lately? I tried ringing her last week, but she didn’t answer. No, not for ages. She mentioned something about helping her mum with a bit of gardening and getting really into it. Said her mum’s roses were flourishing. It’s nice to see her doing something she enjoys, she seemed a bit down when we last chatted. Yeah, she was. Remember when she was trying to learn Portuguese? Gave that up pretty quickly, didn't she? She gets easily distracted if it’s not immediately rewarding, I think. Definitely. It’s a shame though. She's got such a good brain. She needs something to focus her energy on. I'm going shopping on Saturday, fancy joining? There's a sale on at Primark, apparently good deals on handbags.

Right, so, parking was a nightmare, weren't it? Honestly, this place – Bold Street – they could charge a fella’s arm and a leg for ten minutes. Could’ve walked quicker, I reckon. But me mum was proper moaning about her knees, you know? Tell me about it. I had to circle twice. Thought I was going to end up on the docks. Honestly, Liverpool City Council and parking… a match made in misery. So, you managed to wrangle her out of the car alright? Did she see that new Egyptian exhibit at the World Museum? Aye, she did. She loved it, actually. Proper fascinated by those mummies. She was asking me all sorts about the afterlife and curses, like she's some kinda archaeologist. Can you believe it? Me mum, into ancient Egypt! I was tryin' to explain the carbon dating, but she just waved me away. 'Don't be boring Kevin,' she said. Classic. My nan's the same with history. Anything involving facts, she wants none of it. So, how was the museum overall? Worth the trek, then? Definitely. Though, it’s funny, isn’t it? We’ve got these amazing museums, right on our doorstep, and half the people I know never bother goin'. I'm always tellin’ me classes about Liverpool's heritage, and then they go home and watch reality TV. It's barmy. Speaking of things that are barmy, I had a right carry-on at work today. Little Liam – you remember him, the one who keeps eating crayons? – he'd apparently glued his shoe to the floor. You're jokin'! Liam? Seriously? How’d he even manage that? I don't know! That’s the mystery. The teachers just found him sat there, perfectly calm, tryin' to pull it off. Apparently, the glue was super strong. Took three of them and a whole bottle of white spirit to get him free. He didn't even seem bothered! Just started asking for a biscuit. Bless him. Social work must be a proper rollercoaster, eh? You have your moments of pure chaos. You have no idea. It's rewarding, don't get me wrong, but some days... Anyway, how's the teaching goin’? Still trying to get those Korean students to stop saying "very nice" to everything? Don’t even. It's like a linguistic virus. Everything is  very nice . The paper, the pens, the lesson, the rain outside.

Honestly, Sarah, I’m still feeling a bit…raw about it all. Fiona’s birthday party last weekend. It was lovely, of course, lovely seeing her so happy with Mark, but… watching them together, it just highlighted everything, didn't it? Highlighted what, love? You’ve been quiet about it all week. More quiet than usual, even. Don’t bottle things up, you know. Spill. Just… the ease of it all. They just  fit . Fifteen years, and still that spark, that… certainty. It’s a world away from the messiness of blended families, isn't it? I mean, Ben's getting on so well with Lily, most of the time. Truly. But Leo… Leo still gives me grief about Mark being "not his dad." Even after three years. Three years is a long time, Ange. He’s still little, though. That’s a big concept for a five-year-old to grasp, isn't it? The difference between someone who feeds you and cuddles you, and someone who  is  your dad. All kids react differently. Don’t beat yourself up about it. Mark’s doing a good job, I think. He tries, doesn’t he? Genuinely tries. He does, he really does. And I appreciate it. It's just... sometimes I wonder if I’m expecting too much. Of him, of Leo, of everything. I keep thinking I should be further along, you know? Less doubting, more…smooth sailing. It's exhausting, that mental to-do list. Smooth sailing? Ange, relationships  are  messy. All of them. Even Fiona and Mark - I bet they've had their share of bumps. You just don't see it from the outside. And blenders… well, they’re turbulence city, aren’t they? It’s admirable that you're even trying to navigate it. Most people wouldn't stick it out. It's not just Leo, either. It's… me, I think. It's the guilt. Part of me feels like I'm constantly trying to prove myself. To Ben, to Leo, to Mark… as if I need to earn my place. Like I’m an interloper. A slightly older, slightly more wrinkled interloper. Ange! Don’t talk like that. You  belong . You’re Ben’s partner, you’re a fantastic mum to Leo - even when he's being a miniature terror - and you bring so much joy to Mark’s life. Have you ever considered talking to someone about this, just a few sessions?

Honestly, Mark, you wouldn’t believe the deep dive I’ve been on. Pinterest, yeah? I thought it was just for, like, wedding decorations and pastel-coloured nurseries. Turns out, it's an anthropological goldmine. Right, because researching audience engagement with consumer trends using fabric swatches is  totally  essential for a Research Manager. Don’t undersell it, Liv. Anthropology of home decor, eh? Sounds fascinating. More fascinating than my attempts to explain quantum entanglement to my nan, at least. Aye, well, it's a bit more involved than that. I’m trying to map out seemingly random trends – like a sudden resurgence of macrame planters, or the obsession with mushroom core – and see what's driving them. There’s this real yearning for… grounding, I reckon. Like people are desperate to reconnect with something real, something tangible, amidst all this digital madness. Mushroom core? Seriously? What  is  mushroom core? Is that like, wearing fungi patterns and growing your own chanterelles? It’s… a vibe. Think earthy tones, textures, natural forms. Mushrooms are a recurring motif. It’s all over the place. It's linked, apparently, to a wider interest in foraging and sustainable living. I’ve built a massive board, it’s properly chaotic. You’d laugh. All those beige things. Sounds… intense. It wouldn't surprise me, though. Everything’s cyclical, isn't it? Remember when everyone was obsessed with mid-century modern furniture? Suddenly, it's vintage, retro, desirable. Exactly! But this feels different, somehow. This feels… deeper. Anyway, enough about my rabbit hole. How's the dissertation going? Still battling with the Schrödinger's cat paradox? Don't remind me. It's a beast. I'm starting to suspect my supervisor thinks I’m deliberately trying to confuse him. He keeps asking if I've considered “the inherent subjectivity of observable quantum states.” I just stare blankly and nod. Sounds about right. That’s proper academic speak, that is. Reminds me of that time Mrs. Davison tried to explain Shakespeare to our class. We were all just pretending to listen. Oh, Mrs. Davison! The terror of Year 9. Did she ever manage to get anyone to understand Hamlet? Nah. She mostly just got frustrated and told us to read more. Speaking of reading... Have you heard from Sarah and Liam? It’s Sarah’s birthday next week, isn’t it? Yeah, it is. I sent them a little something – a box of those posh chocolates from that shop near King's Parade.

Right, so this one’s… interesting. It’s a brass Art Deco fitting, apparently. Says it’s been ‘lovingly restored’. Loving restoration could mean anything, couldn’t it? Could mean it was covered in pigeon droppings and someone wiped it down. Let me see. Hmm, yeah, the photography’s not great, is it? Bit dark. And 'lovingly restored' is definitely code for ‘possibly held together with glue and wishful thinking’. How much are they asking? Fifty quid. Fifty quid for something that might fall apart the second I screw it in. I swear, eBay sellers are a law unto themselves. Remember that antique teapot we bought last year? Oh, the one with the chipped spout and the faintly unsettling floral pattern? How could I forget? We paid thirty pounds for that. Thirty pounds for floral distress, as I like to call it. Exactly! It's tempting, though, isn’t it? It would look  lovely  in the dining room. Something a bit more… glamorous than that awful plain thing we’ve got now. It does.
