But we’re trying to be sensible, remember? We’re saving for the deposit. I’ve just been having a look at Rightmove myself. Found a couple more that might be worth a closer look. Oh really? Let's have a peek. Anything even remotely near the budget? Because I'm starting to think we're going to end up in a damp caravan in Skegness. Okay, first one... two-bedroom semi in Chesham. Bit further out than we initially wanted, but the garden’s decent size. And it’s got a… garage. A proper garage, not one of those car-sized sheds. Chesham? Bit far for commuting, isn't it? What are the schools like? Apparently pretty good, according to the Ofsted report. It's £480,000. A little optimistic, maybe, but worth a look. Photos are… bright. Alarmingly bright. It’s giving me a headache. Good heavens, yes! They’ve clearly used every single bulb they could find. It looks like a dentist’s waiting room. Moving on then? Absolutely. Right, next one. This is in Amersham. Larger than Chesham, train station on the doorstep. Three-bedroom terrace. Listed at £525k. Ouch. That's already stretching things a bit. Let's see. Oh! This living room... it’s got… exposed brick? I know! I thought the same. It could be quite cosy. Bit trendy for us though, perhaps?

Honestly, Doreen, this rain is relentless. Feels like it’s been drizzling for weeks. Makes you want to just wrap up in a blanket and never leave the house. Tell me about it, love. I was walking Percy this morning, and I swear I was battling a small river down Willow Way. That poor dog looked like a drowned rat. Sorry I’m late! The bus was a nightmare. Seems like everyone decided to brave the weather this morning. Percy got soaked, then? Dreadfully. He’s currently attempting to dry himself on the sofa. Don't tell him I said that, mind. He's got a sensitive soul, that one. You and that dog! Honestly, Doreen, you treat him better than some of your relatives. Don't you go starting that now, Carol. He's good company, isn't he? Unlike some. So, what's been happening with you? Still having trouble with Mrs. Hawthorne? She was being particularly difficult last week, wasn’t she? Oh, you have no idea. She decided she didn't like the brand of incontinence pads I was using. Said they "felt scratchy." I mean, honestly! I had to run to Boots and get a different box, all because of a bit of a diva fit. Seriously? Some people, eh? You’d think they’d appreciate you looking after them. It's not always about appreciation, is it? Sometimes it’s just about control, I think. Anyway, the worst part is, now all the other families are asking for the ‘nicer’ pads. Expect I'll be running to Boots every week! You deserve a medal, you do. It’s hard work, caring for people, especially when they're… demanding. Remember old Mr. Peterson? Used to complain about the temperature of his tea  every single time . Oh yeah! I heard about that! My Auntie Maureen used to say he was a right grump. Are you still looking at those houses in Paddock Wood, Carol? I am, yes. Found a little bungalow last week. Three bedrooms, decent-sized garden… but the kitchen is truly awful. Orange cupboards, lime green worktops… it’s a crime against good taste. Oh, bless. You could always knock down the kitchen and put in your own. Easier said than done, Doreen. The mortgage is already stretched as it is. And the estate agent said the asking price is ‘firm’. You know how they are.

Honestly, this is fantastic. You really nailed the bake this time, love. Much better than that attempt last month with the sunken middle. Don't remind me! That was a disaster. I think I over-proofed it, didn't I? Right, well, I’m glad you're enjoying it. I was reading this really interesting article this morning, about sleep. Apparently, it’s not just about hours, but the  quality  of those hours. They've done research showing that even a slight increase in core body temperature before bed can disrupt things. Sleep, eh? I could definitely use some improvement there. The kids are keeping me up with all their after-school activities. Balancing that with the business... it's a constant juggle. What were the key takeaways? Well, it mentioned things like a cool room – obviously. But also, avoiding blue light an hour before bed, and… this was a surprising one – eating a small portion of complex carbohydrates, like whole grains,  before  bed. Apparently, they help regulate melatonin production. So, ditch the late-night cheese and crackers and opt for a bit of wholewheat toast instead? Sounds… sensible, actually. Though it requires some discipline, doesn't it? I'm a creature of habit. It does. But apparently, it works! Anyway, it got me thinking about our camping trip next month. We absolutely need to make sure we're setting up camp in a spot that won't leave us sweltering. Away from direct sunlight in the afternoon, preferably. Good point. I was picturing that idyllic spot near the river… but we’ll need to check the sun’s trajectory. Right, so, camping. You know, I was thinking about that time we got completely lost in Barcelona? Remember? Trying to find that little tapas bar near Las Ramblas? Oh, don't remind me! We were wandering around for  hours . I was convinced we were going to end up sleeping on a park bench. Your sense of direction is… let's say, “optimistic.” Hey! It could have been worse. At least we saw some interesting architecture while we were hopelessly turned around! I think the problem was relying on that phone map. It kept updating, shuffling the streets around. That’s the thing with city maps, isn't it? They're utterly useless unless you know the area. I much prefer a good old-fashioned paper map. You can actually  see  the layout of the city.

Right, so, this tiny wee thing… honestly, it's like a furry little potato with eyes. I'm proper chuffed wi' Pip. Pip? You named your hamster Pip? That's… quaint. And a potato, really? You’re being dramatic, Maisie. Dramatic? Nay, I’m being honest! It's round, it's small, and it mostly just sits there lookin’ at me. Proper funny, though. Spent an hour this morning tryin' to get it to run on its wheel. Just stared at it. Then had a good chew on the bar. Aw, that's dead cute! Hamsters are brilliant, aren't they? I had a wee one when I was a bairn, called Buttons. Kept escapin’ his cage. Absolute menace. Buttons, eh? My gran had a hamster called Sooty. Used to hide all its food in its cheek pouches and then try and stuff it all in the water bottle. Disaster. See! They’re natural comedians, these little fellas. But tellin' you, gettin’ Pip into his cage after a play is a proper ordeal. He treats it like a personal insult. I even tried bribin’ him with a sunflower seed. Didn’t work. Maybe you're approaching it wrong. Try gently scooping him up, Maisie. Don't make it a big deal. I’ve tried, love! Gently scooping just results in miniature hamster lunging and teeth nibbling. It's not pleasant, let me tell ya. It's like havin' a tiny, fluffy ninja. You could try a cardboard tube. They love those! Buttons used to spend ages running through and buildin’ little nests inside. Aye, tubes are good. Or a little hamster hammock. They love napping in those. Keeps 'em outta trouble, a bit. Hammock, you say? I might give that a go. Though I reckon he'd just use it as a catapult to launch himself outta the cage. Still, worth a try. Speaking of leaps… did yous see that bloke down the shop? The ginger one? The ginger one? You mean Dave? What about him? He's always down the shop. Aye, Dave. He looked proper flustered today. Like he'd lost his keys or somethin'. An’ his hair was even more… ginger-y than usual. It was practically glowin’. Dave? He's always flustered! He’s got a face like a slapped trout most days. And that hair, honestly. Like a sunset after a particularly dodgy curry. Aye, he's a character, alright.

Right, okay. So, Genghis Khan’s horde is  completely  wiped out. Thanks, Dad. You just obliterated my entire eastern front. Can’t help it, lad. Strategic brilliance, that's what I’ve got. Always have. Liverpool taught me how to see the angles. Besides, you were expanding too fast. Remember what I told you about overextension? Honestly, you two. It’s like listening to a military briefing. And all over a plastic board game! I’m just making some more tea, does anyone want chocolate digestives? The smell alone is making me feel younger. Chocolate digestives sound amazing, Mum. Please! And Dad, lay off the strategic brilliance for five minutes. It's Risk, not a UN peace summit. Just teaching you a thing or two, that’s all. You'll thank me when you're negotiating a deal with a dodgy supplier in Hong Kong. Speaking of dodgy, did you ever find those maps Aaron lent you? The ones for that charity thing? Nope. Think he might have mixed them up with his…recording equipment. Trying to set up that new update for his podcast, wasn't he? Keeps going on about mastering lossless audio. All over my head, really. Aaron’s always been a bit of a tech head. Remember when he tried to build his own drone? It promptly flew into Mrs. Higgins’ prize-winning roses. Good times. Still, a clever lad. Shame about the parties though. Remember ANON’s 21st? Nearly got arrested. Good thing his mum stepped in. Don’t remind me. I spent the entire night trying to keep Sarah from dancing on the table. Speaking of keeping an eye on things… Mum, you haven’t seen my glasses anywhere, have you? I think I left them somewhere earlier. Let me have a look. They're probably perched on your head. You always do that. Right, not there. I'll check the living room. Now, back to the Mongol hordes... It’s your turn, dear. Don’t get too cocky, though. You had terrible luck last Christmas when we played. Terrible luck? I nearly conquered the world! It was a close call. This game is rigged, honestly. Rigged? It's down to skill, son, not luck. Though a bit of both doesn’t go amiss. You know, reminds me of when I was your age, used to gamble on the horses down at the docks. Risk, just with real money.

Honestly, Maisie, I'm feeling proper dodgy about this whole uni thing. Like, am I even cut out for it? Everyone else seems to have their lives sorted, networking like mad and getting internships. I’m still struggling to remember what module is on Mondays. Don’t be daft, Liv! You’re brilliant. You just… process things differently. Remember how you nailed that history essay? The one on the smuggling trade in Cornwall? Dr. Harding practically drooled over it. Yeah, that was a fluke, innit? I just got lucky with the topic. I feel like I should be further along. All those sixth form careers advisors telling me I’d be a 'natural leader'… well, I'm leading nobody but a mountain of overdue library books. They always say that, don’t they? My careers advisor suggested I be a professional pigeon racer. Said I had the ‘right commitment’. Lancaster’s not exactly brimming with pigeons though, is it? Oh, stop it! So, what about you? You seem so determined. Still set on journalism? Yeah, mostly. Though... I was reading this article about AI and how it's going to decimate the industry. Apparently, robots are gonna be writing the news in five years. Robots writing news? Blimey. That  is  a bit scary. What'll you do then? Become a pigeon racer? Don't you dare! I'm kidding. Maybe copywriter. Or social media manager. Something where I can still be creative, but not entirely at the mercy of algorithms and sentient machines. Have you thought about what you might do if… well, if uni doesn't quite click? I've had a few ideas, haven’t I? Remember I was looking at that pottery course down in St. Ives? Proper idyllic, all whitewashed studios and sea views. That  does  sound lovely. A bit far from Liverpool though, doesn't it? Your mum would have a fit. All that way out west… She’d probably love it. She's always gone on about wanting me to 'find my inner peace' and all that. Though, I haven’t a clue how to make money out of pottery. Unless I start making miniature Cornish pasties and selling them to tourists. Now  that ’s an idea. "Hand-crafted Cornish pasties, made with love and clay!" Don't encourage me! Right, changing the subject before I commit to a career in miniature pastry sculpting.

Ugh, this project is brutal. Honestly, Mr. Davies expects us to summarise  everything  about the industrial revolution. Everything! It's like he wants us to write a novel. Tell me about it. I spent, like, three hours last night just trying to understand why people moved from the countryside. It’s just... depressing, innit? All that poverty and factory work. Depressing is an understatement. My grandad used to talk about his dad working in a textile mill. Twelve hours a day, six days a week, earning barely enough to feed the family. It’s hard to imagine now. My mum's been showing me old photos. Black and white, all smoggy. Wembley used to be… different, apparently. Less shiny. You know, less… everything. Definitely. I was reading about child labour the other day. Kids, like eight years old, crawling under machines fixing broken threads. It just doesn't sit right. No. It really doesn't. Sometimes I wonder why governments don’t do more, you know? Like, about poverty, generally. It’s not like we’re asking for mansions. Just… a fair shot, I guess. Exactly! It's easy for them, isn't it? Sitting in Parliament, talking about targets and indicators. They don't see the reality. Remember that article we read in  The Guardian  about the food bank usage increasing? It's crazy. Yeah. It makes you think, doesn’t it? All these companies selling stuff we don't need, and people are struggling to buy food. Consumerism gone mad. Totally. Speaking of mad, did you see that article about the CERN scientists smashing atoms together again? Apparently, they're building a bigger machine? The Large Hadron Collider? Yeah! My cousin's really into particle physics. He keeps trying to explain it to me, but it ends up sounding like gibberish. Something about quarks and… antimatter? Exactly! It's mind-boggling. But it's also kind of amazing, isn't it? Trying to unravel the universe's secrets. It's definitely a more productive use of money than, say, buying another sports car. You’re reading my mind. Although, a limited edition Batman car  would  be pretty cool. Have you seen the new Batman comic? The one with the Court of Owls? Oh my god, yes! It's incredible! The artwork is stunning, and the storyline is so dark and twisty. It’s way better than the last one.

Honestly, darling, this chair is a godsend. My knees are protesting something fierce today. Seems like the damp's got right into them. Yeah, it’s been awful weather lately. Feels like it’s been raining non-stop for weeks. My joints are aching too, though not as bad as yours, I reckon. "Not as bad as mine," you say. You’re a spring chicken, still! I’m… well, I’m approaching that age where every movement is a negotiation with my body. Physiotherapy's helping a bit, the exercises are tedious though. I’m supposed to be doing them twice a day. Be honest, are you doing yours? I try. Some days it's just… hard, you know? Makes me feel a bit pathetic, really. Like I'm failing at rehab. Nonsense. It  is  hard. Don't be ridiculous. It takes discipline, and you’re having a tough time as it is. Remember what the physio said – consistency is more important than intensity. Little and often. Besides, you’ve got bigger things on your mind. How’s the recording going? You were so excited about that last week. It's... complicated. The engineer - Mark - is brilliant, absolutely brilliant, but… it’s exposed. I’m singing, alone, in a small room, and every little thing, the breath, the wobble… it's all there. It feels so vulnerable. That’s how it should feel, darling. Honesty is beautiful. Think of it as shedding a layer - a layer of pretense, of trying to be something you’re not. Let your true voice shine through. And Mark’s a professional, he knows how to capture that. What are you working on at the moment? I’m trying to record ‘Hallelujah’. Leonard Cohen’s version. It’s… daunting. Everyone's done it. I’m terrified it will sound like a pale imitation. Well, you’re not everyone. You have your own interpretation, your own feeling. And remember, even Cohen himself said the song wrote  him  as much as he wrote it. Honestly, you have a lovely, distinctive voice. Don't let stage fright - or anything else - steal it from you. Speaking of stealing… have you seen Mrs. Higgins lately? She’s been peering over the fence again, trying to film my hydrangea cuttings! Absolutely scandalous woman. Mrs. Higgins. Always something with her. Remember when she tried to complain about the colour of my curtains? Said they were 'distracting' her prize-winning petunias.

Right then, nearly there! Smells proper good, doesn’t it? I reckon even yer fussy Aunt Brenda would like this one. It's a proper Lancashire hotpot, mind, not that posh stuff you get in fancy restaurants. It does smell amazing, honestly. Better than anything I could ever conjure up in my tiny kitchen. Brenda? Seriously? You’re banking on Brenda liking something? She critiqued the font on my Christmas card last year. Aye, well, she’s a character, isn’t she? But deep down, beneath all that… Brenda-ness, she loves a good bit of proper food. Comfort food, like this. I had a right nostalgia trip making it, thinking back to Gran's kitchen. You wouldn’t believe the size of her oven – fit a small car in there, it did. A car? That’s a bit dramatic, surely? So, what else did Gran make? Just hotpot and Yorkshire puddings, or was she a culinary wizard? Oh, she were a wizard, alright. She could turn leftovers into feasts. Stottie cakes, parkin… she always had something baking. Used to make this amazing rhubarb crumble, with proper tang to it. It’s a lost art, I reckon. Everyone buys shop-bought crumble now. Shame, that is. You should try and recreate it! I'd definitely devour a plate of that. I’ve been trying to get better at baking, but it’s so frustrating. My attempts at sourdough look like volcanic rock, and I nearly set off the smoke alarm trying to make a Victoria sponge. See, that’s where you’re going wrong! You’re thinking too much. Baking's about feel, not science, darlin’. Gran used to say, "If it looks right, it tastes right." And usually, she were spot on. Less measuring, more… intuition. Intuition? That’s terrifying. My postgraduate degree practically brainwashed me into thinking everything had to be precise measurements and controlled variables. I'm trying to loosen up, y'know? Life’s too short to worry about exactly 235 grams of flour. That's exactly what I'm saying! Stressing yourself out over a sponge cake? Honestly. Look, I’ll give you a few of Gran's secrets sometime. She had a knack for knowing when the dough was just right, even without a thermometer. It’s in the fingertips, love. I'd appreciate that. It would be nice to make something decent for once, instead of just ordering takeout.

Right, so, Netflix is suggesting “Anyone But You” to me again. Honestly, it's relentless. Have any of you actually  watched  it? Yeah, I did! Ages ago, though. It wasn't… awful. Silly, definitely silly, but I found it quite entertaining. Properly cheesy rom-com vibes, innit? Like, peak early 2000s stuff. Rom-coms aren’t really my thing, to be fair. Give me a good action flick any day. Just saw "The Beekeeper" last night. Good bit of mindless fun. Lots of explosions. Explosions aren’t exactly cinematic, are they, Conor? I mean, it's adrenaline-pumping, sure, but is it  good ? I caught a bit of "Poor Things" the other week - that was something else. The visuals were incredible. And Emma Stone’s performance… wow. "Poor Things!" My mum watched it! She said it was a bit weird but brilliant. She made me promise not to watch it until I’m, like, seventeen, but I’m going to sneak a peek. Is it really, really weird? Like, alien weird? Not  alien  weird, Millie. Just… unconventional. It’s Victorian but also, very much not. There's a lot to unpack, but it's worth it. And Emma Stone's prosthetics are insane! They do a really good job. See, that sounds interesting. Rom-coms are just…predictable. Though, I do like a good predictable rom-com sometimes, don't I? Just for a bit of brain-off time. What about something a bit older then? Anyone seen "Princess Bride" recently? It always hits the spot. Oh my god, "Princess Bride"! Classic. Cary Elwes and Robin Wright are gorgeous. And Mandy Patinkin as Inigo Montoya? Iconic. “My name is Inigo Montoya. You killed my father. Prepare to die.” Perfection. I remember my wee cousin being obsessed with that film. He’d make me recite the whole “Inigo Montoya” bit. Annoying at the time, but it is a good film. It's clever too, you know? It's poking fun at fairytale tropes, while still being a really charming love story. So much wit. Have you lot seen "Paddington 2"? It’s  surprisingly  brilliant. My friend swore it wasn’t for me, but it was genuinely one of the most heartwarming films I’ve seen in ages. And Hugh Grant is hilarious in it. Paddington! I love Paddington! The marmalade sandwiches! He's so cute! Do you think "Poor Things" has marmalade sandwiches?

Oh my god, I need a cup of tea. Paris was… a lot. My feet are killing me. Seriously, I think I’ve developed permanent plantar fasciitis. Plantar what-now? You sound like you’re trying to win a medical jargon competition. Let me guess, you walked miles in those ridiculous shoes you insisted on taking? They were cute! And they were on offer. Besides, everyone walks in Paris. It's part of the experience! And yes, my feet are paying the price. I think I might have actually hobbled up the Eiffel Tower. You look like you’ve been through a warzone! Paris, eh? How was it? Did you manage to see everything on your list? Everything except the Picasso museum, sadly. We ran out of time. And I spent a good hour nursing a blister the size of a fifty pence piece. Honestly, it was beautiful, the food was incredible, but… exhausting. Liam kept trying to drag me to vintage clothing stores. Liam’s always been a magpie for shiny things and old clothes. He’ll fill his flat with bric-a-brac one day, mark my words. So, tell me properly, love, what happened to your foot? You were limping something awful when you came through the door. Well, it started mildly on Saturday, like a dull ache. Then, after traipsing around Montmartre for hours, it just… escalated. I think I twisted it as well. It’s throbbing now, and I’ve got a giant plaster on it. Doctor's appointment booked for tomorrow, just to be sure. Oh, that's awful! Maybe some ice and elevation? And a really good cuppa. Speaking of which, Mum, are you making a roast? I'm starving and the ward was chaotic today. Needed something hearty after dealing with…well, you wouldn't want to hear about it. Probably not, dear. No, not a roast. Just a simple chicken and veg. Need to keep things light after yesterday's drama with the oven. Remember that, darling? The pilot light went out and nearly set off the smoke alarm. Honestly, you wouldn’t believe the look on the neighbour’s face when I was waving a tea towel out the window trying to fan the smoke away! Oh god, that sounds terrifying. Nearly setting the house on fire trying to resuscitate a pilot light? Only you, Mum. It’s a wonder you haven’t burned the kitchen down already.

"Hey, Chloe! Fancy seeing you here. About to brave another Monday morning, huh?" "Liam! Hey! Yeah, definitely. Monday mornings hit different, don't they? Just grabbing a caffeine kickstart before I head to my supervisor meeting. You teaching your grammar class already?" "Not for another hour. Just needed a coffee and a five-minute breather. How was your weekend? Did you manage to escape Brighton for a bit?" "Actually, yeah! Mum and Dad dragged us all down to Chichester. It’s always a bit… quaint, isn’t it? All those antique shops. They’re obsessed with it. My little brother, Finn, mostly just wanted to chase pigeons. You ever been?" "I have, once. Years ago. It's pretty charming, I’ll give it that. My family's from Bedford, so we usually just stick to that area. Bit less…historical, let's say.” He chuckles. “Though our history is mostly just pubs and rugby. What about you? Croydon born and bred, right?" “Yep! Croydon girl through and through. Not much historical significance there either, mostly just concrete and shops, though it’s getting a lot of new development now. Still, wouldn’t swap it. But Chichester… Mum’s talking about moving down there eventually, which would be a nightmare. I’d barely see anyone." She sighs theatrically. "Work's been mad busy, you know? Dealing with staffing shortages and everything. Being a supervisor is...something." "Tell me about it! I'm wading through a mountain of student essays on passives. Honestly, some of them treat 'was/were + past participle' like a completely alien concept. It’s fascinating, but exhausting. I was reading a bit about the British National Corpus the other day, just for fun, trying to see how frequently passives are actually used in spoken English vs. academic writing. Mind-blowing stuff." "You and your linguistics! You're always diving deep into that stuff. I did linguistics as part of my undergrad, ages ago. Found it fascinating at the time, but retail management has a certain… practical appeal, you know? Pays the bills. Though, that payday can't come fast enough this month. Tuition fees still haunting me, as ever." "Right? Student loans are a life sentence, aren't they? I'm trying to chip away at mine, but it's slow going. I'm actually thinking of taking on some extra TEFL tuition online to boost the funds.

Right, so, like, you just… chuck it in? Seems a bit… easy. It always ends up either rock hard or like, gloopy mush. Dad’s always complaining. No, love, there’s a bit more to it than that. It’s not  rocket science , but it needs a little care. See, you’ve got to rinse it first. That gets rid of the excess starch, stops it going gluey. Rinse it? Why didn’t anyone tell me that before? It’s in the instructions, isn't it? I never read the instructions. Too boring. Most people don’t, do they? . It's right here on the pack. See? "Rinse under cold water until the water runs clear." Right, let's do that. Like that. A good few times. Now, that’s better. Okay, okay. So, then what? Bit of water? How much? I always put too much in. Remember that time I made enough rice for a small army? I do! We practically lived on rice and beans for a week. Don’t do that again! For this amount, a good rule of thumb is twice the volume of rice in water. So, if you’ve got, say, one cup of rice, use two cups of water. It’s the perfect ratio. Two cups… got it. Now do I put the lid on? Mom always has some weird thing about lids. Yes, lid on tight. That’s crucial. It steams the rice perfectly. And you don’t lift it! I know it’s tempting, but you lose all the steam and it won’t cook properly. Patience, love, patience. While that's bubbling away, I’ll chop up some of this bell pepper for the curry. Fancy a vindaloo tonight, or something milder? Ooh, vindaloo! As long as it’s not  too  spicy. Last time you made one, I was practically breathing fire. Remember how red my face got? I remember! You looked like a tomato. Honestly, you've got a fantastic tolerance for heat though. You're like a jalapeno-eating machine. I try to be. Speaking of spicy, saw a thing online about this jelly fish… apparently, some kinds are eaten as a delicacy. Like a spicy noodle dish, but with jelly fish! Jellyfish? Blimey! That’s… unconventional. I can’t imagine that’s ever going to be on my menu, though. Bit too adventurous for me. I’d rather stick to the classics.

Right then. Another Tuesday night. Fish fingers and beans. Luxury dining, this is. Don’t be dramatic, Liam. Mum put a bit of effort in, didn't she? Proper mushy peas this week, too. It's what we do, isn’t it? Though I'm properly skint this month. Bills are mad. Seriously considering switching to the cheap supermarket brand of everything. Even the toilet roll. Can you imagine? You are? That’s rough, Chloe. My student loan doesn't even cover rent and textbooks, let alone anything fancy. Mum’s been helping out a bit, but…well, you know. Student loan. A grand waste of money, if you ask me. All that essay-writing and lectures. Waste o' time. Should’ve just got a trade. Bricklaying, maybe. Stable job, good money... Oh, here we go. The bricklaying lecture again. Liam, you applied for three bricklaying apprenticeships last year and didn't even turn up for the interviews! That's beside the point, Bethany. They weren't good apprenticeships, were they? They wanted you to start at five in the bleedin' morning! Who wants to be up at five? Honestly, you’re impossible. Chloe's right though, Liam. You need  something . You've been moaning about being bored for months. The job centre keeps ringing… The job centre! Right. Lovely lot, them. Offered me a job stacking shelves at Tesco. Stacking shelves, Chloe! Like I’m some kind of robot. I’ve got a degree, haven’t I? History, for goodness sake! It's frustrating, though, isn't it? Having all that education and feeling like it's useless. I'm considering dropping out, honestly. It’s just…overwhelming. All the pressure to get good grades, find the perfect job… Don't you dare, Freya! You’re brilliant at your course! You love journalism. Remember how you were practically bouncing off the walls after that interview with the local newspaper? That was ages ago, Bethany. And it was just a work experience thing. It's different trying to  make  a career out of it. My German’s not even that good anymore. I haven’t practised in ages. You'll be fine. You always are. Remember that time you tried to bake a cake for Grandma's birthday and it ended up looking like a collapsed volcano? You still managed to charm her with it. Aye, volcano cake was a classic.

Cor, this gravy’s reet good, Anon. You've really outdone yerself tonight. Proper hearty, it is. It’s…fine. Bit rich for me, though. My stomach’s been playing up a bit, you know. Aye, well, everyone's stomach plays up now and then. You need to get yourself movin', though, Liam. Sitting about all day isn’t doin’ you any favours. Remember what the doctor said? I know, I know. Exercise. Easy for you to say, Miss Event Co-ordinator, striding about all day organising fancy dos. Me? I sit. I watch the telly. It’s easy, innit? It’s not a fancy do, Liam, it’s work. Hard work! And I'm not exactly 'striding about' all the time. There's loads of emails, spreadsheets, liasing... it’s more stressful than it looks, honestly. Still, at least I'm  doing  something. And you could be doing something too. Even just a little walk around the block. A walk? In this weather? Last time I went out, it rained. I came back soaked. It was a disaster. Honestly, Liam. You’re like a cat. You’ll only venture out when the sun’s shining and you've got a saucer of cream waiting for you. Anon, are you gonna finish your carrots? I like a bit of colour on my plate. Anon: Help yourself, Maisie. So, you were telling me about the conference next month? The one in York? Aye, it's a doozy. Big pharmaceutical company, loads of important folks. I’ve got to make sure everything runs like clockwork – catering, AV, transport… the whole shebang. It's a right handful. Trying to find a venue with enough parking that accommodates coaches and disability access… it’s a nightmare, but I’m slowly getting there. I even managed to get a decent rate at the Principal Hotel. Usually, they’re bleedin’ extortionate. Sounds stressful. You work too hard, you do. Someone’s gotta do it. Though, I wouldn’t mind someone offering to pay me double, that’s for sure. Keeps me on my toes, though, doesn't it? It's good to be challenged. Keeps the boredom at bay. Unlike some people I know... Oi! I’m not bored! I… I enjoy my peace and quiet. And watching Bargain Hunt. It’s intellectually stimulating, you know. Right you are, Liam. Intellectually stimulating. Listen, I’ve been thinking, you should try that walking group Anon mentioned.

Right, lads, that was a lovely dinner, wasn't it? Shame it’s over already. Anyone else for pudding? Nah, I'm stuffed, Mum. That lasagne was brilliant though. Seriously, can we have it again next week? We absolutely can, love. Your dad certainly put his heart into it. Didn’t you, darling? Had to, didn’t I? Someone’s gotta feed you all. I’m still buzzing from that game of tennis earlier. You boys were putting up a good fight. Nearly beat you, Dad! Just a few silly mistakes. A few? You gifted me three easy points! Still, you're getting quicker. You've got potential, Liam. Maybe you should join the club down the road. He's too busy glued to his phone, isn’t he? Speaking of which, what were you looking at on Instagram just now? You were giggling like mad. Just… stuff, Mum. Funny videos. "Stuff"? Come on, let's have a look. Is it more of that ridiculous dancing stuff? No! It's… it's just memes. And this guy, he's got, like, the best moustache. Seriously. It’s like a handlebar meets a walrus. A walrus? Alright, lad. A bit dramatic, isn't it? I quite like a good moustache myself. Reminds me of… well, you know. Who, Dad? Hitler? Don’t say that! Whoa, hold on! Just saying, some of those old photos – proper impressive facial hair. It's history, lads, not an endorsement. Don’t get your knickers in a twist. It’s just… historical. Michael! Perhaps not the best comparison, darling. Especially with teenage boys present. Although, I do think a well-groomed moustache can look quite dashing. Your grandfather could rock one. My mate’s got a little bit of stubble growing in. He's trying to grow a beard but it’s patchy. It’s a bit embarrassing, actually. Don’t laugh, Liam! It takes time to grow a decent beard. I'm thinking about trying one next year. Oh, really, are you? At fifteen? You'll look like a grumpy old man! It’ll be cool! All the older lads at school have beards. Well, it’s not just about having facial hair, is it? It’s about having something to  do  with it. Grooming, shaping… it takes dedication. Like growing a decent tennis serve. Did you see Chloe posted a new picture? She looks amazing.

Aye, this is alright, innit? Nice to be heading back towards Macclesfield. Feel a bit more… settled than Stockport sometimes, even though I’ve lived there near on twenty years now. Yeah, it is nice. Though, you know, I'm still a bit stressed about this furniture situation. Mum’s going mental about it. Oh, tha knows she will. Fancy spending that much on a sofa and a table, though! Near on a grand, she said? It's a really nice set, though. Modern. And ours is practically falling apart. Remember that time the leg fell off during Christmas dinner? How could I forget? Your grandad nearly cleared the entire table trying to stop it! Speaking of grandad… is he alright? Last time I spoke to him he was moaning about Maureen and her blasted jam. Maureen makes a  lovely  jam, Doreen! You’re just being picky. And I’m perfectly alright, thank you very much. Though this journey is a bit bouncy for me today, my hip’s acting up. Sorry, love. Can’t be helped, can it? Just need to get you to the house and give you a sit down with a cuppa. Right, so the furniture. Don’t be buying owt you can't afford, love. Remember when your Auntie Carol got that rosewood cabinet? Sat in the hallway for ten years, gathering dust! I know, I know. Mum's got her eye on it though. And she's convinced she’ll have space for it. She’s been moving things around already. I bet she'll clear out the loft, or something. It’s always a drama. We'll have to book a tip run, won't we? All that old junk... Aye, the tip's chocka full these days. Young people just throwin' owt. Speaking of throwin' owt, did you ever hear back from ANON about her friend’s family? They were wanting to get rid of that load of old porcelain figures, weren’t they? I messaged her, yeah. She said her friend’s sorting through a load of stuff after her partner got ill. Apparently, things are rough for them. It’s awful, isn’t it? Dementia’s a cruel thing. Aye, it is. Terrible. My dear old friend Elsie, lived down the road, she went through it. Heartbreaking for the family. No one should have to watch their loved ones fade like that.

Honestly, Mum, I'm feeling utterly drained. This whole redundancy thing at work is… a lot. They’re dragging it out, you know? Saying they’re ‘exploring all options’ which basically means they're quietly letting me go and stringing me along. Now, now, love, don't you get yourself all worked up. Stress ain't good for you. Exploring all options, they call it. Sounds like fancy speak for “waiting to see if someone else will take the fall.” Happens all the time. At the school, we had that situation with Mr. Davies… remember? Bit of a nightmare, that was. Yeah, but this feels different. It's not like there's another job lined up. I've been applying everywhere, of course, but…it's the uncertainty that’s killing me. What if I can’t find anything? I was just starting to feel like I was really getting somewhere with the project coordination. You're a clever girl, you will. You always have been. Remind me again, how many applications have you sent out this week? And are you keeping up with the gym? A bit of exercise always helps clear the head. I’ve been meaning to get back to my morning walks, you know, since the dodgy knee's settled down a bit. Need to build up some strength again. Probably about thirty, I think. It's exhausting! And the gym… I went yesterday, but honestly, the thought of going again this week feels like climbing Everest. I just want to curl up with a box set and a family-sized bag of crisps. Oh, you and your crisps! You do need to watch that, love. All those ready salts – proper bad for you. Remember what your Grandad used to say? "A little bit of what you fancy does you good, but a whole bag? That's just asking for trouble." He’d always have a bowl of fruit handy, you know. Apples, pears, that sort of thing. Didn't always eat 'em, mind. Preferred his biscuits! He did. God, I miss him. I should call Auntie Carol, I haven't spoken to her in ages. It's just…everything feels so overwhelming right now. I was thinking about that extension, too. We talked about it, and now…I don't know. How are we going to afford it if I'm not working? Hold your horses, love.

This is a bit bland, isn’t it, Mum? Sorry, love. I was trying a new recipe. Little Finn's been a bit fussy lately. He'll eat anything covered in gravy though, the little monkey. Finn's obsessed with Mick at the moment. Keeps shouting 'Mick! Mick!' all day. Can’t get away from it. He does love that programme, doesn't he? It's bright and silly. Better than some of that other rubbish they put on, honestly. Remember when you were little and you were obsessed with Bob the Builder? Yeah, but Mick’s singing is… repetitive. It’s just ‘Stick with Mick, stick with Mick!’ over and over. Well, that’s catchy, isn’t it? That’s what they  want . So, right. Summer holidays. We need a plan for the days. Apart from watching Mick, naturally. I was thinking we could try and get to the pool again. Remember last time? It was packed, though. Packed isn't putting it mildly. More like sardines in a tin. Still, the water was lovely. We could try going early, really early. Like, before anyone else even thinks about it. What about those Japanese lessons I wanted to do? The ones online? Oh, that’s a good idea! I know you’ve been saying you wanted to learn. It's so different to English, isn't it? I tried learning a bit once, years ago, but I couldn’t get my head around it. Just a load of squiggles. It’s actually really interesting. They have, like, three different writing systems. And the grammar is completely backwards. Backwards? Now you’re losing me! Right, well, you give it a go then. I’ll try and help, though I probably won't be much use. Perhaps we can do some together in the evenings after dinner? That would be cool. And I should practice guitar more too. I haven’t really touched it since school finished. That's true. You’ve been promising to practice, haven't you? Maybe we can have a little 'music time' after the Japanese? It would be nice to hear you play again. Maybe. But what about doing stuff  outside  the house? Like, actual activities. Well, there’s always the park. We could try the farmers’ market on Saturday. Finn loves looking at the vegetables, even if he doesn't eat them. And I saw a flyer for a nature walk thing, down by the estuary.

Cor, this is good, innit? Proper cinema popcorn. Beats the stuff you get at the flicks any day. Yeah, it is. Though, to be fair, they’ve stepped up their game a bit recently. Still not as good as homemade, mind. You makin' any of that posh salted caramel stuff you were on about last week? Posh? It’s just butter and sugar, lad! Don’t get yer knickers in a twist. And no, not today. Been buryin’ meself in this draft chapter, see? Need to finish it by the end of the week if I wanna get this submission in. Right, right, the writing. How's it goin'? Still stuck on the Victorian chimney sweep subplot? Tell me about it. He's meant to represent the societal decay, see? But he just keeps wanting to talk about his pigeons. Pigeons, Liam! Is that  really  societal decay? Pigeons represent resilience! They thrive in the harshest environments. Maybe he’s representative of the tenacity of the working class! Think about it. You’re makin’ that up. You're just trying to justify the pigeon obsession. Anyway, it's exhausting. I wish I could just switch off. Like, properly switch off and go on holiday. Remember that trip we talked about to Portugal? Ooh, yeah! Lisbon, right? Sun, sangria, and somewhere that doesn't involve chimney sweeps. We should actually book something. Me mum's been sayin' I need a break. Her dentist appointment drama’s been bringing me down. Dentist? What’s happened now? Apparently, she’s got one of them abscesses. Proper nasty. Been moaning about it all week. Poor lass. She's terrified. Said the dentist was lookin' at her like she’d committed a crime just for askin' about payment plans. Blimey. Dentists, eh? They’re all charlatans, aren't they? Tryin’ to bleed you dry. Makes you wish you could just learn to drill your own teeth. Don't even joke about that! You'd have your jaw all wonky. Anyway, forget the dentist. Portugal. We could try and get some tickets to that Massive Attack gig in Bristol while we're down that way? Massive Attack?! Are you serious? I’d be there in a heartbeat! We’d have to book quick though, wouldn’t we? Those tickets vanish faster than you can say "trip-hop". I'll have a look tonight. Whilst I'm on the internet, I'll see if any of the smaller bands we like are playing anywhere.

Right then, love. So, tell me everything. You’ve been practically buzzing with excitement since you called. New job settled in alright? Sutton Coldfield Primary – that’s a good school, isn't it? Proper catchment area, I heard. It is, Mum! It’s brilliant, actually. The kids are… well, they’re a handful, naturally, but they’re lovely. And the staff! Honestly, everyone’s been so welcoming. Mrs. Davies, the head, is fantastic. Really supportive. It’s just… exactly what I needed. A bit less chaotic than the training placements, that’s for sure. Still getting used to the marking, though. Mountains of it! Marking, eh? Never ends, does it? You always were a conscientious one. Remember when you were little and even your drawings had little neat labels underneath saying "by Lily, age 6"? Oh, God, don't remind me! My perfectionism’s probably going to be the death of me. But I’m enjoying it, Mum, genuinely. It feels… purposeful. It’s miles better than temping at that insurance firm. You know I hated that. Aye, you did. That looked like it was sucking the life right out of you. So, all that hard work paying off then, eh? You deserve it. Now, let's see… you said something about Easter cakes? Have you been baking? Trying to. I saw that Nigella Lawson recipe for hot cross buns, the one with the orange zest and cardamom… it looked so simple. It wasn’t. They ended up looking like misshapen footballs. Nigella’s a master of making things look easy on television, love. Don’t go blaming yourself! I can give you my recipe. It’s foolproof. My nan passed it down to me. Proper old-fashioned ones, studded with dried fruit and covered in a lovely, thick icing. Oh, please do! I'd love that. I was thinking I’d make some for the children at school, but I don't want them to think I can’t actually bake! Though, they'd probably be touched if they were... wonky. It might reinforce their artistic freedom, you know? Artistic freedom through misshapen baked goods? You're getting creative already, aren't you? So, are we still on for next Sunday, then? The Christening? Little Thomas is getting bigger every day! I can't believe it’s nearly here. Yes, definitely! Everything’s been sorted. Auntie Carol’s confirmed she’s flying in, which is a relief.

Your place is lovely, Anon. So much brighter than I remember! You’ve really made it your own. Feels very…Birmingham, doesn't it? Not quite the London I'm used to. Oh, thank you, love! It's taken a while, but I’m finally happy with it. London was… well, London. Too much hustle and bustle for me these days. Birmingham’s got a much nicer pace. And cheaper! You wouldn’t believe the price of postage in London. Still, it’s good to have you here. So, how’s Hertfordshire treating you? Still battling teenagers learning French? You have no idea. They’re a force of nature. Honestly, some days I think I’m teaching them more about sarcasm than the subjunctive. But there are moments, you know? When you see a lightbulb go on and they actually  get  something. Makes the endless corrections worthwhile. What about you? Still keeping them in line at the primary school? Oh, goodness yes. Seven-year-olds are just as challenging, but in a completely different way. Less sarcasm, more glitter and existential questions about why the sky is blue. I’m thinking about retiring actually, in the next few years. It's getting a bit much, the paperwork particularly. All the ‘safeguarding’ and ‘data protection’... it’s endless. Really? That’s massive! What would you do? Travel? Finally finish that quilt you were talking about? A bit of both, I think. I've got a caravan, rather old but she’s reliable. Planning to potter around the coast, see a bit more of Cornwall. And yes, the quilt is still very much a pile of fabric. My granddaughter, Maisie, keeps trying to "help”, which mostly involves adding sequins wherever possible. Sounds idyllic. Maisie sounds delightful. Is she still mad about cats? Remember her obsession with rescuing every stray in the neighbourhood? She is! Absolutely. Although her parents are getting a bit tired of it. Currently, she's petitioning for a rescue Siamese. Apparently, they’re "superior” to moggies. You know kids. Anyway, what about your little Leo? How's the furry tornado doing? He's… a handful. Utterly fantastic, but a handful. He's decided he's a guard dog now. Barks at the postman, the squirrels... even the delivery driver from the local bakery. It's quite entertaining, actually. I'm thinking of getting a dog behaviourist, though. He jumped on my mum’s lap the other day and nearly knocked her over!

Blimey, these are proper good, ANON. Seriously. Better than my Nan's, and she was a legend, honestly. Never could match her matzah balls. What's the secret, then? Don't be stingy with the details, yeah? Alright, alright, don't flatter me too much! It's mostly about the schmaltz, I reckon. Loads of schmaltz. And letting the flour rest, at least an hour. Don’t rush it. My great-aunt Miriam used to say, "Patience, darling, are the secret ingredient to everything good in life. Especially dumplings." She was a card, that one. Miriam was a force of nature. I remember her vividly from my school days. Always had a biscuit in her handbag, and a scandalous story to tell. Such a shame she's no longer with us. This is lovely, ANON. Truly. You’ve outdone yourself. Yeah, seriously. These are exceptional. Better than anything you get in that kosher deli on Brick Lane, too. And that's saying something. Speaking of Brick Lane, are you guys planning on hitting up Beigel Bake afterwards? I'm feeling a salt beef bagel desperately. Don’t need to ask me twice. Need to carb-load after all these helpings! But hold on, ANON, you mentioned something earlier about your mum’s recipe for charoset? The one with the dried apricots? I could murder that. It's not  my  mum’s. It’s my grandma’s, Bubbe Rose’s, recipe. She brought it over from New York back in the fifties. Absolutely crucial ingredient is proper Iranian dried apricots – they're just more…vibrant, you know? Brings out a depth of flavour. I’ll send you the scribbled-on card, it’s a mess, I’m warning you. Probably covered in flour. New York… I was just thinking about the Met. I haven’t been in years. I really must. It’s terribly evocative, isn’t it? All those old families, the history… It reminds me of this film, "Husbands and Wives," by Woody Allen – so brilliantly observed. Have you seen it, FINN? Can’t say I have. Woody Allen’s not really my thing, to be honest. Give me something more… technical. Like "Arrival." That film messes with your head in the best possible way. It’s about linguistics, actually. Amazing how they used the Hebrew root system to represent the language of the aliens. Hebrew, eh? Don’t go getting all clever on me, FINN.

Honestly, Sarah, “Bridgerton” is just… froth. Utter froth. I mean, the costumes are lovely, don’t get me wrong, but the plot! It's thinner than a single ply yarn. And the historical inaccuracies! I spent half the time thinking, “They wouldn’t  dare  do that in Regency England!” Oh, come on, Eleanor! It's a bit of escapism, innit? Not everything needs to be historically accurate. It’s meant to be a bit of fun. Besides, George loves it. And if George is happy... well, you know. I quite enjoyed it, actually. A bit predictable, perhaps, but the cinematography was gorgeous. And I admit, I have a soft spot for a good romance. Though, I agree, the facts were… flexible. My history professor would have had a conniption fit! Flexible is putting it mildly! It's completely fabricated for dramatic effect. I tried to explain to George the intricacies of inheritance laws at the time, and he just blinked at me. He’d rather swoon over the Duke than understand the realities of primogeniture. Men, eh? They’re all the same. Always interested in the dashing hero. What are you reading at the moment, Eleanor? Anything that's a bit more… grounded? I’ve just finished “Wolf Hall” again, actually. Hilary Mantel's prose is just astonishing. It feels so real, you know? Like you’re  there  in Tudor England, smelling the damp and feeling the paranoia. It's a world away from lords and ladies fanning themselves in a drawing-room. Ah, “Wolf Hall.” A classic. I tried reading that a few years ago, but I found it a bit dense, to be honest. I keep meaning to go back to it and give it another try. I'm currently reading a thriller by Ruth Ware. It's easy to get lost in – perfect for reading on the train. Actually, that leads me to something I wanted to ask you both. Are you still primarily book readers, or do you find yourselves leaning towards eBooks more and more? eBooks? Oh, I tried one, just once. It felt so… impersonal. I like the feel of a book in my hands, the smell of the paper. Give me a proper, weighty hardback any day. And I like to lend books to people, you see. Can't do that with an eBook, can you? Plus, I've got a whole shelf dedicated to cover art.

Blimey, look at this wee thing. Proper retro, innit? Feels like holding a brick compared to what we're used to. Still, gotta admire the sheer resilience, eh? Remember when Nokia were  the  phone? You couldn't shake one of these, could ya? Dropped 'em down stairs, took 'em swimming… they just kept on tickin’. They did, didn’t they? My grandad had a Nokia. He swore by it. Said it was the only thing that kept him connected to the outside world when he was out on the farms during cold weather. And you're right, indestructible, the things were. This is a bit different, though. Feels like it'd shatter if you looked at it wrong. Aye, well, progress, eh? Fancy callin' it progress when you spend half your life worrying about scratch marks. Right, let's get these thingamajigs sorted, then. I'm guessin' you've got the manual, love? Though with modern phones, manuals are practically extinct. Just shove it in your pocket and hope for the best. Got it here, yeah. Though it’s mostly diagrams. I’m more of a ‘poke around until something works’ sort myself. First things first, gotta get the data connected, though. The Wi-Fi here is… patchy, to say the least. Are you struggling with that at all? I’m having a devil of a time finding the signal. It keeps saying “authentication required” even though I know I’m entering the right password. Authentication, is it? Sounds like one of them fancy new security features. Let me have a look. Right, right... see here, it’s askin’ for a “PEAP” type of connection, is it? You’ve got to select that, not just standard WPA2. It’s a bleedin’ nightmare, these things. The designers clearly never spent a day in a pub trying to get online. They think everyone lives in a fibre-optic wonderland. PEAP! That's it! I knew I was missing something. You’re a lifesaver! Honestly, I hate setting up phones. It's always some obscure setting or a button I can’t quite find. Makes you realise how dependent we’ve become, doesn’t it? Back in the day, a phone was just... a phone. You picked it up and you talked. Exactly! No endless downloads, no updates, no privacy policies longer than  War and Peace . Do you want me to set up your email, lass?

Right, so, for Liam’s birthday, what are we thinking? He really wants a Red Panda plushie, doesn’t he? Like,  really  wants one. He certainly does. He’s been going on about them for weeks. A Red Panda, eh? Bit niche, innit? They’re a bit pricey, aren’t they? I had a look online – they’re not cheap little fellas. "Dah! Dah!" Yeah, but he’d love it! And I reckon he'd appreciate it more than, like, another Lego set. He's got loads of those. What about a Malamooche? I saw one down at the park the other day. Proper fluffy and friendly looking. A Malamooche? You mean an Alaskan Malamute? Of course, you do. Don’t be daft, love. We can’t get a dog! Do you know how much work that is? Especially with Finn here. And we’re already going to Ireland every other weekend to see my mum. It's a lot. I know, I know. Just saying! It was a big one, though. Like, the size of a small pony. Anyway, back to Liam’s present. Maybe we could do a joint present? Like a really big one? A joint present is a good shout. We could do the Red Panda  and … maybe something smaller? He's been on about getting back into board games. Remember that Monopoly set he got last Christmas? He barely touched it. Oh yeah! He played it like, twice. Maybe something different? Like Ticket to Ride? He seemed interested in that when we were at Josh’s. Or… what was that film we saw last week? The Japanese one? You mean 'Spirited Away'? That was lovely, wasn’t it? He did seem captivated by it. But I'm not sure it’s the best  present . It’s more of an experience. Still, it’s nice you're thinking. It's good he's showing interest in things other than screens. He’s been glued to that iPad lately, hasn’t he? Keeps asking when he can have a laptop to do his homework properly. He does. Says all his mates have laptops. I told him he can use mine when he needs it for school stuff. But he wants his own, obviously. Speaking of screens... did you manage to get those gymnastics videos Liam wanted? For when he's bored? I did! They were on sale. I got him a whole bunch - different routines, different levels.

Aye, this is reet nice, isn't it? Proper cosy after that wind comin' off the moor. Makes you appreciate a good Christmas, doesn't it? I mean, remember that year at Nan's? The tree practically fell over onto Uncle Barry. Right, I’ve got a picture of that somewhere. It was chaos! Your Auntie Maureen nearly had a heart attack trying to stop it. Christmas at your nan’s was always…an experience. It's nothing like Christmas in Manila, though. My Lola’s Christmas was huge. The whole extended family, grandparents, aunts, uncles, cousins… like fifty people crammed into a two-story house. And the food! Mountains of lechon, pancit, puto bumbong… Fifty people? Heavens to Betsy. That sounds rather overwhelming, dear. Christmas was always much smaller in my family. My father was a stickler for tradition. Roast goose, plum pudding, carols sung around the piano… very proper. We’d always go to the Bath Abbey carol service, too. So lovely. I remember Christmas in Bognor Regis was usually quite wet. Never a white Christmas, unfortunately. Still, we’d brave the seafront, bundled up in coats and hats, and always had fish and chips on Christmas Day. Mum said it was a tradition. Though, I always thought it was because she couldn’t be bothered to roast a turkey! Fish and chips for Christmas? That's…bold! Nan would’ve never stood for it. It was always roast beef, every single year. Even when we were all struggling for money, she’d find a way to get a massive joint. Said it weren't Christmas without it. You know, I never really understood how different Christmas traditions could be until I came over here. In the Philippines, we started celebrating as early as September! "Ber Months," we call them. Stores start playing Christmas music and putting up decorations. It's…a long celebration. And we have this tradition called "Simbang Gabi," nine days of dawn masses leading up to Christmas Eve. Really spiritual, you know? That sounds rather special. We had our own little rituals, of course. Every year, my grandmother would make her special mince pies. Tiny ones, with extra spice. And she’d always hide a silver coin in one of them. Whoever found it was supposed to have good luck all year. Good luck, eh? I always thought that was a bit superstitious. I’m much more of a numbers man, you see.

Honestly, this is lovely, Anon. It's so…you. All these bookshelves, the comfortable chairs, the scent of old paper and something baking. Did you make that apple crumble I smell? Indeed, I did. Figured a bit of home comforts were in order after a particularly stressful week battling spreadsheets. How are things with you, Eleanor? Still wrestling with endless transcripts? You have no idea. This one is a recorded interview with a pigeon fancier. Apparently, the nuances of plumage are  vital  to a thorough transcript. I’m trying to remain objective, but I keep wanting to add little notes like "utterly baffling" or "please send help." At least the pay’s decent. Pigeon fancier, you say? Good heavens. Well, at least you're gaining experience in, shall we say, niche areas. And here I was, fretting over describing a particularly poignant sunset for my latest piece. Perspective, Eleanor, perspective. Smells divine, Anon! Glad you approve, Margaret. Thought everyone deserved a treat after Eleanor's pigeon-related trauma. So, Margaret, how’s the writing going? Closer to finishing that novel? Last I heard, you were wrestling with a particularly stubborn antagonist. The antagonist and I are currently at a stalemate. He’s proving remarkably resistant to my attempts to…reform him, shall we say. It’s infuriating, but also rather invigorating, to be honest. It's rather like dealing with a very difficult real person. It's all about their motivations, isn't it? What drives them? Keeps a writer occupied. Speaking of driving, have you both seen ‘Sherlock: Reimagined’? The new series? I’m utterly hooked. The plot twists are brilliant, and the cinematography is stunning. Although, I do miss Benedict Cumberbatch. I’ve caught a few episodes. It's decent. A bit…overwrought, perhaps? I preferred the original, to be honest. The constant music and dramatic lighting felt a little forced. Give me a good, solid Agatha Christie any day. I completely agree with David. While I appreciate the ambition of the new show, it lacks the subtle charm of the original. Agatha Christie, now  that’s  storytelling. Proper structure, well-developed characters, and a perfectly plausible solution. They don't make 'em like that anymore. I'm currently re-reading ‘And Then There Were None’ for the tenth time, I think. You two are hopeless. Always clinging to the classics! It’s refreshing to see something modern, even if it is a bit flashy.

Cor, this rain, eh? Proper biblical it is today. Like the world's gone plumb underwater. Never seen it so persistent, ‘avin’ a right good downpour since dawn, it 'as. Remember that flood back in '78? Nasty business that was, down in the Lowfields. Don't remind me, Arthur. The mud was everywhere. Honestly, I think my carpets never quite recovered. Though, you've always got a story, haven't you? Always some memory being dragged up by a bit of rain. Rain? Yes, it  is  quite something. Rather affecting the drainage plans I was discussing with the builders earlier, actually. Had to reschedule the paving for the patio. Annoying, but you can't fight the weather, can you? Builders, are you? Fancy that. Cost a pretty penny, I reckon. Paving is always a rip-off, innit? Remember old Mr. Higgins down the road, tried to lay his own patio with some bricks he’d nicked from a building site. Looked a right mess, it did. Uneven as a badger’s back. Arthur! Don't encourage him, David. He'll regale us with tales of petty crime for the next hour. David, are you having enough tea? I made a fresh pot. Earl Grey, as you like. Thank you, Margaret. That’s very kind. Yes, the tea is excellent. This drainage issue is proving rather complex. The land slopes unexpectedly, and the initial survey clearly underestimated the water runoff. Land slopes, you say? Right, right. My Uncle Percy, he was a surveyor, he was. Used to say, “Arthur, always check the ground. Ground’ll tell you a story, it will.” He was a wise man, Uncle Percy. Though, he did once try to survey my Aunt Mildred’s prize-winning dahlias. Made a right mess of them, he did. Oh, Arthur. You are incorrigible! David, I was thinking… about Eleanor. She’s been rather down lately, hasn't she? Since she finished those art classes. Feels a bit lost, I think. Eleanor? Yes, I’ve noticed. She seemed a little subdued at Christmas. What’s she been up to? Mostly just… moping about. Saying she doesn’t know what to do with herself. She enjoyed the classes, but it seems she's struggling to find the motivation to create anything without the structure of a course. It’s a common problem, I suppose. Finding that purpose again after something’s finished. Purpose, eh?

Right, so caterers are confirmed for the leaving do. Three options, all within budget. I think 'Flavours of the World' is the most popular choice from the initial survey – lots of people wanted something a bit different, you know? Not just sausage rolls and vol-au-vents. Aye, Flavours of the World sounds dead good. Proper decent grub. Much better than those dry canapés Brenda used to get. Remember those tiny quiches? You could practically see through 'em. I do! They crumbled as soon as you touched them. Not ideal for a networking event. So, Friday the 17th, then? We’ve secured the Garden Room? Yep, Garden Room is booked. I’ve sent out a preliminary invite – just a save the date, nothing too formal. We still need to finalize the decorations and music. I was thinking maybe some fairy lights and a playlist that’s… palatable to everyone? No death metal, definitely. Fairy lights are always a winner. And music... how about a mix? A bit of indie, some classic 90s, maybe even a cheeky bit of Abba? You know, to get people dancing. Morning, everyone. What’s all the buzz about? A leaving do? Who are we saying goodbye to? Horace! He's off to the States. It's a bit bittersweet, really. He's going to be working with the US education sector, doing that research on blended learning. Oh, fantastic! Horace deserves all the best. And blended learning research is so crucial right now. Listen, I'm flying to Philly next week, might be able to pop over and see him, give him a proper send-off. That’d be brilliant, Sarah! He’d love that. Speaking of love and sending-offs… I had the strangest thing happen on the way in this morning. Oh? Do tell. Right, I was walking over the bridge, yeah? And I saw this wee bee, proper struggling, caught in a spiderweb. Looked like it was about to give up the ghost. Oh, poor thing. Aye! So, I got all awkward and started trying to disentangle it. Used a twig, very carefully, you know? Took ages! The thing is, I'm terrified of bees! Proper phobic, I am. But I just couldn’t leave it. That's lovely, actually. Very you, Louise. That’s incredibly kind, Louise. Bees are so important, aren’t they? Absolutely vital for pollination. We’re losing so many of them, it’s terrifying.

Ugh, honestly, I'm  done  with history. Just… done. Done? What's up? You were buzzing about the Tudors last week. Said Henry VIII was, like, the most interesting king ever. I  did ! But Mrs. Davies just… she’s relentless. Three source analyses this week! Three! And they're all about obscure trade routes. Who cares about obscure trade routes? I mean, okay, it’s vaguely interesting if you’re, like, a merchant or something, but we’re learning about it in a modern history class! It's not relevant! She does love a good source analysis, doesn't she? You know, remember when she made us do one on that pamphlet about the potato coming to England? That was a weird one. Don't remind me. I still have nightmares about trying to decipher that awful handwriting. Anyway, I’m pretty sure I've got it all wrong. I argued that it was aggressively promoting potatoes, and she said it was “a nuanced perspective on dietary adaptation.” What even  is  a nuanced perspective? It’s just a fancy way of saying “there’s more to it than meets the eye.” Like, maybe it wasn't  just  about promoting potatoes; maybe it was about reassuring people it wouldn’t poison them! Oh. Well, why didn't she  say  that? It would have been a lot clearer. Everything's so complicated with her. It feels like she’s deliberately setting us up to fail. I think she just wants us to think critically. And, you know, spend ages staring at documents until something vaguely insightful pops into our brains. It’s a skill, apparently. A skill I actively wish to avoid developing. What about you? How’s physics going? You seemed… stressed about it yesterday. It  is  stressing me out. Mr. Peterson’s gone totally bonkers with the equations. He keeps saying “visualise the force vectors!” But my brain just sees a bunch of confusing lines no matter how hard I try. And the exam is next week! Oh no! The dreaded physics exam. Remember last year when Liam accidentally drew a dinosaur instead of a resultant vector? Oh my god, I’d completely forgotten! Mrs. Jones nearly died. He said he was “visualizing the evolutionary forces at play.” Classic Liam. So, are you doing extra revision? Because I’m officially boycotting all assignments until next week. My brain needs a break.

Honestly, Mum, this risotto is divine. You've really outdone yourself. I haven't had risotto this good since… well, probably since you made it last Christmas. Aye, well, practice makes perfect, lass. Your dad was moaning earlier, said it smelled too fancy for a Tuesday night. Men, eh? Can’t appreciate a bit of Italian flair. He just said it didn’t smell like sausages, Mum. Big difference. And it  is  really good, by the way. Creamy, perfectly cooked… well done. See? Even Liam appreciates the finer things! Dad’s just waiting for the roast dinner to come back around. Speaking of which, I’m absolutely knackered. Work has been mental this week. Oh, tell me about it. What's been tying you up in knots, love? You look properly drained. It’s the new database system. Remember I mentioned it? They’ve finally rolled it out across the department, and it’s… chaotic. Nothing is where you expect it to be, half the functions don’t work properly, and the training they gave us was practically non-existent. I spent most of today emailing IT, trying to get them to fix a spreadsheet formula. A spreadsheet formula! I have a postgraduate degree, Mum! That sounds brutal. They really didn’t think that through, did they? I’ve seen those rollouts before. It’s always a mess initially, isn't it? Remember the project management software last year? A complete disaster. Exactly! And the worst part is, everyone’s relying on me to be the ‘expert’ because I was involved in the initial scoping meetings. Like I'm supposed to know everything about a system I barely understand. I’m trying to be helpful, but I feel like I'm constantly putting out fires. Well, you are a clever lass, and you’ve always been good at sorting things out. Just breathe, and don’t get yourself worked up about it. Remember what I always say - if you’re feeling stressed, a good cup of tea and a sit down can work wonders. I wish I had time for a good cup of tea and a sit down. I’m already dreading tomorrow. I have that conference call with Zurich first thing, and I have no idea how I'm going to explain the database issues without sounding completely clueless. You won’t sound clueless. Just be honest. Say you’re still getting acquainted with the system and flag up the specific problems you’re encountering.

Right, well that was… a day. Honestly, Sarah, you have no idea. Just when I think things are settling down at work, BAM! New targets, a difficult client… the usual chaos. How was your week? You look tired, love. A bit hectic, to be honest. Little Jamie’s been a right terror. Remember how he was being a bit quiet last month? Turns out he’s been deliberately messing up his homework just to get a reaction. Sixth form are being absolute devils, giving him detention left, right and centre. Maths, English, Geography... it's a wonder he remembers how to breathe! Oh, teenagers. Don't even get me started. My Leo is barely better. He's decided that his bedroom is a biohazard zone. I swear, I'm going to need a hazmat suit to even  look  in there. Detention, you say? Is it really necessary? Sometimes, I think these schools just  want  to fill their disciplinary records. I know, right? It feels like they're looking for an excuse. But he wasn’t exactly forthcoming about what he’d done. Said something about throwing paper aeroplanes in Mrs. Davies' class. Paper aeroplanes! Honestly. He’s too clever for his own good, sometimes, that boy. I had a right telling off from him too, about how I keep nagging him about cleaning his room. It's amazing how they turn it around, isn’t it? Absolutely! It's a skill, honestly. They're born with it. Listen, have you had a chance to look at that letter from the bank about the new mortgage rate? It's a complete nightmare. They’re saying it’s going up again. I’m proper stressed about it. We need to look at tightening the belt a bit, I think. Maybe cut back on subscriptions. Oh, that’s awful. Everything's going up, isn’t it? I was just talking to Mrs. Peterson about it. She said her building society is offering a fixed rate… might be worth looking into? It'll give you some peace of mind, knowing you’re not going to be hit with another surprise increase. I'll have a look when I can. You know, speaking of tight belts, I’m trying to plan out my work schedule for next month. Mrs. Chalmers is off for a week, and she's asked if I can cover some of her cleans.

Right, so, Mr. Henderson actually  complimented  my speed tonight. Said I was "a picture of efficiency." Can you believe it? After two weeks of him breathing down my neck about clearing glasses fast enough. Seriously? That’s actually brilliant, Maisie! He’s usually got something to moan about. Proper grumpy man, isn’t he? Aye, he is. A right misery guts. But I reckon I’ve finally broken through to him. I’ve been watching how that lad, Liam, does it - he's like a ninja with the tray. All those shortcuts, ya know? Pre-pouring the mixers, stacking the glasses just so… I’ve been nicking his tips, basically. Absolutely. Copying the best. Smart move. So, is that going to lead to a raise, do you think? Or just the rare praise? Dunno. Don’t hold your breath. Henderson’s tighter than a drum. But even a little extra would be good. Rent’s due next month, and… well, you know. Costs are just ridiculous these days. It’s not like I’m moaning, though, I’m grateful to have the job. Beats being stuck at home with Mum and Dad, forever. Totally get it. University fees are brutal, that's for sure. I'm working my way through part-time at the campus café, but it’s mostly just washing dishes and refilling sugar sachets. Not exactly glamorous. Oh, come on, that’s still something! At least you’re surrounded by books and, like, actual studying people. I’m surrounded by stag dos and people who’ve clearly had a bit too much cider. Last night, someone spilled a pint down their own trousers. Honestly. Sounds… lively. Do you ever feel like you’re missing out on, you know,  life ? While you’re serving shots and dealing with dodgy behaviour? Sometimes. Aye. I mean, all my friends from school are off backpacking round Southeast Asia or landing internships in shiny offices in London. And here I am, wiping beer stains. But then I remember I’ve got my own little patch of independence. I’m paying my own bills, I'm choosing where to live. And, there's a certain satisfaction in keeping things running smoothly, even on a Friday night when it’s absolute chaos. Plus, free drinks when I'm off shift. Can’t complain about  that , can I? True! Free drinks are a huge perk. It’s just… I feel weird sometimes, like I’m existing in this bubble of studying.

Right then, that’s the fiction cart sorted for today. Anyone got anything exciting planned for the upcoming break? Feels like ages since we've had a decent chunk of time off. Exciting? Not really, love. Going back to Halifax, obviously. Family stuff. My sister's got a new puppy, a little terrier. My grandkids are properly obsessed with it. That's excitement enough for me, I reckon. What about you, Liam? Anywhere sunnier than Salford on the cards? Not this year, sadly. Saving up, really. Tried to book something to Spain, but prices have gone through the roof. Might just do some hiking in the Lake District, if the weather holds up. Bit of fresh air, quiet time to read… you know the drill. Hiking, is it? Ah, that'll be grand. You need the fresh air. Sitting amongst these books all day, it’s easy to become a bit… rooted, like a plant. I’m off to see my niece in Belfast. She insists I come for the Air Guitar Championships. Air Guitar Championships? Seriously, Moira? You’re going to compete? Compete? Heavens, no, Daniel. Just to witness the carnage, dear. It's a yearly tradition, you see. Last year, the winner did a magnificent rendition of "Smoke on the Water." Honestly, the commitment! The facial expressions! Good gracious! I can just imagine. My nephew tried to teach my grandson how to do it. The poor child nearly pulled a muscle. It just looked like a confused flapping motion. Sounds considerably more entertaining than walking up a muddy hillside, to be honest. Although, I'm hoping to spot some red squirrels. Small victories, right? Red squirrels? You’re aiming high, Liam. You’ll be lucky to spot a pigeon in the Lake District. Jokes aside, I'm finally getting some time off. My wife and I are going to Italy. Florence, Rome, Venice… the full works. Been planning it for years. I’ve even booked a pasta-making class. Ooh, Italy! Fancy! Proper treat that. Make sure you bring me back some biscotti, love. The ones with the almonds. I’m having a craving already just thinking about them. Absolutely, Brenda. Biscotti are on the list. Although, my wife keeps insisting on a hot air balloon ride over Tuscany. I’m a little apprehensive. Heights aren't exactly my friend. Last time I was on a Ferris wheel, I nearly fainted.

Oh, come on ref! That was a clear foul! Honestly, you'd think they were blind, wouldn't ya? Relax, Liv. It's football. They miss things. Besides, it’s still early days. Plenty of time for things to turn around. Easy for you to say, eh? You're not a lifelong Sunderland fan. You lot with your Birmingham City, you've got nothing to really  feel  about football. It’s just...not the same. It’s not ingrained in your soul like it is up north. Right, there's that Northeast superiority complex again. I assure you, Birmingham has a rich footballing history. And feeling deeply about a team doesn't require geographical latitude. Aye, well, it  helps . Look at 'em! Absolutely bottling it. They're playing like they've never seen a football before. Remember that time Sunderland beat Liverpool 3-0 at the Stadium of Light? Now  that  was a performance. Vaguely. I was probably studying, to be honest. Though I do recall you calling me for an hour straight after. You were practically delirious with joy. I was! I was! It was magical, it was! This is just... disappointing. I could've picked a stronger team than this with me eyes shut. Alright, alright. Calm down. So, about food. Feeling peckish beyond the chips? I was thinking we could order some burgers from that place down the road - ‘Burger Bliss’ or something equally unimaginative. Burger Bliss? Is that the one with the, like, fluorescent signs and the kids screaming all over the place? The very same. But the burgers are decent. Proper messy, junk-food goodness. What do you reckon? Or something healthier? I could whip up a salad. A salad? Seriously, Dan? We’re watching football! This is a sacred ritual! It requires grease and calories. Massive portions. The more ridiculous the better. Like, a double bacon cheeseburger with onion rings and extra cheese sauce, yeah? That’s what I'm talking about. You are a sight, you know that? You’re like a walking, talking advertisement for heart disease. Don’t knock it till you’ve tried it! Besides, I burn it all off running around at work. Research managing, you know. Constant meetings, frantic emails…it’s exhausting. True, true. Constant stress does warrant some serious comfort food. Alright, Burger Bliss it is then. Double bacon cheeseburger for the lady, and what will you have, Your Majesty?

Right then, Grandma, this tea's champion stuff. Proper brew. Mum, you've been practicing, haven't you? Aye, lad. Needed a bit o' warming up on a day like this. Cold wind's brewin', it is. Reminds me o' winters when I were a lass. Snow drifted up to the windows, it did. Couldn’t see a thing. Don't remind me, Mum! I remember those winters as a kid. School was shut for a week, wasn't it? Playing in the snow until our fingers were numb. You two and your snow stories. I’m more of a sunny holiday man, myself. Speaking of sunny, did you ever see "Casablanca," Grandma? Proper classic, that. "Casablanca"? Oh, aye. Saw that at the Plaza, back in '43 or '44. Used to sneak in sometimes, mind. Cost a few pennies, it did. Humphrey Bogart, wasn't he? Handsome man. Though I always preferred Clark Gable, myself. "Gone With The Wind," now that was somethin'. Made me cry buckets. “Gone With The Wind”! That was a marathon, wasn't it? I remember watching it with you, Mum. You cried through half of it. And Dad always complained about the length of it. He was more of a Westerns man, you know. John Wayne, all that. See, I'm more into the modern stuff, to be honest. Marvel films, that sort of thing. All the special effects, you know? Keeps you on the edge of your seat.
