Though Mum keeps saying they're all just noise and explosions. Well, there's a bit of truth in that, isn’t there, Tom? It’s all a bit…much for me sometimes. Give me a good period drama any day. Something with some proper acting. Though, I did enjoy that “Paddington” film, actually. Really charming. Paddington? What's Paddington? Sounds like a fancy biscuit. It's a bear, Grandma. A little bear from Peru who comes to London. Gets into all sorts of scrapes. It’s actually really good, though. Proper feel-good film. Might show you one of these days. Actually, reminds me of when I was a kid and I got a little BMX bike. Oh, your BMX! You were always covered in mud after a ride. Remember the time you crashed into Mrs. Higginbottom’s rose bushes? Don’t remind me! She gave me a proper telling off. Never did live that down.

Honestly, this pancake chaos is exactly why I swore I’d only make crumpets. Look at you two! Leo, you’ve got more batter on your face than on the plate. And Maisie, you’re pushing your pancakes around like they owe you money. It’s lumpy, Mummy. Lumpy? It’s buttermilk pancakes, darling. They're meant to be a little rustic. Eat one. Please? It's Pancake Day! I even put some blueberries in. Blueberries are icky. I want chocolate spread. Leo! We talked about this. Too much sugar before dinner. Besides, you had chocolate spread on your toast this morning. Think about Thomas in my class. He doesn’t have even toast some mornings. His mum works two jobs, and sometimes they rely on the food bank. It makes you appreciate things, doesn't it? Is Thomas sad? Sometimes. But he's a lovely boy, very bright too. He helped us all with a tricky maths problem in assembly today. Speaking of assembly, did you two listen when I was telling you about the author, Lucy Boston? No! It was about Green Knowe! Remember, I read you that story last year? The one with the old house and all the ghosts and the history? It was brilliant! The whole school was so quiet, listening to the story. It's rather magical, isn’t it? I thought you'd like it. Ghosts? Was there a scary ghost? Not scary, darling, more… mysterious. It’s about families and history. It made me think about all the people who lived in this old house before us. Anyway, less thinking, more pancakes. Honestly, you're both driving me mad. I'm not hungry. Oh, for goodness sake, Leo! You were gobbling down your cereal five minutes ago. Don’t you want to go to the Science Museum this weekend? I booked those tickets ages ago. We could see the space exhibit! Space? With rockets? Yes, rockets! And planets! And maybe even a robot. But only if you eat a few pancakes first. Deal? But… And then, after the Science Museum, we  must  make sure we wash our hands properly before we touch anything else. Especially door handles. Germs, you know. Remember what we talked about with flushing the toilet? You make a funny face when you flush! I do, don't I? Well, it's important to press the handle down with your elbow, not your hands.

Honestly, this General Tso’s chicken is a bit…bland, isn't it? I was expecting more of a kick. Remember that place we used to go to in Sheffield? They absolutely nailed the sweet and spicy thing. Nah, it’s alright. Perfectly edible. Better than that dodgy takeaway we had last month, anyway. You were practically gagging on the spring rolls. They  were  a bit suspect, weren't they? I swear the duck was giving me the side-eye. Still, beats cooking. Speaking of suspect, did you see that article about the pigeon infestation in Westminster? Apparently, they’re using cathedral gargoyles as nesting spots! Westminster pigeons, eh? Probably used to the tourists chucking them chips. More interesting is the news about that new fertiliser they're testing. Could revolutionize crop yields, apparently. Though, you know, always a risk with these things. Fertiliser? Seriously, Finn? Of all the things to bring up while we're drowning in soy sauce. Can we stay on a slightly less agricultural track, please? Sorry, just…a lot of my world revolves around things that grow. It’s hard to switch it off. Besides, it's good news. More food, less hunger...though probably more Westminster pigeons to feed off the surplus. You're thinking about fields when we're trying to enjoy some takeaway. Did you hear from Liam? He was having a rough time with his grandma's funeral, right? Not recently. I sent him a text a few days ago, just to check in. He seemed pretty wiped. It’s awful, isn’t it? Funerals always feel so…performative, even if you're genuinely grieving. All those forced smiles and platitudes. Absolutely. My auntie Brenda’s funeral was like a networking event for miserable people. Everyone trying to out-sad everyone else. It was deeply unsettling. That's a brutal way to put it, Elara, but I get it. It's… strange. I haven’t been to many funerals, actually. Mostly just pets. Dogs, you know? Easier to feel genuine with a dog. Fair point. So, film night this weekend? I was thinking of putting on  Paddington 2 . It’s pure, unadulterated joy. Ooh, yes! Perfect antidote to bleak funeral conversations. I'm in. Absolutely. Although, I'm slightly wary of Hugh Grant singing. Is it as bad as people say? It's legendary. In a  very  bad way. But it’s part of the charm.

Honestly, remembering Mrs. Higgins next door in the old house… she was a force of nature, wasn’t she? Always had a prize-winning marrow at the village fete. And the gossip! Goodness, she knew everything about everyone. Ah, Mrs. Higgins. Strong woman. Knew how to get things done. Wolverhampton didn't have prize-winning marrows like that. More coal dust and stubbornness, if I recall. Though, my Aunt Elsie – she grew spectacular roses. Almost as flamboyant as Mrs. Higgins was with her opinions. You two are taking me right back! Remember when Mrs. Higgins accused young Timmy Baker of stealing her best marrow? It turned out a badger had rolled it into his garden. She wouldn't apologise for a week! No, she wouldn't. Timmy's poor mother was mortified. And then, just a few weeks later, she was complaining about foxes raiding her strawberry patch. You’d think she'd learn! Reminds me of my sister, Margaret. Always blaming the cat for things she'd done herself. A cat couldn’t be trusted, according to her. Though, she did make a rather excellent rice krispy cake. Do you remember those, dear? Oh, absolutely! You used to make them every Christmas. Loads of melted marshmallows and extra butter. Pure indulgence! I haven't had a good rice krispy cake in ages. We should make some. That would be lovely. I’ve got that new recipe I was telling you about - uses brown rice krispies, a little healthier. Though, I’m not sure if it tastes quite as good. Healthier? Nonsense! The best things in life aren’t healthy. That’s what I always said in accounting. Simplify the ledger, but don’t sacrifice the joy. That's a wonderful philosophy! Speaking of things that are slightly worrying… I was reading about those driverless cars. Honestly, the thought of relinquishing control like that… I know, right? It's fascinating technology, of course, but slightly terrifying. Especially when you think about the potential for hacking. Or failing software! Failing software. We had that with the treasurer at the cricket club once. Lost all the accounts. Just vanished. Thankfully, young Arthur – a bright lad – sorted it out. Took him a week. But the chaos… . You know, air travel used to feel so much safer. Now… all these computers managing everything. It's the layers of automation, isn’t it? Removes the human element.

Right, nearly ready! Just needs a little more… ooh, Elsie, darling, please don’t draw on the cupboards again! But Mummy, I'm drawing a dragon for Chinese New Year! A sparkly one! See? It needs scales! Dragons don’t have  scales  like dinosaurs, Elsie! They have… shining plates! Like armour! Roar! That’s a very interesting take, Leo. Very thorough. Elsie, darling, cupboards are not for dragon scales, okay? We've got paper. Lots of paper. Remember what we talked about? This is for special drawings. But… but dragons are  important ! It's the Year of the Dragon! My teacher, Miss Davies, showed us pictures. They were HUGE! Bigger than Jupiter, even! Well, they  are  important. And impressive! Jupiter is a very big planet though, you're right to point that out. Remember we were looking at pictures of the planets the other day? Saturn with its rings… Did you know some dragons in Chinese stories have rings, too? Not like Saturn’s, but like… flowing ribbons of clouds! Ribbons? Cool! Can I draw a dragon with ribbons then? And rocket boosters? Rocket boosters? Now you're getting ambitious! Absolutely. You can draw whatever you want, little man. Just not on the kitchen cupboards. Elsie, do you want to come and draw your sparkly dragon on the big paper? We can use glitter this time! Glitter?! Yes, please! And can we eat noodles afterwards? The duck noodles you make are the  best ! Almost ready then. Absolutely noodles. And spring rolls. And… oh, I got some those little sesame balls today, the ones you both love. Can I play the drums  after  the noodles? I need to practice the beat for ‘We Will Rock You’! Of course, sweetheart. We'll fit it in. And Elsie, how's your piano practice going? Mrs. Peterson says you're getting really good at 'Twinkle, Twinkle'. It's okay. It's a bit boring. I wish I could do aerial hoop like you, Mummy! It looks so amazing! It  is  amazing, isn’t it? It takes a lot of practice. Maybe when you’re a little bit older. Until then, we can watch videos! Do you remember that  Barbie and the Great Adventure  one? The pearl princess one? Yeah! The one with the sparkly sea creatures! And Barbie had to learn to fly! Exactly! It takes courage and hard work. And sometimes… a little bit of magic.

Blimey, this is proper lovely, innit? Bit warmer than I was expecting, mind you. Forecast back home said rain. Proper London drizzle. Yeah, it's beautiful. Though, I am slightly sunburnt already. Forgot to reapply after lunch. Didn't expect it to be  this  warm in October. The Airbnb was a bit of a gamble, though. Pictures made it look metres from the Trevi. "Metres" is pushing it, Liv. It's a good fifteen minute walk. But the balcony! The balcony is worth it, isn’t it? Best view of the rooftops I've had in ages. And your mum loved it, right? She was practically bouncing. She was! She kept saying, “This is  glamorous , Liv! Like Audrey Hepburn!” She's been snapping photos of everything. My Instagram is overflowing. Honestly, I'm starting to think she's enjoying this more than I am. Speaking of photos, did anyone manage to capture that crazy scooter incident near the Pantheon earlier? I swear, that bloke nearly took out a whole family. Yeah, I got a snippet. Pretty sure it’s going straight onto my story. Roman driving, eh? It's an Olympic sport, I reckon. Speaking of snaps, your Mum's looking alright in those photos, Chloe. She's having a right laugh. She is. She’s been practicing her Italian, which is hilarious. Mostly she just says "Grazie, molto!" to everyone and everything. She nearly tipped a poor waiter twenty euros for bringing her a glass of water. Classic Mum. So, dinner tonight? I was thinking that little trattoria near Campo de' Fiori. The one Marco recommended. Supposed to be incredible. Sounds spot on. I'm starving, to be honest. I’ve been trying to learn a bit of Italian, but it's no use. My brain just won’t click. Feels like I'm trying to swallow a dictionary. Tell me about it. I’ve been here six months now, and I still butcher the language. It's got so many nuances. My Italian colleagues just roll their eyes whenever I try. “Un baristà, ma senza parole!” they say. A barista, but without words! You picked it up pretty quickly, though, didn't you? Six months and you're holding down a job. My Italian’s awful. I just point a lot. Helps keep things moving in the cafe, you know? Especially when it's busy. What about your cousin, Leo?

Right, so, initial thoughts on the hen do options? I've been trawling through Pinterest for like, three hours, and I’m starting to feel slightly manic. Like, feather boas and glitter cannons are calling my name, but is that  really  what Chloe wants? Chloe? Chloe’s more of a gentle aromatherapy session and a nice walk in the countryside vibe, if we’re being honest. Remember that time we tried to take her karaoke? She hid in the bathroom for half an hour. Oh god, yes! The sheer horror on her face! That was classic Chloe. I think we definitely need to steer clear of anything too… loud. I saw a package deal for a spa weekend in the Cotswolds, though. It was looking pretty decent. Afternoon tea, massages, cream teas… Ooh, the Cotswolds! That’s a good shout, Liv. Very Chloe-esque. We could even do a little crafting session while we’re there. Remember that macrame wall hanging workshop we all loved last year? Crafts? At a hen do? I mean, I love crafting, don’t get me wrong. Remember that disastrous attempt at gingerbread houses I made for Christmas? Nearly burned down the kitchen. Oh, Rosie! Those were legendary. The leaning tower of gingersnap! It was a  spectacle . But yeah, maybe a slightly less ambitious craft than gingerbread architecture. What about making little floral crowns? Or decorating tote bags? Something cute and manageable. I’m in for floral crowns! It’d be so Instagrammable. We could even get some little succulents to plant in them afterwards – little reminders of the day. Plus, it’s something we can all do together, and Chloe would actually enjoy it. It’s less about the wild party and more about celebrating her, right? Yeah, you’re right. It’s about Chloe. I just… I feel this pressure to make it  amazing . Like, it needs to be the hen do to end all hen dos. Relax, love. Chloe will be happy as long as she’s surrounded by her favourite people, eating cake, and not being forced to sing karaoke. Speaking of cake, I've been experimenting with a new lemon drizzle recipe. It's proving… challenging. You've been baking?! Tell me everything! Is it using that Nigella Lawson recipe you mentioned? The one with the ridiculously complicated glaze? It is! And it's fighting me every step of the way.

Blimey, this smells… intense. You sure this chilli recipe isn't gonna blow me socks off, Liam? It’s proper fiery already. Nah, it'll be alright, Ben. Just needs a bit more time to simmer. I toned down the scotch bonnets a bit, remember? You were complaining last time about needing a fire extinguisher handy. Aye, well, last time I might have slightly underestimated the heat. Nearly set off the smoke alarm. Mum was not pleased. Though, I did feel like a dragon for a good hour afterwards. Speaking of feeling like something, I think I'm coming down with something myself. My throat’s scratchy, and I've got that proper heavy feeling in my head. Ugh, not again! You’re always catching something. Likely that dodgy curry you had on Tuesday. Honestly, Ben, you need to be more careful. Did you get any proper sleep last night after that design deadline? Sleep? What’s sleep? I swear, my brain just decided to re-edit the whole brochure at 3 am. Felt like I was wrestling a rogue paragraph. And no, I didn’t get much. Just little cat naps. I’ll pop to the chemist tomorrow, get some lozenges. Right. And some actual rest. Seriously. You’re pushing yourself too hard. Anyway, about that trip to Barcelona… I was looking at hotels online. Prices are ridiculous! Have you seen them? Cor! Those beachfront places are proper extortionate, aren’t they? What about something a bit further back? Near the Gothic Quarter, maybe? It'd be more interesting, wouldn’t it? Better for wandering about, finding proper tapas places. Yeah, I thought so too. Found a few decent-looking options. Nothing fancy, just clean and central. One had rave reviews for its breakfast – apparently, they do a mean churro. Churros are essential. It’s practically a travel requirement. So, what's the budget looking like then? Mum said she’d chip in a bit, no? She said she’d  consider  chipping in a bit. Classic Mum. She'll probably offer to knit us matching hats instead. I was thinking, if we booked something now, we could potentially snag a deal. Plus, I've been saving. Maybe we could split it three ways with Sarah? She's been saying she needs a getaway. Sarah would love Barcelona. She's always going on about Gaudi. Three ways would definitely make it more manageable.

Right then, Marjorie, let’s get this shopping list sorted. We need to be organised, don’t we? Otherwise we'll end up forgetting the oatcakes again, and you know how you get without your oatcakes! Don’t remind me, Patricia! It’s a disaster. Oatcakes, definitely. And those fancy biscuits from Thornton’s, the ones with the dark chocolate. Remember those? They used to be a real treat. Oh, and we need washing powder, of course. The sensitive skin kind. My eczema's been playing up something awful. Sensitive skin, yes. And teabags, naturally. Yorkshire Gold, you know my preference. Should we get some of those calendar fobs too? The ones with the little knitted animals on them? They’re so jolly, aren’t they? Oh, they are. Though, last year’s badger was a bit… intense. Looking a bit too much like he was plotting something. Still, a nice reminder of dates. We'll definitely need those. Now, speaking of dates, I was just thinking about these birthday cards we need to send. Such a bother trying to figure out ages. Little Timmy Henderson is turning eight now. Eight! It feels like only yesterday he was in my class, covered in glue and desperately trying to make a paper parrot. Oh, paper parrots! Remember all that art and craft we did at school? Miss Davies was a stickler for symmetrical wings, wasn't she? And everything had to be painted with those awful, smelly watercolours. Purple for the beak, naturally. Absolutely. And the stringy, scratchy wool we used for felt! I used to get wool all over my hands. Do you recall the hockey boots? Those awful, heavy things we had to wear in primary school? My ankles ached for days after a session on the field. I wasn't very good, you know. More interested in sketching daffodils than scoring goals. You always were the artistic one. I was more of a… well, a runner. Not particularly good, but I ran. Remember Mrs. Perkins, our music teacher? She tried to get us all to join the recorder club. Dreadful! The noise! Oh, the recorder. A symphony of screeching. But it did inspire me, in a way. It made me want to understand sound properly. That's partly why I considered sound recording at university, you know. Though history ended up winning out. Social history, specifically. It fascinated me.

Right then. This is lovely, really lovely. Much more… settled than that flat you had in London, eh? Feels like a proper home already. Though, Holsworthy... bit of a change from Southend, wouldn't you say? It is, Dad. But a good change, I think. And it’s gorgeous here, isn't it? The countryside is just… incredible. Remember how you always used to complain about not having a garden? Well, look at this! Don’t get him started on that garden, love! He'll be out there like a man possessed the moment the weather clears up. Though, he’ll probably need a few lessons first. Bless him, he nearly took out the rose bushes at your old place trying to prune them. Now, that's not entirely fair! I was… experimenting. Besides, roses are tricky things, aren’t they? Anyway, tell me about these neighbours. You mentioned they're quite friendly? They are! The couple next door, Mr. and Mrs. Pengelly – lovely people. Brought us a welcome basket the other day, full of homemade scones and jam. Proper Devon hospitality. And across the lane, there's old Mrs. Trethewey. She’s a bit… eccentric, but in a charming way. She’s a keen gardener, too, so I reckon you two will have plenty to talk about. Scones and jam, you say? That's a good start. Eccentric gardeners I can handle. I spent years dealing with difficult managers, a few eccentric flower enthusiasts won’t faze me. Did they say anything about the area? Any local gossip? Oh, there's  always  local gossip, isn't there? Apparently, there’s been a bit of a kerfuffle about the new planning permission for that housing development down by the river. Some people are worried it'll spoil the view. It  might  a little, but it’s needed housing, Dad. And apparently, they're building a new community hall as part of the project. A community hall… that’s positive. Though, knowing councils, I suspect it'll have gone over budget and the builder will be cutting corners. Reminds me of the debacle with the school refurbishment down in Leigh-on-Sea… Let's not get started on council projects, dear. We’re supposed to be celebrating your move! Have you had a chance to look at the walking group yet? They meet every Tuesday, apparently, and do a lovely circular route along the coast.

Aye, it’s dead annoying, this. The screen's cracked again. Proper spiderweb pattern it is. Seriously, Liam? How many times is that now? You’ve smashed that phone more times than I've had history essays. Did you drop it again trying to catch a pigeon? Don’t start, Liv. It weren't a pigeon this time. It were the… the sofa. I leaned back a bit sharp, and  pop . It's just… clanky things everywhere in this house, ya know? Always something gettin’ in the way. Clanky things? Liam, your coordination is the problem, not the furniture. You should probably just bite the bullet and get a new one. New one? With what money, Liv? You know I’m no’ exactly swimmin’ in dough. I’ve been havin’ a look online, though. Found a decent one on that Wish thing… looks alright. Wish? Oh god, Liam, no! Don’t tell me you're buying a phone off Wish. You’ll get some knock-off that’ll die after a week. Remember that charger you got? Lasted about three hours and smelled like burning plastic. Aye, well, it were better than nothin’ at the time. But this one… the reviews were decent. Lots of people sayin’ it's alright. Only £25. Reviews on Wish are usually fake, Liam. And £25 for a phone is practically giving it away. You’re setting yourself up for disappointment. I saw a refurbished Samsung Galaxy A32 on eBay for about £80. A proper one. Eighty quid? That’s daylight robbery! I'd need to win the lottery first. Besides, I've been lookin' at some listing on Facebook Marketplace. There's one fella near Maryport sellin’ an iPhone 8 for fifty quid. Said it’s “lightly used” and “works perfectly.” Maryport? That’s a fair trek. And "lightly used" could mean anything. Did you message him? Did you ask him about the battery health? Aye, messaged him. He hasn’t replied. Probably gets loads. Keeps gettin’ on, doesn't it? I'm thinkin' of going down later, seein' if I can get a look at it. Please be careful, Liam. Don’t go on your own, alright? And don't give him any money until you’ve had a proper chance to check it over. And check the battery! Battery health is crucial. Alright, alright. Mum’s goin’ to Cleator Moor this afternoon.

Right then. This place is… well, it’s certainly got character, hasn't it? A lot more character than that soulless flat in Southend. Doesn’t feel like a house, more like a home already. Though, I must say, these radiators are a bit temperamental. You've managed to get them working properly, have you, Claire? Nearly, Dad. Just a few quirks to iron out. This Victorian plumbing is a nightmare, honestly. I think one of them’s leaking a tiny bit near the bedroom. I’ll need to get someone in to take a proper look, but it’s not urgent, is it? Urgent enough to stop the damp creeping in, dear. Can’t have a damp house in Devon, not with the weather we get. Reminds me of when young Timmy got stuck in that flooded ditch down by the farm… nearly froze his toes off! Don't remind me. Timmy was always getting into scrapes. Still is, I bet. Speaking of getting into things, how’s this lunch coming along? Smells lovely. I was thinking something simple, just sandwiches and maybe some crisps? No, no, Dad, I’m making lamb stew. It’s slow-cooked, really hearty. Perfect for a blustery day like today. And I’ve got that apple crumble you like for dessert. It wouldn't be lunch without it! Ooh, apple crumble! You are spoiling us, Claire. Thank you. It'll be good to get out in the fresh air. Are you still planning that coastal walk tomorrow, Claire? The one you were talking about, down towards Hartland Quay? Yes! I’ve checked the tides and the weather forecast. It looks promising – a bit windy, but dry. We could pack a picnic. It's a really lovely stretch of coast, Mum. A bit challenging in parts, but the views… absolutely stunning. I was thinking we could go past Clovelly maybe? Clovelly! Good heavens. That’s a bit far, isn't it? All those steps. My knees aren’t what they used to be, you know. Remember that trek we did in the Lake District? Nearly killed me. Yes, I remember. You grumbled the entire time! Come on, Dad, it'll be good for you. Fresh air, exercise… stop getting so dramatic. He's got a point, dear. Perhaps just down to the little cove near here then? We can still get a wonderful view, and it’s much easier going.

Right, that was glorious. Seriously, your shepherd’s pie is a masterpiece, Elara. I haven't had anything that good in ages. Glad you liked it, Tom. It’s Mum’s recipe, you know. Luckily, she wrote it down this time, instead of relying on vague instructions whispered across the kitchen. You’d have been lost trying to make it. Vaguely whispers? That sounds about right for her. Though I’m eternally grateful for her culinary skills, even if the methods are… chaotic. So, tell me, how was the school day? You looked a little stressed when you walked in. More Ofsted drama? Worse, actually. It wasn’t Ofsted. It was… Timothy. Timothy? The little terror who permanently smells like glue and chalk dust? The very one. He apparently decided to 'improve' the staff room by drawing a mural on the whiteboard. A  very  detailed mural. Of dinosaurs fighting pirates. And he insists it’s historically accurate. Historically accurate dinosaurs fighting pirates? That’s… impressive dedication to inaccuracy. Did the headteacher have a conniption? Nearly. He spent a good twenty minutes trying to explain the concept of “appropriate use of school property” to a seven-year-old whose eyes were shining with artistic pride. It was… surreal. I ended up having to mediate, offering to help Timothy create a proper art display for the school hallway. I bribed him with glitter. Lots and lots of glitter. Glitter. Of course. The universal currency of educators. Sounds exhausting, though. Are you feeling alright? You seem more drained than usual. It’s just… it’s the constant pressure, you know? The paperwork, the meetings, the assessments. And then you get a Timothy incident thrown in. It's just a lot. I feel like I’m constantly firefighting. It's not the rewarding work I thought it would be. I get that. Research can feel similarly relentless sometimes. Grant applications, publications, endless data analysis… it can feel like you’re chasing your tail. Have you thought about talking to someone at work? About the workload, I mean? The union rep, perhaps? I’ve toyed with the idea. But it's just… I don't want to rock the boat. Plus, everyone is so stretched. I'm sure they’d just tell me to prioritise and manage my time better. Which, frankly, I’m trying to do! Do you ever feel like your work is just… consuming you?

Honestly, this lamb is a bit tougher than I thought it would be. I should have braised it longer, shouldn't I? Though, to be fair, sourcing decent lamb these days is proving a right nightmare. Everything's imported, innit? Don't fuss, love. It’s perfectly alright. Bit chewy, yeah, but not awful. At least you cooked it. Half the time I'm grabbing a ready meal after a day wrangling the marketing team. Speaking of which, Sarah's been really pushing for a new slogan. "Innovate. Inspire. Integrate." She said. Nearly choked on my tea. Oh, God, that  is  dreadful. Sounds like something from a corporate training video. Honestly, I’d struggle to use that in a copywriting brief. Too… generic. I mean, a good slogan needs a spark, doesn't it? Something memorable. Slogans, slogans. Always wanting a fancy slogan. Back in my day, we just said what it was, and people bought it. "Reliable decorators, best price." Done. Simple as that. None of this flowery nonsense. And you get paid to  think  of these things? Blimey. You’re lucky you did, Derek. Remember Uncle George trying to come up with a slogan for his flower shop? "Petals of Paradise"? Absolutely mortifying. Mum still brings it up at Christmas. Oh, bless George. He was a character, wasn't he? Anyway, back to the lamb… I was reading about those genetically modified sheep they’re breeding now - apparently, they're supposed to produce milk that's specifically for human babies. Bit unsettling, isn’t it? Brings to mind that story about Dolly. Unsettling is putting it mildly. Playing God, that's what it is. Though, you know, if it could help infants... I suppose there's a case to be made. It’s the ethics, innit? Everything's got an ethical angle these days. Makes you weary. It does. I read an article the other day about how AI is being used to write advertising copy. Apparently it can mimic different writing styles. It's a bit scary, to be honest. What's the point of going to university if a computer can do your job? A computer writing advertising? Don't make me laugh! You can't replace a bit of common sense and a London accent. Trust me. I’ve seen it all over the years. You need to  feel  the customer, see what they’re looking for.

Aye, that rhubarb crumble was champion, wasn't it? Honestly, Mrs. ANON makes a mean crumble. Better than me mam’s, and that’s saying something! She's been perfecting it for, well, forever, practically. Champion, you say? Aye, it was a fine crumble. Reminds me of my Gran’s, she used to make 'em with spotty apples, you know. Not the shiny ones they sell nowadays. Proper, honest apples. You wouldn’t get those in the shops back then. Had a bit of bite to 'em. It  was  delicious, honestly. Though, I have to admit, I’m still trying to figure out how she gets the crumble topping so perfectly crisp. Is it the kind of flour she uses? Or maybe the butter temperature? You and your engineering brain, Liam! It’s just…crumble, innit? She’s never given me a secret recipe. Just says, “A bit of this, a bit of that, love.” Proper vague, she is. But it always turns out brilliant. You’d think it’d be easy to replicate, wouldn't you? It's all in the feel, lad. The feel of the dough. My Gran, she didn't measure nothing. Just felt it, you know? Years of experience. Can’t teach that. Though, everything’s different now, isn’t it? Supermarkets, weighing scales…makes it all a bit…mechanical. There’s definitely something to that. It’s precision versus intuition, I suppose. In engineering, we’re all about precision. But sometimes, a bit of intuition is what you need to solve a problem. It's finding that balance, isn’t it? Brings me to mind of a consultancy job I was on in Azerbaijan. The soil composition was all wrong for the planned structure and we had to come up with some alternative methods ensuring the building's structural integrity. Azerbaijan? Blimey, that’s a fair bit away! What were you doing oot there then, Liam? I was working on a new infrastructure project - a high-speed rail link. The terrain was… challenging. Needed a full redesign of the foundation, and a completely new system of soil stabilization. It was intense, but fascinating to learn about their local building techniques. Absolutely world away from Sunderland, I'd wager! Azerbaijan, eh? Never been further than Blackpool myself. Blackpool… used to go there every year with my mam and dad when I was a lad. Donkey rides, stick of rock… proper seaside holiday.

Right, so, the reading list for 'Modernist Literature' is… ambitious, to say the least. I've been wrestling with it all afternoon. Are you sure we need to include Woolf  and  Joyce in the first module? It's a bit much, isn’t it? First year students. Ambitious is good, love. They’re not fragile things, these students. They need to be challenged. And honestly, Woolf and Joyce are foundational. You can’t really talk about Modernism without touching on both. Besides, we covered some of the basics in the preparatory materials. Not the full text, obviously, just key extracts. I know, I know. It’s just… I remember being utterly lost trying to decipher  Ulysses  at uni. And I had a decent background in literature! These poor things, many of whom will have only read Harry Potter. It's just going to be a wall of dense prose. We can build bridges. We’ll spend a good chunk of the seminar dedicated to navigating Joyce’s style. Breakdown the stream of consciousness technique. Talk about the influence of Dublin…make it relatable. Remember how we managed to make Chaucer accessible last year? Yes, the Chaucer improv workshop was a roaring success. Although, I’m still slightly traumatised by those students attempting to embody the Pardoner. Right, moving on. The assessments... I’m thinking a shorter essay on Virginia Woolf, focusing on her use of interior monologue, and then a group presentation on a chosen Modernist text. What do you think? The essays are good. But the group presentation... how will you ensure everyone contributes equally? Last year’s project on Victorian poetry was a disaster; half the group did all the work, the other half just stood around looking confused. Don’t remind me. I spent a week rewriting one group's presentation on Tennyson before I could even hand it in. I was considering a peer assessment element, where students mark each other's participation. A bit brutal, I know. Brutal, but potentially effective. I’ve read a few studies that suggest peer assessment, with proper guidance of course, can improve engagement. We definitely need to establish clear expectations upfront – what constitutes good contribution, what kind of support is required. Agreed. Right, onto food. I'm thinking we should order in tonight. I'm not feeling particularly inspired after battling with Joyce. Thai? Indian? Something that doesn't require any actual effort.

Honestly, this coffee machine is driving me mad. It hisses and groans like a disgruntled badger. I’ve tried everything Maureen suggested, descaling it three times, but it's still leaving a sludge at the bottom of the pot. It's supposed to relax me in the mornings, not give me a headache! Sludge, you say? Might need a whole new one then, Nan. Honestly, technology. Remember when a cup of tea was just a cup of tea? No fancy contraptions involved. Aye, simpler times. Though, the principles were the same – heat water, add leaves. It’s just…efficiency, eh? That's what they tell you. Promises of efficiency, ends up just making more mess. Like this whole move, really. Don't even start on the move, Michael. I'm still reeling from the removal quotes. Three of them, and they’re all astronomically high! I had visions of a couple of lads with a van and a bit of rope, not a fleet of trucks and a foreman! And storage…the storage costs are absolutely outrageous. Where are all these people finding the money to store their lives in metal boxes? Yeah, I had a look at some quotes myself. It's brutal. Did you factor in insurance for the storage unit? That’s another chunk. Have you considered getting a few more quotes? Maybe from smaller, local firms? It's bigger than just the money, though, isn’t it? Moving decades of belongings…it’s a symbolic thing. It's like…packing away pieces of your past. Precisely! And what am I going to  do  with all this stuff? I’ve kept everything. Every school report, every birthday card, every chipped teacup. Sentimental nonsense, my sister calls it. But it's  my  sentimental nonsense. It's not nonsense, Nan. It's your history. But maybe a ruthless cull is in order? You don’t need twenty-seven ceramic owls, do you? Very funny. You try parting with Bartholomew. He’s been watching over me since 1987! Anyway, enough about owls and storage. Did you hear about the latest in the Labour leadership? It's a right mess, isn’t it? A mess is putting it mildly. It's disheartening, truly. Used to think Labour stood for something…a bit of hope, a bit of fairness. Now it’s just… infighting and soundbites. I agree. It’s been sad to watch.

Right, so, "Basil." Seriously, Chloe? You’re naming your sourdough starter Basil? It sounds like a character from a Victorian novel. It does, doesn’t it? But it  works , alright? He's got a lovely, bubbly personality, Basil. And honestly, after calling my last one “Doughy Dave,” I felt I deserved something with a bit more…class. Plus, my nan always used to grow basil. It’s a connection. You’re both ridiculous. A bubbly personality? It’s flour and water, Chloe! My cafe, "The Heron’s Nest," is a much better name, I reckon. Evokes a sense of calm, you know? Like the river. Heron’s Nest, eh? Nicely done, Lara. We got a few of those back home, too. You know, along the Murray River… big, nasty buggers when they get hungry. Not exactly calming, though. This restaurant is eerily quiet, isn’t it? Feels like we’ve rented it out for the afternoon. Yeah, bit spooky. Good grub though, can’t fault it. Did you guys ever consider canal boat holidays, like, properly living on one? My aunt did it for a year. Said it was brilliant, but a lot of scrubbing. No way. I like my kitchen, thank you very much. I don't want to be dodging low bridges and scrubbing algae off a hull. Though, I  did  read something about canal boats being surprisingly kosher-friendly. Apparently, you can get all your ingredients delivered. Kosher canal boats? Seriously? That’s a niche market. I’d need a business plan for  that . Imagine the plates though, specifically designed for narrowboats. See? That's the sort of thing that keeps you up at night! Speaking of things that keep you up… I'm thinking about joining Fabric again. They changed the sound system apparently. Fabric? Still? Thought that was gone bust years ago. Though, good music does get you through a rough baking day. Remember that time I accidentally put salt instead of sugar in a batch of raspberry jam? Honestly, thought I was going to cry. Needed a serious club to forget about that. Oh god, Chloe, that's horrific! Sticky, salty jam... My Uncle Barry once put mustard on his pizza. Said it was a ‘culinary adventure’. We all just stared at him. Mustard on pizza? That's pretty wild. We have this weird thing in Australia, Vegemite and cheese toasties. It’s…an acquired taste.

“Right, so, listen to this. Liam messaged me.  Liam . From Tinder. The one with the, like, suspiciously posed gym pics.” “Oh,  him . The one you said looked like he photoshopped himself onto a motorbike? What did he say? Don't tell me he wants a date.” “He did! He wants to ‘grab a coffee and chat’. Chat about what? His biceps? I swear, if he starts talking about protein shakes…” She shudders theatrically. "Honestly, are all Tinder guys like that? It’s a plague, isn’t it? Remember that bloke I matched with, Mark? He spent the entire conversation describing his pet iguana." "Mark and his iguana! Proper legend, that was. Though I reckon you should go, Chloe. Coffee's free, innit? And you can just give him the ‘I’m not interested’ speech if he’s a right knob.” “Yeah, what Maisie said. A free coffee's never a bad thing, Liv! Besides, you never know, he might surprise you. Though, let’s be honest, the gym pic thing is a red flag the size of a football pitch.” "I'm just… wary, you know? Last time I went for coffee with someone from Tinder, he spent the entire time talking about his ex. Like, a  detailed  timeline of everything that went wrong. It was like a therapy session, but I was paying for the coffee." “See! That’s exactly what I'm afraid of! I just want a nice, normal bloke who can, like, hold a conversation that doesn’t involve bragging or trauma dumping.” “Speaking of trauma dumping, have you three heard about what happened at Sarah’s house this weekend?” “No! What? Did Greg finally blow a gasket after all those late-night gaming sessions?” “Worse, actually. Apparently, he decided to ‘improve’ the kitchen… with glitter paint.  Glitter paint  Maisie! The whole kitchen is shimmering. Apparently, Sarah’s threatening to seal him in the pantry.” “No way! Glitter paint? He’s taking the ‘sparkle’ thing a bit too far, isn't he? Poor Sarah. She’ll have glitter in her hair for weeks.” “Glastonbury all over again! Remember last year and the glitter explosion everywhere? I was finding it in my shoes for months. Honestly, living with boys… it’s a constant adventure. A slightly chaotic, very messy adventure.” “Tell me about it. At uni, Ben left a plate of lasagne in his room for a week.

Right then, Doris, you were saying about that fella on the telly last night? The one all riled up about the pensions? Aye, Arthur. That was Basil Fawlty, wasn't it? Only, seems a bit more worked up than usual, even for 'im. Saying the government's bleedin’ the pensioners dry. Something about the triple lock being a con. Oh, don’t listen to him, George. Basil’s got a face like thunder most of the time, hasn't he? Probably just missed his afternoon sherry. It’s a complex system, the triple lock. It’s supposed to protect us, you know. Supposed to, is it? Well, that’s the rub, Doris. ‘Supposed to’. They change things, don’t they? Like they did with the winter fuel allowance. Promised us the earth, then whittled it away bit by bit. Reminds me of that bypass they planned round Norwich back in '86. Promised it'd ease the traffic – never got built. Just a load of bother and a load of wasted council tax. Typical. You and your bypasses, George. Always bringing up the bypass. Remember old Mr. Higgins gettin’ all worked up about it too? Said it'd ruin the view from his prize-winning roses. Oh, Mr. Higgins. He was a character, wasn't he? Used to bring us cuttings, he did. I’ve got a lovely pot of geraniums now, thanks to him. But George has a point, you know. It’s about trust. You can't trust politicians. Never could, never will. They say one thing, do another. Exactly! They're all the same, aren’t they? Labour, Tory, Lib Dem…don’t make a blind bit of difference. It’s just one lot of swindlers replacing another. They’re all after your money, plain and simple. And us, we’re sitting here, reliant on these benefits. It's no way to live, is it? Well, what else are we supposed to do, George? You tried applying for jobs, didn’t you? Remember all that bother with the council? Saying your qualifications were ‘overqualified’ for a shelf-stacking position. Can you believe it? A civil engineer, deemed too clever for stacking shelves! Don't remind me. Felt like a right clown. They looked at my CV, saw I’d designed bridges and drainage systems, and figured I was a threat to their casual labour pool. Typical Norfolk, innit? Closed off, insular...

This is lovely, love. Really is. You’ve outdone yourself. Though, honestly, I’m still stuffed from that bit of cake Mrs. Henderson offered after bridge this afternoon. Honestly, the woman! Always pushing sweets on you. Mrs. Henderson and her relentless sugar mountain. You'd think she was running a bakery, not a bridge club. Did you win today? Absolutely not. Lost miserably. Agnes got a spectacular hand. You know Agnes; always a bit smug when she’s winning. I swear, she’s practicing. It’s not a natural talent, that. Not like you at darts, always steady. Practice makes perfect, love. And Agnes probably has been playing longer than you have. So, how was the rest of it? Did you have a good natter? Anything interesting happening in the bridge world? Not particularly. Carol was going on about her grandson's football team again - apparently they're contenders for the league this year. Honestly, I don't understand the obsession. It's just kicking a ball about. But she was positively beaming about it. You know how she gets. Work’s been… work. Same old, same old. The new marketing campaign’s heading nowhere fast. They seem determined to stick with this terrible colour scheme. Bright orange and lime green! Who even  likes  that combination? Sounds dreadful. What are they thinking? You tried suggesting a change, didn't you? Of course, I did! But Mr. Davies just patted me on the hand and said, “We’re going with ‘youthful vibrancy,’ Sarah. It’s what the research says.” The research probably conducted by a chimpanzee with a crayon, if you ask me. It’s just… frustrating. I put so much effort into it, and it feels like it's being ignored. It’s always the way, isn’t it? People in charge often think they know best. At least you're fighting the good fight. Fundraising’s been a bit calmer today. Managed to secure a small grant from the Rotary Club for the children’s playground revamp. Nothing huge, but every little bit helps. That's brilliant, love! You're making such a difference. The playground really does need doing. Poor little ones have to dodge rusty swings and splintered benches. Are the kids settled alright? I haven't seen Sophie and Tom all week. They've been swamped with university deadlines, haven’t they? They are. Sophie’s got a massive essay due on the impact of Romantic poetry on modern advertising.

Honestly, this rain. It's relentless. Tarnow’s usually… calmer, weather-wise. Feels like a perpetual English November, doesn't it? Not that I'm used to sunshine anymore, of course. Aye, it's proper grim. Makes Bury seem bright by comparison, which is saying something. Just saw a picture on Instagram – me mum’s garden back home. Roses are still blooming! Can you believe it? It's bizarre. And I’m freezing just looking at it. Roses in October? Remarkable. You're braving it then, going back for Uncle George, aren’t you? Dreadful news, that. Must be tough. It is. It’s just…everything is tough, isn’t it? Booking the flights was a nightmare. Ryanair's pricing is, well, shocking. And then dealing with the funeral directors… it just piles up. I feel like I’ve been dodging a cold for weeks, too. Everything feels… heavy. Oh, my dear. I know that feeling all too well. The weight of things. You take care of yourself, love. A good cup of tea and plenty of rest. Remember what the doctor said after your awful bout of flu last year? Easy for you to say, you’re mastering the art of ‘plenty of rest’ permanently! Honestly, I envy you sometimes. This whole TEFL thing… it's good money, I suppose, but it’s exhausting. The children's classes are utter chaos, and dealing with the parents… ugh. I dreamt last night I was being chased by a horde of five-year-olds demanding biscuits. I do remember wanting something to  do . Remember when we were little, and we pretended we were explorers? Hunting for treasure in the Cam? I always wanted to be an archaeologist, you know. Digging up history. Something… tangible. You always did. You were good at it, too – meticulous and observant. I was always the one dashing off on some wild goose chase. Actually, thinking about it, teaching is a bit like archaeology in a way. You’re uncovering knowledge, piece by piece. Though I suspect slightly fewer snakes. A valid point. This teaching thing… does it feel like home to you, then? Being away from Bury, I mean. This… life. That’s a tricky one. Poland is…nice. Beautiful, even. So much history here. And the people are lovely. But… it’s not  home , is it? Not really. Bury will always be Bury. It's the familiarity, I think.

Honestly, this Earl Grey is a bit weak, innit? You’d think a proper London pub could manage a decent cuppa. Still, beats the rain outside. It’s alright. Better than instant, at least. And the rain's rather dramatic, wouldn't you say? Adds to the atmosphere. How's the copywriting going? Still battling with those avocado toast descriptions? You know it. They want “evocative,” “rustic,” “Instagrammable.” I’m pretty sure "it’s mashed avocado on bread" is the most accurate description, but apparently that doesn't sell. The client wants me to describe the  feeling  of eating it. I’m genuinely losing the will to live. Had to come here for a proper breather. Oh, I feel you. Client briefs can be the absolute worst. Remember when I had to write a blurb about… what was it? Luxury dog beds? Apparently, Fido deserves a "bespoke slumber experience.” Oh, my god, no! You're having a laugh! Seriously though, is the survey programming keeping you sane? Is that still paying the bills? Yeah, it’s alright. It’s not exactly intellectually stimulating, but it pays pretty well, thankfully. Plus, it means I can afford to actually  eat , unlike some of us who are living off Tesco meal deals. I was thinking we could grab some proper lunch later, somewhere nice? My treat. Seriously? You’d do that? That’d be amazing, yeah. I’m proper skint at the moment. That freelance life, eh? One month you're swimming in it, the next you’re counting pennies. Speaking of skint… have you heard from Amelia lately? She was moaning about her rent last time we spoke. Not recently, no. I think she's still trying to scrape together the deposit for that flat share in Hackney. Poor thing. She's been working ridiculous hours at the vintage shop. I saw her Instagram – she looks absolutely knackered. We should try and catch up with her soon. Maybe next week? Yeah, definitely. We should! She needs a proper night out. And maybe some financial advice, if she’ll let us. Actually, on the subject of needing advice... have you made any progress with getting settled in for your postgraduate studies? Still living back home in Oxford? Almost. I’m moving into a flat in Bloomsbury next Friday! It's tiny, but it's mine. And it's a  lot  closer to the university.

Right, that’s enough. Honestly, you two are going to be the death of me. Five am? Seriously? But Mummy! The sun’s up! And Percy wants to practice his tightrope walk! Me too! Can we, can we? Please, Mummy? Percy, darling, the sun's only  just  up. It’s barely light. And a tightrope walk involving the kitchen chairs is a  very  bad idea. Remember last time? But I almost didn’t fall! I nearly made it all the way across. Liam cheated, he bumped me. He did not! I saw him. He was trying to help. Strategically repositioning you. Strategically repositioning. That's a good one, Liam. Alright, alright, no tightrope walking  inside . Perhaps we can see about the garden later, if the weather holds. But right now, let’s all eat something before we get into any more ambitious acrobatics. Are you two hungry? Starving! Can I have rainbow sprinkles on my porridge? Please, please, please? I want sausages! And pancakes! With maple syrup! Right, both of you are trying to kill me with requests before I've even finished my coffee. Sprinkles are a maybe. Sausages and pancakes... potentially. But you need to eat your porridge  first . And Liam, stop building a fort out of cereal boxes. It’s going to collapse. Mummy, have you ever been to a circus? Of course! When I was a little girl. We went to see Cirque du Soleil once. It was incredible! All those amazing aerialists. Aerialists? Like… flying people? Exactly! And clowns, and jugglers, and… well, lots of amazing things. We're going to the Neon Moon event next month remember? Ooh, yeah! With the glow sticks! Will there be jugglers? I think so! They've got some really talented performers lined up. I saw a preview online. One of the acts is doing some incredible balancing… it’s kind of like tightrope walking, but with… well, you'll see. It’s much better. My tower is going to be taller than a circus tent! I hope so, darling. Just be careful it doesn’t fall on the cat. Right then, so, plans for today. After breakfast, I was thinking we could pop down to the village shop for some bits and bobs. And then, if the sun's out, maybe a walk in the fields? Can we look for fairies? We can certainly  look  for fairies. Though I can’t guarantee we’ll  find  any.

Honestly, David, this constant doom and gloom about the Conservatives… it’s exhausting. I know you feel strongly, but can’t we just enjoy the scenery for a bit? Look at that field – the light on the gorse is gorgeous. Enjoy the scenery, Eleanor? When the country’s hurtling towards… well, let’s just say something unsettling? It’s difficult. And it’s not just the Conservatives, is it? It's the whole system. The entrenched power structures. You know, back in Nantyglo… things were simpler. Difficult, yes, but simpler. A community pulling together. Grandad, you always say that. Everything was simpler back in Nantyglo. Remember when you tried to convince us you single-handedly won the village fete egg-and-spoon race? Rhys! That was a masterful display of athleticism! And the competition was fierce, I’ll have you know. It was a turning point, really. Showed the younger generation that grit and determination could overcome anything. Reminds me a bit of what we need now, really. A bit of… of Welsh grit in Westminster. Welsh grit and a hefty dose of realism, I suspect. But honestly, are we really going to dissect the political landscape whilst hurtling through Devon? I’m trying to concentrate on this roundabout. Right, right. Roundabouts. A modern plague, those are. Speaking of things that plague me... this whole Brexit thing. Still can't fathom how so many people voted for it. It feels like a collective act of historical amnesia. We’ve spent centuries building connections, trading, forging allegiances… and then  poof . Well, some people genuinely believed it was the right thing for the country, Grandad. And maybe they had a point, even if I don’t agree. Ignoring their concerns isn’t helpful. I’m not ignoring their concerns, Rhys. I’m simply… bewildered. My father, bless him, he worked in the steelworks in Ebbw Vale. A staunch Labour man. He'd be horrified to see the state of the industry now. And the impact of those decisions… it ripples outwards, doesn't it? It does. And it’s not just the Brexit vote. Look at the cost of living crisis. They’re completely out of touch. Remember when I was editing that book on Truss's short time as prime minister? The sheer bafflement of the authors! They couldn't quite believe how a politician could be so… detached. Can we talk about something else?

Right, so, I was thinking about those Helen Moss stories you two love. The ones about the mischievous pixie, Pipkin, who swaps everyone's shoes. Remember? Pipkin! Yes! He put Grandma's slippers on the dog last time! It was funny! And he put Daddy's big boots on the cat! The cat looked  so  silly! Did you see it, Rosie? I did indeed, Finn. It was a picture. And that's given me an idea. What if Pipkin doesn’t just swap shoes? What if he swaps… personalities? Really? Like, what? Well, imagine! Mummy wakes up and she's got Finn's dinosaur obsession. All she wants to do is roar and stomp around! And I’m Mummy! I have to make breakfast and tell everyone to be quiet! That would be  amazing ! Exactly! Or imagine I woke up and I was you, Finn. I’d be running around pretending to be a T-Rex all morning. No marking essays, just roaring! You’d be a very silly Teacher, Rosie! Probably! But what would Pipkin do  that  day? What would be the big problem he’d cause by swapping our personalities? Maybe he’d swap the Teacher's voice with a frog’s! Ribbit! Ribbit! Oh, Finn, you’re brilliant! A frog-voiced teacher trying to teach phonics. That's chaos! It’s definitely better than just shoes. Do you know what, I’m going to write this down. I might actually try and get it down on paper. Can I help? I can draw Pipkin! He has to have sparkly wings! Absolutely! Sparkly wings are essential. And Finn, you can tell me all about what a T-Rex teacher would  do . We’ll make it a whole series! Imagine, “Pipkin's Personality Pranks!” Can he swap Mr. Henderson's voice too? The one from school? Oh, Finn! That's a dangerous suggestion! Mr. Henderson's voice is a force of nature already! Although... what if Pipkin swapped him with a very quiet mouse? A squeaky mouse! Then he’d have to whisper all his instructions! Yes! Perfect! You two are seriously inspiring me. Speaking of stories, I was thinking of going to the Linton Book Festival next month. It's got a children’s author talk, and they have a storytelling tent. Would you two fancy going? A real book festival? Like in a story? Sort of! It's full of books and people who write them and tell stories.

Honestly, I'm feeling really guilty about this curry. It smells amazing, but every time I cook something so heavily veggie, I’m reminded of…everything. Everything being? The existential dread of our consumption habits? Because I feel you. It’s hard not to. Especially with all the stuff about cultured meat coming out. Shmeat, you mean. Sounds like something out of a sci-fi film. I saw an article the other day about how they’re getting closer to scaling up production. It’s wild. Still feels a bit… dystopian, though. Exactly! And ethically… it's not a simple answer, is it? Like, on the one hand, no more factory farming, massive win. On the other hand, are we just creating another layer of technological dependence? Another potential point of control? I think it’s complex. I mean, the animal cruelty aspect is huge. I spent a few shifts at that sanctuary last month, you know, with the rescued pigs… It just reaffirmed for me that we don't  need  to eat them. The sheer suffering... It’s horrifying. Absolutely. It’s not just the slaughterhouses either. Think about the land used to raise livestock, the deforestation, the methane emissions… it’s contributing to climate change at an alarming rate. It's another level of oppression, really, isn't it? Oppressing the environment, the animals… It's all intertwined, isn’t it? I was reading somewhere that even eating a purely plant-based diet still has an environmental impact, though, because of transportation and farming practices. It's compounding. Makes me want to just… take a vitamin tablet and disappear. Dramatic much? Though, I get it. I've been supplementing with B12 for ages. Pretty sure I’m more efficient at absorbing it now than I ever was. You should consider it, Elara. Especially with your tendency to forget about proper meals when you're on shift. I know, I know. Mum's been on at me. She keeps sending me links to articles about the importance of iron too. She's convinced I'm anemic, even though the last blood test said I was totally fine. Honestly, sometimes I think her anxiety manifests as nutritional advice. My aunt's the same. Constantly suggesting I take cod liver oil. It tastes like sadness and disappointment. So, shmeat… Imagine, cultured steak, no cows harmed. Would you eat it? I… I don’t know.

Right then, almost ready. How was your day, David? Did you manage to wrestle that budget into submission? Don’t even  ask . It was a proper battle, Sarah. Young Tom in accounts, bless his cotton socks, tried to convince me we needed a new ergonomic chair for every single employee. Ergonomic! As if they’re all doing back-breaking warehouse work. I told him to stick to spreadsheets and leave the furniture decisions to me. Honestly, the younger generation… Sounds stressful, Uncle David. I'm starving, by the way. What are we having? It smells amazing. Lamb stew, love. Proper hearty stuff. Needed after a day like yours too, I imagine. Still battling those social media algorithms, are you? Pretty much. They’re changing something  again . It's like they  want  me to pull my hair out. I was trying to get some traction for a new campaign, and it just... vanished. Poof. Gone. Wasted hours. Seriously considering setting up a little Etsy shop and just selling handmade candles. Less stressful. Candles, eh? That's a bit of a shift from copywriting, isn't it? Your mum would be thrilled, though. Always going on about supporting small businesses. She would, wouldn’t she? She’d be making you little lavender pouches to go with everything. Remember that time she tried to teach the French exchange student how to say "pass the biscuits"? It was a disaster. He ended up saying something that sounded suspiciously like "pass the eels." Oh, God, yes! I remember that! He went bright red. Poor thing. Mum's pronunciation... let's just say it’s unique. She’s convinced ‘squirrel’ is pronounced ‘squirl’. It's a family trait, I think. I still struggle with “rural.” Comes out like "rooral." It’s embarrassing when I'm talking to the planning committee. Don’t worry, nobody notices. They’re too busy arguing about the placement of lampposts. Speaking of embarrassing… have you seen the state of the washing machine? It's making this awful clunking noise. I think something’s come loose. Oh, no! Not again. Last time, it left blue dye all over everything. Remember Dad’s white shirts? They looked like Smurfs. Don't remind me. I swore I'd buy a new one, but Sarah keeps saying it's "perfectly functional." Perfectly functional and threatening to ruin my wardrobe, more like. It is! Well, mostly. Just needs a little… encouragement.

Honestly, you two. Butterfly forks. Really? I spent a fortune on proper silverware, and all you want are the novelty ones. It's supper with O and I, not a children's tea party. But Mum, they’re cool! I found them in the drawer. And O likes butterflies. Remember? Yeah, and I’m pretty sure I saw some dragon ones too. Maybe we can get those out for O? It’d be a theme! Butterfly and dragon supper. Right, that’s it. No novelty forks tonight. We are having a civilised meal. Especially given the…the solemnity of the day. Two minutes of silence. Do you even understand why we’re doing that? Yeah, Mum. Remembrance Day. For the people who died in wars. My history teacher, Mr. Davies, was really going on about it. Said it’s important not to forget. Is it about Russia too? I heard something about that on the news. Something about the war there. Partially, yes. It's about remembering all conflicts. And yes, it's particularly poignant given the situation in Ukraine. Two minutes of silence allows us to reflect on the sacrifices made, and to consider the ongoing suffering. It’s not just about poppies, you know. It’s about empathy and understanding. So, like, thinking about people who don’t have butterfly forks? Precisely. A very eloquent summation, actually. Look, the point is, we’re lucky. We have a roof over our heads, we have food on the table, and we have forks, albeit non-butterfly ones. Let’s remember that. And let’s be quiet for two minutes. Properly quiet. Okay. But… my birthday’s next week. Can I have a butterfly fork then? Just for my cake? We'll see. We'll definitely see. Your birthday is something to celebrate, yes. But timing is everything, isn’t it? Speaking of birthdays, your Uncle David called earlier. Apparently, he’s trying to learn Russian. Really? Why? He said he wants to be able to read Dostoevsky in the original. Apparently, he thinks the nuances get lost in translation. Bit ambitious, if you ask me. He’s always been a bit of a showman. Does that mean Russia is like, important for reading? Like Shakespeare is for England? That’s a really insightful question, actually. In a way, yes. Russian literature has shaped the world. Tolstoy, Chekhov, Pushkin… They explored ideas about humanity, faith, and suffering in ways that still resonate today.

Right then, Operation Holiday Brainstorm is officially underway! So, Cornwall, Adventure Island, or V&A? Thoughts, anyone? Adventure Island! Please, please, please! With the pirate ship! And the big wheel! I want to win a giant teddy! Cornwall... beaches... sandcastles... big waves! See? Two very different approaches. Adventure Island is brilliant for a day out, definitely, but it's...intense. And the queues! Remember last time? We practically aged a decade standing in line for the log flume. Cornwall is lovely, but it's more of a proper holiday, isn’t it? A week of relaxation. Although, the weather is always a gamble, isn't it? But the pirate ship! It goes  really  high! And you can see the sea! I know, pet. It's fantastic. But think about it – Cornwall has cream teas! And pasties! And we could build a  massive  sandcastle. Maybe even find some crabs! Crabs? Can we keep one? We can look for one, darling, but keeping it… well, they need to be in the sea, don't they? They wouldn't be very happy in a paddling pool. Cornwall sounds boring. Pirate ships are much more exciting. Boring?! Cornwall is full of adventure! Imagine exploring smugglers’ tunnels! And seeing seals! We could go surfing lessons, or coasteering if you're feeling brave. Coasteering? What's that? It’s like...climbing and scrambling along the rocks by the sea. With a grown-up helping you, of course! Anyway, before this spirals out of control… how about we compromise? One day at Adventure Island, and then a few days in Cornwall? We could do both! Really? Adventure Island  and  Cornwall? Possibly. If your dad agrees. It does mean more expense, you know. Speaking of, I need to look at those gluten-free pasties they do in St Ives. Remember how poorly you were feeling last time, love? We need to be really careful this year. Will I be poorly again? No, sweetheart. We’ll get delicious gluten-free pasties – maybe even some dairy-free ones too, just in case. We’ll be fine. It’s just something we have to keep an eye on. Can we have ice cream? Of course, you can have ice cream. Gluten-free, dairy-free, or regular? The possibilities are endless! Although… …this stew needs a bit more seasoning. I’m so tired, though. Marking those A-Level essays has completely wiped me out. Honestly, some of them… the arguments are just nonsensical.

Ugh, Mr. Davies really set us up for failure with that history essay. Seriously, ‘Analyze the socio-economic impact of the Enclosure Acts on rural communities’. Who even  thinks  of a question like that? Tell me about it! I spent, like, three hours last night just trying to define “socio-economic.” It’s not something you really learn organically, is it? My mum just kept saying “Google it, Liam!” as if that’s a helpful answer. My dad tried to help, but he just went on a massive tangent about farming. Apparently, he knew a guy who knew a guy who was affected by the Enclosure Acts. It was all… rambling. I ended up more confused than when I started. Classic dad move. Mine just kept trying to relate it to football. "Think of it like the team losing their stadium, Finn! Where do they play then? What happens to the fans?" It's not the same, Dad! Seriously! Anyway, I'm thinking I'll just focus on the peasant uprisings. Seems a bit easier to grasp than the whole complex economic thing. Smart. I'm probably going to waffle on about the workers going to the cities, becoming factory workers, and then feeling exploited. Pretty standard stuff, I guess. Mrs. Patel seems to like the standard. True. She's got that look, you know? The 'I want to see a well-structured argument, not your existential crisis' look. Definitely. I saw you in maths today, though. You were giving Mark Jenkins a proper earful. What was that about? Long story. He kept messing about, bouncing a pen off my head while I was trying to work out those ridiculous quadratic equations. I told him, once. He did it again. I might have raised my voice a little. A little? You nearly made Mr. Singh have a heart attack. He looked like he was going to suspend you. I know, I know! I just… sometimes he does it on purpose. He  knows  I hate being distracted. I swear, that kid thrives on chaos. You need to report him to one of the prefects. Sarah Miller's pretty solid, right? She takes things seriously. Yeah, but she's always hanging around with Chloe and her crew. They're all so… intense. Like they're trying to  be  prefects, you know? It’s a bit cringe. Tell me about it. Do you think they even  like  cycling?

Honestly, this road's a nightmare. Proper pot-holed, isn't it? Makes you bounce about like a bairn in a bouncy castle. You’d think they'd do summat about it. Sunderland's roads are bad enough, but this… this is just criminal. It's not ideal, no. Hertfordshire isn't exactly known for its pristine infrastructure. Though, to be fair, this stretch is a bit worse than most. It's on the repair schedule, apparently. Apparently? Yeah, that’s what they always say. "Apparently." That word’s gotten a right good workout today, hasn’t it? Apparently we’re going to have a nice evening. Apparently the weather's supposed to hold. Apparently this road is being fixed. It’s just… typical, innit? Promises, promises. Makes you want to take your bike. You thinking of dusting off the Ridley? It would be quicker, certainly, dodging all these craters. Though, with the wind picking up, it might be a bit of a slog. Aye, I was. Was having a wee think about it. Might need a new inner tube, though. Last time I rode it, felt like I’d got a dodgy one, practically flat by the time I got to Ryhope. Honestly, these things, they can go at any minute. Just like you - expecting a calm ride, then bam, puncture. Very poetic analogy, love. You should write it down. I could give your bike a quick look over before you commit to a ride. I’ve got that little pump and tyre lever in the boot somewhere. Engineer’s instinct – always gotta tinker. You're a lifesaver, honestly. Always were. Speaking of tinkering, did you catch the cricket yesterday? Proper embarrassing, wasn't it? Root’s been looking absolutely knackered. Awful. Just awful. The batting lineup needs a complete overhaul. They're reliant on too few players. Crawley's got to start delivering, and Stokes… well, he's doing his best, bless him, but he can’t win the game single-handedly. It’s demoralising, isn’t it? Demoralising is putting it lightly! Gets yer blood boiling, doesn’t it? They’re supposed to be the best. Remember when we'd watch it with me grandad? Sunday afternoons, cups of tea, biscuit crumbs everywhere. Proper memories. Now it’s just… a train wreck. Yeah, those were the days. Simpler times. Although, you know, even back then, England weren’t always winning.

Honestly, this menu is a nightmare. They’ve changed it again. Everything seems to have a different sauce option now. Sweet and sour, hong shao, curry…how am I supposed to choose? It's decision paralysis! Just pick something, Liv. We’re starving. And they’re about to score! Which, by the way, is amazing. “Just pick something”? Easy for you to say, Mr. Prefers-Anything-With-Meat-And-Soy-Sauce. This is a culinary decision! It affects the entire evening. I want flavour, I want texture, I want…surprise! Oh, you're ordering? Excellent. I'm utterly famished. Seriously, I've been staring at spreadsheets all day trying to craft the perfect bid narrative. My brain feels like mush. Any recommendations? That’s what I’m trying to figure out! And you, Maisie, waltz in here demanding recommendations when you haven't even offered to help decipher this menu hieroglyphics! Sorry! I was just in the zone. Intense focus. Besides, you’re usually the culinary adventurer. You always find the obscure dishes everyone else is too scared to try. Remember that crispy duck with plum sauce you discovered last year? Divine! You’re both overthinking it. Kung Pao chicken is always a winner. Reliable. Solid. Gets the job done. Like a good defender. See? Football analogy. Kung Pao is fine, but it’s... predictable. I was thinking maybe the Eggplant in Garlic Sauce? But then I’m worried it'll be too gloopy. What do you think, Maisie? You’re the expert. Hmm, Eggplant in Garlic Sauce can be risky. Sometimes it's amazing, sometimes it's just… eggplant-y. Alright, let's play it safe then. They do a really good Lemon Chicken, don’t they? I liked that last time. Nice and zesty. Lemon Chicken? Seriously? That’s basically fried chicken with lemon juice. You can get that anywhere. It's not  just  fried chicken with lemon juice, Ben! It's got a lovely, slightly sweet glaze. And it's considerably less horrific than trying to navigate this ridiculous sauce labyrinth. He’s got a point, though. It’s a bit… bland. I do love a good mapo tofu, but I’m not sure they do it authentically here. Last time I ordered it, it tasted like it had been made with ketchup. Ketchup?! That's an abomination! You should've sent it back. I did! But they just said they were "out of fermented bean curd" which, honestly, is the most British excuse for a culinary failure I’ve ever heard.

Right then, Annie, you were saying about the pressures at the Royal? Sounds like absolute madness, doesn't it? I read something the other day about waiting lists... astronomical. Makes you wonder how anyone gets proper care. Astronomical is putting it mildly, Karl. It’s bordering on inhumane. We're seeing people having to wait months, sometimes over a year, for specialist appointments. And that’s just the appointments, never mind the actual treatment. It’s got so much worse, really. I’ve been here fifteen years, and I’ve never seen it this bad. They're constantly asking us to see more patients, quicker, with fewer resources. It’s not sustainable. I can imagine. Academia’s got its own pressures, of course. Funding cuts, student expectations... a constant battle to justify existing, you know? But at least I'm not dealing with people's physical suffering directly. It must be soul-destroying, feeling like you’re constantly firefighting. It is. It really is. Especially when you  can’t  do what you want to do for people. There’s a lovely young lad, Jamie, came in last week. Had a nasty cough, suspected bronchitis. Simple enough, usually. But no antibiotics available on the ward. Protocol. Apparently, they're trying to combat antibiotic resistance. Fair enough, in principle, but what about  him ? I had to send him home with paracetamol and advice to rest. I felt dreadful. Crikey. That’s rough. They've got those things, haven’t they? Those Delayed Discharge protocols? Where they’re holding people in beds who are medically fit, just because there's nowhere else for them to go. Oh, don't get me started on Delayed Discharge! It's turned the whole system on its head. We’re full of people who could be at home with a bit of support, but they’re blocking beds for people who  need  them. And the social workers… they're stretched so thin. It's a domino effect. It’s a right mess, innit? Still, you're doing good work, Annie. You're on the front line. Trying to. Speaking of front lines, have you seen what Mrs. Peterson's doing with her front garden? Honestly, Karl. It's an eyesore. Plastic flamingos, gnomes, wind chimes... the lot. It's like Blackpool illuminations, but with garden ornaments. Oh, aye. I noticed. Rather… exuberant, isn’t she? Always a lot of shouting, too.

Right then, Arthur, you were saying about that fella down the street, young Liam, yeah? The police were 'round again weren't they? Aye, they were. Shouting match, apparently. Something about music too loud. Kids, eh? Always pushin’ boundaries. Though, Liam’s a good lad, really. Bit rough ‘round the edges, mind. Just needs a bit o' guidance. This area...it ain’t easy, is it? Not for the youngsters. No, it isn't. It’s a challenge, that’s for sure. I was reading an article the other day about the strain on social services. They're stretched thin, desperately so. Welfare cuts haven't helped, have they? Putting more pressure on families, forcing young lads like Liam into… well, difficult situations. Welfare! Don't even get me started on that. Back in my day, at least you got a bit of respect. Now, they treat you like you're leeching off the system. Never worked a day in me life, as you know, but I always felt…a bit more worthy, if you get me meanin’. Now it’s just suspicion and paperwork. Endless paperwork. I understand the sentiment. The bureaucracy can be suffocating. It’s not about dignity, is it? It's about ticking boxes. Though, I’ve seen some incredible work done by social workers, under tremendous pressure. They’re heroes, really, the unsung ones. Heroes? The only heroes I’ve seen are the ones fightin’ in the war, son. These days… it’s all about politics. This immigration business, for example. They’re blinkered, the lot of ‘em. Bringing folks over, expecting them to just slot right in. It's a recipe for chaos, I tell you. Arthur, I appreciate your views, but I think you're oversimplifying things. It's more complicated than that. People come here for all sorts of reasons - seeking refuge, opportunity… Refuge? Opportunity? There’s plenty of opportunity if you're willin' to work for it! My da, he worked the docks. Hard graft, it was, but it put food on the table. No handouts, just elbow grease. This generation… they expect everything on a plate. Times have changed, Arthur. The docks are gone. The kind of work your father did, that's largely disappeared. And it wasn't always easy for  him , was it? I’ve read accounts from the era. Gruelling conditions, long hours... Aye, it was hard. But it built character!

Aye, this is alright, I suppose. Not like me Nan's stottie cake, mind you. Nothing ever is. Though, posh salad in Cambridge... who'd 'ave thought it? It's perfectly acceptable, Chloe. And Cambridge  is  known for its nice things. Don't knock it until you've tried the punks. Are you settling in alright for the conference? Everything running smoothly with the corpus data? Smooth-ish. The sheer volume of it is a bit… overwhelming. I thought I were prepared, but there’s just so much to wrangle. Especially with the new annotation project, the one focusing on regional dialects. Makes me feel a bit like a hypocrite, really, going on about North East dialects when I'm buried in data from everywhere else. That’s fascinating though, isn’t it? Your perspective would be invaluable, Chloe. You practically  live  amongst the data of North East speech patterns. Don’t feel guilty! It's a strength, not a weakness. So, are they letting you feed any of your own observations in? They’re saying they are, Lucy. But it’s all about quantifiable metrics, isn’t it? They want numbers, percentages, frequency of usage. Hard to put a number on the way a word feels, you know? Like ‘canny’. It doesn’t just mean ‘okay’ up north. It's a whole vibe. A whole backstory. You’re describing the elusive ‘affect’ versus ‘effect’ debate all over again, aren't you? Quantifying nuance is always a challenge. Especially with something as fluid and subjective as language. This reminds me of a project I was working on in Philly, trying to categorize the different uses of "jawn." Utterly impossible! "Jawn?" What's a jawn? Sounds like something you'd buy from a sweet shop. It’s… well, it's everything. It can be a person, a place, a thing. It's incredibly versatile. It’s Philly slang, you know. It's the reason I have a permanently confused expression. Sounds wonderfully complex. Chloe, you’re right to feel a bit frustrated with the rigid metrics. Perhaps you can suggest a more qualitative approach as well? Just a thought. I 'ave, actually. Sent a few emails. Got a bit of a polite brush-off, to be honest. They're set in their ways, these researchers. Fancy words and complicated diagrams, that's what they like. Don't let it get you down.

Right then, where were we? Oh yes, you were saying your research into online dialects – fascinating stuff, really. It's all moving so fast, innit? I mean, you barely recognise the abbreviations people are using these days. Back in my day, "LOL" was practically a declaration of genuine amusement, now it’s just…sprinkled in everywhere. Exactly! It’s become a near-obligatory filler. And the regional variations online are incredible. I’ve been tracking how younger people in Hull are incorporating phrases and spellings that wouldn’t have existed twenty years ago. It’s adapting faster than spoken language in some cases.
