Makes you wonder what the future of linguistic study will look like, doesn't it? Less focus on place, and more on platform? Proper mind-bending, that. Reminds me of a conversation I had with one of my students, bless ‘im. Bright lad, from Bristol originally. He was explaining the nuances of 'peng' - you know, meaning attractive. I’m trying to keep up, I really am, but it feels like I’m learning a foreign language. Want to know the funny bit? He then casually dropped “innit” into explaining the origins of the word. A proper Bristolian-London hybrid. Oh, that’s brilliant! The layers of influence. It's like linguistic palimpsest – different layers of meaning over time. Did you try to explain that concept to him? It would have been a prime teaching moment! Tried, didn't I? Went right over his ‘ead, I think. He just gave me a look like I was speaking Martian. Honestly, teaching medieval Anglo-Saxon to undergraduates sometimes feels easier. At least they're confronted with a language they're not  supposed  to understand! You're brave, tackling Anglo-Saxon! My wife’s German, and even  she  says it sounds like cats fighting. We watched a documentary the other week about the origins of the Germanic languages. Fascinating how much influence Old English had on German, even though it’s so different now. Has it changed your perspective on your own research in any way? Actually, it has, a bit. It's reinforced the idea that language is constantly shifting, of course, but also that there are long, deep currents underneath the surface – influences that stretch back centuries. Thinking about the roots of words, you start to see patterns, connections… it’s a bit like unearthing an archaeological dig, isn’t it?

Right then, love. Grandparents due any minute, aren’t they? Did you get the biscuits out, Ben? Chocolate digestives, like Gran likes? Aye, Nana. Got 'em. And the shortbread for Grandad, too. Did you remember to put the heating up a bit? He’s always moaning it’s nippy. Course I did, lad. Wouldn’t want him catching a chill. Malton’s a bit colder than Hull, you know. Used to grumble about the cold myself when I were a lass visiting my auntie up 'ere. Not like our nice, sheltered East Riding. Speaking of sheltered, did you tell your auntie Sheila not to bring that blasted wind chime again? Last time it nearly drove Grandad mad! Told her. She said she’d leave it in the car. But you know her, she’ll probably ‘forget’. Oh, my goodness, is that telly blaring already? Can scarcely hear myself think! All this modern technology… back in my day, we had the wireless and we were grateful for it! Don’t you start, Elsie. Always moaning. It’s only a bit of background noise. More noise from those blasted tractors down the road! Now, now, both of you! No need for moaning. It’s lovely to see you both. Elsie, you’re looking as bright as a button! And Arthur, did you manage to get your slippers on okay? Ben’s made a proper fuss with the biscuits, so you’ll be sorted. Biscuits, eh? Chocolate digestives, you say? Well, that’s a start. Though nothing beats a good cup of strong tea. Your tea’s always been lovely, Margaret. Better than most, I reckon. Tea’s alright. I’d like a bit of that shortbread though. My knees are aching something awful today. Must be this damp weather. Can I get you both drinks, then? Nana made a fresh pot. That’d be grand, Ben. Thank you, love. Arthur, do you want milk and sugar? Just how you like it. And Elsie, no sugar for you, as always. Keeps your teeth nice and sparkley, you said? Sparkley as a new penny, I am. Though I’m not so sure about my knees. They’re protesting something fierce today. Reminds me of the time I fell down Mrs. Higgins’ well when I was a girl... Fell down the well? Elsie, you told that story last Christmas! Well, it's a good story, Arthur!

Oh, look at this! Remember Sarah’s disastrous attempt at recreating that Korean street food stall at her birthday? The kimchi fried rice was… an experience, wasn’t it? An experience is putting it mildly. More like a biohazard. She really did commit, though. Bless her. It’s amazing she even  tried  frying rice in her tiny kitchen. Did she ever figure out the right rice-to-gochujang ratio? I doubt it. Apparently, the fire alarm went off three times. She sent me a frantic text saying she was considering ordering pizza instead. And then she posted a selfie covered in red pepper flakes, looking utterly defeated. Classic Sarah. She’s not one to give up easily, despite everything. She’s got grit, that one. Makes me wonder if any of the other lot are thinking about doing a reunion. It’s been far too long. I was just thinking that! I miss them all dreadfully. Especially Liam. He sends the occasional email, very formal and professional, full of academic jargon. Doesn’t exactly scream ‘wild student days,’ does he? Remember that time he tried to convince us all that falconry was a legitimate hobby? Oh, goodness. He was so serious about it. Armed with that ridiculous leather glove and a pamphlet about raptor care. He looked like a character out of a Jane Austen novel. Did he ever actually get a falcon? I don’t think so. His dad put his foot down, apparently. Something about the logistics of keeping a bird of prey in a terraced house in Clapham. It was a lot. Anyway, I was looking at some photos from that summer trip to Italy… remember Florence? How could I forget? We ate gelato for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. My waistband hasn't forgiven me. The Uffizi was incredible, though. I still get chills thinking about seeing Botticelli's 'Birth of Venus' in person. Absolutely. And that tiny restaurant tucked away down a side street? The one with the checkered tablecloths and the grumpy waiter who didn’t speak a word of English? That was  the  best pasta I’ve ever had. I’ve been trying to recreate that sauce ever since, with zero success. You need to find a good supplier of San Marzano tomatoes – that’s the key. And don't skimp on the basil. Fresh, fragrant basil. Honestly, sometimes I think we should just move to Italy.

Ugh, mornings. Proper state I'm in. Last night was…a lot. Tell me about it! My head feels like someone’s been using it as a football. Though, to be fair, watching the lads play wasn't exactly a relaxing pre-drinks activity either. You were at the match? Didn't realise. I thought you said you were going to that indie gig? Nah, cancelled that. Liam dragged me along. He’s obsessed, bless him. Honestly, the chanting… it’s just noise, innit? Though, I gotta admit, the atmosphere was buzzing. Proper carnival vibes. Buzzing alright. I accidentally ended up doing shots of something bright blue. Don't even remember ordering it. Chloe insisted. Chloe and her adventurous spirit! Always leads to trouble, that one. What even was it? Blue Curacao and something horrifying, probably. Honestly, no clue. Tasted like regret and bubblegum. Anyway, afterwards we ended up at The Velvet Rope. Big mistake. Oh lord. The Velvet Rope? That place is a black hole for your bank account and dignity. What happened? Don’t tell me you were line dancing. Worse. There was this guy. Proper…charming. Kept calling me “princess” and trying to buy me another one of those blue things. Oh, you’re kidding! A princess? You? You're more of a rogue, aren't you? What did you do? Kick him? Almost. Sarah had to physically remove me from the dance floor before I ended up in a full-blown argument about the proper way to pronounce “scone.” Apparently, he thought it was "scone" like 'gone'. You did  not  argue about scones with a man who was trying to ply you with coloured liquor! That's peak you. You're honestly brilliant. Liam would’ve been mortified watching that. He’d probably be trying to score a last-minute ticket to the match. Speaking of, how’d they do? Managed a draw. Bit of a damp squib if I’m honest. Felt like they were playing someone else’s game. Typical. Still, kept me entertained enough. Though, I’m definitely sticking to Netflix and biscuits tonight. My body is begging for mercy. I need to start on that exercise regime properly. Been putting it off for ages. Tell me about it. My mum's been on at me about joining that yoga class she keeps going on about. Says it’ll de-stress me. I told her my stress comes from avoiding boys in nightclubs offering sugary cocktails.

Honestly, between you and me, I’m dreading Gran’s visit. Not  her  specifically, bless her heart, but the sheer effort. It’s just… a lot. I haven't had to put on so much of a performance since I finished teaching. A performance? You’re being dramatic, Mum. It's a weekend. We’ll make it nice. And Dad’s happy to do the lion’s share of the heavy lifting. Besides, she loves Cumbria. Remember how she used to rave about the Lake District when we were little? I do. But that was when I had a bit more energy, didn't I? And less… responsibility. She’ll want to see the gardens, the lake, that dreadful little tea room in Keswick with the scones that crumble into a million pieces. Crumble nicely though, don’t they? Makes it easier to just eat them with your fingers. Less faffin’ about. See? David, you’d be happy living on chips and complaining about crumbs. It’s a skill, really. A survival trait, love. Essential for these later years. Less bother. Right, well, I was thinking about the bedding. Gran’s a light sleeper. Should we put her in the spare room with the thicker mattress? It’s quieter too, away from the main road. That’s a good idea, darling. Yes, the thicker mattress is crucial. Her back isn’t what it used to be. Did you manage to find that lavender spray I asked for? The one with the chamomile? I did! It’s in the linen cupboard. Just a quick spritz to help her relax. Are we doing the tour of the village again? She always asks about old Mrs. Henderson and her prize-winning roses. Of course. I’ll have to remember she’s forgetting things more often now. Last time, she asked me three times if I’d visited her sister. It was heartbreaking. Speaking of forgetting things, did you see the result of the Manchester United game yesterday? Absolute disgrace. They have no grit. No… …no backbone! Here we go. Don’t start, Dad. Gran's coming, remember? We can't have a full-blown rant about football. But it’s outrageous! Rashford missed a sitter! A sitter, I tell you! Anyone could’ve put that away. And the manager… the blame lies squarely with the manager. Absolutely no tactical awareness. David, please. Let's try and keep the conversation light, alright?

Right, so, about this laptop… Honestly, I’m still fuming. One minute I'm grading essays, the next it's face-planting onto the rug. A full-on kamikaze dive. Oh, Liam, that’s awful! Luckily, it wasn't a total disaster, right? You managed to get it working again? Barely. The screen’s got this weird ripple to it now. Makes reading code a nightmare. I’m starting to suspect the cat had something to do with it. He was eyeing it with a particularly suspicious glint. Cats will be cats, dear. My Brenda, the cat, once managed to knock over a whole shelf of china. Sent it shattering everywhere. Didn't even look guilty. Cats. Always causing trouble. Though, you know, back in my day, we didn’t have these fancy laptops. We had typewriters. Now  those  were robust. You could knock one down and it'd still probably be working. Grandad, you’re exaggerating! But honestly, Liam, is it insured? It is, technically. But the excess is almost as much as I paid for it. It’s not worth claiming, really. Just a reminder to be more vigilant. By the way, has anyone noticed this water? It tastes… weird. Like chalk. Oh, that's Southern Water, isn't it? They’re notorious. It's been like that for ages. I switched to bottled water. It's a pain, I know, but it’s better than drinking that stuff. What are you drinking, Sophie? Just tap water, actually. I’m getting used to it. It’s not  terrible . More…mineral-y? I was reading about all the different types of water – alkaline, spring, distilled… It’s a rabbit hole. Rabbit hole? Back in my day, water was water. Straight from the tap. Didn’t need all these fancy labels. Speaking of things that need fixing, I've been meaning to get round to that wobbly leg on the table. I thought I could try patching it with some wood filler. It's just a bit of DIY, really. DIY? Don’t go getting yourself hurt, Liam. Remember when I tried to hang a shelf? Ended up with plaster dust everywhere and a wonky shelf. It’s best left to the professionals. We should definitely go for a walk along the seafront later. Brighton’s looking lovely, even with this slightly drizzly weather. That sounds nice. Shame about the bin strikes though, the seagulls are having a field day.

Oh, honestly, dreadful result for the Villa. Absolutely dreadful. Two-nil down by half-time? How on earth did that happen? Aye, I saw. Proper hammering, didn't they? Man City’s just… relentless, isn't it? You’d think they'd let someone else have a chance, wouldn't you? Still makes for good drama, mind. Though I suppose you’re not thrilled. Drama? It’s a misery! I swear, watching them just exacerbates this… this gloom. This Poland gloom. You feeling alright, Auntie Eleanor? Still struggling with the SAD? It does get you down, especially with the weather. Tarnow isn’t exactly known for its sunny disposition. It is. It is. Though, you know, the coffee here  is  rather good. Much better than that lukewarm stuff we used to get at… Well, never you mind. This is a decent flat white. That's one small mercy. It is, isn't it? Best coffee I’ve had since… well, since leaving home, truthfully. Makes a difference. Tell you what, this student, Marek, he's really starting to get his head around the conditionals. Progress! Sometimes it’s just one small thing, like understanding “If I had gone…” and suddenly, it clicks. That’s wonderful, dear. It’s lovely when you see that spark. They rely on you, you know. Especially these exam years. That pressure… It’s a weight. I know, yeah. It’s hard not to feel responsible, isn’t it? Like, if they fail, it's… well, a bit of me fails too, I suppose. I was thinking of doing extra practice papers with him this week, just to build his confidence. Although, I wouldn’t put it past my headteacher to add more lessons on top of my already packed schedule. Oh, those people. They’re terrible. Absolutely terrible for workload. Did you ever… think about going back to England and working on a farm? My cousin, Cecil, he’s got a place in Somerset. He’s always complaining he can’t find reliable help. Me? On a farm? Auntie Eleanor, I'd be chasing sheep all day, and I have zero tolerance for muddy boots. Give me a classroom any day. Though, I do miss having dogs. Remember Buster, when I was little? I used to spend hours playing with him down at the park. He was a proper scruff, but I loved him. Oh, Buster!

Right, nearly there then. Smells better than it looks, doesn't it? It's a bit…rustic, I'll admit. Gran's recipe for Lancashire hotpot, mind. Always makes the house smell like Sunday afternoons at her house. Yeah, smells alright. Bit much for me, though. I'm more of a burger and chips kinda guy, to be honest. Not a big fan of all that… well, everything. Don’t be ridiculous, Liam! It smells amazing. And Annie’s Gran’s cooking is legendary. Remember that Christmas pud she made last year? It was practically a work of art. Aye, that was something else. Needed a chisel to get through it, that did! Seriously though, I’m starving. This conference saving has killed me. We've got that marketing launch next week, and the bloody caterers are STILL chasing me about dietary requirements. Gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free… you’d think people just liked eating air! Marketing launch, eh? Sounds important. Proper office job, that. Must be a bit intense. Tell me about it. Non-stop emails, spreadsheets bigger than my bedroom, and trying to keep everyone happy. It's exhausting, but it's alright. Pays the bills, doesn't it? What's been happening with you, Liam? Still wrestling with pipes and things? Yeah, pretty much. Got a new site this week, down near Stourbridge. Bit of a trek, but the money's decent. It's honest work, though. You know, actually  doing  something. Feels better than shuffling papers all day. Honestly, try it, Liam. It’s actually really good. The potatoes are lovely. Annie, you’ve outdone yourself. Glad you like it, Chloe! So, Chloe, fancy dress party next Saturday still on cards? I’ve been browsing Depop, and there's this incredible vintage dress… I reckon I could look proper smashing in it. It's a bit 70s, floral print, with these massive sleeves. Fancy dress? What's the theme? It’s "Decades". Apparently, someone’s going as a Victorian chimney sweep. Sounds… dusty. It will be! It’s at that new pop-up bar on Mill Road. Apparently, they've got a cracking cocktail menu. I'm thinking 90s. I might wear my old Spice Girls platform shoes. They're a bit knackered now, but… nostalgic, you know? And you should definitely go for the 70s dress, Annie. You’d look fab. Seriously, though… dating scene still quiet for you?

Blimey, look at this place, eh? Proper little oasis this is, Gordon Square. Not quite as picturesque as a Somerset valley, mind you, but still… nice. These lime trees are looking right healthy too. Reminds me a bit of that place down near Bath, you know, the Prior Park landscape gardens. It is pleasant. Bit busier than I’d anticipated for a Tuesday afternoon, though. Loads of folks just…existing, aren’t there? You’d think Londoners would be rushing somewhere, always. Though, I did see a little boy just now, chased a pigeon right across the path. Absolute joy on his face. Aye, that's a good 'un. Brings you back, doesn't it? Reminds you what it’s all about. Speaking of joy, did I tell you about the Chinese delegation we had in yesterday? Bright bunch. All here learning English, obviously. No, you didn’t. What were they like? Hope they’re enjoying London. It can be a bit… overwhelming for people coming from somewhere so different. Lovely bunch. Keen as mustard. One fella, Jing, was asking me about pandas. Apparently, he’s been to Chengdu and was worried about them being okay. Said the zoo back home was showing them, but…you know, the news. Yeah, the news… it’s not always the happiest, is it? Bears are majestic creatures. I remember reading a thing about the bears in Yunnan, their habitat's shrinking something shocking. Makes you think about the wider world, doesn’t it? Absolutely. It does. Makes you appreciate a simple Devon lane, doesn’t it? Driving through those hills… now  that’s  a landscape. Though, don't get me started on trying to navigate those roads in a rental car. You need nerves of steel, you do. Last time I was there, nearly drove into a flock of sheep. I can imagine! I’m dreading trying to get to the Isle of Wight in the summer. The ferry queues… nightmare. Remember that trip to Tibet we talked about? That was something else. The sheer scale of the mountains… astounding. Though, the tourist infrastructure was… well, let's just say it wasn't exactly Parisian elegance. Paris… don't even start. They’ve ruined it with all the selfie sticks and overpriced trinkets. It’s lost its charm, hasn't it? Still, I suppose that's the price of popularity. You know, my supervisor, Professor Davies, he's been on at me about my chapter on language acquisition amongst TEFL teachers in China.

Right, so remind me again  why  I’m crammed in the passenger seat of a ridiculously posh motor when I could be cuddled up with a cuppa and watching Bargain Hunt? Because you promised you’d look over the simulations, Chloe, and tell me if I’ve missed anything glaringly obvious. And because, let’s be honest, you like being crammed into ridiculously posh motors occasionally. Aye, well,  occasionally . It’s not exactly my natural habitat, is it? Feels…sterile. Like a hospital waiting room, but with better leather. And definitely smells fancier. Remind me how much this thing costs again? Don't even ask. It's...a significant number. Look, the simulations are on your tablet. I spent the whole of yesterday battling with the fluid dynamics model. It's driving me mad. Particularly the behaviour of the reinforced polymer at extreme pressure. Right, right. Polymer stuff. Sounds brilliant. You know I'm good at spotting errors in data, not so much with…science-y things. Just tell me what you want me to look for specifically. Is it about the bridge supports or something? Mostly the supports, yeah. They’re the critical pathway. The simulations show they  should  be holding, but there's a subtle oscillation I can't quite explain. It’s not catastrophic, not yet, but it's concerning enough that I wanted a fresh pair of eyes on it. Someone who isn’t swimming in the calculations. Oscillations... Right. Well, it  does  look a bit… jerky, doesn't it? See here, on line 47. This peak… it's a bit sharper than the others, isn’t it? Let me see… You’re right! Blimey. That’s…unexpected. I hadn’t noticed that. I've been so fixated on the overall trend I completely missed it. That’s brilliant, Chloe, seriously. You picked up on that immediately. I told you I was good at spotting anomalies. It's what I  do  at the archive. Finding things that don't quite belong. It's like a giant digital version of Marie Kondo-ing history. Right, well, thank you for Marie Kondo-ing my engineering project then. Okay, this changes things. I need to rerun the analysis, incorporating that new data point. It could mean revising the damping system entirely. Damping system? Sounds fancy. Will it mean more late nights for you? You've been looking a bit peaky lately. Probably.

Cor, this is reet good, Anon. Proper lush. You’ve outdone yourself. Cheers, Elara. Glad you like it. Mum's been experimenting with different hummus recipes again. She's obsessed, you know? It  is  delicious. Honestly, having something this decent to eat feels like a tiny luxury lately. Between deadlines and… well, everything. Everything? What’s got you down, Liv? You’ve been lookin’ a bit peaky these last few weeks. Like you’ve barely slept. It's just… a lot. Work’s been intense. And, to be honest, the whole dating app scene is exhausting. It’s one awful guy after another. Serial ghosters, people who only want a hook-up, you name it. I swear, half the profiles are just stolen Instagram photos. Tell me about it. My mate, Ben, downloaded one and lasted about an hour before deleting it. Said it made him feel like he was selling himself. Aye, it's reet depressing, isn't it? I tried Tinder once. Ended up on a date with a bloke who spent the whole time talkin’ about his Warhammer collection. Didn't even ask me me name! Oh, bless. See? That's what I mean. It's all so… performative. Like everyone is trying to be someone they're not to get a swipe right. I just want to meet someone… normal. Someone who likes dogs and doesn't think mansplaining is a personality trait. That’s a pretty solid wish list, Liv. Don’t settle. Don’t get sucked in by the shiny stuff. Exactly! You need someone wi' substance, lass. Someone who’ll bring you a cuppa when you're poorly and laugh at your daft jokes. That sounds amazing, Elara. I’m starting to think it doesn’t exist. It does! It's just… requires patience and discerning eyes. Mum always says, "Good things come to those who wait." Though I suspect she spends most of her time waiting for the kettle to boil. She's reet, though. Patience is key. Though, I’ll admit, I'm not the most patient person on the planet. Got no time for faffin' about. You're the most organized person I know, Elara. You practically run your entire conference on sheer willpower and spreadsheets. Clearly, patience isn’t needed when you’re managing hundreds of delegates and caterers. Aye, well, that's different. That's control. This… this lovey-dovey stuff?

Honestly, Liam is driving me up the wall. Again. Liam from accounts? What has he done now? Something involving spreadsheets and passive aggression, I presume? Worse. He’s trying to take credit for my presentation. The whole thing! I spent weeks on it, pulling all-nighters, and he’s just waltzing in this morning like he single-handedly devised the marketing strategy. No way! Seriously? That’s… appalling. Did Gareth notice? Gareth has to realize that, right? Gareth’s being his usual infuriating self. He mumbled something vague about “teamwork” and "pooling resources.” Ugh. You know Gareth – always wanting to avoid confrontation. It's leaving me to deal with this. I’m thinking of sending an email to him just outlining my contribution, but I don’t want to look petty. You’re not being petty, you’re being factual. Liam is being a massive, data-manipulating leech. Definitely send the email. Keep it professional, factual, and let it be clear where the bulk of the work came from. Don't give Liam any fuel for his fire. And copy Gareth CC'd. That way he can’t pretend he wasn’t aware of it. That's probably what I should do. I'm just worried it will make things awkward. You know how Liam is – he'll sulk and mutter under his breath. And Gareth will probably shuffle his feet and pretend he doesn't see it. Awkward is better than him getting away with it. Seriously, you’ve got to stand up for yourself. You’re brilliant at your job, you deserve recognition. And honestly, the office drama is exhausting. How was your patient load today? Anything… intense? Actually, surprisingly quiet. A couple of routine check-ups, a few anxiety cases, the usual. One patient, Sarah, she's… it’s hard to describe. She’s been struggling with the aftermath of a really nasty breakup. It’s heartbreaking. She keeps replaying the whole thing in her head, every single detail. It's like she's trapped in a loop. Breakups are brutal, especially when you’re stuck in that cycle. Have you tried encouraging her to focus on what she  gained  from the relationship – even if it’s just growth or learning something about herself? Yeah, we've been trying. It's slow going. It’s just… I remembered my own breakup with Tom, and the relentless replay of every conversation, every fight...

Right, so, you two are  really  set on this whole good versus evil thing, aren't you? It’s quite the philosophical debate for a Tuesday afternoon. Honestly, I was just trying to get dinner on the table. But Auntie Sarah, it  is  important! Is the dragon really bad? Or is he just… misunderstood? He breathes fire! Fire's bad! It burns things! Alright, alright, settle down, you two. Of course, fire can be dangerous, Finn. But dragons, like lots of things in stories, aren’t always just one thing. Think about the stories Nana used to tell us. Remember the Green Knight? Yes! He was scary! He was, wasn’t he? Big and green and... well, a bit grumpy. But he was also testing the knights, making them prove their bravery and honour. He wasn’t  evil  for evil’s sake. He was a challenge. And didn’t Sir Gawain eventually pass the test? He did! He almost didn’t though, didn’t he? About the lady… Yes, Finn. That’s another layer to it, isn’t it? Being tested in different ways. It's not always about fighting a monster. Sometimes, it’s about doing the right thing even when it's hard, or when nobody’s watching. Like when I shared my biscuits with Leo at school, even though I really wanted them all myself? Yes, darling, precisely like that. That was a very brave and kind thing to do. See? Not all 'good' things involve slaying dragons. But dragons hoard treasure! That’s greedy! Greedy is bad! It is, isn’t it? But even those stories have… nuances. Sometimes the treasure  represents  something else. Maybe it's about power, or control, or fear of losing what you have. It’s rarely just about shiny gold coins. Remember the story of the goblin who guarded the bridge? He wasn’t inherently bad, he just wanted to be acknowledged. He was lonely. So, even goblins can be sad? Absolutely. And even dragons. Think about it. They’re often guarding something precious, whether it's treasure or a secret, or even protecting their young. They might seem scary, but they're often acting out of something understandable, even if it’s not  nice . So, it's not always black and white? Like my colours? Blue is good, and brown is… mud? That’s a brilliant analogy, Finn! Exactly. Life, and stories, are full of greys.

Right, so Anon’s school trip… filming a documentary about the local wildlife reserve? Sounds… ambitious, doesn't it? Especially for Year 4. It is a bit, but Mrs. Davies is really keen. She says it's a fantastic opportunity for them to learn about conservation and develop their media skills. Plus, apparently, the reserve is beautiful this time of year. Is there squirrels? I really like squirrels! Yes, darling, there are definitely squirrels. Lots of them, I'm told. And rabbits, and maybe even a badger if you're very lucky! Will I see a fox? A big one? Possibly, Leo. But we’ll need to be very quiet and sneaky. It’s their home, remember? We're just visitors. Well, as long as they’re supervised properly. All this kit… cameras, microphones… it’s a recipe for chaos with that lot, isn’t it? I'm worried about them wandering off. And that leg of Anon’s… Is it getting any better? It's still a little tender, but she’s managing. She’s been doing her stretches. The physio said to really focus on those hamstring exercises. I told her she could be a superstar hamstring demonstrator! I am! Look! Right you are, superstar. Good for you. Still though, I'd hate for it to flare up on the trip. Are they taking a first-aider? Yes, Mrs. Davies mentioned a nurse volunteer is going along. And I’ve packed Anon a little ice pack just in case. She's been so brave about it, really. I’m proud of her for wanting to go, even with her leg. It's a big deal for her, you know? I do know. It's lovely. It's just… I worry. Always do. Speaking of things needing attention, have you been to the gym this week? I'm trying to get back into a routine. That running machine is calling my name. I managed a couple of sessions, yeah. It's hard to fit it in with everything else, isn’t it? Leo’s been having a rough patch with bedtime, and Anon’s leg has needed a bit of extra attention. But I actually enjoyed it, surprisingly. Managed to get a decent run in on the treadmill. Good on you. I need to push myself. I keep making excuses. "Oh, I’m tired," “got a bit of a headache”.

Right then, Barry. Lovely to see you. Didn't realise you’d be bringing Maureen along too. Good for her to get out. Always good to see you, Arthur! Maureen’s been feeling a bit cooped up lately, you know. The arthritis is playing up something fierce this winter. So, a nice lunch out is just what the doctor ordered. How are you holding up yourself? Still marking essays until midnight? Something like that. They're becoming increasingly...creative, let’s say. Fifteen-year-olds inventing Shakespearean sonnets about TikTok influencers. You wouldn't believe it. Still, keeps the mind sharp. Though I am feeling my age, I must admit. This nagging ache in my knee… Doc says it’s just wear and tear. Wear and tear, eh? That's what they all say, isn't it? I've got a dodgy shoulder myself these days. Tried that osteopath down on Ship Street, you know. Seemed to help a bit, though he had this rather alarming fixation with chakra alignment. Chakra alignment? Good heavens. I'm sticking to paracetamol and lukewarm baths, thank you very much. Listen, have you been following the local elections? The Green Party seems to be gaining traction. Oh, the Greens. Always good for a bit of a stir, aren’t they? Planting trees and banning plastic straws. Noble intentions, I suppose, but will it actually solve the real problems? My mate, Dave – you remember Dave, used to work for me at the caravan yard? – says they’re putting his business at risk with all this talk of eco-friendly caravans. It’s a tricky balance, isn't it? We need to think about the planet, obviously, but you can’t just cripple local businesses in the process. Though, Dave's caravans were never exactly eco-friendly, were they? More like slightly rusty and covered in questionable stains. You’re not wrong there! Still, he makes a living. Speaking of making a living, heard any whispers about the old Woolworths building getting repurposed? Thought it might be a good opportunity for some new shops. I heard something about it being turned into luxury apartments. Honestly, it’s getting ridiculous. More and more empty properties owned by foreign investors and barely a decent shop to be found. They're pricing everyone out. Exactly! Used to be you could find a bargain at the boot sales down at the Levels.

Honestly, Liam, you wouldn’t  believe  the conversation I had with Brenda from accounts today. She was going on about succulents. Succulents! Like I need more things to look after. My fiddle leaf fig is practically a full-time job already, you know? Brenda? From accounts? She’s fallen for the millennial plant craze, then. It’s a slippery slope, lass. Starts with a succulent, ends with a miniature jungle taking over your flat. You'll be networking with botanists next. Aye, don’t I know it. And she was giving me advice! “Direct sunlight, but not too much, a little misting…”. It's brutal, isn't it? Like, can't I just water it now and again and hope for the best? I’m a Research Manager, not a horticulturalist. You’re a Research Manager who apparently lacks confidence in her ability to keep a plant alive. It’s endearing, really. Though I'm convinced Brenda’s advice probably has merit. My mum's got a veritable greenhouse – she could probably resuscitate a plastic plant. She’d probably try! Speaking of things that require dedicated maintenance… have you looked at the latest collections from Loewe? The prices are ridiculous. Absolutely ludicrous. I saw a scarf – a  scarf , Liam – for £800. Eighty quid? Cor blimey! That’s…that’s bordering on the obscene, isn't it? I can’t justify that. I’m practically living off instant noodles to fund this PhD, as you well know. Though I did treat myself to a new pair of trainers last week. On sale, mind you. Trainers are acceptable. A scarf? Criminal. It's all part of the cycle, isn't it? The influencers, the fast fashion, then suddenly everyone's obsessed with…Loewe. What's next, solid gold wellington boots? Don’t even joke! Although… It  would  be waterproof. Practicality, lass. It's the key. You know, I was reading an article the other day about how some hedge funds are investing in luxury goods as a hedge against inflation. Apparently, it’s considered a ‘safe haven’ asset. Of course it is. Because when the world’s collapsing, you’ll be wishing you had a £800 scarf. I'd rather have a pasty, personally. A decent Cornish pasty. Have you tried one from that place near the market? The one with the line snaking around the corner? Yes, they’re brilliant. Proper flaky pastry, lovely filling… far more sensible than luxury scarves.

Honestly, this light is just  perfect  for painting. It's so… brooding. Reminds me of some Turner landscapes. I was showing the students some last week, and half of them just stared blankly. Said it was “depressing.” Depressing! It's beautiful melancholy! Typical. They want bright, primary colours and perfectly rendered avocado toast. No room for the sublime these days. How was the lecture overall? You were prepping that module on Romanticism, weren't you? It was… a mixed bag. They’re struggling with the concept of nature as a powerful, sometimes destructive force. All they know is nature documentaries narrated by David Attenborough. Everything’s cuddly and harmonious. I tried to illustrate it with the Orca documentaries we watched last month. Showing them the brutal efficiency of a pod hunting seals… And they were horrified? Appalled, absolutely. One girl actually gasped. I had to quickly steer the conversation back to Shelley and Wordsworth. It’s like they can’t reconcile the beauty of the poetry with the raw, sometimes horrific reality of the natural world. It’s a bit of a philosophical tightrope walk, isn’t it? Presenting art about nature, and then reminding them that nature isn’t all fluffy bunnies. It is. It's like the whole culture’s softened, ironically, over concerns about violence. I was marking that essay on contemporary television violence last week – a right mess, some of it. Accusations of desensitisation flying around, very passionate but rather shallow analysis. It's the responsibility angle, isn’t it? Whether it  causes  violence, or simply  reflects  it. Everyone wants to point fingers. My mum was saying the other day, she worries about the games the little ones play. Full of pretend gunfights and explosions. My niece is obsessed with Paw Patrol. Seismic activity and daring rescues every five minutes. At least it's well-intentioned. Though I do wonder if puppies saving the day is scarring them for real-world crises. You’re being overly dramatic! Although… remember that documentary about the squatters in 1980s London? The sheer ambition of trying to disrupt the property market with paint and plywood... It felt strangely… romantic. Now  that  is a strong comparison to Shelley and Wordsworth. Romantic squatting? Well, there  is  a certain rebellious spirit, isn't there? A yearning for something different, a rejection of the established order. It’s all about reclaiming space, metaphorically and literally.

This Ceylon’s a bit weak, isn't it, love? Reminds me of that stuff they served at the social club back in '78. Remember that social club, Sheila? Down on the Old Yarmouth Road… Oh, don’t remind me, Arthur! The dust and the damp. And the bingo nights... far too much shouting. Though, the sausage rolls were decent. Freelancer’s got a nice cuppa going, though. Much better than that muck. So, you were saying about these hostels? Running 'em sounds…complicated. Complicated is a mild word, Sheila. It’s a right kerfuffle, it is. Lots of folk needing a bed, you see. And not always easy folk, mind. Need a good head on your shoulders, that's what. Freelancer’s been doing a grand job though, keeping it all ticking over, bless ‘im. It’s a complex logistical problem, really. You’re managing diverse needs, budgets are often tight, and you have safeguarding responsibilities. Reminds me a bit of resource allocation in schools, actually. Different priorities constantly vying for attention. Though, I imagine the emotional toll is higher with hostels. Safeguarding, you say? Sounds frightening. Always worried about the youngsters. Speaking of youngsters, have you seen those photos Freelancer put on Facebook? The ones from the summer fete? Little Maisie looked a right picture in that flower crown. Aye, seen ‘em. Little Maisie does have a smile on 'er, she does. Brings a bit of sunshine into things, that one. Though, I was more interested in that car Freelancer’s got. That new electric thing, innit? Fancy. Never thought I’d see the day when a car ran on electricity. Remember when a Ford Anglia was considered fast? Electric vehicles are a significant engineering challenge, actually. The battery technology is constantly evolving. The density, the charging infrastructure... it’s fascinating. It’s leveraging principles of electrochemistry and materials science on a massive scale. It’s not just about plugging in, it’s about efficient energy storage and transfer. Science, science, science! Always with the science with you, John. I remember when my dad used to complain about how things were always changing. He ran a greengrocer’s, you see. “Everything’s plastic these days,” he’d grumble. "No proper rhubarb anymore, just imported rubbish.” Hardworking man, my dad. Worked from dawn ‘til dusk. Aye, hardworking folk. My mum ran a little sweet shop. Tiny place, Costessey. Smelled of licorice and sugary pop.

Honestly, David, I'm still reeling from marking those essays. It's… a wide spectrum, isn't it? Some are brilliant, genuinely insightful, and then you get others where you're questioning if they even  understand  what academic literacy means. Yeah, I noticed similar trends in my own course, actually. It's pretty disheartening when you see a student who clearly has potential, but their written work is riddled with… well, let’s just call it a lack of academic rigor. It felt like they were writing something they  thought  a lecturer wanted to hear rather than engaging with the material critically. Precisely! It’s performative, isn't it? They hit the keywords, maybe drop in a theorist or two, but there's no actual  analysis . And the referencing... don't even get me started. Footnote chaos. It’s a lot like what I used to see back in recruitment, actually. Recruitment? Really? I didn't know you'd had a life before teaching, Eleanor! Oh, a long one! Before this, I was a senior recruitment consultant for a fairly large firm in London. It felt like a different world, but surprising parallels, actually. Trying to spot genuine skills and qualities versus someone just dazzling you with jargon and a well-rehearsed story. You'd have candidates who’d completely embellished their experience, thrown around buzzwords like "synergistic solutions" and "proactive paradigm shifts," all to sound impressive. Oh, I can imagine. It's the same here. Students mimicking academic language without truly grasping the underlying concepts. It's often louder than the actual argument. It’s almost a… strategic obfuscation? Exactly! Strategic obfuscation! That's perfect. It's about presenting an image of competence, rather than demonstrating it. In recruitment, you'd see it in CVs. A wall of buzzwords, vague descriptions, and inflated responsibilities. The trick was to dig beneath the surface, to ask the right questions that forced them to actually  prove  they’d done what they claimed. Same principle applies here, I think. Direct questioning in seminars, targeted feedback on drafts... we need to force them to justify their assertions. So, you see a link between the kinds of performativity you observed in recruitment and what you're seeing in their academic essays? That's actually quite insightful. It's easy to compartmentalise – one’s a professional environment, the other an educational one – but the underlying motivation seems to be similar.

Honestly, this Victorian literature is drainin' me. Like, Dickens was a genius, yeah, but readin' about workhouses all day? It’s a bit bleak, innit? Tell me about it. I'm tryin' to make sense of Milton’s Paradise Lost. Seems like everyone's perpetually fallen. Speaking of which, I'm Liam, by the way. Just tryin' to survive this semester. Hi Liam! I’m Chloe. Yorkshire lass, like. Studying History. Dickens is my favourite though, surprisingly. I find the social commentary brilliant. The bleakness is a side effect of shining a light on some awful truths, you know? Oh, a History student, are you? Fancy. I'm Bethany. English Lit. And you're right, Chloe, there’s a bit more to it than just misery, I guess. It’s just… a lot. Hi everyone. I’m Anya. Nice to meet you all. I’m studying… well, it’s a bit complicated. It’s called Applied Linguistics. It’s about how language works, basically. Applied Linguistics? Sounds interesting! Like, you could figure out why people use certain phrases, or why some accents are misunderstood? Exactly! And a lot about how language changes and evolves. It’s surprisingly interconnected with things like sociology and psychology. I moved here from India a couple of years ago, so I'm always fascinated by the nuances of accents and dialects. My English was pretty good before, but learning all the different regional variations here has been a  journey.  A journey is right! I’m used to the Bradford twang, so hearing the Manchester accent, like Chloe’s got, took a bit of getting used to. It's lovely though, genuine. It’s all good up north, innit? It’s like, you can tell where someone's from just by listenin' to 'em. It’s a proper identifier. It's comforting, you know? Definitely. Back home, everyone sounds the same... well, almost. Gets a bit dull, actually. Whereabouts in Yorkshire are you from, Bethany? Bradford. Proper Bradford, near Eccleshill. You've probably never 'eard of it. Loads of terraced houses and chip shops. It’s brilliant for a curry though. So, Liam, what do you do when you're not battling Milton? I work at Carter's, down the high street. Sales assistant. Mostly shoes. Surprisingly stressful when a customer wants a size 7 but insists they're a 6.5. Keeps you on your toes, though.

Cor, this is reet good, innit? Proper scoff. Thanks for havin' us, ANON. No worries at all, Maisie! Glad you're enjoying it. So, you were saying about your cousin, Liam? The one who just joined the army? Aye, Liam. He’s gone then, properly gone. Off to… well, somewhere warm, apparently. Somewhere with sun and sand. Not Doncaster, that’s for sure. He’s been talkin’ about it for ages, really. Joining up, seeing the world, all that. I'm a bit gutted though, to be honest. He’s the only one left in the family who’s still… well, still around the house, ya know? Me and the others have all flown the nest. It’s a big step. My mate, Chloe, her brother joined a few years back. She was devastated at first, but he seems to be really thriving now. Sent her loads of pictures from, I think it was Cyprus? It does look pretty amazing out there. Aye, he sent me a postcard. Just a picture of a palm tree and "Wish you were here!" Like, yeah, I do, but I’m also proper worried about him. It's just... a bit scary, isn't it? Knowing he's going to be somewhere, doin' things. It is. But he wanted it, right? And it sounds like he's really settling in well. Did he say what he’s training to do? Something with logistics, I think. Apparently, they need folk who are good at organising things. He was always good at that, even as a lad, keeping all his Lego sets in order. Right proper neat freak. Ha! Well, that's a valuable skill, isn’t it? Speaking of organising things… I’ve been meaning to get back into scrapbooking. I used to be obsessed with magazines, ripping out all the fashion pages. Do you still read magazines? Not as much as I used to. I used to have a stack of 'Company' and 'Brides' in my bedroom. Me mum were mortified, said it were a waste of money. Now I mostly get my inspiration online. Pinterest's my go-to, for conference decor and things like that. Plus, you can get reet good deals on things there. Easier than lugging a load of magazines around. Pinterest is brilliant. I've found some amazing DIY tutorials on there. I found one for making custom laptop skins, using heat transfer vinyl.

Honestly, Liam. You wouldn’t  believe  the email I got from Mr. Hawthorne today. Wants me to redesign the entire south wing of Blackwood Manor. Apparently, Lady Blackwood thinks it's "lacking gravitas." Gravitas! Like a building can have gravitas! Blackwood Manor? You’re serious? Isn't that the one where they say the butler haunts the library? The very one. And he’s apparently very opinionated about the new panelling. Said it felt “too modern.” I nearly choked on my Earl Grey. You know I love a bit of gothic revival, but this is just ridiculous. Oh, bless her heart. Seriously though, you're basically being paid to appease a fussy old woman. You should charge extra for the emotional labour. Exactly! I'm sending him a draft with slightly more ornate corbels, just to shut him up. Then I’m going to suggest adding a gargoyle. A  giant  gargoyle. Now you’re talking! A gargoyle will show some gravitas. So, is this a proper commission, or just another endless revision cycle? It's a proper commission, thankfully. They're actually redeveloping the grounds, too. Apparently, some distant relative with a trust fund and a penchant for rare orchids has decided to revitalise the whole estate. Orchids? At Blackwood Manor? That’s a bit… jarring, isn't it? You have no idea. It's all very 'modern botanical garden' and zero 'creepy ancestral home.' I’m already dreading the mood board. Speaking of jarring… did you hear about that whole debacle with the council and the new housing development on the old brewery site? You mean the one they’re trying to cram in all those tiny apartments? Yeah, it’s outrageous. Foot and a half of green space per flat. They're calling it 'sustainable living.' Don’t even start me. It’s just blatant profiteering, isn't it? They’ll charge a premium for "urban convenience" and then people will be crammed in like sardines. Where's the community? Where's the space to actually  live ? It’s the same everywhere, isn’t it? They bulldoze all the character out of a place and replace it with identical grey boxes. And the people who protest get labelled as NIMBYs. You know, my cousin, Chloe, she’s coming up from London next week. Says she’s bringing a… friend. Oh? A boyfriend? Spill! Is he an architect? Please tell me he’s an architect.

So, Mum, Dad, what do you think? Bit of a change from Gillingham, eh? Bit smaller, definitely. It's lovely, honestly. Cosy. And really bright! I love all the plants. It’s… tidy. Too tidy, almost. Don't get me wrong, it's a nice flat. Better than that bedsit you were in, Alex. But it's missing a bit of… character. Where’s the clutter? A man needs some clutter! Don’t listen to him, love. He thinks clutter equals life experience. It just means he can't throw anything away. Alex, you've done a grand job. Very modern. Though, could do with a few more… well, things. Right. 'Things'. I'll add it to the list. We're trying to minimise, you know? Utility bills are a killer. And I'm convinced we’re ending up with half the world’s plastic bags, despite my best efforts. We do reuse them! For the cat, mostly. And for carrying groceries. Plastic bags... Back in my day, we used newspaper. Strong stuff, newspaper. You could wrap a whole roast chicken in it. These flimsy things now… ridiculous. It's the way of the world, Arthur. Trying to be responsible, isn’t it? Though, I do worry about the plastics in the sea. It's terrible, really. Speaking of worry, Alex, are you eating properly? You look a bit thin. All this teaching, are you having time to look after yourself? I'm fine, Mum. It’s just stressful sometimes. The students… they all have different accents and pronunciations. Getting them to say 'scone' properly is a nightmare. Do you say it with the 'o' or the 'u'? It’s a national debate! Right! Enough about pronunciation. Scones! Fresh out of the oven. With clotted cream and jam, properly. Not that stuff you get with lemon curd pretending to be clotted cream. Now you’re talking. A proper cream tea. You know, your Nan used to make the best scones. They were enormous. They could practically be used as doorstops. Oh, she did! Massive! And always a little bit burnt around the edges. But delicious. Arthur, you remember when you tried to win that competition at the village fete for the best scone? Don’t remind me. Those judges… biased, I tell you. Completely biased. My scone was perfectly acceptable. Just a little… dense. A little dense is putting it mildly, Dad.

Bleugh, this latte’s a bit weak, innit? Not like a proper Northern brew. Mind you, I shouldn't complain - at least it's not rainin'! Proper lashed down back home this mornin’. Flooded the market, apparently. Oh, really? That’s rough. Kent's been relatively calm, thankfully. Bit breezy, but nothin’ dramatic. Still, you’d think this time of year we’d have had a proper frost by now. Seems like climate change is just… messing with everything. Aye, tell me about it. I was readin’ an article online earlier, proper depressing stuff. About how the North Sea’s gettin’ warmer and it’s affectin’ the fishin’ industry. My grandad was a fisherman, you know? Proper gutted him to see it changin' like that. Yeah, that’s awful. I was just looking at figures about coastal erosion - parts of Norfolk are practically disappearing. My dissertation touched on some mitigation strategies… but honestly, it feels like we're just applying plasters to a gaping wound. Exactly! All this talk of net zero and carbon capture… it’s all well and good, but it feels like it's just a way for politicians to pat themselves on the back while the world burns. Speaking of politicians… did you see what that bloke Johnson said yesterday? Absolute gibberish, as usual. Oh, don’t even get me started. I try to avoid the news. It’s bad enough dealing with concrete and traffic flow diagrams all day without having to grapple with the fallout of whatever they’re doing – or not doing. It's enough to drive you mad. Still, gotta keep informed, right? Aye, though some days it feels like ignorance would be bliss. How’s the civil engineering goin’ anyway? Still workin’ on that new bridge project? Yeah, the A14 upgrade. It’s… comprehensive. A massive headache, to be honest. Constant issues with planning permissions, environmental impact assessments… the usual. And the public consultation last week was a nightmare. You wouldn’t believe some of the things people are worried about. One lady was convinced it would disrupt the migration of pygmy hedgehogs. Honestly? Pygmy hedgehogs? That’s brilliant! People will worry about anything, won’t they? At least it's not dealing with corpus linguistics. Try siftin’ through ancient dialects for errors all day. Nearly drove me to drink during my PhD. Sounds… intense. What are you workin’ on now, specifically?

Honestly, the staffing levels at the ward are just… laughable this week. We’re a patient short all over the place, and Mr. Henderson is still insisting on doing his rounds at a snail's pace. It's like he  wants  us to be run ragged. That's rough, Auntie Carol. Sounds worse than when you were telling me about that agency nurse who kept forgetting to administer the medication. Don't remind me! That was a nightmare. At least  this  is just chronically understaffed, rather than actively dangerous. Though, I did have to have a little word with young Ben the other day. He’s got a good heart, bless him, but he’s utterly hopeless at taking blood pressure. Three attempts, each one higher than the last! Ben? Bless his cotton socks. He’s always been a bit clumsy, hasn’t he? Remember when he knocked over Mrs. Peterson's oxygen tank at the Christmas party last year? Oh, don’t! The look on her face... Anyway, yes! He's a sweet lad, but needs a lot of guidance. I’ve suggested some extra training, but I doubt it’ll happen anytime soon. The budget, you know. It's the same at the care home, really. We're constantly short-handed. Mrs. Davies keeps complaining, says we don’t have enough time to properly help her with her meals. It’s just… demoralizing, isn’t it? It must be. At least as a copywriter, I can just complain to my laptop. Though, even that's stressful sometimes when the client wants something completely ridiculous. Like, seriously, requesting we use the word "synergy" in  every  sentence. Oh, I know that feeling! Patients asking for things that are medically impossible. "I want a cure for my aches and pains, Nurse, and it needs to be chocolate flavoured!" Speaking of chocolate, are we having that little get-together next weekend? Lily's birthday. Absolutely! I'm making my Victoria sponge, of course. Can't have a birthday without a proper Victoria sponge. Are you bringing your famous apple crumble, Diane? Wouldn't miss it for the world. Though, I'm not sure about the decorations this year. Little Lily’s got this obsession with dinosaurs now. Everything needs to be dino-themed. Dinosaurs! That’s brilliant! I'll bring some dino-shaped cookies. I found a recipe online. Hopefully, they won’t look too terrifying.
